title: P0: Live FrankenSQLite readiness self-invalidates healthy WAL by quarantining empty SHM
description: During controlled Agent Mail recovery on 2026-08-25, the server successfully opens and writes a reconstructed FrankenSQLite mailbox, then startup/periodic family cleanup quarantines an empty storage.sqlite3-shm while preserving a healthy framed WAL. The guarded same-engine read-only readiness path subsequently rejects the exact family because WAL exists without SHM. HTTP /health remains 503 and read-oriented MCP calls fail even while writes and full integrity checks succeed. This is an internal policy contradiction between classify_sqlite_family_cleanup/apply cleanup and preflight_bound_live_franken_family, not the reconstruct duplicate-row defect.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic regression reproduces the live FrankenSQLite family shape and proves same-engine readiness can query committed WAL state without mutating source bytes or names. Canonical/offline WAL-without-SHM ambiguity remains fail-closed. Damaged/truncated WAL, orphan nonempty SHM, nonregular sidecars, and namespace identity drift remain refused. Focused tests, fmt, and RCH check/build pass; controlled live server returns HTTP 200 readiness and Agent Mail read/write calls both succeed.
close_reason: FrankenSQLite live readiness now accepts certified SHM-less/empty-SHM WAL families without cleanup mutation while canonical ambiguous WAL families remain fail-closed.

title: macro_prepare_thread self-deadlocks 120s (SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT): WriteDbPool guard held across whois/fetch_inbox read-surface calls
description:
Found 2026-07-27 while verifying br-w9v59 via run_fixtures_against_rust_server_router (hidden until now because that test has been red on the health_check storage_root fixture drift since a22c1821, 2026-07-18).

MECHANISM: macros.rs macro_prepare_thread takes 'let pool = get_db_pool()?' (macros.rs:310) whose WriteDbPool holds an archive_read::WriteGuard for the entire function. It then awaits crate::messaging::fetch_inbox (macros.rs:426) — and in the register_if_missing=false variant crate::identity::whois (macros.rs:346) — both of which call get_read_db_pool -> archive_read::acquire_if_needed. The acquire ready-gate (archive_read.rs:1218/:1262) requires WRITERS_ACTIVE == 0, but the caller's own guard keeps it >= 1, so acquisition spins rebuilding until the 120s BUILD_TIMEOUT and surfaces SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT ('archive-read snapshot acquisition exceeded its 120 second deadline').

SCOPE: file-backed DBs only (memory DB short-circuits open_read_db_pool to Ok(None)), which is why memory-DB unit tests never see it. Deterministic 120s stall + error on EVERY production macro_prepare_thread call against a file mailbox since 301f5024 (br-lwwq5) moved read surfaces onto the archive-aware read pool. Swept the tools crate: macro_start_session, macro_contact_handshake, macro_file_reservation_cycle are clean (no held pool across read-surface awaits); macro_prepare_thread is the only holder.

REPRO: cargo test -p mcp-agent-mail-conformance --test conformance run_fixtures_against_rust_server_router — fails at macro_prepare_thread_no_llm after 120s+ (134s total run).

FIX: scope the write pool to its two genuine uses (resolve_project + list_thread_messages) and drop it before register/whois + fetch_inbox; no observable output change.
close_reason: Fixed and verified. Root cause: macro_prepare_thread held its WriteDbPool (whose archive_read::WriteGuard keeps WRITERS_ACTIVE >= 1 for the whole function) across awaits of whois and fetch_inbox, which acquire the archive-aware read pool; acquire_if_needed's ready-gate requires WRITERS_ACTIVE == 0, so acquisition spun rebuilding snapshots until the 120s BUILD_TIMEOUT — a deterministic self-deadlock on every file-backed-DB call since 301f5024 moved read surfaces onto the read pool. Clean-env control on remote worker vmi1149989 reproduced identically (122.46s) pre-fix. Fix (macros.rs): write lease scoped to resolve_project + list_thread_messages and dropped before register/whois/fetch_inbox; thread listing moved ahead of registration (no observable output change). Swept the tools crate for other holders: macro_start_session, macro_contact_handshake, macro_file_reservation_cycle are clean — this was the only site. Proof: run_fixtures_against_rust_server_router went from 134s-fail (SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT at macro_prepare_thread_no_llm) to ok in 16.31s; full conformance crate suite now exit 0 (13/13 binaries); cargo fmt clean; clippy -D warnings clean on mcp-agent-mail-tools + mcp-agent-mail-conformance.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Clean-env control confirmed before the fix: identical 120s deadline failure on remote worker vmi1149989 (122.46s run, no live server, fresh temp storage) — deterministic and environment-independent, matching the WriteGuard-held-across-read-await mechanism. Fix applied in macros.rs: write lease now scoped to resolve_project + list_thread_messages and dropped before register/whois and fetch_inbox; thread listing moved before registration (no observable output change — thread messages are independent of the calling agent's registration). Verification pending: run_fixtures_against_rust_server_router rerun.

title: ATC Track 9: TUI Screen + Robot Command Integration
description:
# Track 9: TUI & Robot Integration

## What
Surface ATC state in the TUI operations console and the robot CLI so operators
can monitor the ATC's decisions, override them, and understand what it's doing.

## TUI Integration Options

### Option A: Dedicated 16th Screen (MailScreenId::Atc)
A full ATC dashboard screen showing:
- Agent liveness map (Alive/Suspect/Dead with posterior probabilities)
- Conflict graph visualization (agents as nodes, wait-edges as arrows)
- Recent decisions timeline (from evidence ledger)
- Calibration guard status (coverage %, safe mode indicator)
- Session summary (latest synthesizer output)
- Loss matrix tuning controls (for power users)

### Option B: Integrate into Existing Screens
- System Health: add ATC subsection with calibration status
- Agents: annotate each agent with ATC liveness assessment
- Reservations: highlight deadlock cycles with colored borders
- Dashboard: add ATC intervention count to metrics

Recommendation: Start with Option B (less code, immediate value), add Option A
as a future enhancement if the ATC proves its worth.

## Robot CLI Integration
New robot subcommand: `am robot atc`

```bash
# Current ATC status
am robot atc --format toon

# Recent decisions
am robot atc --decisions --limit 20

# Agent liveness assessments
am robot atc --liveness --format json

# Conflict graph
am robot atc --conflicts --format json

# Session summary
am robot atc --summary --format md

# Force safe mode on/off (operator override)
am robot atc --safe-mode on
am robot atc --safe-mode off
```

## TUI Keybindings
If Option A screen is implemented:
- Tab 16 / keyboard shortcut to navigate
- `s` toggle safe mode
- `d` drill into decision detail
- `r` request immediate summary synthesis

## Dependency
- Requires Track 8 (Engine Integration) — ATC must be running
- Requires Track 4 (Evidence Ledger) — for decision display
- Requires Track 7 (Session Synthesizer) — for summary display

## Files
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/system_health.rs` (ATC section)
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/agents.rs` (liveness annotations)
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/reservations.rs` (deadlock highlights)
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/robot.rs` (new atc subcommand)

## Tests
- Unit: ATC section renders in System Health screen
- Unit: liveness annotations show correct state per agent
- Unit: robot atc subcommand produces valid toon/json/md output
- E2E: `am robot atc --format json` returns valid JSON

title: ATC Learning Epic: durable experience ledger, live autonomy, and regret-bounded adaptation
description:
# ATC Learning Epic: Durable Experience Ledger, Live Autonomy, and Regret-Bounded Adaptation

## Goal
Turn AirTrafficControl from a mostly observational or heuristic subsystem into a live, learning control plane that records what it did, why it did it, what happened next, and how future policy should change.

## Why This Exists
The current ATC has useful pieces: decision records, liveness tracking, conflict graphs, summaries, and operator views. What it does not yet have is a durable experience-learning loop. It needs a narrow, append-only experience ledger, delayed outcome attribution, compact state capture, materialized statistics, risk-bounded adaptation, fairness and anti-starvation guards, user-legible surfaces, and regime-aware rollback.

## Core Design Rules
- SQLite is the authoritative raw experience store.
- Raw ATC learning history is not written to Git by default.
- Hot-path capture must stay O(1) per decision/event.
- Outcome resolution must be monotone and idempotent.
- Adaptive logic must remain conservative for high-risk actions.
- Exploration is allowed only for low-risk actions and only under an explicit budget.
- Shadow mode stops being the public default; live execution becomes the normal path.
- User-facing surfaces must distinguish observation, action, suppression, and deliberate no-action without becoming noisy.
- The system must not concentrate intervention friction, false-action harm, or operator-noise burden onto the same agent/project/cohort without explicit budget and explanation.
- Verification must include comprehensive unit/property coverage, detailed E2E scripts, and artifact-rich failure logging.

## Selected Math Families
- online learning plus regret bounds for policy adaptation
- conformal risk control for false-action budgets
- empirical-Bayes shrinkage for sparse strata
- changepoint or regime detection for nonstationarity
- sequential evidence monitoring for calibration and rollback
- constrained optimization and fairness-style harm budgeting for anti-starvation and concentration control

## Success Criteria
- every ATC decision can be traced to a durable experience row
- every action either resolves to an outcome or is explicitly censored
- materialized stats support learning without raw-history rescans
- policy promotion, rollback, regime changes, and fairness guard activity are auditable
- operators and agents can see open experiences, regret, calibration stress, fairness/burden concentration state, current regime, and actionable next steps
- no agent, project, or important cohort silently absorbs unbounded intervention/noise concentration as the price of aggregate utility gains
- the entire system remains performance-bounded, low-noise, and safe under sparse/noisy data
- verification proves correctness, user-visible behavior, and failure diagnosis quality rather than only passing exit codes

## Acceptance Criteria
- the epic is self-contained enough that future contributors can understand the system goals, safety envelope, user goals, fairness constraints, and proof expectations without chat archaeology
- later phase beads can refine this contract but must not contradict the design rules here without explicitly updating the epic
- user utility, fairness, comprehensive verification, and forensic diagnosability are treated as first-class success conditions alongside mathematical correctness

## Scope Structure
This epic is intentionally split into phase epics for foundations, live capture, adaptive math, operator visibility, and replay/verification.

title: ATC Learning Phase 1: foundations, schema, and invariants
description:
# Phase 1: Foundations, Schema, and Invariants

This phase defines the data contract and operational envelope for ATC learning. The later capture and adaptation work should not invent ad hoc fields or write paths; they should plug into a stable experience model with explicit storage, latency, safety, and verification budgets.

## Deliverables
- canonical ATC experience tuple and lifecycle
- compact state/stratum encoding scheme
- SQLite tables, indexes, and migration plan
- retention/compaction/audit-snapshot policy
- explicit proof obligations, invariants, performance budgets, and implementation-surface ownership

## Acceptance Criteria
- later phases can implement capture, learning, and operator surfaces without inventing incompatible data contracts or side channels
- the phase explicitly defines the storage, performance, and safety envelope that later work must stay within
- the verification branch can derive what must be proven from this phase alone, including invariants, boundedness, and auditability expectations

title: ATC Learning 1.1: experience tuple, lifecycle, and identifiers
description:
# ATC Learning 1.1: Experience tuple, lifecycle, and identifiers

## Why
ATC currently has decision records and effect plans, but not a durable experience tuple that can survive long enough to learn from delayed outcomes.

## Deliverables
- define the canonical fields for an ATC experience row
- split decision_id, experience_id, effect_id, trace_id, claim_id, and evidence_id cleanly
- define the lifecycle state machine: planned -> dispatched -> executed|failed|throttled|suppressed|skipped -> open -> resolved|censored|expired
- define idempotent resolution semantics and one-decision-to-many-effect rules
- define how deliberate no-action and safety-gated suppression are represented so later surfaces and tests do not invent ad hoc states
- document which fields are required for learning vs optional for audit

## Acceptance Criteria
- the lifecycle contract explicitly distinguishes executed, failed, throttled, suppressed, skipped, resolved, censored, and expired states
- the identifier model is specific enough that later persistence, audit, replay, and test beads can refer to the same IDs without reinterpretation
- future implementers do not need chat history to understand the canonical experience row or state machine

## Important Notes
This bead is the canonical data-model contract for the rest of the ATC learning work. Future implementers should not need chat history once this issue is complete.

title: ATC Learning 1.10: implementation surface map across crates, runtime hooks, and operator/event paths
description:
# ATC Learning 1.10: Implementation surface map across crates, runtime hooks, and operator/event paths

## Why
The original ATC learning plan explicitly called for translating the design into concrete code changes across the Rust workspace. That work should not remain implicit. Future implementers need one bead that tells them where each part of the design lands: core, db, storage, server, tools, CLI/robot, TUI/web surfaces, and the verification layers.

## Deliverables
- map the durable experience model to the exact crates and modules that own types, persistence, and runtime updates
- map the append and resolution hooks across operator loop, tool dispatch, message events, reservation events, websocket/state snapshots, robot output, and verification harnesses
- identify the write-path boundaries, hot-path boundaries, cold-path/audit boundaries, and artifact-emission boundaries by crate
- define the cross-crate interface contracts so later implementation beads do not invent overlapping responsibilities
- map which crates and surfaces need unit/property tests, replay fixtures, E2E scripts, performance harnesses, and artifact capture hooks
- record the intended implementation order by crate/surface so future work can execute from the bead graph without re-reading prior chat history

## Acceptance Criteria
- a future implementer can derive both code ownership and verification ownership from this bead alone
- the bead makes it clear where logging, audit artifacts, and user-facing surfaces are sourced so later work does not scatter responsibility
- the implementation order is explicit enough to support parallel work without semantic overlap

## Important Notes
This bead is the execution map that turns the ATC learning design into an actionable Rust workspace plan. It should make clear where code belongs and where it absolutely does not belong.

title: ATC Learning 1.2: compact feature vector, strata, and quantization budgets
description:
# ATC Learning 1.2: Compact feature vector, strata, and quantization budgets

## Why
The learning system needs context, but storing verbose JSON per action will create IO churn and slow scans. We need a compact, versioned, numerically stable state representation.

## Deliverables
- choose the fixed-width hot-path features to persist as columns or compact integers
- define the quantization scheme for liveness, conflict, thread, and budget signals
- define the stratum key used for conformal risk control and shrinkage buckets
- define `feature_version` and evolution rules for future extensions
- document explicit storage and latency budgets for the chosen encoding

## Acceptance Criteria
- the feature set and quantization scheme are explicit enough that the schema, append, rollup, and test beads can implement them without inventing incompatible encodings
- storage and latency budgets are concrete enough to reject bloated feature additions before they reach implementation
- the stratum key and `feature_version` rules are defined tightly enough that later shrinkage and conformal beads can rely on them without hidden assumptions

## Important Notes
Favor basis points, bounded counters, enums, and ratios over free-form blobs. Rare or future-facing context can go into a tiny versioned extension payload, but hot learning features should stay cheap.

title: ATC Learning 1.3: SQLite schema, migrations, and indexes for experiences and rollups
description:
# ATC Learning 1.3: SQLite schema, migrations, and indexes for experiences and rollups

## Why
SQLite is the right authoritative store for raw ATC learning history, but the schema must be narrow, append-friendly, and resolvable without full scans.

## Deliverables
- define the raw experience table(s) and the minimal supporting rollup/state tables
- define indexes for open-experience lookup, resolution, stratum queries, and policy or regime slicing
- define the migration strategy and backfill behavior for existing installations
- specify how rollups are updated without violating hot-path budgets
- document why raw history stays in SQLite while Git only receives selected audit artifacts

## Acceptance Criteria
- the schema supports append, point lookup, open-resolution, and grouped rollup queries without falling back to full-table scans in steady state
- migration and backfill rules are explicit enough that future implementers do not need to guess how existing installations should transition
- the SQLite-vs-Git boundary is defined clearly enough that replay, audit, and operator-surface beads can consume the right source of truth without duplication

## Important Notes
The schema should optimize for append, point lookup, and small grouped scans. Avoid designs that require joining large JSON blobs or rebuilding rollups from scratch in steady state.

title: ATC Learning 1.4: retention, compaction, archive policy, and policy snapshot strategy
description:
# ATC Learning 1.4: Retention, compaction, archive policy, and policy snapshot strategy

## Why
Raw experience history is valuable for learning, but unbounded retention and Git writes will eventually make the system noisy and expensive.

## Deliverables
- define retention windows for raw rows, unresolved rows, materialized statistics, audit artifacts, and any scenario-linked forensic evidence that must remain comparable across verification runs
- define compaction rules that preserve learning value while reducing storage churn
- define what gets archived to Git: policy bundles, regime summaries, promoted exemplar traces, or periodic human-readable audits
- define what explicitly does not get archived by default
- define operator-visible lifecycle rules for old data, stale regimes, and archived-vs-live evidence
- define how retention/compaction choices preserve replay comparability and audit discoverability over time

## Acceptance Criteria
- the plan makes it clear what data stays hot, what is compacted, what is archived, and what is intentionally dropped
- retention rules preserve both learning utility and later forensic/debugging value for the verification branch
- archive policy remains low-write-amplification while still leaving users and operators able to find the evidence they need

## Important Notes
The target is durable learning with low write amplification. Git should hold explainability artifacts, not high-volume telemetry exhaust.

title: ATC Learning 1.5: invariants, performance budgets, and conservative fallback contract
description:
# ATC Learning 1.5: Invariants, performance budgets, and conservative fallback contract

## Why
Adaptive systems are dangerous when their safety invariants are implicit. This bead turns those assumptions into explicit engineering contracts.

## Deliverables
- define hot-path complexity and latency budgets for decision logging, event resolution, summary reads, and operator-surface refreshes
- define invariants for monotonicity, idempotent resolution, bounded memory growth, and absence of accidental raw-history scans on user-facing paths
- define freshness/staleness and partial-data contracts so surfaces must say when state is degraded rather than silently pretending calm
- define the conservative fallback policy under sparse data, drift, write pressure, broken calibration, or incomplete execution truth
- define rollback triggers and non-regression obligations for behavior-changing policy updates
- define explicit false-action, silent-failure, user-noise, and diagnostic-artifact-completeness budgets that later math, surfaces, and tests must respect
- capture the proof obligations future code and tests must satisfy

## Acceptance Criteria
- the contract covers acted paths, deliberate no-action paths, safety-gated suppression paths, and stale/partial-state paths rather than focusing only on successful interventions
- the budgets are concrete enough that later performance, property-test, surface, and rollout beads can verify them directly
- future implementers can tell what must happen when confidence is low, evidence is stale, snapshots are partial, or the system becomes too noisy

## Important Notes
This bead is the guardrail for the rest of the backlog. If a later change cannot satisfy this contract, it should not ship.

title: ATC Learning 1.6: baseline current ATC behavior, risk, and resource budgets before adaptation
description:
# ATC Learning 1.6: Baseline current ATC behavior, risk, and resource budgets before adaptation

## Why
The alien-artifact execution loop starts with a baseline. Without one, the project cannot tell whether the learning stack actually improved correctness, latency, operator utility, or safety.

## Deliverables
- capture the current ATC behavior before learning changes: what decisions it makes, what effects actually execute, what is safety-gated, and what remains inert
- capture the current mix of executed interventions, deliberate no-action, and noisy or low-value signals so later work has a real comparator for operator calm
- capture the current latency, memory, IO, contention, and artifact-write budgets relevant to ATC hot paths
- make the failure-cost asymmetry explicit across advisories, probes, releases, and higher-force interventions
- define reproducible baseline collection commands/manifests, scenario IDs where applicable, and artifact locations so later before/after comparisons are mechanically repeatable rather than reconstructed by hand
- define the baseline comparator that later optimization and adaptation work must beat or preserve
- record the current operator-surface limitations and current test/diagnostic blind spots so later UX and verification improvements have a concrete before/after reference

## Acceptance Criteria
- the baseline covers user-facing calm/noise behavior, not just raw runtime metrics
- the baseline package is reproducible enough that future maintainers can regenerate or compare it without consulting chat history
- later optimization and rollout work can point to a concrete before/after baseline without reconstructing it from chat history
- the bead captures both operational and observability gaps in the pre-learning system

## Important Notes
This bead exists to prevent self-congratulating adaptation with no comparator. Later policy and performance changes should point back to this baseline.

title: ATC Learning 1.7: assumptions ledger, EV gate, and transparency cards for mathematical decisions
description:
# ATC Learning 1.7: Assumptions ledger, EV gate, and transparency cards for mathematical decisions

## Why
The learning design uses several mathematical families. Their assumptions, expected-value justification, interaction constraints, and operator-facing rationale need to be captured explicitly so future changes do not drift into decorative or unsafe complexity.

## Deliverables
- record the assumptions ledger for adaptation, conformal control, shrinkage, regime detection, rollback, and any other material controller added later
- record the EV or relevance or risk gate for each major method family in the design, including why it helps users and what failure mode it is meant to control
- define the transparency-card format for policy changes and major mathematical decisions, including the policy IDs, evidence IDs, regime context, and operator-facing rationale the card must carry
- define what evidence would justify escalating mathematical sophistication versus stopping, and what evidence would justify simplifying, disabling, or removing a method family that is no longer earning its keep
- record assumption-invalidating signals and “this method is now suspect” indicators so future operators do not need to rediscover when the math stopped matching reality
- ensure future contributors can understand the why behind the design without consulting prior chat history

## Acceptance Criteria
- a future implementer can tell from this bead alone when a new mathematical mechanism is justified, when it is not, what evidence would be required to promote it, and what evidence would justify simplifying or retiring it
- transparency cards are defined concretely enough that later audit and operator-surface beads can expose rationale without inventing a second format
- the bead explicitly protects against math-for-math’s-sake complexity by tying every major method family back to user value, safety, diagnostic value, or explicit sunset criteria

## Important Notes
This bead is not optional documentation fluff. It is the reasoning contract that keeps the learning stack auditable, understandable, and worth operating.

title: ATC Learning 1.6: baseline current ATC behavior, risk, and resource budgets before adaptation
description:
# ATC Learning 1.6: Baseline current ATC behavior, risk, and resource budgets before adaptation

## Why
The alien-artifact execution loop starts with a baseline. Without one, the project cannot tell whether the learning stack actually improved correctness, latency, operator utility, or safety.

## Deliverables
- capture the current ATC behavior before learning changes: what decisions it makes, what effects actually execute, and what remains inert
- capture the current latency, memory, IO, and contention budgets relevant to ATC hot paths
- make the failure-cost asymmetry explicit across advisories, probes, releases, and higher-force interventions
- define the baseline comparator that later optimization and adaptation work must beat or preserve
- record the current operator-surface limitations so later UX improvements have a concrete before/after reference

## Important Notes
This bead exists to prevent self-congratulating adaptation with no comparator. Later policy and performance changes should point back to this baseline.

title: ATC Learning 1.7: assumptions ledger, EV gate, and galaxy-brain transparency cards
description:
# ATC Learning 1.7: Assumptions ledger, EV gate, and galaxy-brain transparency cards

## Why
The learning design uses several mathematical families. Their assumptions, EV justification, and interaction constraints need to be captured explicitly so future changes do not drift into decorative or unsafe complexity.

## Deliverables
- record the assumptions ledger for adaptation, conformal control, shrinkage, regime detection, and rollback
- record the EV/relevance/risk gate for each major method family in the design
- define the operator/developer transparency-card format for policy changes and major mathematical decisions
- document what evidence would justify escalating mathematical sophistication versus stopping at a simpler approach
- ensure future contributors can understand the why behind the design without consulting prior chat history

## Important Notes
This bead is not optional documentation fluff. It is the reasoning contract that keeps the learning stack auditable and understandable.

title: ATC Learning Phase 2: live capture and outcome-resolution wiring
description:
# Phase 2: Live Capture and Outcome Resolution Wiring

This phase connects the ATC's existing live execution paths to the new experience ledger. The intent is to capture real decisions, real effect executions, and real downstream events so outcomes can be resolved from production evidence instead of test-only hooks.

## Deliverables
- durable append path for decisions/effects/executions
- real execution-truth capture from the operator loop
- message, reservation, conflict, deadlock, participation, and session-synthesis event wiring
- unresolved-experience index and timed/censored resolver
- live executor default, real probe action, and tightened effect semantics

## Acceptance Criteria
- the learning stack is fed by authoritative production events rather than inferred state or placeholder paths
- executed, failed, suppressed, skipped, and censored states become first-class machine-readable facts across the runtime
- later learning, surface, and verification beads can consume this phase as the single source of truth for what actually happened in production

comments.author: codex
comments.text: Phase 2 is where the earlier ATC completion backlog lands: durable capture, live execution, real probes, and production event wiring. The main intent is to replace ornamental ATC math with real production evidence.

comments.author: codex

title: ATC Learning 2.1: durable append path for decisions, effects, and executions
description:
# ATC Learning 2.1: Durable append path for decisions, effects, and executions

## Why
ATC cannot learn unless every relevant decision becomes a durable experience record. The current in-memory ledger is not enough.

## Deliverables
- append ATC decisions into the durable experience store at creation time
- attach the relevant IDs, policy revision, action family, and compact context snapshot
- ensure effect plans and execution attempts are linked back to the originating decision or experience
- make append behavior robust to duplicate or repeated signals
- keep the hot path O(1) and avoid large object cloning or string bloat

## Acceptance Criteria
- every relevant decision, effect, and execution attempt can be durably linked without ambiguous fan-out or missing identity edges
- capture is idempotent under repeated signals and cheap enough to remain on the hot path
- later resolution, summary, and verification beads can treat the append path as the authoritative starting point for learning history

## Important Notes
This bead is about capture, not about labeling or adaptation. It should make the raw evidence durable first.

title: ATC Learning 2.2: execution result capture from the operator loop
description:
# ATC Learning 2.2: Execution result capture from the operator loop

## Why
A decision that never executed is not the same as a decision that executed and failed. The learning system needs execution truth, not just intent.

## Deliverables
- record whether an effect executed, failed, was throttled, was skipped, or was suppressed by policy
- capture execution timestamps and any bounded failure reason needed for later attribution
- feed the execution result back into the experience row without violating idempotence
- separate transport or runtime failure from policy failure in the stored outcome evidence
- preserve explicit env overrides while making live execution the normal operator path

## Acceptance Criteria
- executed, failed, throttled, skipped, and suppressed are canonical machine-readable states rather than ad hoc strings or implied behavior
- execution truth is rich enough for labeling automata, operator surfaces, and verification suites to agree on what really happened
- the plan makes clear that live execution is the default posture while still leaving explicit override knobs available for controlled exceptions

## Important Notes
This bead is where the experience ledger stops being a pure decision log and becomes a real action ledger.

Remote rch verification is blocked by unrelated compile failures in /data/projects/sqlmodel_rust/crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite (Arc<str>/Arc<[u8]> conversion mismatches). Leaving bead in progress until shared dependency tree is green again.

title: ATC Learning 2.3: wire message, advisory, probe, and ack events into outcome resolution
description:
# ATC Learning 2.3: Wire message, advisory, probe, and ack events into outcome resolution

## Why
Many ATC actions are validated by messaging behavior: later activity, direct acknowledgements, thread participation, or the absence of either.

## Deliverables
- wire message-sent, message-received, ack, and later-activity signals into the resolver
- connect advisory and probe actions to their attribution windows
- define how thread participation and later activity close or fail message-driven experiences
- distinguish positive resolution, negative resolution, and censoring by system shutdown or missing project context
- ensure repeated events do not double-resolve the same experience

## Acceptance Criteria
- message-driven outcomes resolve deterministically, idempotently, and with project scoping intact
- acknowledgement, later-activity, and participation signals are differentiated clearly enough that tests and operator explanations can agree on why an experience resolved
- missing context or shutdown paths become explicit censoring states rather than silent drops or ambiguous failure labels

## Important Notes
This bead is about turning live messaging behavior into deterministic outcome evidence, not about free-form NLP or LLM interpretation.

title: ATC Learning 2.4: wire reservation, conflict, and deadlock events into outcome resolution
description:
# ATC Learning 2.4: Wire reservation, conflict, and deadlock events into outcome resolution

## Why
Release requests, conflict advisories, and deadlock interventions need to be judged by what actually happened to reservations and conflict structure afterward.

## Deliverables
- wire reservation grant, release, and conflict signals into the resolver
- connect deadlock-cycle changes and blocked-edge disappearance to relevant experiences
- define how reservation-side events resolve release, conflict, and intervention actions
- preserve project scoping so cross-project noise does not contaminate labels
- ensure graph maintenance and outcome resolution agree on the same underlying event semantics

## Acceptance Criteria
- reservation and deadlock outcomes are derived from authoritative live signals rather than stale inferred state or test scaffolding
- project scoping and deduplication rules are explicit enough to prevent false labels from repeated or cross-project events
- conflict-graph maintenance and outcome resolution consume one coherent event model instead of diverging over time

## Important Notes
This is the bridge between the conflict graph and the learning ledger. It must stay deterministic and cheap.

title: ATC Learning 2.5: open-experience index and timed/censored resolution engine
description:
# ATC Learning 2.5: Open-experience index and timed/censored resolution engine

## Why
Delayed feedback is normal in ATC. We need a small, explicit unresolved set rather than scanning history to see what is still waiting on evidence.

## Deliverables
- maintain an in-memory open-experience index keyed by decision or experience identity
- maintain a bounded per-target or per-cohort frontier of open candidate causes so overlapping interventions can be inspected for eligibility without rescanning history
- drive timed resolution and expiration windows from that index
- emit explicit censored, expired, or causally-confounded outcomes when evidence never arrives cleanly enough to support a trustworthy label
- ensure restart and recovery semantics for open rows are well-defined
- keep memory bounded and lookup O(1)

## Acceptance Criteria
- the open set stays bounded, restart-recoverable, and explicit enough to support long-delay, overlap-heavy, and crash-recovery scenarios without guesswork
- expiration, censoring, and confounded-attribution states become first-class states visible to rollups and operator summaries rather than silent row mutations
- the plan guarantees that the system can answer both \"what is still unresolved?\" and \"what is unresolved because competing causes overlap?\" without any raw-history scan

## Important Notes
This bead is the runtime backbone of delayed attribution. Without it, the rest of the math is mostly ornamental or causally overconfident.

title: ATC Learning 2.6: make live execution the default and replace fake probe intent with a real probe action
description:
# ATC Learning 2.6: Make live execution the default and replace fake probe intent with a real probe action

## Why
ATC cannot learn from real outcomes if the normal mode is inert or if probe actions are placeholder strings instead of real effects.

## Deliverables
- make live execution the default executor mode while preserving explicit override knobs
- replace the probe-intent placeholder with a real probe action path
- ensure probe executions are durable, attributable, and visible to the operator surfaces
- record intervention telemetry whenever the operator loop actually executes an effect
- remove or demote public-facing shadow semantics so they no longer define the system's default behavior

## Acceptance Criteria
- the default operator posture is live execution, with any non-live mode remaining an explicit override rather than the ambient behavior
- fake probe intent is removed from the normal path and replaced by a real, durable, attributable probe effect
- executed, suppressed, or skipped probe behavior is visible to learning state, operator surfaces, and verification scenarios instead of disappearing behind placeholder semantics

## Important Notes
This bead is both a utility fix and a prerequisite for meaningful learning.

title: ATC Learning 2.7: audit and tighten release/advisory/probe effect semantics for safety and utility
description:
# ATC Learning 2.7: Audit and tighten release/advisory/probe effect semantics for safety and utility

## Why
The earlier ATC completion work explicitly called for reviewing whether advisory, release, and probe effects are safe, useful, and worth the operator or user disruption they create. That concern deserves a first-class implementation bead.

## Deliverables
- audit the current effect families for unsafe, noisy, or low-value behavior
- tighten message content, execution rules, and preconditions for release, advisory, and probe actions
- distinguish clearly between low-risk nudges and high-risk interventions
- define repetition-suppression, cooldown, escalation, and operator-facing remediation rules so repeated low-value advisories or probes do not become spam
- ensure outward-facing effect content stays concise, actionable, and tied to the concrete signal, evidence, and next-step guidance that triggered it
- make the tightened semantics visible to the outcome resolver and learning system
- document the intended utility model for each effect family so later adaptation is optimizing something real

## Acceptance Criteria
- each effect family has explicit utility, safety, and precondition rules that later adaptation and user-surface beads can rely on without reinterpretation
- low-risk nudges and high-risk interventions are separated clearly enough that exploration and admissibility policies do not blur them later
- repeated low-value or redundant effects are explicitly suppressed, cooled down, or escalated according to deterministic rules rather than left to ad hoc caller behavior
- user/operator-facing effect content gives concrete remediation and evidence pointers instead of generic noise
- any effect family that remains too noisy or unsafe to justify optimization is explicitly constrained rather than silently kept in scope

## Important Notes
This bead is about making the actions themselves worth learning over. A bad action family with a perfect learner is still a bad system.

ATC-focused `rch` test execution is currently blocked before test run by an unrelated existing const-trait compile error in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/atc_fairness.rs` (`u32::from(u16)` inside const fns).

title: ATC Learning 2.8: thread participation graph and session-synthesis wiring from live message events
description:
# ATC Learning 2.8: Thread participation graph and session-synthesis wiring from live message events

## Why
The earlier ATC completion backlog explicitly called out wiring real domain message events into session summaries and thread participation tracking. That signal is also important for learning features and for understanding coordination pressure before conflicts erupt.

## Deliverables
- wire live message events into the thread participation graph, not just into raw message counters
- make session synthesis and thread-level coordination features update from the same production event stream
- expose the derived participation state to the learning feature pipeline without rescanning history
- keep participation updates deterministic and project-scoped
- document how thread participation influences advisories, probes, and downstream risk signals

## Acceptance Criteria
- participation and session-synthesis state update from the production event stream only, not from periodic rescans or test-only reconstruction
- the derived state is deterministic and project-scoped enough that summaries, learning features, and tests can all consume it without disagreement
- the bead makes clear how thread participation changes downstream risk and actionability instead of leaving it as an ornamental metric

## Important Notes
This bead ensures message traffic affects more than inbox counts. It becomes a real coordination signal in the ATC kernel.

title: ATC Learning 2.9: conflict-graph maintenance and blocking-conflict ingestion from live reservation results
description:
# ATC Learning 2.9: Conflict-graph maintenance and blocking-conflict ingestion from live reservation results

## Why
The earlier ATC completion work explicitly called out two separate needs: keep the conflict graph updated from live grant or release events, and ingest blocking-conflict information from reservation conflict tool results. That wiring needs to be explicit, not assumed.

## Deliverables
- parse live reservation conflict results into blocking-conflict observations usable by ATC
- update conflict-graph state from reservation grant and release events in production paths
- ensure conflict-graph maintenance and learning or outcome attribution share the same event semantics
- prevent duplicate or stale conflict edges from distorting later labels and summaries
- document the authoritative source of truth for blocking relationships versus active reservations

## Acceptance Criteria
- live reservation results produce authoritative blocking-conflict observations with explicit deduplication and stale-edge handling
- conflict-graph state, outcome resolution, and operator summaries all consume the same conflict semantics instead of drifting apart
- the bead leaves no ambiguity about whether production runtime events or test scaffolding own the conflict graph

## Important Notes
This bead exists because the conflict graph is only useful if it is fed by real runtime events rather than test scaffolding or stale inferred state.

title: ATC Learning Phase 3: adaptive math stack and safety envelope
description:
# Phase 3: Adaptive Math Stack and Safety Envelope

This phase turns captured experiences into useful adaptation. It covers outcome labeling, sufficient statistics, shrinkage, conformal budgets, regret-bounded policy updates, regime detection, fairness/anti-starvation constraints, contamination/anti-gaming robustness, interference-aware credit assignment, controller composition, and automatic rollback.

## Deliverables
- deterministic outcome automata
- materialized sufficient-stat rollups
- shrinkage across sparse cohorts
- conformal risk budgets by action family and stratum
- finite-policy adaptation with exploration constraints
- fairness, anti-starvation, and per-entity harm budgets
- contamination detection, influence-limiting, and anti-gaming safeguards for strategic environments
- interference-aware attribution, causal eligibility windows, and confounded-outcome handling for overlapping interventions or exogenous changes
- regime detection, control composition, and safe rollback logic

## Acceptance Criteria
- the phase yields bounded adaptation over an explicit policy family rather than unconstrained self-modification
- sparse data, drift, stressed risk budgets, fairness/harm-budget pressure, suspicious or contaminated evidence, and causally confounded outcomes all lead to conservative behavior that is inspectable and testable
- later user-surface and verification beads can explain both action and deliberate non-action, including fairness-driven vetoes, contamination-driven distrust, or robustness-driven throttles, from the contracts defined here
- the phase makes it explicit when ATC may learn from an outcome, when it must defer or censor because attribution is ambiguous, and how that choice becomes visible to users and audits

title: ATC Learning 3.1: outcome labeling automata and censoring rules by action family
description:
# ATC Learning 3.1: Outcome labeling automata and censoring rules by action family

## Why
ATC needs deterministic, machine-checkable rules for what counts as success, failure, suppression, or censoring. Without that, the learning loop will drift into ad-hoc label noise.

## Deliverables
- define action-family-specific labeling rules for probe, advisory, release, conflict, and no-op/suspect actions
- define how safety-gated suppression, throttling, and skipped execution states feed into the labeling automata
- define attribution windows, causal eligibility windows, and delay handling
- define how overlapping eligible causes, exogenous recoveries, or concurrent operator changes downgrade confidence, split credit in bounded ways, or force censoring instead of false precision
- define censoring reasons, ambiguity/confoundedness reasons, and expiration behavior
- define realized_loss and reward semantics consistently across action families
- document ambiguous cases and how they are downgraded to censoring or explicit confounded-attribution states instead of forced labels

## Acceptance Criteria
- the labeling automata consume real execution-truth states rather than inferring outcomes from intent alone
- acted, deliberately non-acted, safety-suppressed, and causally confounded paths all have explicit deterministic treatment
- the plan explicitly prevents overlapping interventions or natural recovery from being silently converted into confident single-cause labels
- future verification beads can turn this bead directly into replay expectations and property tests

## Important Notes
This bead turns execution truth plus delayed evidence into stable labels. If it is vague, the rest of the adaptation stack becomes statistically noisy or causally dishonest.

title: ATC Learning 3.9: safe policy-improvement certificates with doubly-robust off-policy evaluation and anytime-valid confidence sequences
description:
# ATC Learning 3.9: Safe policy-improvement certificates with doubly-robust off-policy evaluation and anytime-valid confidence sequences

## Why
Policy promotion is the single highest-leverage and highest-blast-radius adaptive move in the ATC design. A candidate policy can look better in simple regret tables while still being biased by selection effects, weak support overlap, optional stopping, or hidden tail-risk on user-facing noise. The plan needs an explicit mathematical certification layer that blocks promotion unless ATC can demonstrate, with auditable evidence, that the candidate is better enough and safe enough to replace the incumbent.

## Deliverables
- define the promotion-certificate artifact that must exist before any candidate policy revision can displace the incumbent
- define the regime-aware off-policy evaluation stack for candidate-versus-incumbent comparison using doubly-robust or augmented inverse-propensity estimation rather than raw win-rate heuristics
- define overlap/support diagnostics, clipped or stabilized importance-weight controls, and refusal-to-certify behavior when counterfactual support is too weak
- define anytime-valid confidence-sequence or e-process style evidence thresholds so policy promotion remains valid under continuous monitoring and optional stopping
- define tail-risk and operator-noise protection so a candidate cannot be promoted on mean utility alone while worsening false-action spikes, spamminess, or other bad tail outcomes
- define blocker reason codes and machine-readable certificate fields for sparse data, unstable regime, overlap failure, weak lower bound, tail-budget violation, or unresolved attribution backlog
- make certificates traceable to policy IDs, revisions, regimes, strata, experience slices, and comparator baselines so later audits and surfaces can explain both promotions and non-promotions
- define what evidence can still be reused across regime boundaries and what must be reset, discounted, or explicitly marked as non-transferable

## Acceptance Criteria
- no candidate policy can be promoted without a positive, auditable improvement certificate against the incumbent rather than a heuristic score alone
- the design uses refusal-to-certify as a first-class safe outcome when overlap, attribution quality, or regime stability is inadequate
- promotion requires non-inferiority or bounded degradation on user-noise and tail-risk budgets, not just average reward improvement
- downstream summary, audit, explainability, unit-test, E2E, and rollout beads can all point to this bead as the canonical contract for why a promotion was allowed or denied

## Important Notes
This bead is the bridge between causal inference, sequential validity, tail-risk control, and operator trust. It is deliberately stronger than a generic "candidate scoring" story: the whole point is to turn policy promotion into something that is certifiable, inspectable, and safely blockable.
notes: Duplicate of canonical safe policy-improvement certificate bead br-0qt6e.3.9

title: ATC Learning 3.11: fairness, anti-starvation, and per-agent/project harm budgets
description:
# ATC Learning 3.11: Fairness, anti-starvation, and per-agent/project harm budgets

## Why
A globally efficient ATC can still be user-hostile if it repeatedly burdens the same agent, project, or cohort because those cases are easier to measure, easier to optimize against, or more visible in the telemetry. The learning stack needs an explicit fairness and anti-starvation contract so it does not concentrate probes, advisories, suppressions, false positives, or intervention friction onto the same targets while claiming aggregate utility gains.

## Deliverables
- define the fairness observables ATC should track across agents, projects, and other relevant cohorts: intervention frequency, false-action exposure, suppression exposure, unresolved-backlog burden, probe burden, and operator-noise concentration
- define anti-starvation rules so quiet, low-volume, or low-visibility agents/projects are not systematically ignored when they actually need attention
- define per-agent, per-project, or per-cohort harm budgets and concentration limits that constrain both act-time decisions and policy adaptation
- define the interaction between global expected utility and fairness constraints, including when a fairness or anti-starvation guard vetoes an otherwise attractive action or policy move
- define machine-readable fairness debt, burden-concentration, and most-impacted-target indicators that can flow into summaries, audits, and rollout checks
- define how fairness state decays, resets, or is reweighted across regime changes so old concentration does not either vanish too fast or poison the future forever
- document what forms of asymmetry are acceptable, what forms are suspicious, and what evidence would justify deliberate unequal treatment

## Acceptance Criteria
- no agent, project, or tracked cohort can absorb an unbounded or poorly explained share of probes, advisories, suppressions, or false-action harm simply because it is easier for the learner to optimize there
- the fairness contract is explicit enough that later surfaces, audits, and tests can distinguish healthy prioritization from harmful concentration or starvation
- the design states what happens when fairness constraints conflict with short-horizon global utility, including which side wins and how that decision is made visible
- future verification beads can derive anti-starvation, bounded-concentration, and fairness-budget tests from this bead alone without chat archaeology

## Important Notes
This bead is not about flattening all distinctions or banning prioritization. It is about preventing a mathematically sophisticated system from becoming quietly unfair, annoying, or trust-eroding to the exact users it is supposed to help.
notes: Implemented fairness, anti-starvation, and harm-budget contract in atc_fairness.rs; targeted rch check/test passed, core clippy still blocked by unrelated modules.

title: ATC Learning 3.12: feedback-loop contamination detection, anti-gaming safeguards, and adversarial robustness
description:
# ATC Learning 3.12: Feedback-loop contamination detection, anti-gaming safeguards, and adversarial robustness

## Why
ATC is not learning from a neutral laboratory. It learns from agents, operators, and systems that can respond strategically or accidentally distort the evidence stream. Interventions can change observability, agents can learn to look alive without being healthy, noisy cohorts can dominate labels, and duplicated/delayed/replayed signals can make the learner over-trust bad evidence. Without an explicit anti-gaming and contamination contract, the rest of the math can still be elegant while the system learns the wrong lesson.

## Deliverables
- define the contamination and strategic-behavior threat model for ATC learning: replayed or duplicated events, spoofed liveness, performative acknowledgements, message floods, reservation churn, operator-induced selective labeling, coordinated agent behavior, intervention-caused observability shifts, and other self-fulfilling or self-canceling feedback loops
- define the observables and machine-readable suspicion states for evidence quality at the experience, actor, cohort, policy, and regime levels
- define how suspicious evidence is downweighted, quarantined, capped in influence, excluded from promotion evidence, or retained only for monitoring rather than control
- define robust aggregation or influence-limiting rules so a small number of adversarial or low-quality traces cannot dominate policy updates, fairness state, or previews
- define how contamination suspicion affects admissibility gates, certificates, previews, summaries, fairness logic, rollback triggers, and operator-visible reason codes
- define how ATC distinguishes real improvement from intervention-shaped observability artifacts, label leakage, or strategic adaptation by the agents it supervises
- define recovery, decay, and re-entry rules so contaminated evidence does not poison the future forever but also cannot be forgotten instantly without explanation
- define how audit artifacts and operator surfaces expose "data not trusted" conditions without collapsing into paranoia or noisy false alarms
- define efficiency constraints so robustness checks use maintained statistics, bounded state, and targeted diagnostics instead of expensive full-history rescans

## Acceptance Criteria
- the plan explicitly prevents policy promotion, preview trust, or unsafe action confidence from silently relying on obviously suspicious or strategically contaminated evidence
- future surfaces and tests can explain when ATC is acting on trusted evidence, when it is monitoring but not trusting certain data, and why that happened
- the robustness contract is specific enough that unit tests, E2E scenarios, audits, and rollout gates can derive anti-gaming and contamination cases from this bead alone without chat archaeology
- the bead strengthens the learning system without turning it into opaque paranoia theater or unbounded forensic overhead

## Important Notes
This bead is not optional hardening polish. It is a core requirement for any autonomous learning loop that operates in a strategic environment and supervises actors that can react to the system itself.

title: ATC Learning 3.13: interference-aware credit assignment, overlapping intervention attribution, and causal eligibility windows
description:
# ATC Learning 3.13: Interference-aware credit assignment, overlapping intervention attribution, and causal eligibility windows

## Why
ATC does not operate in a clean single-cause world. Multiple interventions can overlap in time, operators can change controls mid-stream, exogenous project events can resolve a problem naturally, and one action can change the observability of another. If the learner credits or blames the wrong cause, it can look mathematically disciplined while adapting in the wrong direction. This bead exists to make attribution itself first-class, rather than assuming every resolved outcome belongs cleanly to one decision.

## Deliverables
- define the interference model for ATC learning: simultaneous or overlapping interventions, operator control changes, natural recoveries, exogenous load or coordination shifts, and observation-only events that occur inside an attribution window
- define causal eligibility windows and candidate-cause sets so the system knows which open experiences are even eligible to receive credit or blame for a given downstream outcome
- define how overlapping eligible causes are handled: downgraded confidence, censoring, explicit ambiguity states, bounded multi-touch credit, or "do not learn from this" outcomes when identifiability is too weak
- define how attribution confidence or confoundedness is represented in experience rows, rollups, summaries, previews, certificates, and audit artifacts
- define how interference-aware attribution interacts with contamination detection, fairness/burden accounting, regime changes, and rollout decisions so overlapping causes do not silently distort other guardrails
- define efficient runtime structures for maintaining the open-experience frontier per target or cohort, candidate-cause lookup, and attribution resolution without full-history rescans or unbounded combinatorial blowups
- define how the system distinguishes true improvements from natural recovery, parallel operator intervention, or competing ATC actions that would otherwise produce false learning signals
- define operator-visible reason codes and explainability hooks for "improved but attribution uncertain", "confounded by concurrent change", and "insufficient causal isolation to update policy"

## Acceptance Criteria
- the plan explicitly prevents ATC from treating every resolved outcome as a clean label when overlapping causes or exogenous changes make attribution ambiguous
- later math, surface, and verification beads can explain when ATC learned from an outcome, when it refused to learn, and why attribution confidence was downgraded
- the attribution contract is strong enough that summaries, previews, audit artifacts, unit tests, E2E scripts, and rollout reviews can all reuse it without inventing incompatible causal stories
- the design keeps attribution honest without exploding runtime cost, history scans, or operator cognitive overhead

## Important Notes
This bead is the causal honesty layer for the learning loop. It should make the system more trustworthy to users by teaching it to say "multiple things happened; I cannot honestly assign credit yet" instead of silently learning the wrong lesson.

title: ATC Learning 3.14: safe value-of-information control, identifiability debt, and targeted low-risk experiment design
description:
# ATC Learning 3.14: Safe value-of-information control, identifiability debt, and targeted low-risk experiment design

## Why
Even with strong logging, certificates, contamination defenses, and interference-aware attribution, ATC can still get stuck in uncertainty-limited regimes where the system cannot safely learn enough from ambient production behavior alone. The smartest next step is to make ATC an active but disciplined scientist: it should know when uncertainty, confounding, or sparse support is blocking improvement, maintain an explicit identifiability-debt ledger, and spend tiny, low-risk, budgeted experiments or probes only when the expected information value clearly beats the user-noise and safety cost.

## Deliverables
- define an identifiability-debt ledger for action families, cohorts, and policy questions where current evidence is insufficient for confident adaptation, certification, or attribution
- define a safe value-of-information or knowledge-gradient scoring layer that estimates the expected learning value of a candidate probe, advisory variant, randomized tie-break, or low-risk intervention against its user-noise, fairness, contamination, and tail-risk cost
- define experiment eligibility gates so only low-risk, reversibly bounded actions can ever be chosen for information gain, and only when the normal policy is uncertainty-limited rather than already decision-sufficient
- define experiment budget tables across action family, cohort, regime, and time window so learning pressure cannot silently grow into spam, unfair burden concentration, or operational chaos
- define how targeted experiments are announced, previewed, logged, and linked to the experience ledger so later attribution, certificates, and audits know that an action had both control value and information value
- define how active experiments interact with contamination defense, interference-aware attribution, fairness budgets, and rollback so the system never learns aggressively from suspicious or strategically distorted settings
- define when the correct decision is "do not experiment" because the regime is unstable, the evidence is contaminated, the likely user burden is too high, or the incremental information value is too small
- define compact runtime artifacts for the whole stack: identifiability-debt tables, value-of-information scores, experiment-eligibility automata, budgeted experiment scheduler, and machine-readable reason codes for why an information-seeking action was allowed or refused

## Acceptance Criteria
- the plan explicitly upgrades ATC from passive learning only to safe active information acquisition, but only inside a strict low-risk and low-noise envelope
- later surfaces and tests can explain when a probe or intervention was issued partly to reduce uncertainty, what debt it was meant to repay, and why that was worth the cost
- the design makes "do not experiment" a first-class safe outcome when information value, fairness, contamination, or operator burden do not justify action
- the new learning mechanism is specific enough that summaries, previews, explainability cards, E2E scripts, and rollout gates can all reuse it without inventing incompatible stories

## Important Notes
This bead is the dual-control / active-experimentation layer for ATC. It is radically accretive because it lets the system learn faster and more honestly under sparse or confounded evidence, while still staying bounded, auditable, and user-respectful.

title: ATC Learning 3.2: materialized sufficient statistics and EWMA/delay rollups
description:
# ATC Learning 3.2: Materialized sufficient statistics and EWMA/delay rollups

## Why
The learning loop cannot afford to rescan raw history. It needs maintained statistics that summarize outcomes by the dimensions that matter.

## Deliverables
- define the per-stratum, per-action, per-policy rollups needed for learning
- maintain resolved and open counts, realized-loss aggregates, EWMA loss, and delay histograms
- define update semantics when rows resolve or are censored
- make the summaries cheap to query from the operator loop and robot or TUI surfaces
- document which statistics are authoritative and which are derived caches

## Acceptance Criteria
- maintained statistics are sufficient for learning, summaries, and verification without raw-history rescans in steady state
- update semantics are explicit enough that later work can reason about resolve, censor, and delay effects without inventing side rules
- authoritative-versus-derived boundaries are clear enough to prevent operator surfaces and math components from reading incompatible states

## Important Notes
This bead exists to keep the adaptive loop fast and explainable at the same time.

title: ATC Learning 3.3: empirical-Bayes shrinkage across agent, project, and program strata
description:
# ATC Learning 3.3: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage across agent, project, and program strata

## Why
Many ATC buckets will be sparse. If the system trusts tiny sample counts too aggressively, it will overfit and make unstable policy moves.

## Deliverables
- define the cohort hierarchy used for shrinkage: global, program, project, agent, and action-family strata
- choose the shrinkage model for success/failure and realized-loss estimates
- define minimum-support behavior and how posterior estimates back off to broader cohorts
- expose the effective sample size or strength-of-evidence concept for inspection
- document when shrinkage should be disabled or reduced under clear high-support evidence

## Acceptance Criteria
- sparse buckets cannot produce aggressive policy movement without explicit support and visible fallback to broader cohorts
- the shrinkage hierarchy is concrete enough that learning, summaries, and tests can all agree on where evidence is borrowed from
- operators and verification suites can inspect effective sample size or equivalent evidence strength rather than treating shrinkage as hidden magic

## Important Notes
Shrinkage is here to prevent unstable behavior, not to hide uncertainty. The system should stay conservative when evidence is thin.

title: ATC Learning 3.4: conformal risk control and per-action false-action budget tables
description:
# ATC Learning 3.4: Conformal risk control and per-action false-action budget tables

## Why
ATC needs a mathematically explicit brake on harmful actions. Learning is only useful if false positives stay bounded for each action family and operating stratum.

## Deliverables
- define the stratum-aware conformal or CRC budget tables ATC will maintain
- define the nonconformity scores used for each action family
- define bucket starvation and merge fallback behavior
- define budget-consumption, cooldown, and recovery semantics so operators and tests can tell whether action is blocked because evidence is weak, a budget is exhausted, or the system is intentionally cooling down
- define how risk budgets gate action admissibility and exploration
- expose operator-visible health indicators and reason categories when a budget is healthy, stressed, cooling down, or actively blocking action

## Acceptance Criteria
- the risk tables define explicit false-action budgets by action family and stratum rather than vague "be conservative" guidance
- starvation and merge fallback rules are explicit enough that sparse buckets cannot silently widen risk beyond the intended safety envelope
- operator and verification beads can tell when a budget is healthy, stressed, cooling down, or blocking action from this bead alone
- suppression due to risk budgets is explainable enough that downstream surfaces do not collapse it into generic silence

## Important Notes
This bead is the explicit brake pedal for adaptive ATC. If it is underspecified, the rest of the math becomes unsafe.

title: ATC Learning 3.5: finite-policy regret-bounded adaptation engine
description:
# ATC Learning 3.5: Finite-policy regret-bounded adaptation engine

## Why
ATC should adapt over a small, explicit family of policy artifacts rather than mutate free-form thresholds in uncontrolled ways. It also needs an internal candidate-scoring path so the system can keep learning from counterfactual comparisons without falling back to a user-visible inert shadow mode.

## Deliverables
- define the finite family of candidate policy artifacts for ATC to choose among
- define the regret signal and update rule used to compare incumbent and candidates
- define the internal off-policy or counterfactual scoring path used to evaluate non-selected candidates from the recorded experience stream
- define promotion criteria, support floors, and sample-efficiency thresholds
- keep policy updates auditable through policy IDs, revisions, strata/regimes, and evidence summaries
- document why the chosen policy family is expressive enough without becoming un-debuggable

## Acceptance Criteria
- the bead explicitly distinguishes live execution from internal candidate scoring so the plan cannot regress into public shadow-mode inertia
- candidate promotion requires attributable evidence tied to realized outcomes plus counterfactual or off-policy scoring records
- the design states what happens when data is too sparse, too stale, or too unstable to justify promotion

## Important Notes
Internal counterfactual evaluation stays. Public-facing inert shadow mode does not. This bead is about learning safely from alternatives while keeping the real system useful by default.

title: ATC Learning 3.6: regime detection, hysteresis, and history discounting
description:
# ATC Learning 3.6: Regime detection, hysteresis, and history discounting

## Why
History cannot be pooled forever as if workloads were stationary. ATC needs to know when the environment has changed enough that old evidence should count less.

## Deliverables
- define the changepoint or drift signal ATC will monitor
- define regime IDs, hysteresis, minimum dwell or stabilization rules, and transition criteria
- define what gets reset, discounted, frozen, or merely annotated across regime changes
- gate policy promotion during unstable transitions
- define operator-visible transition reasons and compact “what changed” summaries so a regime flip is diagnosable rather than mysterious
- make regime state inspectable from summaries and operator tooling

## Acceptance Criteria
- regime transitions are explicit, inspectable, and protected by hysteresis so the system does not flap between states under noisy evidence
- old evidence cannot silently contaminate new policy movement after a real regime shift
- transition states are explainable enough that downstream surfaces and audits can show whether the system is stable, transitioning, cooling, or frozen
- later audit, surface, and verification beads can tell when the system is stable, transitioning, or frozen from this bead alone

## Important Notes
This bead is the nonstationarity contract. If it is vague, the learning system will either overreact to noise or stay stuck on stale history.

title: ATC Learning 3.7: admissibility gates, exploration budget, and automatic rollback
description:
# ATC Learning 3.7: Admissibility gates, exploration budget, and automatic rollback

## Why
Adaptive control without a strict safety envelope is not acceptable here. The system needs explicit bounds on when it may act, when it may explore, when suspicious evidence should reduce trust instead of increasing confidence, and when it must retreat.

## Deliverables
- define the action-tier model separating low-risk and high-risk actions
- define the exploration budget and the conditions under which exploration is allowed
- define the admissibility gate that combines calibration, conformal budgets, regime state, sparse-data checks, and contamination-suspicion or evidence-quality checks
- define automatic rollback triggers and fallback-to-incumbent behavior
- document why high-risk actions remain conservative even when low-risk actions adapt, and why suspicious evidence should tighten rather than relax the gate

## Acceptance Criteria
- exploration is permitted only for explicitly allowed low-risk action families under a bounded budget with auditable triggers
- rollback and fallback-to-incumbent rules are machine-readable and operator-visible rather than hidden in prose or implementation folklore
- the safety envelope makes suppressed or blocked actions legible instead of collapsing them into ambiguous non-behavior
- the gate can explicitly refuse action or refuse to trust recent evidence when contamination, gaming, or observability distortion is suspected

## Important Notes
This bead is where the learning system earns the right to act.

title: ATC Learning 3.8: controller-composition rules, timescale separation, and anti-oscillation design
description:
# ATC Learning 3.8: Controller-composition rules, timescale separation, and anti-oscillation design

## Why
The learning stack combines multiple adaptive controllers: calibration/e-process alarms, conformal risk budgets, shrinkage, regret-bounded policy updates, fairness/anti-starvation guards, regime detection, and rollback logic. Without an explicit composition contract, they can interfere or oscillate.

## Deliverables
- define the update order and authority boundaries among the adaptive components
- define the timescale separation between fast guards, medium-horizon policy updates, fairness-budget adjustments, and slow regime changes
- define anti-oscillation rules and hysteresis where multiple controllers interact
- document what can veto what, and in what order, when the system is under stress
- make fairness and anti-starvation guards first-class citizens in the composition matrix rather than implicit side constraints
- provide a compatibility matrix that future contributors can use before adding another controller to the ATC stack

## Acceptance Criteria
- controller ordering, veto rules, and timescale separation are explicit enough that future implementation and tests can detect oscillation, authority inversions, or fairness-controller bypasses
- the composition rules preserve calm operator behavior instead of letting adaptive components create contradictory, unfair, or rapidly flapping outputs
- future contributors can evaluate a new controller against this bead alone without re-deriving the system’s control-theory contract from chat history

## Important Notes
This bead is the missing control-theory glue. It prevents the adaptive pieces from fighting each other or quietly routing harm into whichever controller happens to be easiest to optimize.

title: ATC Learning 3.9: safe policy-improvement certificates with doubly-robust off-policy evaluation and anytime-valid confidence sequences
description:
# ATC Learning 3.9: Safe policy-improvement certificates with doubly-robust off-policy evaluation and anytime-valid confidence sequences

## Why
Policy promotion is the single highest-leverage and highest-blast-radius adaptive move in the ATC design. A candidate policy can look better in simple regret tables while still being biased by selection effects, weak support overlap, optional stopping, hidden tail-risk on user-facing noise, strategically contaminated evidence, or causally confounded outcomes where multiple interventions or exogenous changes overlap. The plan needs an explicit mathematical certification layer that blocks promotion unless ATC can demonstrate, with auditable evidence, that the candidate is better enough and safe enough to replace the incumbent.

## Deliverables
- define the promotion-certificate artifact that must exist before any candidate policy revision can displace the incumbent
- define the regime-aware off-policy evaluation stack for candidate-versus-incumbent comparison using doubly-robust or augmented inverse-propensity estimation rather than raw win-rate heuristics
- define overlap/support diagnostics, contamination-evidence diagnostics, attribution-confounding diagnostics, clipped or stabilized importance-weight controls, and refusal-to-certify behavior when counterfactual support, causal isolation, or evidence trust is too weak
- define anytime-valid confidence-sequence or e-process style evidence thresholds so policy promotion remains valid under continuous monitoring and optional stopping
- define tail-risk and operator-noise protection so a candidate cannot be promoted on mean utility alone while worsening false-action spikes, spamminess, or other bad tail outcomes
- define blocker reason codes and machine-readable certificate fields for sparse data, unstable regime, overlap failure, suspicious evidence, attribution confounding, weak lower bound, tail-budget violation, or unresolved attribution backlog
- make certificates traceable to policy IDs, revisions, regimes, strata, experience slices, comparator baselines, attribution-confidence state, and any evidence-quality quarantines so later audits and surfaces can explain both promotions and non-promotions
- define what evidence can still be reused across regime boundaries and what must be reset, discounted, or explicitly marked as non-transferable

## Acceptance Criteria
- no candidate policy can be promoted without a positive, auditable improvement certificate against the incumbent rather than a heuristic score alone
- the design uses refusal-to-certify as a first-class safe outcome when overlap, attribution quality, causal isolation, regime stability, or evidence trust is inadequate
- promotion requires non-inferiority or bounded degradation on user-noise and tail-risk budgets, not just average reward improvement
- downstream summary, audit, explainability, unit-test, E2E, and rollout beads can all point to this bead as the canonical contract for why a promotion was allowed or denied

## Important Notes
This bead is the bridge between causal inference, sequential validity, tail-risk control, robustness to contaminated evidence, interference-aware attribution, and operator trust. It is deliberately stronger than a generic candidate-scoring story: the whole point is to turn policy promotion into something that is certifiable, inspectable, and safely blockable.

title: ATC Learning Phase 4: operator surfaces, audit artifacts, and explainability
description:
# Phase 4: operator surfaces, audit artifacts, explainability, and preflight visibility

## Why This Exists
If the adaptive ATC core becomes more sophisticated while the user-facing surfaces stay vague, stale, or post-hoc, the system will feel clever but unsafe. Phase 4 exists to make the learning system legible before, during, and after action.
