title: Dual-mode interface program: MCP-first default + opt-in agent-first CLI
description:
Background:
Users asked for an explicit dual-mode interface strategy:
1) MCP mode must remain the default.
2) A separate setting (OFF by default) can disable MCP-first behavior and enable a full agent-first CLI command surface.
3) When MCP mode is ON, CLI invocation should fail fast with a clear message like "Agent Mail is not a CLI!" and actionable guidance.

Why this matters:
The current surface area is confusing across binaries and command families. We need one coherent contract so operators, agents, and docs all align.

Outcome:
A production-ready dual-mode architecture with explicit guardrails, clear UX, test coverage, and rollout playbook.

Program-level definition of done:
- Mode contract is documented and enforced.
- MCP default remains unchanged.
- CLI mode is explicit opt-in.
- Denial path in MCP mode is deterministic and tested.
- CLI mode command parity roadmap is implemented and validated.
design: Dual-mode interface is implemented as a single authoritative mode decision (resolver) consumed by all entrypoints. Mode controls command dispatch policy, UX messaging, and allowed command families. MCP mode remains default and is conservative by design; CLI mode is explicit opt-in via config switch.
acceptance_criteria: 1) MCP mode is default and denies CLI command execution with canonical message/hints. 2) CLI mode opt-in enables documented command families with agent-first ergonomics. 3) Behavior is validated by unit/integration/conformance/perf tests. 4) Docs and rollout playbooks are updated.
notes: Planning assumptions: no implicit mode auto-switching; no hidden compatibility shims; no mode decisions duplicated in per-command handlers. This epic intentionally front-loads policy/contract work to avoid implementation drift.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Execution blueprint:
1) Finish Track 1 policy artifacts first (contract, denial UX, allowlist, parity matrix).
2) Build Track 2 resolver/config foundation.
3) Implement Track 3 guardrails and Track 4 command families in parallel where dependencies permit.
4) Run Track 5 validation suites as hard gate.
5) Complete Track 6 docs/rollout only after quality gates pass.

Parallelization guidance:
- Track 1 tasks can be split among spec owners but must converge before Track 3/4 starts.
- Track 4 command families (4.2-4.7) are parallelizable after 4.1.

Risk notes:
- Primary risk is accidental CLI execution in MCP mode; treat denial path as security boundary.
- Secondary risk is parity drift; close via 4.8 + 5.3 conformance checks.

title: Track: Mode contract, UX policy, and scope definition
description: Background: lock down product/behavior contract before code changes. Deliverables: dual-mode invariants, denial UX contract, MCP-mode allowlist, and command-parity target matrix. Reasoning: implementation without policy hardening will reintroduce ambiguous behavior and drift.
design: Policy-first track: freeze invariants and UX contracts before touching code. This track is the source of truth for downstream implementation and tests.
acceptance_criteria: ADR approved; denial UX contract approved; MCP-mode allowlist approved; parity target matrix approved and linked by dependent tasks.
notes: Without this track, implementation risk is high due to ambiguous operator expectations and contradictory command behavior.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Track 1 intent: define policy before code.

Do not start implementation beads that depend on this track until the artifacts are explicit and approved.

Required artifacts from this track must be referenced directly in downstream PRs/tests to prevent interpretation drift.

title: ADR: define dual-mode invariants (MCP default, CLI opt-in)
description:
Background:
We need a durable contract for dual-mode behavior to prevent ambiguous implementation choices.

Deliverables:
- Formal invariants for MCP mode (default) vs CLI mode (opt-in).
- Exact definition of what "mode" controls (routing, parser behavior, help text, exit semantics).
- Explicit non-goals (no silent auto-switching, no implicit fallback between modes).

Definition of done:
ADR accepted and referenced by all downstream implementation beads.
close_reason: done

title: Spec: MCP-mode CLI denial UX contract and exit-code policy
description:
Background:
The denial UX is a product surface and must be deterministic, not ad-hoc.

Deliverables:
- Canonical denial phrase (e.g., "Agent Mail is not a CLI!").
- Exit code policy and stderr/stdout policy.
- Required remediation hints (how to enable CLI mode or use MCP path).
- Tone/verbosity requirements for agent-facing workflows.

Definition of done:
A signed-off denial UX spec consumable by implementation and snapshot tests.
close_reason: done

title: Spec: MCP-mode meta-command allowlist
description:
Background:
Even in MCP mode we likely need a tiny set of meta commands (help/version/config) to stay operable.

Deliverables:
- Enumerated allowlist for commands permitted when MCP mode is ON.
- Rationale per allowed command.
- Security/usability tradeoff analysis.

Definition of done:
Allowlist artifact ready for guard implementation and tests.
close_reason: done

title: Spec: MCP-to-CLI parity target matrix
description:
Background:
The request asks for an equivalent CLI command surface; we need an explicit parity target before implementation.

Deliverables:
- Mapping of MCP tools/resources/macros to CLI commands/subcommands.
- Gap labels: exact parity, partial parity, intentionally out-of-scope.
- Prioritization notes for agent-first workflows.

Definition of done:
Parity matrix published and linked by all CLI implementation beads.
close_reason: done

title: Track: Configuration + runtime mode-resolution foundation
description: Background: mode switching must be deterministic and shared across binaries. Deliverables: config flag semantics, precedence rules, mode resolver, diagnostics visibility, and invalid-combination checks.
design: Build a core resolver + config precedence model so mode behavior is deterministic and reusable across binaries and future surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Config switch defaults correctly; resolver is shared; mode visibility appears in diagnostics/startup; conflicting mode inputs fail fast with actionable errors.
notes: This track is intentionally infrastructure-heavy because all denial/permitted behavior depends on resolver correctness.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Track 2 intent: one resolver, one truth.

Implementation principle:
- No per-command ad-hoc mode logic.
- Resolver provenance must be visible in diagnostics to simplify support incidents.

If resolver behavior changes, update Track 5 tests first to preserve trust boundaries.

title: Implement config switch for CLI mode (default OFF) with precedence rules
description:
Background:
Mode switching requires one explicit setting that is OFF by default for CLI mode.

Deliverables:
- Introduce and document config key(s) for enabling CLI mode (default false).
- Define precedence across env/config/flags.
- Define backward-compat behavior for existing deployments.

Definition of done:
Config schema updated with deterministic precedence and tests-in-waiting references.
close_reason: done

title: Implement shared InterfaceModeResolver in core
description:
Background:
Mode decisions must not be duplicated across binaries.

Deliverables:
- Shared `InterfaceModeResolver` (or equivalent) in core layer.
- Resolver returns normalized enum + provenance (where mode came from).
- Deterministic behavior under missing/conflicting settings.

Definition of done:
Both binaries can call one resolver and get identical decisions.
close_reason: done

title: Expose resolved interface mode in startup + diagnostics surfaces
description:
Background:
Operators need immediate visibility into active mode and why it was chosen.

Deliverables:
- Surface resolved mode in startup summary output.
- Surface resolved mode in config display/diagnostics endpoints.
- Ensure data is available for support/debug workflows.

Definition of done:
Mode observability is visible in all startup + diagnostics pathways.
close_reason: done

title: Add hard validation for conflicting mode inputs
description:
Background:
Invalid combinations (e.g., conflicting flags) should fail early and explicitly.

Deliverables:
- Validation rules for contradictory mode-related arguments/settings.
- Clear error messages that tell users what to change.

Definition of done:
No silent fallback on contradictory mode input.
close_reason: done

title: Track: MCP-mode CLI denial path and guardrails
description: Background: default MCP mode must reject CLI flows with a precise, consistent UX. Deliverables: pre-dispatch gate, denial renderer, allowed meta-command path, and comprehensive tests.
design: Centralized gate before command dispatch in am. Guard behavior references policy artifacts from Track 1 and resolver outputs from Track 2.
acceptance_criteria: Non-allowlisted CLI invocations in MCP mode are denied consistently; allowlisted meta commands work; output and exit codes are stable and test-covered.
notes: The guard is deliberately centralized to reduce bypass risk and to keep policy logic out of individual command handlers.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Track 3 intent: fail-safe default posture.

Guardrail principle:
- Deny by default in MCP mode; explicitly allow only approved meta commands.
- Error text and exit code are API-level contracts for automation.

Any variance in message/exit behavior should be treated as a breaking change and tested via snapshots.

title: Implement centralized MCP-mode CLI gate in am
description:
Background:
MCP mode must block CLI command execution at a single choke point.

Deliverables:
- Pre-dispatch guard in `am` command path.
- Guard references resolver output rather than ad-hoc checks.
- Guard only allows commands from the approved MCP-mode allowlist.

Definition of done:
CLI execution is impossible in MCP mode except approved meta commands.
close_reason: done

title: Implement canonical denial renderer: 'Agent Mail is not a CLI!'
description:
Background:
The denial response is part of product UX and must be consistent everywhere.

Deliverables:
- Canonical renderer for denial message and hints.
- Stable wording and formatting suitable for humans and agents.
- Stable exit behavior.

Definition of done:
All blocked CLI invocations produce the same contract-compliant output.
close_reason: done

title: Wire MCP-mode allowlisted meta commands through guard
description:
Background:
Usability requires that essential introspection commands still work in MCP mode.

Deliverables:
- Wire allowlisted meta commands through guard path.
- Verify non-allowlisted commands are denied.
- Provide explicit docs and hints for why behavior differs.

Definition of done:
Allowlist behavior exactly matches policy artifact.
close_reason: done

title: Test suite for MCP-mode denial path (unit + integration + snapshots)
description:
Background:
Guardrails regress quickly unless denial-path behavior is locked by focused tests.

Deliverables:
- Unit tests for guard decision matrix and allowlisted meta-command routing.
- Integration tests for nested subcommand denial decisions at the command-dispatch boundary.
- Focused snapshots for denial renderer output (message text, exit semantics, stream placement).

Non-overlap boundary:
This bead is component-level denial-path validation only; full cross-command matrix/e2e behavior belongs to br-21gj.5.2 and br-21gj.5.6.

Definition of done:
Any accidental CLI enablement in MCP mode is caught immediately with high-signal failures.
notes: Produces denial-path fixtures consumed by higher-level matrix/e2e layers; avoids duplicate end-to-end scenario expansion.
close_reason: done

title: Track: CLI-mode command parity implementation (agent-first ergonomics)
description: Background: when CLI mode is enabled, operators expect a coherent command surface approximating MCP capability with agent-first UX. Deliverables: command framework and domain command groups for identity/project, messaging, reservations, contacts/acks, macros, and diagnostics.
design: Implement CLI command families in modular groups using one framework and one output/error contract, guided by parity matrix and agent-first UX constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Each command family is implemented with parity evidence, consistent UX, and closure audit confirming no untracked gaps.
notes: Families are separable for parallel execution; dependencies enforce foundation first, then domain groups, then closure audit.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Track 4 intent: implement parity in cohesive command families with consistent ergonomics.

Work sequencing:
- 4.1 first, then parallel family implementation, then 4.8 closure audit.

Ergonomics rule:
- Every family should expose clear human output and machine JSON output with predictable structure and remediation hints.

title: Build shared CLI command framework for CLI mode
description:
Background:
Command parity work will fragment unless we standardize command architecture first.

Deliverables:
- Shared handler conventions and error model for CLI-mode command families.
- Shared argument normalization and output adapter hooks.
- Agent-first ergonomics baseline (naming, defaults, predictable structure).

Definition of done:
All subsequent command-family beads build on a common framework.

title: CLI parity: identity/project/product command family
description:
Background:
Identity/project/product flows are foundational for all other operations.

Deliverables:
- Agent identity and project/product command surface in CLI mode.
- Consistent output and error semantics.
- Alignment with parity matrix target.

Definition of done:
Identity and project/product flows are first-class in CLI mode.

title: CLI parity: messaging/thread/search command family
description:
Background:
Messaging/thread workflows are central to agent coordination and must be ergonomic.

Deliverables:
- CLI-mode message send/reply/fetch/search/thread commands.
- Thread-centric, agent-first defaults where safe.
- Behavior aligned with MCP semantics per parity matrix.

Definition of done:
Core messaging workflows are usable end-to-end in CLI mode.

title: CLI parity: file-reservation lifecycle command family
description:
Background:
File reservations are central to multi-agent safety and must be reliable under conflict-heavy workflows.

Deliverables:
- CLI-mode commands for reservation create/renew/release/list/conflict introspection.
- Explicit TTL/exclusive semantics and deterministic conflict output.
- Clear ownership/context surfaces (agent, reason, expiry, overlap holder list).

Validation requirements:
- Unit tests for TTL parsing, overlap detection, exclusive/shared rules, and renewal boundaries.
- Integration matrix rows in br-21gj.5.2 covering MCP-mode denial and CLI-mode allow behavior for reservation commands.
- Script-level e2e traces in br-21gj.5.6 with structured per-command logs.

Definition of done:
Reservation lifecycle is complete, predictable, and diagnosable for operators and agents.
notes: Non-overlap: this bead owns reservation command implementation only; semantic parity assertions and broad e2e orchestration are owned by br-21gj.5.3 and br-21gj.5.6.
close_reason: Implemented Reserve/Renew/Release/Conflicts subcommands with full SQL handlers, conflict detection, TTL enforcement, and 23 tests (11 clap parsing + 9 integration + 3 existing)

title: CLI parity: contact + acknowledgement command family
description:
Background:
Contact approvals and acknowledgement flows are policy-sensitive and easy to regress.

Deliverables:
- CLI-mode contact request/approve/reject/policy command coverage.
- CLI-mode ack/mark-read flows with deterministic pending/fulfilled state transitions.
- Clear error contracts for blocked contacts, missing links, and stale ack-required messages.

Validation requirements:
- Unit tests for state transitions and policy edge cases.
- Integration matrix rows in br-21gj.5.2 for MCP-deny/CLI-allow behavior.
- E2E script traces in br-21gj.5.6 including acknowledgement timelines and failure bundles.

Definition of done:
Contact and acknowledgement workflows match policy intent and are operationally debuggable.
notes: Non-overlap: this bead implements contact/ack command behavior; cross-surface semantic conformance and perf/security gating are in br-21gj.5.3 and br-21gj.5.4.

title: CLI parity: macro command family
description:
Background:
Macro commands are a productivity multiplier and must be first-class in CLI mode.

Deliverables:
- CLI-mode macro support for session/thread/file-reservation/contact workflows.
- Agent-first defaults with explicit override visibility to avoid hidden behavior.
- Macro output contracts that are both human-readable and machine-consumable.

Validation requirements:
- Unit tests for macro argument normalization, defaulting, and override precedence.
- Integration matrix rows in br-21gj.5.2 for macro invocation in both interface modes.
- E2E scripts in br-21gj.5.6 with step-by-step macro expansion logs and reproduction commands.

Definition of done:
Macro workflows are practical, deterministic, and traceable in CLI mode.
notes: Non-overlap: macro implementation only; parity closure/accounting is handled by br-21gj.4.8 and semantic conformance by br-21gj.5.3.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Implemented all 4 macro CLI commands (start-session, prepare-thread, file-reservation-cycle, contact-handshake) with full arg parsing, async handlers using DB queries directly, and 12 unit tests covering minimal + all-flags parsing and help text. All tests pass.

title: CLI parity: tooling + diagnostics command family
description:
Background:
Tooling/diagnostics commands are essential for support, automation, and operator confidence.

Deliverables:
- CLI-mode commands for tooling directory/schemas/metrics/locks and diagnostics-equivalent views.
- Stable JSON output options for automation and CI consumption.
- Actionable help text that points to next troubleshooting steps.

Validation requirements:
- Unit tests for output schema stability and argument validation.
- Integration matrix rows in br-21gj.5.2 confirming mode-gated behavior.
- E2E script coverage in br-21gj.5.6 with artifact capture for diagnostic command failures.

Definition of done:
Diagnostics/tooling workflows are discoverable, scriptable, and stable across mode changes.
notes: Non-overlap: this bead implements tooling command surface only; release/readiness checks remain in br-21gj.6.4.

comments.author: RedHarbor
comments.text: Started implementation. Fixed tooling/diagnostics wiring regressions in CLI: updated handler field mappings to current core metrics/lock schemas and validated command execution. Validation status: cargo check --all-targets PASS, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings PASS, cargo fmt --check reports unrelated pre-existing diff in crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/config.rs. Smoke verified: am tooling directory --json, am tooling diagnostics --json, am macros --help.

title: Parity closure audit for all CLI command families
description:
Background:
Parity implementation needs explicit closure so no command family is silently omitted.

Deliverables:
- Audit checklist mapping every parity-matrix row to an implemented command or explicit defer/out-of-scope rationale.
- Cross-link evidence to implementation beads and validation artifacts.
- Gap register with owner and follow-up bead IDs for any accepted deferrals.

Non-overlap boundary:
This is an implementation-coverage audit, not a behavioral test suite. Runtime validation belongs to br-21gj.5.x.

Definition of done:
No hidden parity gaps remain, and every omission is intentional, documented, and traceable.
notes: Canonical parity-coverage ledger consumed by docs and rollout tracks.

title: Track: Validation, conformance, performance, and security
description: Background: dual-mode behavior is high-risk without deep validation. Deliverables: unit/integration/conformance/perf/security test suites that prove mode correctness and prevent regressions.
design: Canonical validation pipeline: (1) unit resolver/guard invariants, (2) integration + e2e mode matrix harness, (3) semantic conformance assertions against MCP behavior, (4) perf/security regressions, (5) golden snapshots + CI artifact retention. Each stage consumes the previous stage outputs to avoid duplicated test logic and drift.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit coverage exists for resolver/precedence/conflict logic. 2) Integration matrix and shell e2e scripts exercise MCP-ON deny + CLI-ON allow paths with detailed structured logs and reproducible artifacts. 3) Conformance assertions verify CLI semantics match MCP tool semantics for supported operations. 4) Perf/security regressions are measured and enforced. 5) Snapshot contracts and CI artifact retention make failures diagnosable without reruns.
notes: Overlap-control rule: child beads in this track must define explicit non-overlap boundaries and reuse shared harnesses/artifacts rather than re-implementing scenario logic.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Track 5 intent: quality gate, not optional cleanup.

Blocking policy:
- Track 6 rollout/docs should not be marked complete until 5.2/5.3/5.4 pass.

Validation focus:
- Correctness (mode behavior), semantic parity (CLI vs MCP), and abuse resistance (bypass attempts).

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Planning consolidation note (2026-02-08): de-overlapped validation into explicit pipeline stages. Canonical flow is now br-21gj.5.1 (unit invariants) -> br-21gj.5.2 (integration+e2e matrix harness with structured logs) -> br-21gj.5.3 (semantic conformance) -> br-21gj.5.4 (perf/security regressions) with br-21gj.5.5 (text contract snapshots), br-21gj.5.6 (rich e2e scripts/artifacts), and br-21gj.5.7 (CI gating + artifact retention). This avoids repeated scenario logic across beads while improving diagnosability.

title: Unit tests: mode resolver, precedence, and invariants
description:
Background:
Mode behavior correctness starts with resolver/guard invariants and fast deterministic tests.

Deliverables:
- Unit tests for mode defaults, precedence, and conflicting input handling.
- Unit tests for allowlist/deny decision helpers with explicit edge-case tables.
- Structured unit-test diagnostics for failing invariants (showing mode source/provenance and selected policy path).

Definition of done:
Core mode semantics are locked by fast deterministic tests with high-signal failure logs.
notes: Fastest feedback layer in validation pipeline; upstream dependency for CI quality gates.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Implemented 28 unit tests for InterfaceModeResolver, mode precedence, and invariants in config.rs. Tests cover: InterfaceMode helpers (default, is_mcp, is_cli, display, equality), ModeProvenance display, ResolvedMode display, explicit override precedence, env var override precedence, binary default fallback, validate() conflict detection, precedence invariants (explicit > env > binary default), and edge cases (same-as-default override, empty env var, validate with explicit override). Refactored resolve()/validate() to use internal resolve_with_env()/validate_with_env() methods for safe testing without process env mutation (respects #![forbid(unsafe_code)]). All tests pass, clippy clean.

title: Integration + e2e matrix harness: MCP-deny vs CLI-allow with structured logs
description:
Background:
Mode toggling behavior must be proven end-to-end across representative command families and invocation contexts.

Deliverables:
- Shared matrix harness covering MCP mode deny paths and CLI mode allow paths.
- Rust integration tests plus shell e2e scripts that execute the same matrix rows.
- Structured logs per test row: mode, command, expected decision, actual decision, exit code, stderr/stdout digest.
- Artifact output format for later conformance/perf/security stages.

Non-overlap boundary:
This bead validates routing/decision behavior and invocation mechanics only. Semantic equivalence assertions belong to br-21gj.5.3.

Definition of done:
Matrix harness is reusable and produces deterministic, richly logged artifacts for downstream validation stages.
notes: Canonical source of truth for dual-mode scenario matrix and shared test harness artifacts.

title: Semantic conformance suite on top of matrix harness
description:
Background:
After routing behavior is proven, we need semantic parity evidence for supported operations.

Deliverables:
- Conformance assertions that compare CLI-mode outcomes against MCP-tool outcomes for the parity matrix.
- Explicit checks for success paths, validation failures, and policy-denied paths.
- Drift report format identifying exact mismatches by operation and field.

Non-overlap boundary:
This bead does NOT rebuild matrix execution plumbing; it consumes artifacts/harnesses from br-21gj.5.2.

Definition of done:
Conformance suite demonstrates semantic alignment or documents justified exceptions with explicit rationale.
notes: Consumes br-21gj.5.2 outputs; no duplicate scenario execution logic.

title: Performance + security regressions on conformance-validated surface
description:
Background:
Perf/security gates should run after behavioral and semantic correctness are established.

Deliverables:
- Regression checks for dispatch latency and hot-path behavior on the validated command surface.
- Security tests for mode-bypass attempts, malformed mode inputs, and denial-guard evasion attempts.
- Detailed benchmark/security logs keyed by matrix operation identifiers.

Non-overlap boundary:
This bead does not define semantic expectations; it enforces SLO/security constraints on the surface already validated by br-21gj.5.3.

Definition of done:
No significant regressions, bypass attempts are blocked, and evidence is captured in reproducible logs/artifacts.
notes: Gate runs after conformance; security/perf signals are tied back to matrix operation IDs for triage.

title: Golden snapshots for denial/help/usage contracts
description:
Background:
Textual UX contracts drift silently unless snapshots are managed as first-class artifacts.

Deliverables:
- Golden snapshots for MCP-deny messaging, mode-specific help, and usage output.
- Snapshot diff tooling/output conventions for fast triage.
- Snapshot review checklist to distinguish intentional UX updates from regressions.

Non-overlap boundary:
This bead focuses on textual contract stability only; behavioral correctness remains in br-21gj.5.2/5.3/5.4 and br-21gj.3.4.

Definition of done:
Output contract drift is automatically caught and diagnosable from snapshot artifacts.
notes: Text-contract lock layer; intentionally separate from semantic/perf/security layers.
close_reason: Golden snapshot system implemented: 3 new tests (golden_denial_message_format_contract: 5 denial messages validated against canonical format + fixtures, golden_cli_help_snapshot_stability: 6 help outputs saved as golden fixtures, golden_usage_error_format: 2 usage error cases). Snapshots in tests/fixtures/golden_snapshots/ (11 files). bench_golden.sh expanded with denial capture + additional CLI help. Fixed 2 pre-existing clippy issues in cli lib.rs.

title: Dual-mode e2e script suite with rich structured logging
description:
Background:
We need shell-level, operator-realistic validation beyond Rust integration tests.

Deliverables:
- New e2e scripts for dual-mode behavior (MCP default deny + CLI opt-in allow) covering all parity command families.
- Rich per-step logs: timestamp, mode source/provenance, command, expected vs actual decision, stderr/stdout excerpts, exit code.
- Failure bundle artifacts (raw output, normalized summary, reproduction command).
- Deterministic log formatting for CI diffability.

Definition of done:
A single commandable e2e suite can reproduce mode bugs with actionable logs in one run.
notes: Canonical script-level e2e layer. Must produce detailed structured logs (mode provenance, command, expectation, decision, exit code, output digests), plus failure bundles with one-command repro instructions. Non-overlap: avoids redefining semantic assertions already covered in br-21gj.5.3.

title: CI quality gates + artifact retention for unit/integration/conformance/e2e logs
description:
Background:
Validation only helps if CI enforces it and preserves enough evidence for fast triage.

Deliverables:
- CI wiring that runs unit, integration, conformance, perf/security, and new dual-mode e2e suites.
- Standardized artifact upload: matrix logs, conformance drift reports, perf/security summaries, snapshot diffs.
- Failure summary format that points directly to failing mode/command scenario and reproduction command.
- Guardrails to prevent silent test-skip regressions.

Definition of done:
CI gates dual-mode changes with reproducible artifact trails sufficient for single-pass debugging.
notes: CI gatekeeper layer. Must enforce execution of unit/integration/conformance/perf/e2e suites and publish durable artifacts for every failing scenario. Include anti-regression checks for accidental test skipping and artifact schema drift.

title: Track: Documentation, rollout, migration, and operations
description: Background: behavior changes affect operators and automated agents. Deliverables: docs updates, migration guide, rollout/kill-switch playbook, and post-release monitoring checklist.
design: Operationalization track converts implementation into safe adoption: docs, migration guidance, staged rollout, fallback strategy, and monitoring loop.
acceptance_criteria: All operator docs updated; migration playbook published; rollout/kill-switch plan approved; release/post-release checklists include mode-specific verifications.
notes: This track ensures the feature is supportable in production and that future teams can operate it without relying on tribal knowledge.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Track 6 intent: make the change operable and supportable.

Operational expectations:
- Docs must state MCP default clearly and show explicit CLI mode enablement.

frankensqlite UPDATE statements don't persist changes (VDBE parameter bug)
description:
## Summary
UPDATE statements in frankensqlite report '1 row affected' but don't actually persist the changes to the database.

## Reproduction
From mcp-agent-mail-db search_recipes tests:
1. INSERT recipe with name='v1' - works correctly
2. UPDATE SET name='v2' WHERE id=1 - reports 1 row affected  
3. SELECT WHERE id=1 - returns row with name still 'v1'

## Root Cause Analysis
VioletDawn investigated the VDBE execution path:
- Variable opcode correctly reads parameters from bindings
- SqliteValue::partial_cmp correctly compares Text values
- execute_statement_dispatch passes params to VDBE engine
- engine.set_bindings(params.to_vec()) is called

The bug appears to be in UPDATE codegen or execution - the changes aren't being written back to the database even though rows_affected is set.

## Impact
- 14 mcp-agent-mail-db tests fail due to this bug
- Any UPDATE with text parameters won't persist changes
- Blocks Search V3 recipes, TUI V2 features that modify records

## Files to investigate
- /dp/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/codegen.rs (codegen_update)
- /dp/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/engine.rs (UPDATE execution)
- /dp/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs (execute_statement)
notes: IvoryHill fixed placeholder ordering in codegen.rs. 394/399 tests now pass.
close_reason: Fixed UPDATE placeholder ordering in codegen.rs

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: OpusOrchestrator: Root cause identified. In emit_expr() at codegen.rs:3771-3776, anonymous placeholders all get hardcoded index 1 instead of being sequentially numbered. For 'UPDATE t SET name=? WHERE id=?' with params ['v2', 1]: both ? get Variable opcode with p1=1, so both read params[0]='v2'. The WHERE clause becomes id='v2' instead of id=1, matching no rows. Fix: implement parameter renumbering pass before codegen to convert anonymous placeholders to numbered ones. Secondary issue: count_matching_rows() at connection.rs:1537-1554 executes WHERE clauses without params, causing incorrect affected-row counts.

comments.author: JadeEagle
comments.text: JadeEagle investigation: Bug also affects INSERTs across connections. test_robot.sh shows register_agent succeeds on same connection but set_contact_policy fails on different connection. This is frankensqlite commit persistence issue.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: OpusOrchestrator: Further investigation shows frankensqlite codegen.rs has corrupted references - 'Opcode::n' instead of 'Opcode::Variable' (likely from incomplete search/replace). This blocks proper parameter binding for UPDATE statements. The codebase needs stabilization before the parameter bug can be properly fixed. Multiple concurrent agent edits have left fsqlite-vdbe in an inconsistent state.

This blocks cleanup tests.

comments.author: JadeEagle
comments.text: Confirmed root cause. At codegen.rs:171, 3812, and 4032-4034, anonymous placeholders get hardcoded to index 1. For UPDATE with 3 params, all get Variable p1=1, reading params[0]. Fix: add renumbering pass to convert anonymous ? to ?1, ?2, ?3 in order.

comments.author: JadeEagle
comments.text: Test confirms UPDATE hangs: test_update_anonymous_placeholders_numbered_correctly times out. The VDBE Variable opcode handler at engine.rs:2376 looks correct (reads 1-indexed params). The hang suggests an infinite loop in execution, possibly in table scan (Rewind/Next cycle) or comparison (Eq/Ne). Codegen at codegen.rs:2733-2788 correctly renumbers placeholders for UPDATE (SET starts at 1, WHERE at set_count+1). Issue may be in how the WHERE clause comparison evaluates with the reordered params.

comments.author: JadeEagle
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION SUMMARY:

1. Root cause: In codegen_update (line 2648), the placeholder renumbering logic is correct - SET placeholders get 1..N, WHERE gets N+1..M.

2. emit_expr correctly uses b.next_anon_placeholder_idx() which increments properly.

3. BUT test_update_anonymous_placeholders_numbered_correctly hangs - never completes. This suggests an infinite loop in VDBE execution.

4. The Variable opcode handler (engine.rs:2376) is correct - reads 1-indexed from bindings.

5. Likely hang location: The Rewind/Next loop or WHERE clause evaluation. Need to add VDBE tracing to confirm.

NEXT STEPS:
- Enable VDBE opcode tracing for the failing test
- Check if Loop/Rewind/Next is properly terminating
- Check if WHERE comparison is stuck in loop
- May be an issue with how the cursor interacts with the MemDatabase after UPDATE

comments.author: JadeEagle
comments.text:
CRITICAL FINDING: UPDATE hangs ONLY when setting non-IPK columns!

- UPDATE t SET id = 5 WHERE id = 1  → WORKS (IPK column)
- UPDATE t SET v = 'new' WHERE id = 1  → HANGS (TEXT column)

This matches mcp-agent-mail-db failures: UPDATE agents SET contact_policy = ? WHERE... (contact_policy is TEXT, not IPK).

Root cause is likely in codegen_update handling of non-IPK column assignments. The IPK path has special handling (moves rowid). Non-IPK updates go through different code path that hangs.

comments.author: JadeEagle
comments.text:
DEEP DIVE: DELETE + Next handling

The VDBE has pending_next_after_delete tracking (engine.rs:820-822). When Delete runs:
1. StorageCursor path (line 2168): calls sc.cursor.delete()
2. MemDatabase path (line 2173): calls db.delete_at(root, pos)
3. Both set pending_next_after_delete flag (line 2189)

In Next (line 1650):
- If pending_next_after_delete is set, it skips advancing cursor
- For StorageCursor: just checks !eof() 
- For MemDatabase: checks position < rows.len()

The hang may be:
1. B-tree cursor in invalid state after delete+insert
2. Infinite loop if cursor position doesn't advance properly
3. Issue in how UPDATE's delete-then-insert interacts with cursor

Need to add VDBE opcode tracing to see exact execution path.

comments.author: JadeEagle
comments.text:
SESSION SUMMARY:

Key finding: UPDATE hangs ONLY on non-IPK columns. IPK updates work.

Test created and stashed: 'git stash list' shows 'br-22iss: JadeEagle test for UPDATE hang investigation'

The test confirms:
- CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) → works
- INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'alice') → works  
- UPDATE t SET id = 5 WHERE id = 1 → works (IPK)
- UPDATE t SET name = 'bob' WHERE id = 1 → HANGS (TEXT)

Likely cause: Different code paths for IPK vs non-IPK column updates in codegen_update. The IPK path has special handling around lines 2809-2839 that may avoid the cursor positioning issue after DELETE+INSERT.

Handoff: Need to trace VDBE opcodes to find exact hang location.

title: A.2: Wire S3-FIFO into ReadCache replacing IndexMap LRU
description:
**Background**

The current ReadCache in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/cache.rs` uses five `OrderedRwLock<IndexMap<K, CacheEntry<V>>>` instances for project-by-slug, project-by-human-key, agent-by-key, agent-by-id, and inbox-stats. Each uses IndexMap's insertion order as a proxy for LRU ordering, with `move_index(idx, last)` on access and `shift_remove_index(0)` for eviction.

The eviction functions `lru_evict_if_full()`, `lru_evict_if_full_tuple()`, `lru_evict_if_full_i64()`, `lru_evict_if_full_u64_i64()` (lines 591-646) all follow the same pattern: retain non-expired, then pop from front while over capacity. This is where the O(n^2) cost manifests.

**Scope / Adoption wedge**

Replace the `IndexMap<K, CacheEntry<V>>` backing stores with `S3FifoCache<K, CacheEntry<V>>` from A.1. The CacheEntry struct (lines 64-100) carries `inserted`, `last_accessed`, `access_count`, and adaptive TTL logic. With S3-FIFO, the frequency counter in S3-FIFO replaces `access_count`, and TTL expiry is checked on access (lazy expiry).

Specific changes:

1. Replace `projects_by_slug: OrderedRwLock<IndexMap<String, CacheEntry<ProjectRow>>>` with `projects_by_slug: OrderedRwLock<S3FifoCache<String, CacheEntry<ProjectRow>>>`.
2. Same for `projects_by_human_key`, `agents_by_key`, `agents_by_id`, `inbox_stats`.
3. Remove the four `lru_evict_if_full*` functions -- S3-FIFO handles eviction internally.
4. In `get_project()` (line 242), replace the IndexMap lookup + move_index + shift_remove_index pattern with `s3fifo.get(&slug)` which returns `Option<&mut CacheEntry>` and internally handles promotion.
5. In `put_project()` (line 292), replace `map.insert()` + `lru_evict_if_full()` with `s3fifo.insert(key, entry)`.
6. Preserve the `CacheEntry` struct's TTL and adaptive TTL logic -- the S3-FIFO frequency counter supplements but does not replace the time-based expiry.
7. Add a `feature = "s3fifo"` flag to the crate. When disabled, fall back to current IndexMap LRU. Default: enabled.

**Risks / Safe Mode**

- Risk: Dual-index caches (project has slug + human_key indexes, agent has key + id indexes). Both indexes must stay in sync. When S3-FIFO evicts from one index, the entry must also be removed from the other.
- Mitigation: Add an `on_evict` callback to S3FifoCache that the ReadCache uses to remove the corresponding entry from the sibling index.
- Fallback trigger: If any test that previously passed now fails, or if cache hit-rate (measured by CacheMetrics) drops below 90% of baseline.
- Safe mode: `#[cfg(feature = "s3fifo")]` gates. Without the feature, the current IndexMap code is compiled.

**Validation / Isomorphism proof plan**

1. Run the existing 20 cache tests (in `cache.rs` mod tests) with S3-FIFO backing. All must pass.
2. Run the stress tests in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/tests/stress.rs` (`cache_coherency_mixed_workload`) with S3-FIFO.
3. Measure hit-rate before and after using `CacheMetrics::snapshot()` in a synthetic workload (Zipf distribution, alpha=1.0, 100K accesses, 1000 unique keys, cache capacity 100).
4. The isomorphism proof: for any access sequence S and cache capacity C, `s3fifo.get(k).is_some() == true` implies the value is correct (same value that was inserted). This is a weaker property than LRU equivalence (the *eviction decisions* may differ) but guarantees correctness.

**Tests (6 required)**

1. `readcache_s3fifo_project_hit_miss` -- same as existing `project_cache_hit_and_miss` but with S3-FIFO
2. `readcache_s3fifo_agent_dual_index_sync` -- eviction from agent_by_key also removes from agent_by_id
3. `readcache_s3fifo_capacity_respected` -- insert > capacity items, verify len <= capacity
4. `readcache_s3fifo_adaptive_ttl_preserved` -- hot entries still get extended TTL
5. `readcache_s3fifo_warm_agents_bulk` -- bulk insert path works with S3-FIFO
6. `readcache_s3fifo_hit_rate_not_regressed` -- synthetic Zipf workload, hit-rate >= 0.97 * lru_hit_rate
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- IndexMap-backed LRU is replaced by S3FifoCache in all targeted ReadCache fields without removing features
- Legacy lru_evict_if_full* helpers are retired or delegated with no dead code paths
- Dual-index synchronization via on_evict callback remains correct under concurrent access patterns
- Unit tests verify cache metrics, key visibility, and eviction ordering invariants after migration
- Integration/stress tests prove parity with pre-migration behavior for message/project/agent lookups
- E2E scenario validates end-user inbox/search behavior remains unchanged while cache policy changes
- Diagnostics include per-field cache policy state and migration parity counters
notes:
## Plan-Space Review Findings (2026-02-13)

**CRITICAL: Dual-index lock ordering hazard.** When S3-FIFO evicts from `projects_by_slug`, the `on_evict` callback must also remove from `projects_by_human_key`. But eviction happens inside `insert()`, which is called while holding the write lock on `projects_by_slug`. Acquiring `projects_by_human_key`'s write lock inside the callback creates nested lock acquisition. With `OrderedRwLock`, verify that `DbReadCacheProjectsByHumanKey` has a higher level than `DbReadCacheProjectsBySlug`. If not, this deadlocks. **Design decision needed:** either (a) collect evicted keys during insert and remove from sibling AFTER releasing the first lock, or (b) merge both indexes into a single S3-FIFO with a composite value type.

**CRITICAL: A.1 must add `remove()` method first.** `invalidate_project()` and `invalidate_agent()` call `map.shift_remove()`. A.1's current scope has no `remove()` method. This is a blocker — file a dependency note on A.1.

**CRITICAL: `on_evict` callback not in A.1 scope.** A.2 assumes A.1 provides an `on_evict` callback mechanism, but A.1 doesn't include it. Either add it to A.1's scope or handle eviction notification at the A.2 level using a collect-then-cleanup pattern.

**Additional tests needed:**
- `readcache_s3fifo_invalidate_project` — invalidate by slug, verify human_key entry also gone
- `readcache_s3fifo_invalidate_agent` — invalidate by key, verify by-id entry also gone
- `readcache_s3fifo_concurrent_access` — run `cache_coherency_mixed_workload` stress test with S3-FIFO
- `readcache_s3fifo_feature_flag_off` — with feature disabled, verify IndexMap LRU still works

**Verify InternedStr bounds:** The bead uses `(i64, InternedStr)` as a key type. Verify that `InternedStr: Hash + Eq + Clone` for S3-FIFO compatibility.
close_reason: Wired S3-FIFO into ReadCache replacing IndexMap LRU. All 5 OrderedRwLock<IndexMap> fields replaced with OrderedRwLock<S3FifoCache>. Removed 4 lru_evict_if_full functions. Added s3fifo feature flag (default on). 34 cache tests + 8 s3fifo tests + stress test passing. 6 required tests added.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# R2.1: `am robot status` — The Mega-Command

## What
Single command that tells an agent everything it needs to know right now. Equivalent to glancing at all 11 TUI screens simultaneously.

## Data Sources (7 queries aggregated)
1. **health_check** tool → overall health status (ok/degraded/error), uptime
2. **fetch_inbox** → unread, urgent, ack_required counts (filter by current agent)
3. **views/ack-overdue resource** → ack_overdue count
4. **file_reservations resource** → my_reservations[], reservations_expiring_soon count
5. **tooling/metrics resource** → tool error rates for anomaly detection
6. **messages table** → messages_last_hour count (query: WHERE created_at > now - 3600s)
7. **agents table** → agents_active count (WHERE last_active_at > now - 900s, i.e. 15min)

## Output Structure
```
_meta.command: robot status
health: ok
uptime_seconds: 86400

inbox_summary:
  unread: 3
  urgent: 1
  ack_required: 2
  ack_overdue: 1

recent_activity:
  messages_last_hour: 12
  agents_active: 4
  reservations_active: 7
  reservations_expiring_soon: 2

anomalies[1]{severity,category,headline}:
  warn,ack_sla,2 messages pending ack > 30 minutes

my_reservations[3]{path,exclusive,remaining_seconds}:
  src/**,true,2400
  tests/**,false,3200
  docs/API.md,true,180

top_threads[3]{id,messages,participants,last_activity}:
  FEAT-123,8,3,5m ago
  BUG-456,3,2,1h ago
  PLAN-789,12,4,2h ago

_actions[3]:
  am robot inbox --urgent
  am mail ack --project P --agent A 142
  am robot thread FEAT-123
```

## Implementation Approach
- Use `open_db_sync()` (CLI sync SQLite pattern from MEMORY.md)
- Each data source is a separate function that returns its section
- Aggregate into a single `StatusData` struct
- Anomaly detection logic:
  - ack_overdue > 0 → warn
  - tool error rate > 10% → warn
  - reservation expiring < 5min → warn
  - health degraded → error alert
- `_actions` generated from anomalies:
  - ack_overdue → suggest `am mail ack`
  - urgent unread → suggest `am robot inbox --urgent`
  - top active thread → suggest `am robot thread <id>`

## Agent/Project Resolution
- Project: `find_project_for_cwd()` or `--project` flag
- Agent: `AGENT_NAME` env var, or `coding_agent_session_search` auto-detect, or `--agent` flag
- If agent not resolved, skip agent-specific sections (my_reservations, inbox_summary)
  and add _alert: "agent not detected, use --agent to specify"

## Acceptance Criteria
- Returns all sections with real data from DB
- Anomaly detection produces correct alerts
- _actions list is non-empty when anomalies exist
- Works without agent identity (degraded but functional)
- Completes in <100ms for typical DB sizes

title: Track 9: am e2e harness — Native suite runner and artifact library (phased replacement for scripts/e2e_*)
description:
## Purpose
Begin migration of large Bash E2E orchestration surface (`scripts/e2e_test.sh`, `scripts/e2e_lib.sh`, and delegated suites) into native Rust test tooling with equivalent artifact fidelity.

## Why this track exists
The E2E stack is the largest remaining shell surface (>11k script LOC across `scripts/*.sh`), with heavy `python3/curl/expect/tmux` coupling. It is robust but not portable and difficult to evolve with typed contracts.

## Scope
- Native E2E runner entrypoint for listing/running suites.
- Native artifact writer equivalents for critical bundle outputs (`summary.json`, `bundle.json`, repro metadata).
- Progressive migration strategy: start with high-governance suites used by release gates.
- Keep current shell suites runnable during transition.

## Out of scope
- Immediate total replacement of all E2E scripts in one pass.

## Deliverable
A phased, dependency-aware path from shell E2E orchestration to Rust-native harnessing, with no loss of release-gate confidence.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Native `am` path is authoritative for this track and does not require external script/Python runtime for primary behavior.
- Functional parity (or explicit intentional deltas) is documented with a self-contained rationale and migration notes.
- Comprehensive unit + integration + e2e coverage exists for this track's surface area, including failure-path assertions.
- Harness-core unit/integration rigor is explicitly proven via `T9.11` before CI cutover/deprecation tasks can close.
- Test runs produce detailed machine-readable logging artifacts (JSON summaries, command traces, stderr/stdout capture, timing, repro metadata) suitable for CI governance.
- User-facing docs and troubleshooting guidance are updated so operators can diagnose failures quickly without external plan context.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# Track 9 Deep Notes: Native E2E Harness (Phased)

## Problem statement
E2E scripts are functionally strong but operationally heavy (bash + python + terminal tooling). A big-bang rewrite is risky, so we migrate in phases.

## Phase strategy
1. Build native artifact primitives and runner framework.
2. Port release-critical suites first (dual-mode, mode-matrix, security/privacy).
3. Run equivalence checks in CI while shell suites remain fallback.
4. Deprecate shell entrypoints only after evidence-backed parity.

## Key risk controls
- Preserve existing artifact schema and reproduction metadata early.
- Avoid dropping forensic richness during migration.
- Keep environment-specific suites (e.g., TUI/a11y) on compatibility adapters until native drivers are stable.

## Expected long-term outcome
A portable, typed E2E system where shell scripts are optional wrappers, not required infrastructure.

title: P1: Restrict installer OMP bearer writes to the effective active profile
description: install.sh detect_mcp_configs adds the default OMP agent config and enumerates every existing named profile even when a different profile is active. setup_mcp_configs can therefore refresh the live HTTP bearer into inactive profiles that OMP will not read, expanding secret persistence and diverging from OMP's actual directory authority. For a named active profile it also advertises the default config; for PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR it advertises both the override and default.
acceptance_criteria: Installer OMP discovery emits only the effective active user MCP config family selected by OMP_PROFILE over PI_PROFILE, or the default PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/root authority when no named profile is active. It never scans or writes inactive profiles and does not add the default path beside a named or overridden authority. Mutation-sensitive shell tests seed active, inactive, default, and custom-dir sentinels and prove only the effective target is advertised/mutated; invalid and symlinked profile controls remain fail-closed.

comments.text:
# T1.9: E2E Test Suite for `am ci`

## What to test

End-to-end validation of the `am ci` subcommand ensuring all 13 gates execute correctly,
reports are generated in the expected format, and edge cases are handled.

## Test cases

### test_ci_quick_mode
Run `am ci --quick` and verify:
- All quick gates run (skip_in_quick gates are skipped)
- JSON report has schema "am_ci_gate_report.v1"
- Skipped gates show status "skip"
- Exit code 0 when all gates pass
- NDJSON sidecar file created alongside JSON report

### test_ci_full_mode
Run `am ci` (no --quick) and verify:
- All 13 gates attempted (including E2E scripts)
- Report includes all 4 categories: quality, performance, security, docs
- pass_rate computed correctly for each category

### test_ci_specific_gate
Run `am ci --gate "Format check"` and verify:
- Only the named gate runs
- Report contains exactly 1 gate entry
- Other gates not present in report

### test_ci_parallel_flag
Run `am ci --quick --parallel` and verify:
- Gates within same category run concurrently
- Report still generated correctly
- Timing is faster than sequential (heuristic check)

### test_ci_json_output
Run `am ci --quick --json` and verify:
- Output is valid JSON to stdout
- Contains gate_logic section with 3 named gates
- Contains go_condition string
- pass_rate is null for categories with 0 required gates

### test_ci_failure_handling
Intentionally break formatting (create unformatted .rs file), run `am ci --quick`:
- Format check gate should fail
- Exit code should be non-zero
- Report shows the failing gate with status "fail"
- stderr capture contains the actual error output

### test_ci_ndjson_sidecar
Run `am ci --quick` and verify the .gates.ndjson sidecar:
- File path derived from JSON report path (replace .json with .gates.ndjson)
- Each line is valid JSON (not pretty-printed)
- Each entry has: category, name, status, elapsed_seconds, command
- Number of entries matches number of gates run

### test_ci_env_vars
Verify environment variables are passed to child processes:
- CARGO_TARGET_DIR, DATABASE_URL, STORAGE_ROOT, AGENT_NAME
- HTTP_HOST, HTTP_PORT, HTTP_PATH

## Implementation notes
- Create as tests/e2e/test_ci.sh following existing E2E patterns
- Use e2e_lib.sh assert functions
- Include detailed logging with pass/fail counts
- Clean up temporary files (unformatted .rs) after test

title: H.2: Wire into evidence ledger display + tests
description:
**Background**

The TransparencyWidget from H.1 needs to be integrated into the TUI screens wherever adaptive decisions are displayed, and the EvidenceLedgerWidget from B.3 should support drill-down into the TransparencyWidget.

**Scope / Adoption wedge**

1. Add `TransparencyWidget` to the tool metrics screen, showing adaptive decisions for the currently selected tool.
2. Add `TransparencyWidget` to the cache stats display, showing recent eviction decisions.
3. In the `EvidenceLedgerWidget` (B.3), add a drill-down action that opens the `TransparencyWidget` at L2 for the selected entry.
4. Add keyboard shortcuts: `Enter` to drill down one level, `Escape` to go up one level, `1-4` to jump to a specific level.

**Risks / Safe Mode**

- Risk: Adding widgets to existing screens increases render cost. Mitigation: TransparencyWidget at L0 is a single cell per decision point; negligible cost.
- Fallback trigger: Feature flag `tui-transparency` (default: enabled).

**Tests (4 required)**

1. `transparency_metrics_screen_integration` -- tool metrics screen renders with TransparencyWidget
2. `transparency_cache_screen_integration` -- cache stats display includes eviction transparency
3. `transparency_drill_down_from_ledger` -- select entry in ledger, drill down to TransparencyWidget L2
4. `transparency_keyboard_navigation` -- Enter/Escape/1-4 navigate levels correctly
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- TransparencyWidget is wired into tool metrics and cache stats displays without removing existing information
- Unit tests validate keyboard shortcuts, focus handoff, and drill-down state restoration
- Integration tests verify handoff from EvidenceLedgerWidget to transparency drill-down and back
- E2E PTY scenario validates full operator journey across Enter/Escape/1-4 shortcuts
- Feature flag tui-transparency behaves correctly in both enabled and disabled modes
- Diagnostics include navigation breadcrumbs, selected item identity, and render/update timing
notes:
## Plan-Space Review Findings (2026-02-13)

**CRITICAL: No file paths or keyboard nav spec.** Add:

- **Tool metrics screen:** `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/tool_metrics.rs` — add `TransparencyWidget` below the tool detail panel, showing decisions for the selected tool.
- **Cache stats display:** `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/system_health.rs` — add `TransparencyWidget` in the cache statistics section.
- **EvidenceLedgerWidget:** Created by B.3 in `tui_widgets.rs`. The drill-down action instantiates a `TransparencyWidget` with the selected entry's data.

**Keyboard navigation state machine:**
- L0 (Badge): Enter → L1, Escape → no-op, 1-4 → jump to level
- L1 (Summary): Enter → L2, Escape → L0, 1-4 → jump
- L2 (Detail): Enter → L3, Escape → L1, 1-4 → jump
- L3 (DeepDive): Enter → no-op, Escape → L2, 1-4 → jump
- Focus gain → reset to L0 (or preserve last level? Design decision: preserve)
- Press 4 with no data for L3 → stay at current level, flash warning

**Widget communication:** The screen passes `&[EvidenceEntry]` to the `TransparencyWidget` on each `view()` call. No message-passing needed — the widget reads entries and renders. Level state is owned by the screen, not the widget.

5. `transparency_empty_ledger` — widget renders "No decisions recorded" placeholder

title: [TRACK 5] Contact Policy Violation Message Parity
description:
GOAL: Contact policy violation messages must exactly match Python, including the
suggested remedies, example tool calls, and auto-handshake messaging.

CONTACT POLICIES: open, block_all, auto, contacts_only

ERROR MESSAGES:

1. CONTACT_BLOCKED (block_all policy):
   Msg: "Recipient is not accepting messages."
   Simple, no data payload.

2. CONTACT_REQUIRED (approval needed):
   Msg: "Contact approval required for recipients: {recipient_list}. Before retrying,
   request approval with `request_contact(project_key={project_expr},
   from_agent={sender_expr}, to_agent={target_expr})` or run
   `macro_contact_handshake(project_key={project_expr}, requester={sender_expr},
   target={target_expr}, auto_accept=True)`. Alternatively, send your message
   inside a recent thread that already includes them by reusing its thread_id."

   Data: {
     "recipients_blocked": sorted(set(blocked_recipients)),
     "remedies": [...],
     "auto_contact_attempted": [...],
     "suggested_tool_calls": [
       {"tool": "macro_contact_handshake", "arguments": {...}}
     ]
   }

3. Auto-handshake note (appended when auto_contact_if_blocked was tried):
   "Automatic handshake attempts already ran for: {agents}; wait for approval
   or retry the suggested calls explicitly."

BLOCKING CHECKS ORDER:
1. Allow self messages (sender == recipient)
2. Check block_all policy -> immediate CONTACT_BLOCKED error
3. Check auto policy + recent message from sender -> OK
4. Check approved AgentLink exists -> OK
5. Otherwise -> add to blocked_recipients list

ACCEPTANCE: Error messages match exactly, suggested_tool_calls structure matches,
auto-handshake messaging matches.

comments.text:
## E2E Harness Shell-to-Native Migration Contract

### Overview
This document defines the phased migration architecture and compatibility contract between the shell-based E2E harness (`scripts/e2e_lib.sh`, ~2500 lines) and the planned native Rust E2E harness.

### 1. Artifact Parity Requirements

#### 1.1 Required Artifact Files (MUST produce identical schemas)
| File | Schema | Description | Parity Level |
|------|--------|-------------|--------------|
| `summary.json` | summary.v1 | Test counts, timestamps, suite name | **EXACT** |
| `bundle.json` | mcp-agent-mail-artifacts.1.0 | Complete manifest with SHA256 hashes | **EXACT** |
| `meta.json` | meta.v1 | Extended metadata (git, timestamps) | **EXACT** |
| `metrics.json` | metrics.v1 | Performance metrics | **EXACT** |
| `repro.json` | repro.v1 | Deterministic replay metadata | **EXACT** |
| `fixtures.json` | fixtures.v1 | Fixture identifiers | **EXACT** |
| `trace/events.jsonl` | trace-events.v1 | Event trace log | **EXACT** |
| `logs/index.json` | logs-index.v1 | Logs index | **EXACT** |
| `screenshots/index.json` | screenshots-index.v1 | Screenshots index | **EXACT** |

#### 1.2 Supplementary Files
| File | Description | Parity Level |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `repro.txt` | Human-readable repro command | **COMPATIBLE** |
| `repro.env` | Sourceable env vars | **COMPATIBLE** |
| `diagnostics/env_redacted.txt` | Environment dump (secrets redacted) | **COMPATIBLE** |
| `diagnostics/tree.txt` | Directory tree dump | **COMPATIBLE** |
| `transcript/summary.txt` | Test transcript | **COMPATIBLE** |

### 2. Schema Definitions

#### 2.1 summary.json (schema: summary.v1)
```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "suite": "string",
  "timestamp": "string (YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS)",
  "started_at": "string (RFC3339)",
  "ended_at": "string (RFC3339)",
  "total": "integer",
  "pass": "integer",
  "fail": "integer",
  "skip": "integer"
}
```

#### 2.2 bundle.json (schema: mcp-agent-mail-artifacts.1.0)
```json
{
  "schema": {"name": "mcp-agent-mail-artifacts", "major": 1, "minor": 0},
  "suite": "string",
  "timestamp": "string",
  "generated_at": "string (RFC3339)",
  "started_at": "string (RFC3339)",
  "ended_at": "string (RFC3339)",
  "counts": {"total": "int", "pass": "int", "fail": "int", "skip": "int"},
  "git": {"commit": "string", "branch": "string", "dirty": "bool"},
  "artifacts": {
    "metadata": {"path": "meta.json", "schema": "meta.v1"},
    "metrics": {"path": "metrics.json", "schema": "metrics.v1"},
    "summary": {"path": "summary.json", "schema": "summary.v1"},
    ...
  },
  "files": [
    {"path": "string", "sha256": "string", "bytes": "int", "kind": "string", "schema": "string|null"}
  ]
}
```

#### 2.3 repro.json (schema: repro.v1)
```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "suite": "string",
  "timestamp": "string",
  "clock_mode": "wall|deterministic",
  "seed": "integer",
  "run_started_at": "string (RFC3339)",
  "run_start_epoch_s": "integer",
  "command": "string"
}
```

#### 2.4 trace-events.v1 (JSONL format)
```json
{"schema_version":1,"suite":"string","run_timestamp":"string","ts":"RFC3339","kind":"string","case":"string","message":"string","counters":{"total":0,"pass":0,"fail":0,"skip":0}}
```

### 3. Determinism Controls (MUST implement)

| Env Variable | Description | Default |
|--------------|-------------|---------|
| `E2E_CLOCK_MODE` | `wall` or `deterministic` | `wall` |
| `E2E_SEED` | RNG seed for stable IDs | YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS (numeric) |
| `E2E_TIMESTAMP` | Artifact directory timestamp | Current UTC |
| `E2E_RUN_STARTED_AT` | RFC3339 logical start time | Current UTC |
| `E2E_RUN_START_EPOCH_S` | Epoch seconds for logical clock | Current epoch |

**Invariant**: Given identical seed and clock_mode=deterministic, two runs MUST produce byte-identical artifacts (excluding actual timestamps in wall-clock mode).

### 4. Migration Phases

#### Phase 1: Pilot Suites (2-3 suites)
**Scope**: Simple assertion-heavy suites with minimal subprocess coordination
- `test_artifacts_schema.sh`
- `test_bench_smoke.sh`
- `test_cli.sh`

**Success Criteria**:
- Native runner produces identical `summary.json` for pilot suites
- Native runner produces valid `bundle.json` that passes `e2e_validate_bundle_manifest`
- Repro commands work for both shell and native runners
- CI runs both shell and native, compares summary.json bytes

#### Phase 2: Subprocess Suites
**Scope**: Suites that spawn/manage server processes
- `test_http.sh`
- `test_stdio.sh`
- `test_guard.sh`

**Success Criteria**:
- Process lifecycle management (start/stop/wait/timeout) is equivalent
- Port binding retry logic produces same behavior
- Server log capture is equivalent

#### Phase 3: Complex Coordination Suites
**Scope**: Multi-agent, concurrent, long-running suites
- `test_concurrent_agents.sh`
- `test_concurrent_conflicts_e2e.sh`
- `test_crash_restart.sh`

**Success Criteria**:
- Timing-sensitive assertions pass with deterministic clock
- Race condition handling is equivalent
- Failure recovery behavior matches

#### Phase 4: Full Migration + Deprecation
**Scope**: All remaining suites
- Convert all 30+ E2E scripts
- Remove shell harness dependency
- Native-only CI

**Success Criteria**:
- All suites pass in native runner
- No shell script E2E dependencies remain
- Documentation updated

### 5. Fallback Policy

#### 5.1 When Native Runner Unavailable
If `am e2e run` is unavailable (cargo build failure, env misconfiguration):
1. CI falls back to `./scripts/e2e_test.sh <suite>`
2. Fallback is logged in CI artifact metadata
3. No deployment gate bypass

#### 5.2 Compatibility Mode
During migration, support `AM_E2E_RUNNER=shell|native|auto`:
- `shell`: Force shell harness
- `native`: Force native runner (fail if unavailable)
- `auto`: Prefer native, fallback to shell (default)

### 6. Success Metrics

#### Per-Suite Migration
| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Assertion count match | 100% |
| summary.json byte-match | 100% (deterministic mode) |
| bundle.json validation | 100% |
| Execution time ratio | <1.5x shell time |
| Memory overhead | <100MB |

#### Full Migration
| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Suites converted | 100% (30+) |
| CI reliability | 99.9% (flake rate <0.1%) |
| Cold start time | <5s |
| Total E2E time reduction | >30% |

### 7. Exit Code Semantics

| Code | Meaning | Parity |
|------|---------|--------|
| 0 | All assertions pass | **KEEP** |
| 1 | One or more assertions fail | **KEEP** |
| 2 | Usage error (bad args, missing deps) | **KEEP** |
| 3+ | Reserved for future use | **NEW** |

### 8. Intentional Deviations

| Shell Behavior | Native Behavior | Rationale |
|----------------|-----------------|-----------|
| Bash LCG for seeded IDs | Rust Xoshiro256++ | Better distribution |
| jq-based JSON generation | serde_json | Type safety |
| Shell `date` command | chrono crate | Cross-platform |
| find/grep for file ops | walkdir/glob | Performance |

### 9. Validation Strategy

#### 9.1 Unit Tests

title: [epic] World-Class Installer and Seamless Python-to-Rust Migration
description:
# [Epic] World-Class Installer and Seamless Python-to-Rust Migration

## Problem Statement
Running curl pipe bash claims success, but am still launches the OLD Python version.
The Rust installer drops binaries in ~/.local/bin but the Python installer wrote a shell alias
(alias am=cd repo and scripts/run_server_with_token.sh) into ~/.zshrc which takes
precedence over any binary in PATH. Even source ~/.zshrc does not help because the alias
is re-sourced and wins again.

## Root Causes
1. Python am is a shell alias, not a binary -- aliases beat PATH lookups in all shells
2. Rust installer does not detect or displace the Python installation
3. No database migration -- Python DB has TEXT timestamps, Rust expects i64 microseconds
4. No MCP config takeover -- claude_desktop_config.json still points to Python server
5. --easy-mode is opt-in -- should be default for curl pipe bash installs
6. No post-install verification that the RIGHT binary responds to am
7. No self-update mechanism -- users must re-run installer manually
8. No uninstall or rollback if migration fails

## Success Criteria
After curl pipe bash install:
- am --version prints Rust version (not Python)
- All Python messages/projects/agents/reservations accessible
- MCP configs (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) point to Rust binary
- Python venv/alias cleanly displaced (preserved for rollback)
- am doctor confirms healthy state with no Python remnants
- am self-update works for future versions
- Works on macOS (zsh), Linux (bash/zsh), Windows (PowerShell)

## Architecture
8 tracks, approx 40 tasks, with dependency graph ensuring correctness ordering.

title: T1: Python Detection and Displacement
description:
Track 1: Python Detection and Displacement

The core problem: Python install.sh writes `alias am=...` into ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc.
This alias takes absolute precedence over any binary in PATH. The Rust installer must
detect this alias (and any other Python remnants) and displace them cleanly.

## Scope
- Detect Python am alias in shell rc files (zsh, bash, fish)
- Detect Python am binary/script in PATH
- Detect Python mcp_agent_mail virtualenv
- Detect Python mcp_agent_mail git clone
- Comment out or remove the alias (with backup)
- Stop any running Python server processes
- Preserve Python artifacts for rollback (do not delete)

## Key Insight
The Python alias is delimited by markers:
  # >>> MCP Agent Mail alias
  alias am=...
  # <<< MCP Agent Mail alias
This makes surgical removal straightforward via sed/awk.

title: T1.1: Detect Python am alias in shell rc files
description:
Scan ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/fish/config.fish, and ~/.profile for:
1. The marker block: "# >>> MCP Agent Mail alias" ... "# <<< MCP Agent Mail alias"
2. Any bare "alias am=" line outside the marker block
3. Any function definition "function am()" or "am()"

Return a list of (file, line_number, content) tuples for each match found.

Implementation: Pure bash function in install.sh called detect_python_alias().
Should be callable standalone and from the main install flow.

File: install.sh (new function ~line 266, before preflight_checks)

Output format for machine consumption:
  PYTHON_ALIAS_FOUND=1
  PYTHON_ALIAS_FILE=/Users/jeff/.zshrc
  PYTHON_ALIAS_LINE=142
  PYTHON_ALIAS_CONTENT="alias am=cd /Users/jeff/mcp_agent_mail && scripts/run_server_with_token.sh"

title: T1.4: Displace Python alias (comment out with backup)
description:
Surgically remove or comment out the Python am alias from shell rc files.

Strategy:
1. If marker block exists ("# >>> MCP Agent Mail alias" ... "# <<< MCP Agent Mail alias"):
   - Replace the entire block with a commented-out version plus migration note
   - New content:
     # >>> MCP Agent Mail alias (DISABLED by Rust installer on DATE)
     # Original: alias am=...
     # Rust binary installed at: ~/.local/bin/am
     # To restore Python version: uncomment the alias line below
     # alias am=...
     # <<< MCP Agent Mail alias (DISABLED)
2. If bare "alias am=" without markers:
   - Comment it out with a note: "# Disabled by mcp-agent-mail Rust installer: alias am=..."
3. Create backup: cp ~/.zshrc ~/.zshrc.bak.mcp-agent-mail-TIMESTAMP

CRITICAL: Use atomic write pattern (write to .tmp, verify, rename) to avoid corrupting rc files.
Never modify rc files in-place with sed -i without a backup.

title: T2: Installer Hardening
description:
Track 2: Installer Hardening

The current install.sh has several usability gaps that prevent a seamless first-run experience.
This track addresses all of them to achieve world-class reliability.

## Scope
- Make --easy-mode the DEFAULT for pipe installs (detect stdin is not a tty)
- Ensure PATH is correct and takes precedence
- Add post-install verification (am --version must return Rust version)
- Handle shell config conflicts (alias vs binary precedence)
- Add --migrate flag (default: auto-detect, offer migration)
- Improve error messages with actionable remediation steps
- Add --uninstall flag for clean removal
- Support Windows (PowerShell install script)
- Atomic binary replacement (write to .tmp, rename)
- Handle concurrent installs properly (lockfile)

## Key Design Decision
When install.sh detects it is being piped (stdin is not a tty), it should automatically
enable --easy-mode behavior because the user cannot be prompted interactively.

so the user must manually edit their shell config.

comments.text: REVIEW: Add rollback-on-failure logic. If any step in the migration sequence fails (displacement, DB migration, MCP config update), the installer should: (1) Report which step failed, (2) Restore rc file from backup if alias displacement was done, (3) NOT leave the system in a half-migrated state. The sequence should be: detect -> backup everything -> displace/migrate/update -> verify. If verify fails, offer rollback. This is critical for user trust.

The migration should: (1) Update MCP configs AFTER binaries are installed but BEFORE printing success, (2) Warn user that active MCP sessions will need to be restarted, (3) Consider: should we stop the Rust server if it auto-started and the migration failed? The goal is to never leave the user with a non-functional am command.

title: T2.3: Atomic binary replacement
description:
Current install uses `install -m 0755 $SRC $DEST/am` which overwrites in-place.
If the system crashes mid-write, the binary is corrupted. Fix:

1. Write to temporary file: install -m 0755 $SRC $DEST/.am.tmp.$$
2. Sync to disk: sync (or fsync if available)
3. Atomic rename: mv $DEST/.am.tmp.$$ $DEST/am
4. Same for mcp-agent-mail binary
5. Clean up any stale .tmp files from previous failed installs

On Windows (if we add PowerShell installer), use Move-Item -Force which is atomic on NTFS.

File: install.sh (modify lines 657-658)

4. If alias still wins, print LOUD warning with fix instructions

This is the critical "did it actually work?" step. Without it, the user gets a green

title: T3: Database Migration
description:
Track 3: Database Migration (Python TEXT timestamps to Rust i64 microseconds)

The Python version stores timestamps as TEXT (ISO-8601 naive UTC datetimes like
"2026-02-24 15:30:00.123456"). The Rust version uses i64 (microseconds since Unix epoch).
A seamless migration must convert all timestamps without data loss.

## Scope
- Implement `am migrate` CLI command
- Auto-detect Python database format (TEXT timestamps)
- Convert all timestamp columns across all tables
- Rebuild FTS5 virtual tables (cannot be copied directly)
- Backup original database before migration
- Verify data integrity post-migration (row counts, spot checks)
- Handle edge cases: NULL timestamps, pre-1970 dates, malformed strings
- Idempotent: running migrate twice is safe (detects already-migrated)
- Report migration summary (tables, rows converted, time taken)

## Tables with Timestamps
- projects: created_at
- agents: created_at
- messages: created_at, updated_at
- message_recipients: read_at, ack_ts
- file_reservations: created_at, expires_at, released_at
- agent_links: created_at, updated_at, expires_at
- message_summaries: created_at
- product_project_links: created_at

## Conversion
Python: "2026-02-24 15:30:00.123456" (TEXT, naive UTC)
Rust: 1772106600123456 (i64, microseconds since epoch)
Use chrono NaiveDateTime parsing with div_euclid/rem_euclid for safety.

4. Create backup: cp storage.sqlite3 storage.sqlite3.bak.TIMESTAMP

   a. ALTER TABLE to add _new column (INTEGER)
   b. UPDATE table SET col_new = convert(col) WHERE col IS NOT NULL
   c. Drop old column, rename new column (SQLite requires table rebuild)
6. Rebuild FTS5 virtual tables (drop and recreate with triggers)
7. VACUUM to reclaim space
8. Verify: run T3.1 detection again, confirm "AlreadyMigrated"
9. Print summary: tables migrated, rows converted, time taken, backup path

Tables and their timestamp columns:
- projects: created_at
- agents: created_at  
- messages: created_at, updated_at
- message_recipients: read_at, ack_ts
- file_reservations: created_at, expires_at, released_at
- agent_links: created_at, updated_at, expires_at
- message_summaries: created_at
- product_project_links: created_at

CLI interface:
  am migrate              # Auto-detect and migrate
  am migrate --check      # Just check, do not modify
  am migrate --force      # Migrate even if format unclear
  am migrate --backup-dir /path  # Custom backup location

title: T3.4: Migration safety and rollback
description:
Ensure migration is safe, idempotent, and rollback-capable:

1. Idempotency: Running `am migrate` twice must be safe
   - Second run detects AlreadyMigrated and exits cleanly
   - No partial migration state possible (use transactions)

2. Transaction safety:
   - Wrap each table migration in a transaction
   - If any table fails, rollback that table and continue to next
   - At end, report which tables succeeded and which failed

3. Rollback:
   - `am migrate --rollback` restores from backup
   - Lists available backups with timestamps
   - Prompts for confirmation before restoring

4. Integrity verification:
   - After migration, count rows in each table (must match pre-migration)
   - Spot-check 5 random rows per table: verify timestamp is reasonable
     (between 2020-01-01 and 2030-01-01 in microseconds)
   - Verify FTS5 search still works (run a test query)

title: T5: Storage and Config Migration
description:
Track 5: Storage and Config Migration

Both Python and Rust versions use the same storage root (~/.mcp_agent_mail_git_mailbox_repo)
and the same Git-backed archive format. Config uses .env files. This track ensures seamless
continuity of storage and configuration.

## Scope
- Verify Git archive compatibility (Python and Rust use same format)
- Migrate .env file settings if present
- Migrate notification signals directory (~/.mcp_agent_mail/signals)
- Handle storage_root customization (env var or config)
- Detect and handle database location differences (./storage.sqlite3 vs absolute path)
- Create config directory if needed (~/.config/mcp-agent-mail/)

## Key Insight
The Git archive format is already identical between Python and Rust. No conversion needed.
The .env format is also compatible. The main risk is database path resolution -- Python
uses a relative path by default while Rust resolves it relative to storage_root.

title: T6: Self-Update Mechanism
description:
Track 6: Self-Update Mechanism

Users should be able to update to the latest version without re-running the installer.
This track implements `am self-update` (or `am update`) as a first-class CLI command.

## Scope
- Implement `am self-update` CLI command
- Check GitHub releases API for newer version
- Download and verify new binary (checksum + optional sigstore)
- Atomic binary replacement (write .tmp, rename)
- Handle in-use binary replacement (tricky on Windows)
- Print changelog/release notes summary
- Support --check flag (just check, do not update)
- Support --force flag (reinstall same version)
- Handle network errors gracefully
- Update both binaries (am + mcp-agent-mail)

## Design
Reuse existing install.sh logic where possible but from within Rust.
The self_update crate is already in Cargo.toml dependencies.
On Windows, the running binary cannot be replaced -- use a helper
script that waits for the process to exit then renames.

title: T6.1: Check for updates via GitHub API

Implement version check against GitHub releases API.

Flow:
1. GET https://api.github.com/repos/Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust/releases/latest
2. Extract tag_name from response
3. Compare with current version (from built-in version string)
4. Return: UpdateAvailable { current, latest, url } | UpToDate | CheckFailed { reason }

Handle:
- Network errors (timeout, DNS failure) -> CheckFailed
- Rate limiting (403) -> warn, CheckFailed
- No releases -> CheckFailed
- Pre-release versions -> skip unless --include-prerelease

The self_update crate is already a dependency. Use it if its API is suitable,
otherwise implement directly with asupersync HttpClient.

  am self-update --check   # Just check, print available version
  am self-update           # Check and update

title: T6.3: Atomic in-place binary replacement
description:
Replace the running binary with the new version atomically.

Challenge: On Unix, a running binary can be replaced while executing
(the OS keeps the old inode alive until the process exits). On Windows,
the running binary is locked and cannot be replaced.

Unix strategy:
1. Write new binary to $DEST/.am.new.tmp
2. chmod 755
3. Rename old binary to $DEST/.am.old.tmp (backup)
4. Rename new binary to $DEST/am (atomic)
5. Same for mcp-agent-mail
6. Clean up .old.tmp files
7. Print "Update complete. Restart am to use the new version."

Windows strategy:
1. Write new binary to %DEST%/am.new.exe
2. Create update.bat script that:
   a. Waits for current process to exit (tasklist loop)
   b. Renames am.exe to am.old.exe  
   c. Renames am.new.exe to am.exe
   d. Deletes am.old.exe
   e. Deletes itself
3. Launch update.bat detached and exit
