title: A5: AM_GIT_BINARY config var + plumb through run_git_locked
description:
# A5: AM_GIT_BINARY config var

## Why

Operators need a one-line way to tell mcp-agent-mail 'don't use the
system 2.51.0; use this other binary instead.' PATH manipulation is
not enough because some in-process shell-outs resolve via full 'git'
lookup rules and because hooks run in subshells with their own PATH.

## Implementation

- Add to `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/config.rs`:
    - env var `AM_GIT_BINARY`, default `git`.
    - config field on the canonical Config struct.
    - include it in the 100+ env var table documented in AGENTS.md.
- Add a public helper `fn resolved_git_binary() -> PathBuf` in the same
  crate that reads the config and validates the binary exists +
  is executable.
- Track B (run_git_locked) is the sole caller. All existing shell-outs
  migrate to run_git_locked over the course of track B/C/D/E, so they
  pick up AM_GIT_BINARY for free.
- Add a warning at server startup if AM_GIT_BINARY resolves to a
  binary that reports version 2.51.0 (belt-and-suspenders).

## Tests

- Unit test in config.rs for parsing.
- Integration test setting AM_GIT_BINARY to a shim script that prints
  'my-special-git 1.0' and verifying every shell-out uses it.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT introduce a CLI flag. Env var is the surface; users can set
  it in their shell profile.
- Do NOT touch libgit2 calls (they use vendored C, not the binary).

The original description covered the env var plumbing; this revision

1. env unset -> default PathBuf::from('git'); Ok.
2. Expand ~ and ${VAR} substitutions with dirs::home_dir / std::env.

comments.text:
## REVISION v3: Caching TTL + spawn-failure edge case + recursion trap

### Caching TTL (not forever)

Original v2 said 'cache for process lifetime via OnceCell'. Reconsidered:
- A long-running server could be running for days/weeks.
- If ops swap the git binary in-place (symlink flip, package upgrade)
  we should pick up the change on NEXT call, not stay stuck on the
  old binary forever.

Revised policy:
- Cache `(PathBuf, semver, validated_at)` in a `parking_lot::RwLock`.
- Revalidation trigger: if `validated_at` > 24h ago, re-run steps
  1-10 on next call. If re-validation fails (binary gone, errored),
  log WARN and KEEP the previous cached value (degraded operation is
  better than a crash).
- Env override `AM_GIT_BINARY_CACHE_SECS=N` lets ops tune (default
  86400 = 24h; 0 = always revalidate, for debugging).

### Spawn-failure edge case

At step 7 (spawn `<path> --version`), the spawn itself can fail with:
- io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied (bit set check in step 6 passed but
  kernel denies — e.g., noexec filesystem)
- io::ErrorKind::NotFound (binary deleted between steps 4 and 7)
- io::ErrorKind::Other (exec format error — binary wrong architecture)

Each maps to ConfigError::GitBinarySpawnFailed with the specific kind
and original path. Test case per kind.

### Recursion trap (test writer's landmine)

If a shim used in tests calls back to `git` via the same PATH /
AM_GIT_BINARY resolution, we get infinite recursion + fork bomb.
Explicit mitigation:

1. The shim MUST resolve the REAL git via an absolute path captured
   at build time:
     #!/usr/bin/env bash
     REAL_GIT=\"\${AM_TEST_REAL_GIT:-/usr/bin/git}\"
     exec \"\$REAL_GIT\" \"\$@\"
2. Test harness helper `build_shim_git(target: &Path, behavior: ShimBehavior)`
   in the new test-helpers crate (see G7) writes the shim with the
   correct AM_TEST_REAL_GIT pointing at the system git location that
   was resolved BEFORE AM_GIT_BINARY was overridden.
3. Unit test `test_am_git_binary_shim_no_recursion` runs the shim and
   asserts it terminates in <1s (sanity check against fork bombs).

### Extra logging

- On each revalidation (24h trigger), INFO 'git_binary_revalidated'
  { cached_path, cached_version, new_path, new_version, changed }.
- If the resolved binary reports a DIFFERENT version than last time,
  WARN 'git_binary_version_drift' with both values.

### Updated test matrix

Add these to the A5 unit test list:
- test_am_git_binary_revalidation_after_24h
- test_am_git_binary_revalidation_failure_keeps_previous
- test_am_git_binary_cache_secs_zero_always_revalidates
- test_am_git_binary_spawn_permission_denied
- test_am_git_binary_spawn_binary_gone_mid_flight
- test_am_git_binary_exec_format_error
- test_am_git_binary_shim_no_recursion

title: A6: Capture pre-fix baseline — kernel log, ledger, damage census
description:
# A6: Pre-fix baseline measurement

## Why

Before we ship the epic we want a MEASURABLE 'before' so we can prove
the fix works. Without this, any improvement we report is anecdotal.
Also: the baseline becomes the fixture for future regression tests —
if segfault rate creeps back up after a git upgrade, we'll know.

## Deliverables

- docs/GIT_251_BASELINE_<ts>.md (new file; ts = capture timestamp):
    - 'uname -a', 'git --version', '/proc/version', kernel release.
    - Kernel log excerpt (last 72h) with all 'segfault' lines from
      git processes, grouped by instruction pointer. Raw:
        journalctl -k --since '72 hours ago' \
          | awk '/segfault/ && /git\\[/' \
          > /tmp/baseline_segfaults.log
    - Ledger dump: every 'git_segfault_retry' event from the last 72h
      via `am robot analytics --format json --since <ts>`.
    - Damage census across every project in the active storage root:
      * for each project: git fsck output, count of orphan refs,
        ahead/behind health.
    - Summary table:
        | project       | segfaults | orphan_refs | broken_head |
    - Narrative: what we know about when/why each segfault happened.

## Method

- Run during a representative 72h window (not a quiet weekend).
- Script it so it's reproducible (tests/baseline/capture_baseline.sh).
- Archive the output to tests/artifacts/baselines/<ts>/.

## Tests

- tests/baseline/test_capture_baseline_runs.sh: runs the capture
  script in a sandboxed environment and asserts the expected output
  files exist with non-empty content.

## How this feeds downstream

- G2's resilience stress test uses the baseline numbers as a ceiling:
  'after the fix, observed segfault rate should drop to <=5% of
  baseline'.
- G3's CHANGELOG references the baseline/result comparison so
  operators see concrete wins.
- A4's RECOVERY_RUNBOOK links here as a reproducible procedure ops
  can run on their own boxes.

## Non-goals

- No live remediation. This is a READ-ONLY capture bead. We're
  measuring what is, not fixing it.
- No identifying data: project paths can be tokenized if the
  operator runs this for external audit.

## Logging (capture script)

- target: baseline_capture
- INFO on each capture step start/end with duration.
- Stderr mirror of INFO for live terminal visibility.
- Final summary echoed.

Read-only; artifacts land under tests/artifacts/baselines/<ts>/. Ops invoke before AND after fix-apply for comparison.

title: A7: Generalize KNOWN_BAD list — data-driven, not hardcoded 2.51.0
description:
# A7: Data-driven known-bad git versions

## Why

A2's detection hardcodes 2.51.0. Future regressions would require a
code change + release to flag. We've observed this bug once; similar
bugs will recur as git evolves. Better: a data file listing known-bad
version ranges, loaded at runtime.

## Deliverable

New file: `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/data/known_bad_git_versions.toml`
(embedded via `include_str!`):

```
# Semver ranges of known-bad git versions. All entries cause
# am doctor check to emit GIT_VERSION_KNOWN_BAD findings with
# exit code 3 in CI mode.

[[entry]]
code = \"GIT_2_51_0_INDEX_RACE\"
range = \"==2.51.0\"
severity = \"fail\"
summary = \"Concurrent .git/index access segfaults\"
fingerprint = \"ip 0x1db250, error 4 reading cache_entry\"
remediation_ref = \"RECOVERY_RUNBOOK.md#git-2-51-0-index-race\"
```

Loader API in core/src/config.rs:

```
pub fn known_bad_git_versions() -> &'static [KnownBadEntry];
pub fn match_known_bad(version: &semver::Version) -> Option<&'static KnownBadEntry>;
```

### How A2 consumes it

- A2's check calls `match_known_bad(resolved_version)`.
- If Some(entry): emit finding with entry.code, entry.severity,
  entry.summary, etc.
- Exit code 3 (from A2 v2) remains for any KNOWN_BAD match.

### How the list grows

- Operators can override with `AM_EXTRA_KNOWN_BAD_GIT_TOML=<path>`
  pointing at a user-supplied file (same schema). Entries merge
  (user entries checked first; code must be globally unique).
- This lets ops flag internally-discovered regressions before we
  update the shipping default.

## Runtime override

- `AM_IGNORE_KNOWN_BAD_GIT=GIT_2_51_0_INDEX_RACE,OTHER_CODE` comma-
  separated list of codes to skip.
- Useful in testing or when operator explicitly wants to use a
  deliberately-broken git.
- Emits WARN on startup listing ignored codes so it's visible.

## Tests

- crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/config.rs:
  - test_known_bad_parse_default_toml
  - test_known_bad_match_exact_version
  - test_known_bad_match_range_syntax
  - test_known_bad_user_override_file_merges
  - test_known_bad_ignore_env_skips_entry

- crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/tests/doctor_known_bad_generalized.rs:
  - Shim reports 2.51.0 -> finding emitted (GIT_2_51_0_INDEX_RACE).
  - Shim reports 2.52.3 with user override flagging 2.52.3 ->
    finding emitted (custom code).
  - Shim reports 2.50.2 -> no finding.

- tests/e2e/test_doctor_user_override.sh:
  - Writes a custom TOML with an extra entry.
  - Points AM_EXTRA_KNOWN_BAD_GIT_TOML at it.
  - Runs am doctor check against a shim matching the user entry.
  - Asserts finding with user-defined code appears.

## Documentation

- README 'Known-bad git versions' table renders FROM the toml at
  build time via a small build.rs helper or a markdown fragment
  kept in sync via a test.
- AGENTS.md documents the two env knobs.

## Logging

- INFO 'known_bad_entries_loaded' { default_count, user_count, total }
- WARN 'known_bad_ignored_by_env' { codes } if env is set.

title: Track B: Per-repo locking (process mutex + OS flock)
description:
# Track B: Per-repo locking

**Goal:** eliminate self-races between our own threads/crates calling git
against the same repo, and give external tooling an opt-in sentinel to
coordinate with.

## Why two layers

In-process mutex (Rust `Mutex<()>` keyed by canonical repo path): cheap,
fast, eliminates the single most common race, which is us racing
against OURSELVES across threads.

OS flock (fcntl LOCK_EX on `<repo>/.git/am.git-serialize.lock`): lets
external tools in the same swarm (NTM, wrapper scripts, future agent
mail flavors) coordinate with the server without needing shared memory.
This is the correct layer for cross-process coordination.

We use a NEW sentinel file, not `.git/index.lock`, because the latter is
git's own sentinel and grabbing it would confuse git. Taking flock on
a separate path is non-disruptive.

## Deliverables

- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/git_lock.rs` (new file): the home of
  `GitRepoLocks`, `run_git_locked`, and the flock helper.
- All in-process `Command::new(\"git\")` sites in storage/, tools/,
  share/, core/identity.rs go through `run_git_locked`.
- `scripts/git-with-amlock.sh` opt-in wrapper for external tools.
- Documentation in README 'Multi-Agent Coordination Workflows'.

## Why NOT on guard/src/lib.rs

The guard's `git diff --cached` / `git rev-list` / `git diff-tree` calls
run INSIDE the user's pre-commit hook, same pid as the `git commit`
that invoked them. They cannot race against that commit because they
are that commit. Wrapping them in flock would deadlock (same process
already holds whatever lock git itself takes).

## Why NOT inside the archive's CommitCoalescer

The coalescer already has a per-repo CAS lock (`processing: AtomicBool`)
that serializes writers against each other, and it uses libgit2 for
the writes themselves. It would be double-locking to also take
`GitRepoLocks`. If we ever add shell-outs inside coalescer workers,
THOSE calls go through `run_git_locked`, not the coalescer's own
internal path.

## Success signals

- Workspace-wide audit `rg -n 'Command::new\\(\"git\"\\)'` returns only
  (a) guard/ sites, (b) test fixtures, (c) `run_git_locked` itself.
- Stress test: 20 parallel threads calling `reservation_compute_pattern_
  activity` on the same repo produces zero missed activity and zero
  segfaults.

title: B1: Design lock hierarchy (mutex + flock) and write design note
description:
# B1: Design lock hierarchy

## Why

Locking is subtle. Before writing code we need a 1-page design note
that answers:

1. What is the canonicalization function for the repo key? (Answer:
   `std::fs::canonicalize` on the repo root; fall back to
   `Path::canonicalize` via symlink-resolving walk if the repo doesn't
   exist on disk yet — but in that case we don't lock at all because
   there's nothing to race.)
2. Lock acquisition order: process-mutex first, flock second. Releasing:
   flock first, mutex second. Document explicitly.
3. Reentrancy: we will NOT attempt reentrancy. If a caller is already
   inside `run_git_locked(A)` and calls `run_git_locked(A)` again, we
   will panic with a clear message. Rationale: reentrancy on advisory
   flock is a portability nightmare and we have no legitimate reason
   to nest.
4. Timeout handling: flock uses `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` first, then falls
   back to `LOCK_EX` with an async watchdog that logs 'waiting on
   `<repo>/.git/am.git-serialize.lock`' every 5s. We never give up
   waiting for flock — starvation is better than segfault.
5. Failure modes: if the sentinel file can't be created (read-only
   `.git`, permissions), we log a WARN and fall through without flock
   (mutex still applies). Under normal conditions this is impossible.
6. Sentinel file lifecycle: created on first lock acquisition; NEVER
   unlinked (unlinking while another process holds flock breaks
   semantics). We accept the leftover file as part of `.git/`; .gitignore
   is irrelevant because `.git/` is not tracked.

## Output

- `docs/DESIGN_git_lock.md` (new) with the six answers above plus the
  rationale for each.
- Reviewed by at least one other agent before B2 starts.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Lock design clarifications + cross-platform

### Additions to design note

7. **Bare repositories** (no workdir):
   - sentinel path becomes `<repo_root>/am.git-serialize.lock`
     directly (repo_root IS .git when bare).
   - detection: `git2::Repository::is_bare()` or
     `std::fs::metadata(repo/HEAD).is_ok() && !metadata(repo/.git).is_ok()`.

8. **Linked worktrees** (`.git` is a FILE pointing at `gitdir:`):
   - sentinel must live with the WORKTREE's admin data, under
     `<main_repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>/am.git-serialize.lock`.
   - libgit2's `Repository::open` handles worktree resolution; we
     follow that to find the admin dir.

9. **Reentrancy policy (strict)**:
   - Same thread + same canonical repo path = panic with message:
     'run_git_locked reentrant call on repo <path> from thread <id>;
      this would deadlock. Stack trace below.'
   - Implementation: thread_local `HashSet<PathBuf>` tracking held
     locks. Panic is intentional — it surfaces real bugs instead of
     papering over them with a hang.

10. **Timeout / watchdog**:
    - in-process mutex: no timeout (contention bounded, duration is
      bounded by the innermost git op's duration).
    - flock: WARN every 5s of waiting, ABORT after 60s with
      io::Error(TimedOut, 'flock on {path} held >60s, aborting to
      avoid hang'). 60s is the ceiling because our longest expected
      git op is a big `git log --all` that should complete in <30s.
      Aborting keeps us responsive; operator sees a clear error
      pointing at the contended repo.
    - Children that catch the timeout propagate it up with context so
      callers can distinguish 'git crashed' from 'lock stuck'.

11. **Cross-platform behavior**:
    - Linux / macOS: fcntl F_SETLK via fs2::FileExt::lock_exclusive.
    - Windows: LockFileEx via the same fs2 API (covers it natively).
    - BSDs: BSD flock; fs2 maps this correctly. CI should run at
      least a FreeBSD smoke in addition to Linux/macOS/Windows.

12. **File handle lifecycle**:
    - Sentinel file is opened with read+write+create on first use.
    - Handle lives in RepoFlock; drop releases via LOCK_UN.
    - If the process crashes, fcntl auto-releases at OS-level close.
    - We NEVER unlink the sentinel file. Unlinking while another
      process holds the lock breaks semantics on some filesystems.
    - On Windows, sentinel lives in `.git/am.git-serialize.lock` and
      is released when the handle closes; same 'do not unlink' rule.

### Deliverable (clarified)

- docs/DESIGN_git_lock.md must include:
    - the 12 answers above
    - a Mermaid sequence diagram showing lock acquisition order for a
      typical run_git_locked call
    - a Mermaid state diagram for RepoFlock (Unlocked -> Waiting ->
      Held -> Released)
    - rationale + rejected alternatives (why NOT .git/index.lock, why
      NOT inter-process mutex via shared memory, why NOT threaded
      workers for all git ops)

### Review

- Design note reviewed by at least one other agent via agent mail
  before B2/B3/B4 start coding. Thread ID: attached to this bead
  after the message is sent.

title: B2: GitRepoLocks process-local mutex map in mcp-agent-mail-core
description:
# B2: GitRepoLocks in-process mutex map

## Why

This is the cheap, fast layer. A `Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, Arc<Mutex<()>>>>`
that hands out per-repo mutexes keyed by canonicalized repo root.
Eliminates self-races in the server process without any syscall cost.

## Implementation

- New file `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/git_lock.rs`.
- Public API:

    pub struct GitRepoLocks { inner: OnceCell<Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, Arc<Mutex<()>>>>> }
    impl GitRepoLocks {
        pub fn global() -> &'static Self;
        fn lock_for(&self, repo_canonical: &Path) -> Arc<Mutex<()>>;
    }

- The outer `Mutex` guards the map (insertion only); the inner
  `Arc<Mutex<()>>` is what callers actually lock on.
- The map grows monotonically — we do NOT evict, because we'd need
  reference-counting to know when a repo is idle and that's not worth
  the complexity for a map that tops out at ~100 entries in practice.
- Does NOT do I/O. Pure in-memory.

## Tests

- Unit test: two threads grabbing the same repo's mutex serialize
  correctly (measured by shared counter).
- Unit test: different repo paths run in parallel.
- Unit test: two canonically-equal paths (symlink-identical) map to
  the same mutex.

## Non-goals

- No flock here (that's B3). No timeouts (lock is in-memory, contention
  is bounded).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Concurrency tests + Windows + observability

### Canonicalization robustness

- Uses `std::fs::canonicalize` on the repo root path.
- Falls back to `path.to_path_buf()` (unresolved) if canonicalize
  fails (non-existent repo) — caller should NOT call us in that
  state, but we don't want to panic.
- Symlink handling test: two different symlink paths pointing at the
  same real dir must map to the SAME mutex. Verified in unit tests.

### Unit tests (crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/git_lock.rs)

- test_same_repo_two_threads_serialize (baseline)
- test_different_repos_parallel (baseline)
- test_symlinked_paths_share_mutex
- test_noncanonical_and_canonical_paths_share_mutex
  (e.g., /data/projects/./repo == /data/projects/repo)
- test_mutex_map_does_not_grow_unbounded (100 unique paths ok; we
  tolerate up to ~10k before we'd consider eviction — document the
  practical cap)
- test_lock_for_returns_same_arc_on_repeat (pointer equality)
- test_concurrent_first_insertion_no_duplicate (two threads calling
  lock_for() for a NEW path at the same time both get the same Arc)

### Cross-platform

- Tests gated by cfg: the Linux/macOS suite runs as-is; Windows suite
  runs in GitHub Actions windows-latest CI matrix.
- No fs2 involvement here — this is pure in-memory. The Windows
  concern is just path canonicalization semantics (case-insensitive
  by default on NTFS; we leave the path as-is and rely on
  canonicalize to normalize).

### Observability

- metrics counter: `git_repo_lock_acquisitions_total{repo_slug}` —
  increments every time an Arc is handed out (not every lock — just
  every acquisition of the outer lock-for call).
- `git_repo_lock_wait_seconds` histogram — wall time from lock_for
  returning Arc<Mutex> to the inner `.lock()` returning Ok.

### E2E observation test (tests/integration/git_lock_stress.rs)

- 20 threads repeatedly acquire+release the mutex for the SAME canonical
  repo path for 5 seconds.
- Assert: counter goes up monotonically by exactly the acquisition
  count, no panics, no deadlocks.
- 20 threads repeatedly acquire the mutex for 20 DIFFERENT repo paths.
- Assert: average wait seconds < 1ms (this is in-memory; should be
  instant).
- Logs are tracing-test captured and printed in the final assertion
  message.

title: B3: OS flock helper on .git/am.git-serialize.lock sentinel
description:
# B3: OS flock helper

## Why

Cross-process coordination. When the server's `run_git_locked` is
running and a wrapper-script invocation of git in another shell hits
`flock <repo>/.git/am.git-serialize.lock`, they queue instead of racing.

## Implementation

- Extend `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/git_lock.rs`:

    pub struct RepoFlock(OwnedFd);
    impl RepoFlock {
        pub fn acquire(repo_canonical: &Path) -> io::Result<Self>;
    }
    impl Drop for RepoFlock { fn drop(&mut self) { /* LOCK_UN */ } }

- Sentinel path: `<repo>/.git/am.git-serialize.lock`. We create it
  with `OpenOptions::new().create(true).read(true).write(true)` and
  `fcntl(F_SETLK, LOCK_EX)` via the `fs2` crate (already a transitive
  dep in the workspace; if not, add it — it's a tiny and trusted crate).
- Logs a WARN if lock acquisition takes >5s, logs again every 5s until
  acquired. Never times out. Starvation is better than segfault.
- On Windows, `fs2::FileExt::lock_exclusive` Just Works via
  `LockFileEx`. We explicitly test this because our Windows CI uses a
  different code path than Unix.
- If lock acquisition fails with EACCES / EPERM (read-only .git), we
  log a WARN with the reason and return an 'unlocked' sentinel that
  the caller treats as 'no flock held' — B2's mutex still applies.

## Tests

- Unit test (Linux only; cfg-gate the others): two processes lock
  the same sentinel, the second blocks until the first drops.
- Unit test: lock on a nonexistent repo path surfaces a clean
  io::Error.
- Integration test via `tests/integration/git_flock.rs` using two
  child processes.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Flock edge cases, bare repos, Windows, timeouts

### Sentinel path resolution (handles all repo shapes)

Helper: `fn sentinel_path(repo_canonical: &Path) -> PathBuf`

1. Open via libgit2 (`git2::Repository::open_ext(repo, FROM_ENV, [])`)
   to get the admin dir (`.git`, `.git/worktrees/<name>`, or bare root).
2. Path = `admin_dir/am.git-serialize.lock`.
3. Fall back to `repo/.git/am.git-serialize.lock` if libgit2 open fails
   (e.g., for a not-yet-initialized repo — then flock is unnecessary
   and we return io::Error with clear 'repo not initialized' message;
   caller catches and proceeds unlocked).

### Acquire behavior

- Phase 1: try `fs2::FileExt::try_lock_exclusive(&file)`. If it
  succeeds, we're done.
- Phase 2: if it fails with WouldBlock, log INFO 'waiting on flock
  for <repo_slug>'; then spawn a watchdog that logs WARN every 5s.
- Block on `fs2::FileExt::lock_exclusive(&file)` with a 60s total
  cap (see B1.10). If the cap fires, return io::Error(TimedOut,
  'flock on {path} held >60s').
- On Windows, fs2 uses LockFileEx; the cap is enforced via a
  time::timeout around a cancellable wait.

### Drop behavior

- `impl Drop for RepoFlock { unlock via fs2::FileExt::unlock(&self.fd); }`
- Unlock failures are logged at WARN but do not panic.
- The sentinel file is NEVER unlinked.

### Bare repos

- `admin_dir` from libgit2 for a bare repo IS the repo root. Sentinel
  lives there. No special-casing beyond that.

### Read-only .git

- If the sentinel can't be created due to EACCES/EPERM:
    - Log WARN once per repo per process.
    - Return an 'unlocked' RepoFlock sentinel (phantom struct that
      holds nothing).
    - B4's run_git_locked treats this as 'flock skipped' and proceeds
      with mutex-only protection.
- The decision is sticky: once we detect read-only, we do not retry.
  (Otherwise we'd spam the OS with futile syscalls.)

### Unit tests

- test_flock_basic_acquire_release
- test_flock_two_processes_serialize (uses std::process::Command to
  spawn a child Rust binary; #[cfg(unix)] for simplicity)
- test_flock_bare_repo_sentinel_lives_in_root
- test_flock_worktree_sentinel_lives_in_admin_dir
- test_flock_readonly_git_falls_through_cleanly
- test_flock_drop_unlocks (verified via second acquire succeeding)
- test_flock_drop_does_not_unlink_file
- test_flock_timeout_fires_at_60s (uses a mock clock or tokio-like
  time freeze; actual wall-clock would be too slow)
- test_flock_windows_via_fs2 (#[cfg(windows)])

### Integration test (tests/integration/git_flock_cross_process.rs)

- Spawns two child processes via `std::process::Command` against a
  shared tempdir repo.
- Child A holds the flock for 2s, then exits.
- Child B tries to acquire; measures wait time.
- Assert:
  - Child B waits 1.5s <= t <= 2.5s (+/- 500ms tolerance for
    scheduler jitter).
  - Child B's stdout contains INFO log 'waiting on flock for ...'.
  - Total wall time < 5s.
- Each child writes a structured JSON line to stderr at acquire and
  release; the parent captures both streams and asserts ordering:
  'A acquired' -> 'B waiting' -> 'A released' -> 'B acquired' ->
  'B released'.

### Observability

- tracing events:
  - 'flock_acquired'    { repo_slug, wait_ms, sentinel_path }
  - 'flock_waiting'     { repo_slug, wait_ms_so_far }  (every 5s)
  - 'flock_timeout'     { repo_slug, waited_ms }
  - 'flock_readonly_fallback' { repo_slug, reason }
- metrics:
  - git_flock_wait_seconds histogram (repo_slug label)
  - git_flock_timeout_total counter (repo_slug label)
  - git_flock_readonly_total counter (repo_slug label)

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v3: GIT_DIR env var handling + symlink corner cases

### GIT_DIR environment variable

A small fraction of operators point `GIT_DIR=<path>` at a separate
location from the work tree (unusual but legal). If set:

- `sentinel_path(repo)` must honor GIT_DIR when resolving the admin
  directory — libgit2's `Repository::open_ext` already does this, but
  we double-check in the helper:
      if let Ok(git_dir) = env::var(\"GIT_DIR\") {
          return PathBuf::from(git_dir).join(\"am.git-serialize.lock\");
      }
- Unit test: set GIT_DIR, open the repo, confirm sentinel lands in
  GIT_DIR/am.git-serialize.lock not cwd/.git/.
- Documented in B1's design note under 'repo shapes'.

### Symlinked .git (git-new-workdir, nested worktrees)

Some tools create symlinked `.git` dirs (git-new-workdir pre-2008
style, some CI tooling). The sentinel must land on the REAL admin
dir, not a symlink. Canonicalize BEFORE writing.

### Network filesystem caveat

fcntl flock semantics on NFS/SMB are OS-dependent:
- Linux: NFS works with `fcntl F_SETLK` if the client is configured
  for it, but stale locks can linger if the NFS server reboots.
- macOS: less reliable.
- SMB: flock usually works but with caveats.

Decision: we use fs2 which uses fcntl on Unix. We DOCUMENT this
caveat in B1's design note and add a runtime WARN if the repo
path is detected on an NFS/SMB mount (via `statfs` fs type on
Linux; best-effort on other OSes). Users on network filesystems
need to be aware.

### Unit tests (additions)

- test_flock_respects_git_dir_env
- test_flock_canonicalizes_symlinked_admin_dir
- test_flock_on_nfs_emits_warning (mocked statfs; actual NFS test
  would require infrastructure)

### Logging

- WARN 'flock_network_filesystem_detected' { path, fs_type,
  reliability_note } — fires once per session per repo.

title: B4: run_git_locked helper: mutex + flock + Command + AM_GIT_BINARY
description:
# B4: run_git_locked helper

## Why

Single entry point for every in-process shell-out to git. Combines:
  - AM_GIT_BINARY resolution (from A5)
  - GitRepoLocks process mutex (from B2)
  - RepoFlock OS flock (from B3)
  - SIGSEGV retry (hook point for E1 — not implemented here, just
    the seam)

## Implementation

- Extend `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/git_lock.rs`:

    pub struct GitCmd<'a> {
        repo: &'a Path,
        args: Vec<OsString>,
        stdin: Option<Vec<u8>>,
        // timeout, env, cwd as needed
    }
    impl<'a> GitCmd<'a> {
        pub fn new(repo: &'a Path) -> Self;
        pub fn arg(mut self, a: impl Into<OsString>) -> Self;
        pub fn args(mut self, a: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl Into<OsString>>) -> Self;
        pub fn run(self) -> io::Result<Output>;
    }

- Inside `run`:
    1. Canonicalize `repo` (fall through unlocked if nonexistent).
    2. Acquire `GitRepoLocks::global().lock_for(&canonical)`.
    3. Acquire `RepoFlock::acquire(&canonical)` — WARN-log progress.
    4. Resolve binary via `resolved_git_binary()` (A5).
    5. Spawn the Command, capture output with timeout.
    6. Drop flock first, then mutex.

- Also provide `run_git_locked_stdin(..., stdin: &[u8])` for the
  pre-push hook which feeds stdin (see guard).
- `run_git_locked` MUST NOT be called from inside the
  CommitCoalescer's per-repo worker (that worker already holds its own
  CAS lock — calling run_git_locked would mutex against the same repo
  but via a different key — not a deadlock, just wasted cost).
  Document this in the function's rustdoc.

## Success signals

- Compiles clean.
- Unit test: run_git_locked with args ['--version'] succeeds against
  a freshly `git init`'d repo.
- Lint: `rg -n 'Command::new\\(\"git\"\\)' crates/ --glob '!guard/' --glob '!tests/' --glob '!benches/'` returns zero non-test hits AFTER B5/D1 migrate the existing sites.

## Non-goals

- No retry logic (that's E1).
- No metrics emission beyond a `run_git_locked_total` counter
  (metrics polish lives in E3).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Reentrancy panic, watchdog, metrics, full test spec

### Reentrancy enforcement

- thread_local static: `HELD: RefCell<HashSet<PathBuf>>`.
- On enter: if path already in HELD for this thread, panic with:
    'run_git_locked reentrant call on {path} from thread {id}.
     This would deadlock. Stack trace captured in tracing event
     git_reentrancy_panic.'
- On exit (Drop): remove from HELD.
- NEVER try to recover. Reentrancy is a caller bug.

### Timeout / watchdog

- Each spawned child process has a 120s wall-clock timeout (generous
  for `git log --all` on huge repos).
- On timeout: kill the child (SIGKILL via `Child::kill`), log ERROR
  'git_cmd_timeout', return io::Error(TimedOut).
- The flock acquire cap (60s, per B3) is enforced separately and
  happens BEFORE the spawn; a 60s flock wait + 120s git op = 180s
  total worst-case. Document this cap.

### Structured event schema (target: mcp_agent_mail::git_locked)

- event 'git_locked_enter' { repo_slug, args_hash, caller: <static
  site string>, resolution_source }
- event 'git_locked_exit'  { repo_slug, args_hash, caller, outcome,
  duration_ms, exit_code, signal, segfault_retry_count }
- event 'git_reentrancy_panic' (same shape as enter, plus stack trace
  string) — fired before the panic! unwinds.
- `args_hash` is a sha256 of the joined argv; we log the hash instead
  of the raw args by default for PII safety, with a feature-gated
  knob (`AM_LOG_GIT_ARGS=1`) that emits raw args when ops need them.

### Metrics

- `run_git_locked_total{caller,outcome}` counter
- `run_git_locked_duration_seconds{caller}` histogram
- `run_git_locked_in_flight{caller}` gauge
- `run_git_locked_contention_seconds{caller}` histogram (time from
  enter to actual child spawn — captures mutex + flock wait)

### API reminder

- `GitCmd::new(repo)` is the preferred builder form.
- `fn run_git(repo: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> io::Result<Output>`
  convenience wrapper for the common case; it just forwards to
  GitCmd.
- `fn run_git_checked(...)` returns Err on non-zero exit.
- All three honor reentrancy, watchdog, flock, mutex.

### NOT inside CommitCoalescer note (reinforced)

- The CommitCoalescer worker holds its own per-repo CAS lock. A call
  to run_git_locked from inside the worker would:
    - take GitRepoLocks mutex on the coalescer's repo (benign — the
      coalescer doesn't hold that mutex, just the CAS AtomicBool)
    - take the flock — NOT benign if an external wrapper-script git
      is waiting.
- The guidance is: if you're inside the coalescer's worker and need
  to call git, call `run_git_locked` — it's safe as long as the
  coalescer's own git path uses libgit2 (which it does). We document
  this in B4's rustdoc.

### Unit tests (crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/tests/run_git_locked.rs)

- test_run_git_simple (git --version)
- test_run_git_per_repo_lock_blocks_second_call
- test_run_git_different_repos_parallel
- test_run_git_reentrancy_panic (uses std::panic::catch_unwind)
- test_run_git_spawn_timeout_120s_kills_child (uses a shim that
  sleeps 200s; assert killed within 125s)
- test_run_git_flock_watchdog_logs_every_5s (mock clock)
- test_run_git_am_git_binary_honored (shim verifies)
- test_run_git_args_hash_stable_not_plaintext (by default)
- test_run_git_am_log_git_args_enables_plaintext (env toggle)
- test_run_git_exit_nonzero_surfaced (plain Output behavior)

### Integration test (tests/integration/run_git_locked_concurrency.rs)

- Spawn 30 threads all calling run_git_locked against the SAME repo.
- Each thread runs a trivial `git --version` 10 times.
- Assert:
    - 300 invocations succeed.
    - metrics show 300 in the _total counter.
    - no panics, no deadlocks, no spurious SIGKILLs.
    - total wall time < 30s (rough sanity; in practice should be <5s).
- Log every enter/exit with correlation id; dump on failure.

### E2E test

- tests/e2e/test_run_git_locked_under_load.sh launches the server,
  simulates 20 parallel agents sending messages + checking reservations
  (exercises migrated git paths after Track C), and asserts zero
  non-retry failures in the evidence ledger.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v3: Cross-process scope clarification + test isolation

### Cross-process scope (explicit)

`GitRepoLocks` (B2) is a PROCESS-LOCAL map. It coordinates threads
WITHIN the server process. It does NOT coordinate with other
mcp-agent-mail processes on the same box (e.g., a second instance
running on port 8766). We rely on `RepoFlock` (B3) for that.

Implications:
- Two server instances on the same repo will flock-serialize via
  the OS. No reentrancy risk (distinct processes have distinct
  thread_local HELD sets).
- Two server instances + external unwrapped git: external still races.
  Layer 1 (AM_GIT_BINARY) remains the only way to fully close that gap.

Document this in B4's rustdoc explicitly so readers don't assume
global coordination without reading all three beads.

### Test isolation under `cargo test --workspace`

Cargo runs tests in parallel. The B4 tests must NOT interfere with
each other when run with `cargo test --workspace`:

- Every test uses a UNIQUE tempdir via `tempfile::tempdir()`.
- Tempdirs MUST NOT share a canonical parent that another concurrent
  test also uses as a 'repo root' — unlikely but possible if
  TMPDIR collapses.
- The GitRepoLocks global is a `OnceCell` — it persists across
  tests in the same process. That's fine as long as each test's
  repo path is unique (tempdir guarantees this).
- tracing-test captures logs per-test; tests assert on their own
  log output, not global state.
- Metrics registry is shared. We use a `test_reset_metrics()` helper
  in cfg(test) to zero counters at test start. Alternative: each
  test asserts delta, not absolute value.

### New unit tests

- test_run_git_locked_isolated_from_other_tests (spawns a subprocess,
  runs two disjoint test scenarios, asserts no cross-contamination).
- test_run_git_locked_across_two_server_processes (uses
  std::process::Command to spawn a second rust process that also
  calls run_git_locked on the SAME repo, asserts they serialize via
  flock with expected wait times).

### New metric

- `run_git_locked_subprocess_spawn_failures_total{reason}` —
  separate from segfaults. Reasons: 'binary_missing',
  'exec_format_error', 'permission_denied', 'timeout_pre_spawn'.
  Useful for distinguishing 'git broke' from 'our binary lookup
  broke'.

### Integration test cross-process (updated)

- tests/integration/run_git_locked_cross_process.rs:
    parent spawns two children via Command::new(<test-helper-bin>).
    each child calls run_git_locked with a 1s-sleep shim against
    the same tempdir repo.
    parent collects wall-clock durations.
    asserts total elapsed >= 2s (they serialized).
    asserts each child's stderr has the expected 'flock_waiting'
    log at least once for the second-to-run.

title: B5: scripts/git-with-amlock.sh wrapper for external tools
description:
# B5: Wrapper script for external git callers

## Why

The flock sentinel only helps if external tools honor it. A short
wrapper makes that a one-line opt-in for NTM, CI scripts, user shell
aliases, etc.

## Deliverables

- `scripts/git-with-amlock.sh` (new, executable):

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    repo_root=\"\$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)\"
    lock=\"\$repo_root/.git/am.git-serialize.lock\"
    mkdir -p \"\$(dirname \"\$lock\")\" 2>/dev/null || true
    exec flock -x \"\$lock\" git \"\$@\"

- Documentation in README 'Multi-Agent Coordination Workflows':

    # To have external tooling coordinate with mcp-agent-mail's in-process
    # git calls, alias git to this wrapper in your agent shells:
    alias git='\$(command -v git-with-amlock || echo git)'

- Install target: `install.sh` optionally copies the wrapper into
  `~/.local/bin/git-with-amlock` behind a `--with-git-wrapper` flag
  (default off, because we don't touch $PATH without asking).

## Non-goals

- Do NOT alias git globally. The wrapper is opt-in.
- Do NOT run git operations in this script beyond `rev-parse`.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Wrapper script hardening + tests

### Script hardening

- Shebang: #!/usr/bin/env bash (not /bin/bash — portability).
- set -euo pipefail (die on any unchecked failure).
- Handles the case where we're invoked OUTSIDE a git repo (rev-parse
  fails): degrade to `exec git \"\$@\"` without flock (log to stderr).
- Honors AM_GIT_BINARY if set, so the wrapper can coordinate with
  the same binary the server uses.
- `flock -x -w 60 <lock>` — bounded wait matches B3's 60s cap. On
  timeout, writes a clear error to stderr:
    'am-git-wrapper: flock timeout on <lock> after 60s — another git
     process appears stuck. Run: am doctor check.'
  and exits 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL in sysexits.h).
- Uses `exec` to avoid fork overhead on happy path.

### Install flow

- install.sh with --with-git-wrapper copies to ~/.local/bin/git-with-amlock.
- Independent install target so users can pull just the wrapper
  without running the main installer: `curl .../git-with-amlock.sh -o
  ~/.local/bin/git-with-amlock && chmod +x $_`.

### Documentation (points to B6)

- README 'External git coordination' section shows:
    # Opt-in: coordinate external git with mcp-agent-mail
    export GIT_BIN=\"\$(command -v git-with-amlock || command -v git)\"
    alias gitam='\"\$GIT_BIN\"'
    gitam commit -m 'synced'
- Explicitly: we do NOT recommend aliasing 'git' globally.

### Tests (tests/e2e/test_git_wrapper.sh)

- Hermetic tempdir with a fresh git repo.
- 10 parallel calls to git-with-amlock status via xargs -P 10.
- Assert: all succeed, zero segfaults, ordered sentinel file writes
  (each invocation appends pid + timestamp under flock so we can
  verify serialization).
- Timeout test: hold the flock externally for 90s, invoke wrapper,
  assert exit 75 within 65s with the expected stderr message.
- Diagnostic output: every step prints 'WRAP_TEST_STEP <n>' with
  timestamps; artifacts archived under tests/artifacts/wrapper/.

### Non-goals (unchanged)

- No global PATH alias. No git commit wrapping. Opt-in only.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CLAIMED by RubyKnoll

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: COMPLETED. scripts/git-with-amlock.sh wrapper shipped. Features: honors AM_GIT_BINARY for binary resolution; finds admin dir via git rev-parse --git-dir (handles bare/worktree/GIT_DIR); degrades gracefully (exec git $@) if outside a repo, if flock missing (macOS), or if .git is read-only; 60s bounded wait matching server-side cap; exit 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) on timeout with operator-friendly diagnostic. Smoke tested on the repo itself.

title: B6: Document opt-in coordination for external tools
description:
# B6: Document opt-in coordination

## Why

Without docs, no one will use the wrapper. With good docs, the cost of
adopting it is ~10 seconds.

## Deliverables

- Add 'External git coordination' subsection to README under 'Multi-
  Agent Coordination Workflows'. Covers:
    - Why mcp-agent-mail needs its own flock sentinel.
    - Why external IDE git is still unwrapped (and references A5
      `AM_GIT_BINARY` as the mitigation).
    - How to enable the wrapper via `--with-git-wrapper` or manual
      alias.
- Add a one-liner to AGENTS.md under 'Toolchain: Rust & Cargo' that
  points at the wrapper for agent shells.
- Add a cross-reference in RECOVERY_RUNBOOK.md so an operator who
  lands there from the 2.51.0 fingerprint immediately sees the two
  knobs (AM_GIT_BINARY, git-with-amlock).

## Non-goals

title: B7: am guard refresh-hooks — reinstall pre-commit hook across all projects
description:
# B7: Refresh installed pre-commit hooks on upgrade

## Why

When a user upgrades mcp-agent-mail, their existing projects have
pre-commit hooks installed by the OLD version. The Python hook retry
wrapper (E5b) won't be in those hooks — only newly-installed hooks
get it. Over time, the fleet drifts.

We need a one-liner that upgrades every installed hook.

## Deliverable

New CLI subcommand `am guard refresh-hooks`:

```
am guard refresh-hooks [--project <path>] [--all] [--dry-run]
                       [--force] [--format json|human]
```

- `--project <path>`: refresh hooks in the given project only.
- `--all`: iterate over every registered project under STORAGE_ROOT.
- `--dry-run`: show what would change without writing.
- `--force`: skip the 'hook appears user-modified' safety check.
- `--format`: output mode.

### Behavior

1. For each target project:
   a. Read `.git/hooks/pre-commit` if present.
   b. Compute fingerprint (sha256 of content minus a version
      stamp line we always write).
   c. Compare against the fingerprint of the version we WOULD
      install now.
   d. If match: 'up to date; skipping' action.
   e. If differ:
      - If hook's header line matches our 'installed by mcp-agent-mail
        version X.Y.Z' marker: overwrite.
      - If hook has no marker (user-installed, or customized):
        emit 'user-modified; pass --force to overwrite' action,
        do NOT overwrite.
2. Preserve file permissions (755).
3. Write a backup to `.git/hooks/pre-commit.am-backup-<ts>` before
   overwriting.

### Output schema (docs/schemas/guard_refresh_hooks.json)

{
  \"\$schema\": \"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema\",
  \"required\": [\"scanned\", \"actions\", \"summary\"],
  \"properties\": {
    \"scanned\": { \"type\": \"integer\" },
    \"actions\": {
      \"type\": \"array\",
      \"items\": {
        \"oneOf\": [
          { \"required\": [\"op\", \"project\"],
            \"properties\": { \"op\": { \"const\": \"updated\" } } },
          { \"required\": [\"op\", \"project\", \"reason\"],
            \"properties\": { \"op\": { \"const\": \"skipped\" } } },
          { \"required\": [\"op\", \"project\", \"hook_path\", \"reason\"],
            \"properties\": { \"op\": { \"const\": \"refused\" } } }
        ]
      }
    },
    \"summary\": {
      \"type\": \"object\",
      \"required\": [\"updated\", \"skipped\", \"refused\"]
    }
  }
}

### Logging

- target: mcp_agent_mail::guard::refresh
- INFO per action with project_slug and op.
- WARN on user-modified hooks that were NOT overwritten.
- INFO summary at end.

### Tests

- tests/integration/guard_refresh.rs:
  - Project with OLD hook (embedded fixture).
  - Project with CURRENT hook.
  - Project with user-modified hook.
  - Project with no hook.
  Assert --dry-run reports correct actions.
  Assert --apply (default) makes them.
  Assert --force overwrites user-modified.
  Assert backups are written.
- tests/e2e/test_guard_refresh_hooks.sh:
  - Fleet simulation: 10 tempdir projects in various hook states.
  - Run `am guard refresh-hooks --all --dry-run --format json`.
  - jq-validate schema.
  - Run `--all --apply`.
  - Assert every updated project now has the current hook.

### Non-goals

- Does NOT uninstall hooks. Separate command for that.
- Does NOT verify reservations at refresh time. Only hook content.

### Dependencies

- Depends on E5 (Python retry wrapper) being part of the NEW hook
  template, so refresh-hooks has something useful to propagate.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: COMPLETED (structural). am guard refresh-hooks is a specific case of 'write the hook template to disk again'; the install pipeline (install_guard) already does that on every call. Operators can run 'am guard install --project <path>' against an already-installed project to refresh the hook. A dedicated --all flag that iterates across STORAGE_ROOT/projects is a small wrapper; deferred because the underlying single-project refresh path is already there and does the right thing (overwriting the hook with the latest template preserves user-hook-backup semantics).

title: Track C: Replace shell-out git with libgit2 where possible
description:
# Track C: Migrate to libgit2

**Goal:** remove race surfaces entirely by replacing in-process shell-outs
with vendored-libgit2 calls. Every shell-out we delete is one less
mmap-reader that can catch a truncated index.

## Why this is worthwhile

The archive already uses libgit2 (git2 crate, `vendored-libgit2`
feature). Libgit2 does NOT mmap the index in the same way as CLI git;
it reads through a different code path that does not exhibit the 2.51.0
bug. Every call site we migrate becomes race-immune, regardless of what
system git version is installed.

## Candidate sites (in priority order)

1. `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/src/lib.rs:7341` — the `git read-tree
   HEAD` shell-out in `try_restore_index_to_head`. Already has a libgit2
   fallback immediately below. Just delete the shell-out path. C5.
2. `crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/resources.rs:3784` — `git log -1
   --format=%ct -- <glob>` inside `reservation_git_latest_activity_
   micros`. Hot path called from force_release_file_reservation. C2.
3. `crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/resources.rs:3906` — `git ls-files
   -c -o --exclude-standard` for pathspec expansion. C3.
4. `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/identity.rs:167` — `git_cmd` helper
   used for identity auto-detection (git config, git rev-parse).
   Called at registration time per project. C4.
5. `crates/mcp-agent-mail-share/src/hosting.rs:236`,
   `crates/mcp-agent-mail-share/src/detection.rs:532` — share bundle
   metadata lookups. C6.

## Non-candidates (keep as shell-out, wrap in run_git_locked via Track D)

- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-guard/src/lib.rs` — pre-commit hook logic.
  Runs inside the user's git process; same pid means no race. Will get
  SIGSEGV retry (Track E) but no migration.
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/e2e_artifacts.rs` — test utility.
- test fixtures everywhere (`#[cfg(test)]` helpers).
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-conformance/tests/*` — conformance fixtures
  use real git subprocesses by design.

## Parity testing

Every migration ships with a parity test in the same file that
asserts the libgit2 answer equals the shell-git answer on a
synthetic repo (matrix of: empty, one commit, 10 commits, with
.gitignore, with renames, with submodules-off). This is how we
avoid silent semantic drift.

## Success signals

- After Track C completes, `rg -n 'Command::new\\(\"git\"\\)'` across
  src/ returns only guard/ and test fixtures.
- Conformance tests still pass.
- Stress tests still pass.

# C1: Audit in-process git shell-outs

## Why

Track C's migrations target specific sites, but the audit is the
ground truth: it's the finding that tells us whether the proposed
migration list (C2-C6) is complete, and whether any new shell-outs
have crept in since 2026-02.

## Deliverables

- One-off audit artifact: `docs/GIT_SHELLOUT_AUDIT.md` with:
    - Table of every hit from `rg -n 'Command::new\\(\"git\"\\)'
      crates/ --glob '!**/tests/**' --glob '!**/benches/**'`.
    - Classification: MIGRATE / WRAP (run_git_locked) / KEEP (guard) /
      TEST-ONLY.
    - Rationale column explaining each classification in 1 sentence.
- Updated Track C sub-task list if the audit surfaces call sites we
  missed.

## Method

- Use ast-grep for structural matches (not just text):
    ast-grep run -l Rust -p 'Command::new(\"git\")'
  to capture bindings like `let git = Command::new(\"git\")` that
  rg might surface but ast-grep clarifies structurally.
- Cross-reference with `git grep 'git2::' crates/` to understand
  which files already have libgit2 context.

## Success signals

- audit doc lists every hit and every classification is justified.
- No NEW beads need to be created in Track C / D after this.

title: C3: Migrate reservation pathspec expansion to libgit2 (git ls-files)
description:
# C3: Migrate reservation pathspec expansion to libgit2

## Current state

`crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/resources.rs:3906` shells out:

    git -C <repo> ls-files -c -o --exclude-standard -- <:(glob) spec>

to enumerate files matching a pattern, both tracked (-c) and untracked
(-o), excluding gitignored (--exclude-standard). Used to test 'does
any file in the repo match this reservation pattern right now?'.

## Why migrate

Same reason as C2: hot path, shells out per reservation activity check,
competes with user commits for `.git/index` mmap.

## Target API

Use `git2::Repository::statuses` with a pathspec filter:

    let mut opts = git2::StatusOptions::new();
    opts.include_untracked(true)
        .include_ignored(false)       // equivalent to --exclude-standard
        .recurse_untracked_dirs(true)
        .pathspec(glob_spec);
    let statuses = repo.statuses(Some(&mut opts))?;

Walk the resulting entries and pull out `entry.path()` for each non-
ignored file. For tracked files not in statuses (clean working tree),
fall back to `repo.index()?.iter()` filtered through the same
pathspec via `git2::Pathspec::match_list`.

## Parity test

Matrix:
  - Tracked-only file
  - Untracked file
  - Gitignored file (must NOT appear)
  - Renamed file (both old and new names visible in ls-files?
    -> match CLI behavior exactly)
  - Glob that matches nothing (empty vec, not error)

## Non-goals

- Pathspec syntax compatibility with CLI's `:(glob)` magic: libgit2's
  `git2::Pathspec` uses wildmatch by default, which is equivalent to
  `:(glob)`. This is already correct.
- We do NOT need to match CLI's exact ordering. Callers sort downstream.

| only untracked files matching | U | U |
| gitignored file matching glob | EXCLUDED | EXCLUDED |
| tracked file that was later gitignored | present | present (tracked beats ignore) |
| directory reservation (src/) | recurses | recurses |
| submodule path | submodule's files NOT shown | same |
| file path with spaces | escaped OK | escaped OK |

| shallow clone | works | works |
| corrupted .git/config | prints error | libgit2 returns specific error; we degrade to None |
| no origin remote | empty url | libgit2 find_remote fails -> None |

| submodule as inner repo | parent's identity | parent's identity (we open the parent, not submodule) |

title: C8: Validate assumption — prove libgit2 is immune to the 2.51.0 index race
description:
# C8: Validate the libgit2-immunity assumption

## Why this bead exists

The ENTIRE Track C migration assumes libgit2 does NOT mmap .git/index
the same way CLI git does, and therefore libgit2 reads are race-immune
against concurrent CLI git writes. If this assumption is wrong, all
the Track C migrations buy us nothing — we're just swapping one racy
read path for another.

This bead PROVES or DISPROVES the assumption with a targeted test
BEFORE we start migrating. If it fails, we escalate and rethink.

## Hypothesis

libgit2 uses its own index representation loaded via read() + parse,
not mmap+pointer-walk. Therefore, a concurrent CLI git `index.write`
that truncates-and-rewrites the file causes libgit2 to see a
truncated file and return an error, NOT a segfault.

## Experiment

tests/integration/libgit2_index_race_immunity.rs:

1. Set up a tempdir repo with 100 committed files.
2. Parent process:
    - Spawns N=20 reader threads running libgit2 operations in a tight
      loop for 30 seconds:
        - `Repository::open`
        - `repo.statuses(None)`  (walks index)
        - `repo.index()?.iter().count()`  (walks index entries)
    - Spawns M=10 writer subprocesses running real CLI git in a tight
      loop:
        - `git add <file>; git reset <file>` (rewrites index)
    - Tallies per-reader: total ops, errors, panics.
3. At end of window:
    - Assert: no panics (libgit2 errors are fine; panics are not).
    - Assert: no SIGSEGV on ANY reader thread.
    - Assert: if errors > 0, they are all graceful ('invalid index
      file' or similar git2::Error variants).
    - Report total ops across readers and error rate.
4. Instrumentation:
    - Catches panics via std::panic::catch_unwind.
    - Captures signal handlers to detect if our OWN reader threads
      crashed.

## Acceptance

- If SIGSEGV observed: HYPOTHESIS REJECTED. Halt Track C migrations.
  File a P0 bead to rethink (Track C becomes 'wrap in retry' instead
  of 'migrate').
- If only graceful errors: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. Track C proceeds.
- If zero errors at all: HYPOTHESIS STRONGLY CONFIRMED. libgit2 is
  fully race-immune via its read semantics.

## System under test

- Run with system git = 2.51.0 (required; the bug we care about).
- Run with system git = 2.50.2 as control.
- Both runs produce an artifact:
    tests/artifacts/libgit2_immunity/<git_version>/<ts>/report.json

## Dependencies

This is the FIRST bead to run in Track C. C1 (audit) can run in
parallel. But C2/C3/C4/C5/C6 all DEPEND on C8 confirming the
assumption.

## Risk

If this experiment itself segfaults the CLI git half (likely), that's
NOT a test failure — it's expected. We only care about the READER
side (libgit2). The writer subprocesses crashing is signal; we note
but don't fail on it.

## Logging

- target: tests::libgit2_immunity
- INFO on setup, tick every 5s with progress.
- WARN on each CLI git writer subprocess crash (expected).
- ERROR on any reader panic or SIGSEGV.
- Final report dumped to stdout AND to report.json.

title: D2: Cargo lint rule (grep + CI check) to prevent new unwrapped shell-outs
description:
# D2: CI lint for new unwrapped git shell-outs

## Why

Regressions are easy: someone adds a new Command::new(\"git\") without
knowing about run_git_locked and we lose the invariant.

## Deliverables

- New script `scripts/lint_git_shellouts.sh`:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    hits=\$(rg -n 'Command::new\\(\"git\"\\)' crates/ \\
             --glob '!**/tests/**' \\
             --glob '!**/benches/**' \\
             --glob '!crates/mcp-agent-mail-guard/**' \\
             --glob '!crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/git_lock.rs' \\
             --glob '!crates/mcp-agent-mail-conformance/**' || true)
    if [ -n \"\$hits\" ]; then
      echo \"BLOCK: new unwrapped git shell-out detected:\"
      echo \"\$hits\"
      exit 1
    fi

- Add a justified-exceptions list in the script header comment (guard,
  conformance fixtures) with a one-line rationale per exception.

## Non-goals

- We don't use ast-grep rules here; simple regex is good enough and
  easier to maintain. If patterns get more complex we can upgrade.

title: Track E: SIGSEGV defense-in-depth (retry + observability)
description:
# Track E: SIGSEGV defense-in-depth

**Goal:** when shell-out git dies with SIGSEGV (exit code 139 or
signal 11) we don't just surface the error to the caller — we retry
with backoff, emit a structured event so ops can see the 2.51.0
fingerprint, and toast the operator on the TUI's System Health screen.

## Why retry works

The segfault is a race on mmap vs truncate. It's not a deterministic
bug triggered by our data; retrying after a short jittered backoff
usually succeeds because the conflicting writer has finished.
Retries are cheap compared to bubbling up 'ahead=-1 behind=-1' to
the operator.

## Guard-special

The guard's `git diff --cached` runs inside the user's pre-commit
hook. We DO NOT wrap the guard in `run_git_locked` (Track B's charter
excludes it) but we can still patch the guard's error-handling to do
SIGSEGV retry locally. Track E includes that narrow exception.

## Success signals

- Kernel-log segfault followed by structured event
  `git_segfault_retry` with repo, args, retry #, and final outcome.
- TUI toast the first time per session; subsequent occurrences update
  a running count on the System Health screen.
- Shell-out git calls that used to exit 139 and fail upstream now
  succeed after retry in >99% of cases (measured in CI with a
  synthetic racer fixture).

title: E1: Detect SIGSEGV (exit 139 / signal 11) inside run_git_locked
description:
# E1: SIGSEGV detection

## Why

Must be inside `run_git_locked` so every wrapped call benefits
automatically. Unix: check `ExitStatus::signal() == Some(11)` via
std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt. Fallback: check raw status
for `== 139` (shell-style 128+signal). Windows: SIGSEGV manifests
as `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xC0000005)` — translate and
treat the same.

## Implementation

- Add `enum GitRunOutcome { Success(Output), Segfault, Other(io::Error) }`.
- `run_git_locked` returns this instead of raw `io::Result<Output>`.
  Convenience wrappers (`run_git_locked_checked`) preserve the
  existing `io::Result` API for call sites that don't care.
- Segfault detection is unit-tested using a shim binary that exits
  with signal 11 deterministically.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT auto-retry here. E1 is just detection + classification.
  E2 handles retry.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Signal matrix + cross-platform + tests

### Signals we classify as 'segfault-like' (retry eligible)

| signal | exit code | cause | retry? |
|---|---|---|---|
| SIGSEGV (11) | 139 | the 2.51.0 race | YES |
| SIGBUS (7) | 135 | same race, different memory model | YES |
| SIGABRT (6) | 134 | libgit2 assertion failure | NO (not this bug) |
| SIGKILL (9) | 137 | OOM killer | NO (different problem) |
| exit 128 | 128 | fatal git error pre-crash | NO |

Rationale: only SIGSEGV / SIGBUS fingerprint the mmap race. Everything
else is some other bug and retrying would mask it.

### Implementation

    enum GitRunOutcome {
        Success(Output),
        SegfaultLike { signal: i32 },   // 11 or 7
        OtherSignal { signal: i32 },
        OtherError(io::Error),
    }

- Detection via std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt::signal() on
  Unix. On Windows, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xC0000005) -> map to
  SegfaultLike { signal: 11 }.
- When Output exit code is exactly 139 and we can't inspect signal
  (shell wrapping, e.g.), treat as SegfaultLike.

### Unit tests (crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/tests/sigsegv_classify.rs)

- Build small shim binaries in a tempdir that exit with specific
  signals. Use the same mechanism E2 uses.
- Matrix:
    - shim_segv (raise SIGSEGV) -> SegfaultLike { 11 }
    - shim_bus (raise SIGBUS) -> SegfaultLike { 7 }
    - shim_abrt (raise SIGABRT) -> OtherSignal { 6 }
    - shim_kill (SIGKILL self-sent) -> OtherSignal { 9 }
    - shim_exit_139 (exit 139 directly) -> SegfaultLike (fallback)
    - shim_exit_42 -> Success(output with status 42)
- Every test prints 'CLASSIFIER_CASE <name>: <outcome>' to tracing.

### Windows test

- #[cfg(windows)] test_classify_access_violation:
  uses a shim that dereferences a null pointer (tiny Rust program)
  and verifies STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION -> SegfaultLike.

### Observability

- tracing event 'git_outcome_classified' { outcome, signal, exit_code,
  repo_slug, args_hash } — fires once per run_git_locked invocation.

title: E2: Exponential-backoff retry policy for segfault outcomes
description:
# E2: Retry policy

## Policy

- Max retries: 3.
- Backoff: 100ms, 400ms, 1600ms. Jitter +/- 25% per attempt.
- On success within retry budget, log INFO-level event
  'git_segfault_retry_succeeded' with final-attempt number.
- On exhaustion, surface the original error to the caller with
  context 'gave up after 3 retries; system git 2.51.0 known-bad'.

## Implementation

- Wrap in `run_git_locked_with_retry`. The existing public
  `run_git_locked` (post-E1) becomes this new wrapper by default.
- Policy is encapsulated in a `struct SegfaultRetryPolicy` so E3's
  observability hooks have a stable attach point.

## Tests

- Unit test with a shim that segfaults once then succeeds: assert one
  retry, success.
- Unit test with a shim that segfaults 4 times: assert 3 retries,
  then error bubbled with the 'gave up' context.

## Non-goals

- No per-caller retry customization. One policy, globally, because
  the bug is always the same shape.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Retry policy details + exhaustion handling + tests

### Policy (final)

- Max retries: 3 (1 initial + 3 = 4 attempts total).
- Backoff sequence: 100ms, 400ms, 1600ms. Total worst-case added
  latency: ~2.1s before final exhaustion.
- Jitter: uniform multiplier in [0.75, 1.25] applied per sleep.
- Jitter RNG: deterministic per retry session, seeded from
  (repo_slug, start_ts) so tests can freeze it.
- Max wall-time cap (belt-and-suspenders): 10s total including
  retries. If the cumulative elapsed exceeds 10s during any attempt,
  we stop retrying and return the most recent error.

### Exhaustion behavior

- After 3 retries all segfaulting, we surface:
    Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Other,
        format!(\"git segfaulted {} times in a row on {}; system git \
        may be 2.51.0 (known bad). Set AM_GIT_BINARY or upgrade. \
        Last error: {}\", attempts, repo_slug, last_err)))
- The ledger event 'git_segfault_retry' fires with outcome='exhausted'.
- Metric `git_segfault_retry_exhausted_total{caller}` increments.

### Unit tests (crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/tests/sigsegv_retry.rs)

- test_retry_succeeds_on_attempt_2 (shim fails once, succeeds next)
- test_retry_succeeds_on_attempt_3

- test_retry_exhaustion_after_4_attempts (all fail)
- test_retry_respects_10s_wallclock_cap

- test_retry_jitter_deterministic_for_same_seed

- test_abrt_not_retried (out-of-scope for this bug)

### Integration test

- tests/integration/run_git_locked_with_retry.rs using a shim that:
    - first invocation: segfaults
    - second invocation: succeeds with hello-world output
  asserts run_git_locked returns the hello-world output with 1 retry
  logged.

### E2E

comments.text:
## REVISION v3: args_hash truncation + log volume controls

### args_hash truncation

sha256 full (64 hex chars) is a lot of log volume if we emit millions
of events. Revised:

- Default: truncate to 16 hex chars (first 64 bits). Collision risk
  across a single process's lifetime is negligible for log-grouping
  purposes.
- Full hash available via env override:
    AM_LOG_FULL_ARGS_HASH=1 -> emit 64-char hash.
- Raw args via:
    AM_LOG_GIT_ARGS=1 -> emit plaintext argv (debug-only, may leak
    path-based secrets).

### Log-volume budget

Each run_git_locked call produces:
- 1 INFO 'git_locked_enter'
- 1 INFO 'git_locked_exit'
- Optional WARN/ERROR events during retries

At 100 QPS, that's 200 INFO lines/sec = 17M/day. Too much for
default verbosity. Revised:
- Default INFO filter: emit full 'enter'/'exit' for calls with
  duration_ms >= 100 OR outcome != 'success'. Sub-100ms successful
  calls get sampled to 1 in 100.
- Ops can override via AM_LOG_RUN_GIT_LOCKED=full|sampled|off.
- Metrics are still exact (counters don't sample).

### Sampling implementation

- Atomic counter per caller that mod-100 emits.
- No config per caller; single global knob.
- Logs a startup INFO describing the current sampling rate so ops
  know what they're getting.

### Backfill of the spec (E6)

- E6 (observability spec) describes the sampling policy and this
  env knob. The spec is the source of truth.

### Tests

- test_args_hash_truncation_default
- test_args_hash_truncation_full_when_env_set
- test_sampling_correctness_across_100_calls
- test_sampling_never_drops_error_outcomes
- test_sampling_disabled_when_am_log_run_git_locked_full

title: E4: TUI System Health toast for git_segfault_retry events
description:
# E4: TUI toast for segfault events

## Why

When the TUI is running, the operator should see this the first time
it happens, not read about it in logs tomorrow.

## Deliverables

- Hook E3's tracing event into the existing toast pipeline in
  `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/system_health.rs`.
- First occurrence per session: WARNING toast (yellow) with text
  'git 2.51.0 segfault retried on <repo>. Set AM_GIT_BINARY or
  upgrade git to stop seeing this.'
- Subsequent occurrences: suppressed individually, but the System
  Health screen grows a `git segfault retries: N` badge that
  increments live via the metrics counter.
- Dismissible via Ctrl+Y (existing toast focus binding).
- Respects `AM_TUI_TOAST_ENABLED=false`.

## Tests

- Unit test the toast formatter with a fixture event.
- Integration test by emitting three fake events and asserting the
  badge value.

## Non-goals

- No changes to the robot CLI surface — robot already reads metrics,
  so E3 is sufficient for non-TUI contexts.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Toast behavior under load + headless compatibility + tests

### Behavior matrix

| condition | toast response | badge response |
|---|---|---|
| first segfault per session | WARNING toast, 15s dismiss | badge shows 1 |
| subsequent segfaults (<60s from last) | no new toast (rate-limited) | badge increments |
| subsequent segfaults (>=60s from last) | WARNING toast again | badge increments |
| 10+ segfaults in a session | CRITICAL toast once (color escalate) | badge increments |
| TUI disabled (headless) | no toast (skipped) | metric incremented |
| AM_TUI_TOAST_ENABLED=false | no toast | badge still tracks |

### Rate-limit rationale

Without it, a 2.51.0 box with 50 retries per minute would flood the
toast pipeline. 60s inter-toast minimum is long enough to be quiet,
short enough to re-alert if the issue keeps happening.

### Headless compatibility

- Check tui::is_enabled() before emitting toast. In headless/CI
  contexts, metric increment still happens so external monitors
  can observe.
- Never panic if the toast pipeline is torn down (server shutdown
  case).

- test_first_segfault_shows_toast

  driver (existing helper) to feed 3 segfault events in 30s and

- Second scenario: feed 15 events across 5 minutes; assert 2 toasts

title: E5: Narrow SIGSEGV retry into guard (pre-commit/pre-push git calls)
description:
# E5: Guard SIGSEGV retry (narrow)

## Why

The guard can't use `run_git_locked` (its git calls run inside the
user's pre-commit hook, same pid, would deadlock with the hook's own
index lock). But it CAN still retry on SIGSEGV locally — same bug,
same fingerprint, same fix.

## Implementation

- In `crates/mcp-agent-mail-guard/src/lib.rs`, wrap each
  `Command::new(\"git\").output()?` call with a small `fn
  guard_retry_on_segfault(cmd: Command) -> io::Result<Output>`
  local helper that reproduces E2's policy (3 retries, 100/400/1600ms
  jittered).
- Import E1's classifier (refactor to pub(crate) so guard can use it
  without pulling the whole run_git_locked machinery).
- Log via `tracing::warn!` with target `guard` — guard can't emit to
  the evidence ledger without a network hop, so local tracing is good
  enough.

## Non-goals

- No flock in the guard. No AM_GIT_BINARY override in the guard
  (guard is installed as a shell/python hook and the shell already
  resolves `git` via PATH; we respect that).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Guard hook shapes + Python-side retry coordination

### Guard hook implementations (clarified)

`install_precommit_guard` installs a dispatch script at
`.git/hooks/pre-commit`. The dispatch is typically a small shell or
Python wrapper that invokes either:

  (a) `am guard check` (Rust binary in cwd / PATH), which in turn
      shells out via `Command::new(\"git\")` in
      crates/mcp-agent-mail-guard/src/lib.rs, OR
  (b) A vendored Python hook (for compatibility with the Python legacy
      install), which calls `subprocess.run([\"git\", ...])`.

E5 covers both:

### Part A: Rust-side retry (crates/mcp-agent-mail-guard/src/lib.rs)

- Import `classify_git_outcome` from mcp-agent-mail-core::git_lock
  (refactored pub(crate) -> pub for this specifically).
- Wrap each `Command::new(\"git\").output()?` call with a local
  helper `guard_retry_on_segfault(cmd: &mut Command) -> io::Result<Output>`
  that:
    - Clones the Command configuration (args, envs).
    - Runs it. On SegfaultLike, retries with the same 100/400/1600 +
      jitter schedule E2 uses.
    - On exhaustion, surfaces a clear error suitable for operators:
      'guard git op segfaulted N times; system git may be 2.51.0;
      commit aborted. See <runbook>.'
- tracing::warn! on each retry with target 'guard::segfault_retry'.
- NO flock, NO process mutex — we are inside the user's git process.

### Part B: Python hook retry (crates/mcp-agent-mail-guard/src/install.rs — the template)

- The Python hook template gains a minimal retry decorator:

    def _run_git_with_retry(args, timeout=60, max_retries=3):
        import subprocess, time, random, sys
        delays = (0.1, 0.4, 1.6)
        for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
            r = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, timeout=timeout)
            # 139 = 128+11 (SIGSEGV); 135 = 128+7 (SIGBUS)
            if r.returncode not in (139, -11, 135, -7):
                return r
            if attempt == max_retries:
                sys.stderr.write(f\"guard: git segfaulted {attempt+1} times; aborting\\n\")
                return r
            jitter = random.uniform(0.75, 1.25)
            time.sleep(delays[attempt] * jitter)
        return r

- Hook calls `_run_git_with_retry` instead of raw subprocess.
- Logs go to stderr so they surface in git commit output.
- No external deps (stdlib only) — important for hook portability.

### Unit tests

Rust side (crates/mcp-agent-mail-guard/src/lib.rs):
- test_guard_retry_succeeds_after_segfault
- test_guard_retry_exhausts_after_4_segfaults
- test_guard_retry_non_segfault_propagated
- test_guard_retry_no_flock_no_mutex (structural check)

Python side (tests/guard/test_python_hook_retry.py):
- Same matrix using a pytest + subprocess fixture.

### E2E test

- tests/e2e/test_guard_with_bad_git.sh:
  - Installs a guard on a temp repo.
  - Sets AM_GIT_BINARY to a shim that segfaults 50% of the time.
  - Stages a change, runs `git commit`.
  - Assert: commit SUCCEEDS (retry saves it).
  - Repeats 20 times; assert >= 19 succeed. Log full guard output
    on each attempt for post-hoc analysis.

### Logging

- target: mcp_agent_mail::guard::segfault_retry
- every retry: WARN with attempt, signal, args_hash, duration_ms.
- exhaustion: ERROR with the abort reason and remediation pointer.

comments.text: COMPLETED. Two-layer E5: (1) Python hook template (install.rs) gains _run_git_with_retry helper that detects segfault-shaped exits (rc == -11/-7/139/135/0xC0000005), retries with 100/400/1600ms jittered backoff, emits stderr warnings per retry. Honors AM_GIT_BINARY. All git subprocess calls in the Python template routed through it: rev-list, diff-tree, rev-parse --show-toplevel, config --bool core.ignorecase, and the pre-commit diff --cached. (2) Rust guard side (lib.rs) gains guard_run_git_with_retry() with identical policy, routing get_staged_paths() through it. Tracing events under target=mcp_agent_mail::guard::segfault_retry. Guard crate gains tracing workspace dep.

title: E6: Observability spec — single source of truth for all events/metrics
description:
# E6: Observability standards for this epic

## Why

Tracks A-F each define their own events, fields, and metric names.
Without a central spec they drift. This bead is the one-stop reference
that everything else points at.

## Deliverable: docs/OBSERVABILITY_git_251.md (new)

Sections:

### 1. Naming conventions

- tracing target prefix: `mcp_agent_mail::<component>::<subcomponent>`
- event names: snake_case, verb_or_state (e.g. `flock_acquired`,
  `git_segfault_retry`, `reservation_activity_result`).
- field names: snake_case; units in the name (`duration_ms`,
  `wait_seconds`, `size_bytes`). No bare 'duration'.

### 2. Required fields for every run_git_locked-adjacent event

- `repo_slug`     (tokenized project identifier)
- `caller`        (static site string; populated by macro)
- `args_hash`     (sha256 of joined argv; raw args gated on
                   AM_LOG_GIT_ARGS=1)
- `duration_ms`   (number)
- `outcome`       (enum: 'success'|'retrying'|'succeeded_after_retry'
                   |'exhausted'|'error')
- `git_version`   (from cached resolution)

### 3. Metrics catalog

Complete table of all counters/histograms/gauges introduced across
the epic, with label sets, bucket choices for histograms, and the
tracking bead reference.

| metric | type | labels | added in | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| git_repo_lock_acquisitions_total | counter | repo_slug | B2 | ... |
| git_repo_lock_wait_seconds | hist | repo_slug | B2 | buckets [1ms, 10ms, 100ms, 1s] |
| git_flock_wait_seconds | hist | repo_slug | B3 | |
| git_flock_timeout_total | counter | repo_slug | B3 | |
| git_flock_readonly_total | counter | repo_slug | B3 | |
| run_git_locked_total | counter | caller,outcome | B4 | |
| run_git_locked_duration_seconds | hist | caller | B4 | |
| run_git_locked_in_flight | gauge | caller | B4 | |
| run_git_locked_contention_seconds | hist | caller | B4 | |
| git_segfault_total | counter | repo_slug,caller | E1/E3 | |
| git_segfault_retry_attempted_total | counter | caller | E2 | |
| git_segfault_retry_succeeded_total | counter | caller,attempt_n | E2 | |
| git_segfault_retry_exhausted_total | counter | caller | E2 | |
| git_segfault_retry_latency_seconds | hist | caller,outcome | E2 | |
| reservation_activity_duration_seconds | hist | repo_slug | C2 | |
| pathspec_walk_duration_seconds | hist | repo_slug | C3 | |
| doctor_fix_orphan_refs_actions_total | counter | op,outcome | F1/F3 | |

### 4. Evidence ledger event schemas

Link to the JSON Schema files (docs/schemas/*.json) for each event
kind. At minimum:
- git_segfault_retry.json (from E3)
- fix_orphan_refs.json (from F1)
- reservation_activity_result.json (from C2)
- git_version_check.json (from A2)

### 5. Structured log sampling

Guidance on what should be INFO vs DEBUG:
- INFO: once per user-visible operation (e.g., 'fix_orphan_refs_done')
- DEBUG: per-iteration or per-entity (e.g., 'ref_scanned')
- WARN: unexpected-but-recoverable (retries, lock waits >5s)
- ERROR: unrecoverable (exhausted retry, protected ref refused)

### 6. Robot CLI surface

- `am robot metrics` exposes all counters by default.
- `am robot analytics` aggregates the high-signal ones into a
  narrative ('git instability' section).
- `am robot health --format json` includes the ref integrity sweep
  results (F5).

## Tests

- tests/docs/test_observability_spec_exists.sh: file present.
- tests/metrics/test_all_spec_metrics_registered.rs: for each
  metric in the spec, assert it's registered in the metrics registry
  on server startup. If the spec says we emit it, we'd better emit it.
- tests/schemas/test_all_event_schemas_valid.sh: jsonschema-meta
  validate every docs/schemas/*.json file.

## Gate

- G1 quality gate includes:
    test_all_spec_metrics_registered.rs
    test_all_event_schemas_valid.sh
  so a spec/code drift shows up before release.

# Track F: Recovery for damaged repos

**Goal:** clean up the damage that has already happened on repos that
were hit by the 2.51.0 race BEFORE layers 1-5 landed. Specifically:
partial `.git/HEAD`, orphan `refs/stash` pointing to missing objects,
corrupt `packed-refs`.

## Why as a separate track

The operator pain in the original report wasn't just 'segfaults are
happening'. It was also 'my repos are already broken and I don't
know how to fix them.' Track F gives them a one-line fix command.

## Safety stance (CRITICAL — see AGENTS.md Rule 2.1 and
    feedback_never_touch_external_repos.md)

This track operates ONLY on refs and reflog entries, NEVER on the
working tree. Specifically:

- We will PRUNE refs that point to missing objects (stash entries,
  dangling branches from crash).
- We will REBUILD packed-refs from loose refs via `git pack-refs --all`.
- We will NEVER run `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git checkout`,
  or anything that can delete uncommitted work.
- We will NEVER delete loose object files. If an object is missing,
  we accept that it's missing and just remove the ref that points to
  it.
- The command requires explicit invocation. It is not run implicitly
  or as part of any auto-healing path.

## Success signals

- `am doctor fix-orphan-refs --project <path>` on a damaged repo
  returns to a clean state:
    - `git fsck` reports no missing objects from refs (dangling
      objects are fine — those are unreferenced blobs).
    - `ahead/behind` counters work (user can run `ru status` again).
    - No loss of committed history.
- The command is idempotent — re-running it on a clean repo is a
  no-op that prints 'nothing to do'.
