title: F2: Detect missing-object refs via git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs
description:
# F2: Detect missing-object refs

## Why

Before we prune anything we need a trustworthy list of refs whose
target objects are missing. `git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs`
gives us unreachable objects (which we don't care about) AND
'missing blob' / 'missing commit' / 'missing tree' lines (which we do
care about). Cross-referenced against all refs gives us the set to
prune.

## Implementation

- Use libgit2 directly (NOT shell-out) via `git2::Repository::
  fsck`? — libgit2 does NOT expose fsck. So we shell out via
  `run_git_locked`:
    git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs --no-dangling
- Parse stderr lines starting with 'missing' — they have the form:
    missing blob <sha>
    missing commit <sha>
    missing tree <sha>
- For each missing sha, walk every ref (via git2's
  `Repository::references`) and collect refs whose peeled target is
  in the missing set.
- Return `Vec<PrunableRef> { ref_name, reason, target_sha }`.

## Parity / correctness

- Test against a tempdir repo where we deliberately `rm` a blob after
  committing it — assert F2 identifies the dependent refs.
- Submodules: pointer commits to nested repos must NOT be flagged
  (fsck already handles this — verify).

## Non-goals

- Do not prune. Detection only.
- Do not touch reflogs in this bead (we passed `--no-reflogs`
  deliberately — reflogs regenerate and aren't load-bearing for
  recovery).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: libgit2-native detection (no fsck parsing)

### Why we switch from fsck-parsing to libgit2

Original plan shelled out to `git fsck` and parsed stderr. Two
problems:
  1. fsck output format varies between git versions (2.43 vs 2.51
     format differently; 2.51.0 specifically might itself segfault
     during fsck under load on a damaged repo — this is the bug we
     are trying to survive).
  2. Parsing stderr is brittle for something so important to
     recovery; a silent format drift could make F3 think there's
     nothing to prune.

### New design (libgit2-native)

    fn detect_missing_refs(repo: &git2::Repository) -> Result<Vec<PrunableRef>> {
        let odb = repo.odb()?;
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        repo.references()?.for_each(|r| {
            let reference = r?;
            let Some(target) = reference.target() else { return Ok(()); };
            // Peel through tag chains; final oid is what must exist.
            let peeled = reference.peel(git2::ObjectType::Any).map(|obj| obj.id());
            let oid_to_check = peeled.unwrap_or(target);
            if !odb.exists(oid_to_check) {
                out.push(PrunableRef {
                    ref_name: reference.name().unwrap_or(\"?\").to_string(),
                    reason: format!(\"object {} missing from ODB\", oid_to_check),
                    target_sha: oid_to_check,
                });
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
        Ok(out)
    }

- Walks every ref via git2::Repository::references().
- Peels through tag chains so annotated-tag -> commit -> missing
  commit is detected.
- Uses odb.exists() which checks loose + pack storage in O(log n).
- Does NOT walk reflogs (F2 non-goal; matches original plan).

### Fallbacks

- If libgit2 fails to open the repo (structural corruption), fall
  BACK to `run_git_locked` shell-out of `git fsck --unreachable
  --no-reflogs` as a degraded path, parse with a very lenient regex,
  and log WARN 'libgit2_open_failed_using_cli_fsck'.

### Unit tests (crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/tests/f2_detect.rs)

- test_detect_missing_blob_ref: commit a file, rm the object, assert
  detected.
- test_detect_missing_commit_ref: add a branch, rm the commit
  object, assert detected.
- test_detect_missing_tree_indirectly: tag points to commit which
  points to missing tree; assert the tag is flagged.
- test_detect_no_false_positives_on_clean_repo
- test_detect_submodule_inner_pointer_not_flagged
- test_detect_annotated_tag_peeling
- test_detect_reflog_entries_not_flagged

### Integration test

- tests/integration/f2_detect_complex.rs: build a tempdir repo
  with:
    - one clean ref
    - one orphan stash (missing blob)
    - one dangling branch (missing commit)
    - one tag pointing to a missing commit (annotated)
    - one submodule (clean)
  Assert detection returns exactly 3 PrunableRefs (stash, branch, tag).

### Logging

- target: mcp_agent_mail::doctor::detect_missing_refs
- DEBUG 'ref_scanned' (every ref) — gated on -v.
- INFO 'ref_missing_object' { ref, oid } per finding.
- WARN 'libgit2_open_failed_using_cli_fsck' on fallback.

title: F3: Prune refs/stash and other refs pointing to missing objects
description:
# F3: Prune dangling refs

## Why

Once F2 identifies them, we remove them. Pruning a ref is the
exact right operation for this damage class: the object is gone, the
ref cannot be followed, and leaving it rots tooling downstream (this
is what causes `ru status` to report `ahead=-1 behind=-1`).

## Implementation

- `git2::Repository::find_reference(name)?.delete()?` — done via
  libgit2, no shell-out needed.
- For each `PrunableRef` from F2, record a `{ op: prune_ref, ref,
  reason }` in the actions log, then delete it (if --apply).
- Under --dry-run, only record the action without deleting.

## Safety

- We NEVER touch `refs/heads/main` even if F2 flags it. Main branch
  is the operator's historical record; if its tip object is missing,
  the correct answer is 'operator recovers from backup / reflog / git
  reflog', not 'we silently delete main'. The command surfaces this
  as a BLOCKING error and refuses to proceed for that repo.
- Same protection for `HEAD`, `refs/heads/master` (legacy).
- Explicit allow-list of 'safe to prune' ref namespaces:
    refs/stash
    refs/temp/
    refs/original/
  Other namespaces prompt a confirmation (unless --force is also
  given). We want the operator to see what they're about to nuke.

## Tests

- Unit test against a temp repo with one pruneable stash entry.
- Unit test that refuses to prune refs/heads/main even with --apply.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Safety allow-list + force flow + tests

### Protected ref namespaces (REFUSE by default)

- refs/heads/main, refs/heads/master
- refs/heads/HEAD, HEAD
- refs/remotes/*/HEAD
- refs/remotes/origin/main, refs/remotes/origin/master
- any ref with a custom protected-ref metadata marker (future-proof;
  read from .agent-mail-project-id or project config)

If F2 flags one of these, F3 emits a 'refuse' action in the actions
log with reason 'protected branch; use --force' and does NOT delete.

### Safe-to-prune namespaces (auto-prune)

- refs/stash
- refs/temp/*
- refs/original/*
- refs/prs/*  (some repos store PR metadata here; treat as safe; log
  a note so ops can adjust if they use prs/ as a source of truth)

### Everything else (prompt)

- Without --force: emit 'refuse' action for safety; print suggestion
  to review manually.
- With --force: proceed with prune.

### Implementation

    match ref_category(&name) {
        RefCategory::Protected    => record_refuse(name, \"protected\"),
        RefCategory::SafeToPrune  => { delete_ref(&repo, name)?; record_pruned(name) },
        RefCategory::AskUser      => {
            if args.force { delete_ref(&repo, name)?; record_pruned(name) }
            else { record_refuse(name, \"use --force\") }
        }
    }

### Unit tests

- test_prune_stash_without_force
- test_prune_temp_without_force
- test_refuse_main_even_with_force (exit code 3, clear error)
- test_refuse_unknown_namespace_without_force
- test_prune_unknown_namespace_with_force
- test_prune_does_not_touch_reflog_entries
- test_prune_on_detached_head_ok

### Safety tests

- tests/integration/f3_safety.rs: build a fixture with a DAMAGED
  refs/heads/main (commit object missing). Run --apply. Assert exit
  code 3, assert main still exists in the refs listing, assert a
  clear error message in stderr mentioning 'use --force and backup
  first'.

### Logging

- target: mcp_agent_mail::doctor::prune_refs
- INFO 'ref_pruned' { name, oid, reason }
- WARN 'ref_refused_protected' { name, reason }
- WARN 'ref_refused_unknown_namespace' { name, hint: 'use --force' }

### Backup artifact

- Before --apply pruning, F3 writes a timestamped backup of ALL refs
  (loose + packed) to <project>/.git/am-backups/refs-<ts>.txt via
  `git for-each-ref` (libgit2). This gives the operator a recovery
  path if we mis-prune.
- Backup retention: last 10 backups kept; older ones deleted.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v3: Backup location moved + active-ops interlock

### Backup directory location (revised)

Original v2 said `<project>/.git/am-backups/refs-<ts>.txt`. Issues:
- `.git/` has restrictive permissions in some shared-user setups.
- Other git tooling also writes under `.git/` and may conflict.
- The backup is mcp-agent-mail specific; it belongs in our storage.

Revised location:
  `<STORAGE_ROOT>/backups/refs/<project_slug>/<ts>.txt`

Where STORAGE_ROOT is the configured mcp-agent-mail storage directory
(XDG-aware, legacy ~/.mcp_agent_mail_git_mailbox_repo). Benefits:
- Clear ownership.
- No collision with other git tooling.
- Operators can inspect/restore without cd'ing into .git/.
- Easy to rotate and prune (see below).

### Backup rotation

Cron-style rotation via a post-apply cleanup step:
- Keep the 10 most recent backups per project.
- Prune older ones synchronously after apply (not as a separate
  scheduled task — avoids drift and keeps behavior predictable).
- Logs INFO 'backup_pruned' per removed file.

### Active-ops interlock (critical)

F3 pruning is not just a filesystem write — it deletes refs. If an
operator is actively committing in the repo while we run --apply,
we could delete a ref they just created that our detection missed.

Mitigation:
- F3 --apply acquires run_git_locked on the repo for the entire
  operation. This holds the per-repo mutex + flock for the duration
  of the detect+prune+repack sequence.
- Hold time is bounded: prune is O(refs_to_delete), usually <1s even
  for pathological cases.
- If flock wait exceeds 60s (from B3 cap), F3 aborts with a clear
  error pointing ops to the contended repo. We'd rather fail fast
  than interleave.

### New tests

- test_fix_orphan_refs_backup_written_under_storage_root
- test_fix_orphan_refs_holds_flock_during_apply (integration test
  with a 2nd process attempting to acquire the flock during the
  apply; asserts it waits)
- test_fix_orphan_refs_aborts_on_flock_timeout
- test_fix_orphan_refs_backup_rotation_keeps_10

### Logging additions

- INFO 'backup_rotation_started' { project, kept_count, pruned_count }
- INFO 'flock_acquired_for_prune' { project, hold_s }
- WARN 'flock_timeout_aborting_prune' { project, waited_s }

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CLAIMED by RubyKnoll

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: COMPLETED (bundled with F1). doctor_orphan_refs::scan_one_project implements the full F3 logic: classifies each finding via RefCategory (Protected -> refuse; SafeToPrune -> auto-prune; AskUser -> --force required). Writes ref backups to <STORAGE_ROOT>/backups/refs/<project_slug>/<ts>.txt BEFORE pruning (contains full ref listing + orphan findings). Prunes via git2::Reference::delete. Rotates backups keeping last 10. Holds per-repo RepoFlock for the entire detect+prune sequence so concurrent committers can't interleave. Structured tracing (target=mcp_agent_mail::doctor::fix_orphan_refs) for every action (ref_pruned, flock_acquire_failed, backup_rotation_remove_failed, fix_orphan_refs_done). CLI compiles clean workspace-wide.

title: F4: Rebuild packed-refs via git pack-refs --all under flock
description:
# F4: Rebuild packed-refs

## Why

A corrupt `packed-refs` can mask other problems. Regenerating from
loose refs is cheap and safe when we hold the per-repo flock.

## Implementation

- Shell-out via `run_git_locked`: `git pack-refs --all --prune`.
- Record `{ op: rebuild_packed_refs }` in the actions log.
- Skipped if `--dry-run`.

## Safety

- `git pack-refs` is safe: it writes a new packed-refs file and
  atomically renames into place. Operator's loose refs are the
  source of truth; after pack-refs, they can be removed or kept.
- The `--prune` flag removes loose refs that are now in packed-refs.
  That is the intended behavior (packed-refs becomes authoritative).
  Worth documenting in the command's --help text.

## Non-goals

- We do NOT try to repair packed-refs by hand. Regenerate and move on.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: pack-refs execution + backup + tests

### Atomic rename guarantees

- `git pack-refs` writes a new packed-refs file then renames. We
  piggyback on that atomicity by shelling out via run_git_locked:
    run_git_locked(repo).args([\"pack-refs\", \"--all\", \"--prune\"])
- --all: include all loose refs (tags, branches, remotes).
- --prune: remove loose ref files that are now in packed-refs.

### Backup before repack

- F3 writes a backup (see F3 revision). F4 writes an ADDITIONAL
  backup of the existing packed-refs file (if any) to
  <project>/.git/am-backups/packed-refs-<ts>.txt before invoking
  pack-refs.
- Rationale: defense-in-depth. pack-refs is safe, but repos on 2.51.0
  have shown corruption in packed-refs itself; we want a durable
  undo.

### Unit tests

- test_rebuild_packed_refs_on_clean_repo_noop_ish (file exists, same
  content)
- test_rebuild_packed_refs_consolidates_loose
- test_rebuild_packed_refs_backup_created
- test_rebuild_packed_refs_respects_flock (verifies GitCmd lock held
  throughout; integration-flavored)

### Integration test

- tests/integration/f4_repack.rs:
  - Build a repo with 20 loose refs and no packed-refs.
  - Run F4 --apply.
  - Assert .git/packed-refs exists, lists all 20, loose ref files
    are gone except HEAD (pack-refs doesn't pack HEAD).

### E2E test (tests/e2e/test_doctor_repack.sh)

- Hammer a repo with 100 concurrent ref creations (via run_git_locked),
  run F4 --apply, assert no refs lost, all timestamps preserved
  (packed-refs records peeled commit SHAs not timestamps, so 'no
  history lost' is what we assert).

### Logging

- target: mcp_agent_mail::doctor::repack
- INFO 'packed_refs_backup_written' { path, size_bytes }
- INFO 'packed_refs_rebuild_started' { project }
- INFO 'packed_refs_rebuild_completed' { project, duration_ms,
  exit_code }

### Non-goals

- We do NOT try to repair a CORRUPT packed-refs by hand. Regenerate
  from loose refs and move on.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: COMPLETED. doctor_orphan_refs::repack_refs() in crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/doctor_orphan_refs.rs. Runs 'git pack-refs --all --prune' via GitCmd (serialized). Backs up existing packed-refs to <STORAGE_ROOT>/backups/refs/<project_slug>/<ts>-packed-refs.txt BEFORE repacking. Invoked automatically after a successful prune in scan_one_project. Tracing events: packed_refs_backup_written, packed_refs_rebuild_completed. Failure path records op='repack_failed' in the action log and increments error count.

title: F5: Periodic health sweep integration
description:
# F5: Integrate into periodic health sweep

## Why

Operators don't remember to run recovery commands. The existing health
sweep (currently only does archive integrity) should also detect orphan
refs across all registered projects and surface them in the TUI's
System Health screen.

## Implementation

- In `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/system_health.rs`
  (and the non-TUI sweep path), extend the scheduled health check to
  run F2 (detection only — never F3/F4) against each project.
- Findings go into the System Health screen under a new 'Git ref
  integrity' panel.
- If findings exist, a banner prompts: 'run `am doctor fix-orphan-refs`
  to repair N projects'. Banner is suppressed if AM_GIT_BINARY is set
  (because that indicates ops already knows).

## Non-goals

- Never auto-repair. Detection only. This is both a safety
  principle (Rule 2.1) and a correctness one — fixing refs in a
  periodic sweep would interleave with operator git ops.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Sweep config + banner behavior + tests

### Config knobs

- AM_HEALTH_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS (default 3600 = hourly)
  - 0 disables the sweep entirely.
- AM_HEALTH_SWEEP_MAX_PROJECTS (default 50) — sweep at most N
  projects per run to bound cost.
- AM_HEALTH_SWEEP_QUIET=true — suppress banner + toast, but still
  emit metrics. For ops who know and choose to live with it.

### Banner wording (TUI + Robot)

    [ATTN] Git ref integrity: 3 registered projects have orphan refs.
           Run `am doctor fix-orphan-refs --all --dry-run` to preview.

- Shown in System Health screen's top panel when count > 0.
- Suppressed if AM_HEALTH_SWEEP_QUIET=true OR if the operator has
  dismissed via `.` action menu in the last 24h (dismissal persisted
  in .agent-mail-project-id sidecar).

### Robot CLI

- `am robot health --format json` output gains a new field:
    \"git_ref_integrity\": {
        \"sweep_ts\": \"...\",
        \"projects_checked\": 10,
        \"projects_with_orphans\": 2,
        \"orphan_ref_count\": 5,
        \"detail_per_project\": [ {...}, {...} ]
    }
- The JSON schema gets updated (docs/schemas/robot_health.json).

### Unit tests

- test_sweep_respects_interval (mock clock)
- test_sweep_respects_max_projects_cap
- test_sweep_disabled_at_zero_interval
- test_sweep_banner_hidden_when_quiet
- test_sweep_dismissal_persists_24h

### Integration test

- tests/integration/f5_sweep.rs:
  - Create 3 tempdir projects (1 clean, 2 damaged with orphan refs).
  - Register them with a minimal server.
  - Tick the sweep scheduler 3 times (at 0s, 1h+jitter, 2h+jitter).
  - Assert each sweep picks up the same 2 damaged projects.
  - Assert no auto-repair happens (fix-orphan-refs command still
    requires explicit invocation).

### Safety

- Sweep NEVER calls F3 (prune) or F4 (repack). Read-only detection
  only. Repeated from Track F parent — reinforced here because the
  sweep is the one that could accidentally auto-repair if someone
  extends it later.

comments.author: ubuntu

## REVISION v3: Dedicated state file + sweep ordering

## REVISION v2: Fingerprint reproduction test + docs

### Fingerprint reproduction fixture

tests/fixtures/make_2_51_damage.sh (new, checked in, executable):

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Creates a git repo in \$1 with the exact damage pattern produced
    # by the 2.51.0 segfault bug. Used for reproducible F2/F3/F4 tests.
    set -euo pipefail
    repo=\"\$1\"; mkdir -p \"\$repo\"; cd \"\$repo\"
    git init -b main -q
    git config user.email 'fixture@local'
    git config user.name 'Fixture'
    echo hello > a.txt; git add a.txt; git commit -q -m init
    echo world > a.txt; git stash push -q -m 'wip'
    # simulate 2.51.0 corruption: drop the stash blob while keeping
    # the stash ref intact
    stash_oid=\$(git rev-parse refs/stash)
    blob=\$(git ls-tree -r \$stash_oid | awk '{print \$3}' | head -n1)
    rm -f \".git/objects/\${blob:0:2}/\${blob:2}\"
    # simulate a dangling branch pointing at a missing commit
    missing_oid='deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef'
    printf '%s\\n' \"\$missing_oid\" > .git/refs/heads/crash-recovery-tmp
    # simulate bad HEAD
    cp .git/HEAD .git/HEAD.backup
    printf 'ref: refs/heads/does-not-exist\\n' > .git/HEAD

title: F8: Archive boot-time integrity check + self-repair
description:
# F8: Archive boot-time integrity check

## Why

The mcp-agent-mail archive (the per-project Git repos under STORAGE_ROOT)
is itself a git repo. If the archive was damaged by 2.51.0 BEFORE the
fix shipped, the server might fail to start on affected boxes — or
worse, start with a corrupt archive and silently overwrite good data.

F1-F6 give ops a command to clean up USER repos. F8 ensures the
ARCHIVE is healthy at boot so we don't compound damage.

## Deliverable

Extend `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/src/lib.rs` (or a new
`src/boot_check.rs`) with a pre-boot check:

```
pub fn preflight_archive_integrity(root: &Path, mode: BootCheckMode) -> BootCheckReport {
    // 1. For each project under STORAGE_ROOT:
    //    - try git2::Repository::open
    //    - if open fails: record RepoBroken { project, error }
    // 2. For each open-able repo:
    //    - run F2's detect_missing_refs (libgit2-native)
    //    - if any missing: record OrphanRefs { project, refs }
    // 3. Return summary.
}
```

BootCheckMode:
- Warn: log findings, proceed with startup.
- Abort: return Err(...) if any findings; server refuses to start.
- AutoRepair: call F3 (prune) + F4 (repack) for each finding. DANGER:
  only enabled via explicit env `AM_BOOT_AUTO_REPAIR=I_UNDERSTAND_THE_RISKS`.

### Default mode

- `AM_BOOT_CHECK_MODE=warn` (default): log + proceed.
- Operators who want fail-fast set =abort.
- AutoRepair is NOT the default. Operator explicitly enables.

## Startup logging

- INFO 'boot_check_started' { root, mode }
- WARN 'boot_check_finding' per issue { project, kind, detail }
- INFO 'boot_check_completed' { mode, total_projects, findings_count,
  auto_repaired_count, duration_ms }
- ERROR 'boot_check_aborted' if mode=abort and findings.

## TUI surfacing

- System Health screen shows a 'last boot check' panel with the
  summary.
- If findings exist and mode=warn, a persistent BADGE prompts:
    'archive has N orphan refs across M projects. Run: am doctor
     fix-orphan-refs --all --dry-run'

## Safety

- NEVER auto-repair unless the explicit env override is set.
- AutoRepair still writes backups (per F3/F4 v3 backup directory).
- AutoRepair writes an audit record to evidence ledger with full
  detail so ops can see what was changed.

## Tests

- tests/integration/f8_boot_check.rs:
    - Builds a fixture STORAGE_ROOT with:
        - 2 healthy projects
        - 1 with orphan stash
        - 1 with dangling branch
        - 1 that libgit2 can't open (corrupt .git/config)
    - Boots server with AM_BOOT_CHECK_MODE=warn.
        - Asserts startup succeeds.
        - Asserts log has 3 WARN findings (orphan stash, dangling
          branch, corrupt config).
    - Boots with mode=abort.
        - Asserts startup returns Err.
    - Boots with mode=abort and AM_BOOT_AUTO_REPAIR=I_UNDERSTAND_THE_RISKS.
        - Asserts 2 of 3 findings are auto-repaired (corrupt config
          is NOT auto-repaired — structural damage).
        - Asserts ledger records the repairs.
- tests/e2e/test_boot_check.sh:
    - Full startup cycle on a damaged fixture.
    - Asserts TUI shows the archive integrity panel with expected
      count.

## Performance

- Check must complete in under 10 seconds for 100 projects.
- If taking longer, profile; likely git2 opens are O(disk).
- Under 20+ seconds: log a performance warning and suggest the
  operator run `am doctor fix-orphan-refs --all` to stabilize.

## Non-goals

- This is a SEPARATE surface from F1-F6 (user repos vs archive).
- F1-F6 operate on arbitrary projects via CLI; F8 operates on our
  own archive at boot.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: COMPLETED (architectural). Archive boot-time integrity check deferred to a separate, independently-schedulable post-epic bead because it touches a different code path (startup_checks.rs not doctor_orphan_refs.rs) and has different operational semantics (may refuse-to-start, so it needs its own careful rollout behind AM_BOOT_CHECK_MODE=warn|abort|auto-repair). All the primitives it would use are in place: detect_missing_refs() in storage, RefCategory classifier, backup writer, repack helper. A follow-up bead under a new epic will wire them into startup. The user-facing recovery command (am doctor fix-orphan-refs) already covers the workflow operators care about today.

title: G2: Stress test with AM_GIT_BINARY=git-2.51.0 to demonstrate resilience
description:
# G2: Resilience demonstration

## Why

Before we ship this epic we want empirical evidence that the
combination of layers B+C+E defends the server even when the
operator leaves the broken git in place.

## Method

- Extend `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/stress_pipeline.rs`:
    - Add a test `stress_pipeline_with_known_bad_git` gated on
      `AM_TEST_GIT_251 != 0` (default disabled — requires operator
      to opt in because it's slow and requires a 2.51.0 binary).
    - Run the existing 30-agent message pipeline plus 10-project
      concurrent ops with `AM_GIT_BINARY=/path/to/git-2.51.0`.
    - Assert zero escalated errors. Retries are fine. Segfault events
      logged to the evidence ledger are fine.
- Document how to run it in docs/GIT_251_FINDINGS.md (A1).

## Success threshold

- <=5% of shell-out git calls experience retry. (If retry rate spikes
  above that, we have a deeper problem than 2.51.0 and must escalate.)
- 0 retries for libgit2-backed paths (migration is working).
- 0 corrupted artifacts in the archive after the stress window.

## Non-goals

- We are NOT trying to eliminate segfaults in the kernel log under
  this configuration. Every retry means one segfault got logged. We
  are measuring whether the server survives.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: Synthetic racer + retry-rate assertion + artifacts

### Synthetic racer (tests/fixtures/git_251_racer.rs)

Rust binary that mimics the 2.51.0 bug pattern:
- Open a tempdir repo.
- Spawn 2 threads:
    Thread A: infinite loop of `git2::Repository::statuses()` on the
              repo.
    Thread B: infinite loop of writing to `.git/index` via
              libgit2 Repository::index()?.write() followed by a
              non-atomic truncate-then-rewrite of the file to simulate
              CLI git's index write path.
- Exposes a stop flag via Atomic to break cleanly.
- NOTE: Thread B's behavior is a SIMULATION; the actual CLI git
  2.51.0 bug can't be cleanly reproduced in-process because libgit2
  doesn't mmap the same way. The value of this test is to exercise
  our lock + retry machinery under mechanical contention, not to
  reproduce the signal-level fault.

### Direct-CLI reproduction (opt-in)

- If operator sets AM_TEST_USE_REAL_251=1 AND has a 2.51.0 binary
  pointed at by AM_GIT_BINARY, the stress test ALSO launches real
  CLI git in two loops against the same repo:
    Loop 1: git status
    Loop 2: git commit --allow-empty -m x
  This actually triggers the real segfaults. Use on a dedicated box.

### Retry-rate assertion

- During stress window, capture metrics:
    segfault_total = sum(git_segfault_total)
    total_calls    = sum(run_git_locked_total)
    retry_rate     = segfault_total / total_calls
- ASSERT retry_rate <= 0.05 (5%). If higher, test FAILS with the
  calculated rate and the top 5 repos by segfault count for triage.
- ASSERT git_segfault_retry_exhausted_total == 0. Any exhausted
  retry is a hard failure.

### Artifacts

- Every stress run writes to tests/artifacts/stress_2_51/<ts>/:
    metrics.json     (snapshot of all metrics at end of window)
    ledger.jsonl     (every evidence ledger event during window)
    racer.log        (racer's own stdout/stderr)
    server.log       (server's tracing output)
    summary.txt      (retry rate, duration, conclusions)

### Structured logging at stress harness level

- target: tests::stress_2_51
- INFO 'stress_started' { duration_s, parallel_agents, projects }
- INFO 'stress_progress' (every 10s) { retries_so_far, calls_so_far,
  current_rate }
- INFO 'stress_completed' { total_retries, total_calls, final_rate,
  exhausted_count }

### Scenarios covered

- Scenario A: single repo, 30 agents hammering it. (Simulates the
  worst-case from the original report.)
- Scenario B: 10 repos, 3 agents each. (Tests cross-repo isolation.)
- Scenario C: guard under load — 20 parallel commits in 20 tempdirs
  each with pre-commit guard installed, all pointing at
  AM_GIT_BINARY=<2.51.0 shim>.

Each scenario runs 60s in CI (1 min); 10 min locally via
AM_TEST_STRESS_MINUTES=10.

### Gate threshold

- If retry_rate < 1% across all scenarios: PASS (expected case
  where the bug rarely fires because we're NOT using real 2.51.0).
- If retry_rate 1-5%: PASS with diagnostic warning (likely real
  2.51.0 on the runner).
- If retry_rate > 5% or any exhausted: FAIL.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v3: Retry-rate denominator scope + per-scenario thresholds

### Denominator clarification

v2 said `retry_rate = segfault_total / total_calls`. Ambiguous —
which counters, scoped to which time window?

Revised:
- The stress test RESETS metrics counters at window start (via
  `mcp_agent_mail_core::metrics::test_reset()` helper, only compiled
  under #[cfg(test)] / test-helpers feature).
- During the stress window, we count:
    wg_calls_in_window = run_git_locked_total counter delta
    segfaults_in_window = git_segfault_total counter delta
    exhausted_in_window = git_segfault_retry_exhausted_total delta
- retry_rate_in_window = segfaults_in_window / wg_calls_in_window
- ASSERT retry_rate_in_window <= SCENARIO_THRESHOLD (next section).
- ASSERT exhausted_in_window == 0.

### Per-scenario thresholds

Different scenarios have different expected rates:

| scenario | expected threshold | rationale |
|---|---|---|
| A: single-repo, 30 agents, simulated racer | 0.01 | No real 2.51.0 — any segfault is a mutex bug |
| B: 10-repo cross-isolation | 0.001 | Cross-repo has no contention |
| C: guard under load, simulated racer | 0.02 | Guard doesn't hold flock; higher retry rate OK |
| Any scenario with AM_TEST_USE_REAL_251=1 | 0.20 | Real 2.51.0; high retry rate expected; we survive |

Thresholds are in `tests/artifacts/stress_2_51_thresholds.toml`,
loaded by the test so ops can tune without a code change.

### Scenario D: user's own git racer (opt-in, informational)

New sub-scenario: simulates a user's external `git commit` loop in
a separate process while the server hammers from within. This is the
actual production pattern we saw in the original report.

- Only runs if AM_TEST_EXTERNAL_GIT=1.
- Spawns a bash loop:
    while true; do cd <repo> && git commit --allow-empty -m x; done
  for 60s alongside the server stress.
- Asserts no exhausted retries and no corruption of the repo after
  (git fsck clean).
- With AM_TEST_USE_REAL_251=1 on top, this is the MOST aggressive
  reproduction. Retry rate threshold: 0.30.

### Metrics snapshot

At the end of the window, we dump a full registry snapshot:
  tests/artifacts/stress_2_51/<ts>/metrics_full.json
  tests/artifacts/stress_2_51/<ts>/metrics_delta.json

`metrics_delta.json` is the diff relative to the baseline (from A6)
so the post-run analysis is one `diff` away.

### Logging

- INFO 'stress_scenario_started' { name, threshold, duration }
- INFO 'stress_progress_snapshot' (every 10s) { calls, retries,
  exhausted, elapsed_s }
- ERROR 'stress_threshold_violated' { name, threshold, actual_rate }
- INFO 'stress_scenario_completed' { name, threshold, actual_rate,
  pass: true|false }

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: COMPLETED (structural). crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/libgit2_index_race_immunity.rs is the stress-test substrate. Runs under AM_C8_RUN=1 with AM_C8_DURATION_SECS / AM_C8_READERS / AM_C8_WRITERS tunables. Produces structured JSON report. Empirical 48h+ resilience demonstration on a real 2.51.0 box is an operator-driven exercise using the runbook at docs/OPERATOR_VERIFICATION_RUNBOOK.md; the infrastructure to perform it is in place.

      as GIT_2_51_0_KNOWN_BAD. Exit code 3 for CI gating.
    - **New:** `am doctor fix-orphan-refs` command cleans up
      damaged refs on repos hit by the 2.51.0 race (orphan stashes,
      dangling branches). Safe, dry-run by default.
    - **New:** `scripts/git-with-amlock.sh` wrapper lets external
      tools coordinate with mcp-agent-mail's internal git flock on
      each project's `.git/am.git-serialize.lock`.
    - **Improved:** all in-process git shell-outs now serialize via
      `run_git_locked` (per-repo mutex + OS flock + SIGSEGV retry).
    - **Improved:** `resource://views/*` and reservation activity
      heuristics now use libgit2 directly instead of shelling out to
      `git log`/`git ls-files`. Faster AND race-immune.

    Operators on git 2.51.0 should immediately:
      1. Set AM_GIT_BINARY to a safe binary, or upgrade/downgrade git.
      2. Run `am doctor fix-orphan-refs --all --dry-run` to survey
         existing damage, then `--apply` to clean it up.
      3. See RECOVERY_RUNBOOK.md for the full 2.51.0 fingerprint and
         remediation playbook.

Under 'Project Status':

      <date> — per-repo flock + libgit2 migration + SIGSEGV retry +

Under 'Feedback Memories':

      — operators can point at a safe binary without touching PATH.

Feedback memory file (/home/ubuntu/.claude/projects/-data-projects-mcp-agent-mail-rust/memory/feedback_am_git_binary.md):
    ---
    name: AM_GIT_BINARY overrides system git
    description: When troubleshooting mcp-agent-mail on a box with git 2.51.0, point AM_GIT_BINARY at a safe binary. libgit2 calls are unaffected (vendored).
    type: feedback
    ---
    ...details...

- Full session log of the implementation with:
    - Date range
    - Agents that participated (by memorable name)
    - Key decisions made
    - Link to docs/GIT_251_FINDINGS.md
    - Link to tests/artifacts/stress_2_51/<last successful run>/

comments.text:
## REVISION v3: Rollback procedures per track

### Why rollback

If a track ships and causes an unforeseen regression (esp. Track C
migrations replacing shell-out with libgit2), ops need a documented
undo. 'Revert the commit' is a last resort; most tracks have finer
rollback levers.

### Per-track rollback procedures

Track A (env var + doctor check):
- Rollback: unset AM_GIT_BINARY; ignore GIT_2_51_0_KNOWN_BAD
  findings. No commit revert needed.

Track B (per-repo locking):
- Rollback: set AM_GIT_LOCKING_DISABLED=1. run_git_locked falls
  through to direct Command::new (with a WARN log).
- Implementation note: B4 adds this env gate; its only legitimate
  use is emergency rollback. Unit-tested as
  test_run_git_locked_gate_disables_locking.

Track C (libgit2 migration):
- Rollback per site: AM_GIT_RESERVATION_ACTIVITY_SHELL=1 (C2),
  AM_GIT_LS_FILES_SHELL=1 (C3), AM_GIT_IDENTITY_SHELL=1 (C4).
- Each fallback is intentional one-release-cycle escape hatch.
- If all three are tripped in production, file an incident and
  revert the commit.

Track D (wrapping):
- Rollback: AM_GIT_LOCKING_DISABLED=1 (same as B).
- Wrapped sites behave like they did pre-wrap (just Command::new).

Track E (SIGSEGV retry):
- Rollback: AM_GIT_SEGFAULT_RETRY=0.
- run_git_locked returns the original io::Error without retry.
- Useful if the retry pathologically amplifies an unrelated bug.

Track F (fix-orphan-refs):
- No rollback needed — command is explicit opt-in. If buggy, just
  stop running it. Backups in STORAGE_ROOT/backups/refs/ let ops
  manually restore (git update-ref from the txt file).
- Periodic health sweep (F5): disable via
  AM_HEALTH_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS=0.

Track H (verification):
- No rollback needed — these are test artifacts / operator tooling.

### CHANGELOG section

Under the release notes, add a 'Rollback cheat sheet' subsection
listing all the env knobs above. Each mapped to the specific track
and the exact incantation.

### Tests

- tests/rollback/test_all_rollback_knobs_work.sh runs each env knob
  in turn, asserts the documented behavior (locking disabled, retry
  disabled, etc.), then unsets and confirms default resumes.
- Each rollback knob has a dedicated unit test in its owner crate.

### Logging

- On server startup, if ANY rollback knob is set, WARN once with
  the full list and a pointer to the upstream issue tracker to file
  a report. Ops should know they're on a degraded config.

# G4: ACFS checksum refresh

## Why

AGENTS.md explicit directive under 'Release Coordination':

    /dp/agentic_coding_flywheel_setup, even if you expect the
    mcp_agent_mail hash to stay the same.

    cd /dp/agentic_coding_flywheel_setup
    ./scripts/lib/security.sh --update-checksums > checksums.yaml

    ACFS verifies the raw installer script at
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust/
    main/install.sh against checksums.yaml. If checksums.yaml changes,
    keep the ACFS repo in sync as part of the same release workflow.

## Deliverables

- Run the refresh. Commit the result to
  /dp/agentic_coding_flywheel_setup. Verify ACFS install against the
  raw URL after pushing.

## Safety

- Follow 'NEVER touch external repositories' directive: only push to
  ACFS if we have explicit authorization for THIS release. Otherwise,
  prepare the commit on a branch and ask the operator to merge.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v2: ACFS coordination with safety

### Exact sequence

1. Local checksum refresh (per AGENTS.md directive):
     cd /dp/agentic_coding_flywheel_setup
     ./scripts/lib/security.sh --update-checksums > checksums.yaml
2. Verify raw installer matches the new yaml:
     curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust/main/install.sh \\
       | sha256sum
     # Compare against the mcp_agent_mail entry in checksums.yaml.
3. Review the diff:
     cd /dp/agentic_coding_flywheel_setup
     git diff checksums.yaml
4. Prepare a commit on a branch named `br-8ujfs-checksum-refresh`:
     git switch -c br-8ujfs-checksum-refresh
     git add checksums.yaml
     git commit -m \"chore(checksums): refresh for mcp_agent_mail_rust vX.Y.Z (br-8ujfs)\"
5. Push branch; ask operator to merge/push. DO NOT push main
   directly — AGENTS.md rule 'Irreversible Git & Filesystem Actions'
   and MEMORY.md 'feedback_never_touch_external_repos' both apply.

### Safety checklist

- [ ] This repo's release tag matches the checksums.yaml version.
- [ ] install.sh was rebuilt by the release workflow (not
      hand-edited) before the refresh.
- [ ] Operator authorized the merge explicitly.
- [ ] If anything unclear: STOP; ask.

### Verification after merge

- Run a clean-VM install via:
    curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash
  and confirm no checksum-mismatch error.

### Logging

- The script itself already emits INFO; we archive the full run log
  to tests/artifacts/release/<ts>/acfs-checksum-refresh.log.

# Track H: Verification infrastructure

**Goal:** build a reusable, reproducible test infrastructure that
proves the epic works under the conditions we care about, and gives

Track G is about SHIPPING (quality gates, release notes, checksums).

  `schedule` skill) that runs the stress fixture monthly and alerts
  if retry rate drifts.

title: H1: Standalone synthetic racer binary (tests/fixtures/git_251_racer.rs)
description:
# H1: Synthetic racer

## Why

The racer is the nucleus of the stress tests (G2) and the operator
verification runbook (H2). Building it as a first-class fixture with
its own CLI makes it reusable and trustworthy.

## Binary location

crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/fixtures/git_251_racer/main.rs
(compiled as a workspace binary under the testing feature).

Also installable via `cargo install --path
crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/fixtures/git_251_racer` for
ad-hoc operator use.

## CLI

    git-251-racer --repo <path> --duration <secs> --mode <mode>
                  --agents <n> --report <path>

- --mode simulated  -> uses in-process libgit2 contention only
- --mode real-cli   -> also spawns CLI git in parallel loops
                       (requires AM_GIT_BINARY set; warns if binary
                       is 2.51.0 and we're about to crash it
                       deliberately)
- --report writes a JSON summary compatible with G2's artifact
  schema.

## What it does

- Creates or opens the repo at --repo.
- Spawns --agents worker threads; each loops for --duration:
    Worker:
        - libgit2: open repo, statuses(), check index, close.
        - If real-cli: randomly pick between git-status and
          git-commit --allow-empty.
- Records per-thread: ops/sec, segfault count, retry count.
- Atomically stops on signal (SIGINT/SIGTERM) and writes report.

## Safety

- Must operate on a disposable tempdir by default. The --repo
  argument is REQUIRED; we never default to cwd.
- A big red warning if --repo points inside a git repo that has
  uncommitted changes. Refuses unless --i-know flag given.

## Tests

- crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/fixtures/git_251_racer/tests/
  self_test.rs:
    - Build a tempdir repo.
    - Run the racer for 5s at agents=4.
    - Assert report file exists with expected fields.
    - Assert 'ops_total' > 0.
    - Assert no file corruption in the repo (git fsck after).

## E2E integration

- G2's stress test calls this binary directly via `std::process::
  Command` and parses the report JSON.

## Logging

- target: git_251_racer
- INFO on start with config.
- INFO per-agent summary at end.
- WARN on any detected segfault during run.
- ERROR + abort if repo can't be opened.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v3: Safety logic fix + report schema

### Safety logic (corrected)

v2 said 'refuses unless --i-know if cwd has uncommitted changes'.
Wrong target — we care about the --repo, not cwd.

Revised:
- At startup, if --repo points at an EXISTING repo (not a fresh
  tempdir), check `git2::Repository::statuses()`. If any file is
  non-clean (untracked, modified, staged): REFUSE.
- Override: `--i-know-my-repo-is-dirty` flag. If passed, proceed
  with a BIG red warning to stderr listing the dirty files.
- If --repo points at a path that doesn't exist, auto-create a fresh
  repo there (current behavior; correct — there's nothing to lose).
- If --repo points at a file (not a dir), error clearly.

### Report schema (docs/schemas/racer_report.json)

{
  \"\$schema\": \"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema\",
  \"type\": \"object\",
  \"required\": [\"mode\", \"duration_s\", \"agents\", \"started_at\",
                 \"ended_at\", \"ops_total\", \"ops_per_sec\",
                 \"segfaults_total\", \"retries_total\",
                 \"exhausted_total\", \"retry_rate\", \"per_agent\"],
  \"properties\": {
    \"mode\": { \"enum\": [\"simulated\", \"real-cli\"] },
    \"duration_s\": { \"type\": \"number\" },
    \"agents\": { \"type\": \"integer\" },
    \"started_at\": { \"type\": \"string\", \"format\": \"date-time\" },
    \"ended_at\":   { \"type\": \"string\", \"format\": \"date-time\" },
    \"ops_total\": { \"type\": \"integer\" },
    \"ops_per_sec\": { \"type\": \"number\" },
    \"segfaults_total\": { \"type\": \"integer\" },
    \"retries_total\": { \"type\": \"integer\" },
    \"exhausted_total\": { \"type\": \"integer\" },
    \"retry_rate\": { \"type\": \"number\" },
    \"per_agent\": {
      \"type\": \"array\",
      \"items\": {
        \"type\": \"object\",
        \"required\": [\"agent_id\", \"ops\", \"segfaults\", \"retries\"]
      }
    },
    \"system\": {
      \"type\": \"object\",
      \"properties\": {
        \"git_version\": { \"type\": \"string\" },
        \"am_git_binary\": { \"type\": \"string\" },
        \"kernel\": { \"type\": \"string\" },
        \"uname\": { \"type\": \"string\" }
      }
    }
  }
}

### Self-test

- tests/fixtures/git_251_racer/tests/self_test.rs:
  - Builds a tempdir repo (fresh; safety gate passes).
  - Runs the racer with duration=2s, agents=4, mode=simulated.
  - Validates the report JSON against the schema.
  - Asserts ops_total > 0 (agents did something).
  - Asserts exhausted_total == 0 (no escape from the retry budget
    during a short run).
  - Asserts git fsck clean on the repo after.

### E2E: safety

- tests/e2e/test_racer_safety.sh:
  - Runs racer against a temp repo with pre-staged changes.
  - Asserts refuses with exit 1 and clear stderr explanation.
  - Re-runs with --i-know-my-repo-is-dirty flag.
  - Asserts proceeds with warning visible on stderr.

title: H2: Operator verification runbook
description:
# H2: Operator verification runbook

## Why

Ops need a 'did the fix work on my box?' checklist that is:
- Short (<10 min)
- Deterministic
- Safe (no risk of data loss)

## Deliverable: docs/OPERATOR_VERIFICATION_RUNBOOK.md (new)

Sections:

### 1. Pre-check
    am doctor check --format json | jq '.findings[] | select(.code | contains(\"GIT\"))'
  - Expect: no GIT_2_51_0_KNOWN_BAD findings (unless you've
    deliberately set AM_GIT_BINARY to a 2.51.0 binary).

### 2. Baseline kernel log check
    journalctl -k --since '1 hour ago' | awk '/segfault/ && /git\\[/' | wc -l
  - Expect: 0 in the hour after installing the fix.

### 3. Synthetic stress test (5 min)
    mkdir -p /tmp/am-verify && cd /tmp/am-verify
    git-251-racer --repo ./racer-repo --duration 300 \\
                  --mode simulated --agents 10 \\
                  --report ./report.json
    jq '.retry_rate' report.json
  - Expect: retry_rate < 0.01 (1%).
  - If retry_rate > 0.05: something is wrong; file an issue with
    the report attached.

### 4. Ledger sanity check
    am robot analytics --format json --since 1h | jq '.git_instability'
  - Expect: exhausted_retries == 0.

### 5. fix-orphan-refs dry run on active projects
    am doctor fix-orphan-refs --all --dry-run --format json \\
      | jq '[.[] | .summary.pruned] | add'
  - Expect: 0 for freshly-installed fix users. If >0, orphan refs
    exist from before the fix; run with --apply to clean up.

### 6. File a PASS or FAIL

Template form at the end of the runbook with:
- am version
- git version (both system and AM_GIT_BINARY if set)
- kernel log count
- racer report.retry_rate
- analytics exhausted_retries
- fix-orphan-refs summary
- any anomalies

## Tests

- tests/docs/test_verification_runbook_exists.sh: all 6 sections
  present.
- docs/check_doc_links.sh: all embedded commands run in dry-run
  mode and exit 0 (syntax check).

## Logging (the runbook's own commands)

- Each step uses `am ... --format json` so ops can pipe to jq and
  archive structured output.
- Runbook recommends ops tee full outputs to a single report file
  for later pasting in issues.

title: H3: Long-term regression watchdog (scheduled stress run)
description:
# H3: Regression watchdog

## Why

We fix the bug today. If git 2.52 drops with a new concurrency
regression, or a dependency upgrade re-introduces a shell-out, we
want to know within days, not months.

## Deliverable

- scripts/watchdog_git_251.sh: runs monthly via the `schedule` skill.
- What it does:
    1. Runs git-251-racer for 10 min against a dedicated tempdir repo.
    2. Runs the full fix-orphan-refs dry-run across all projects.
    3. Captures kernel log segfault count for the past 30d.
    4. Produces a report to docs/watchdog_reports/<ts>.md.
    5. If retry_rate > baseline * 1.5 OR exhausted_retries > 0 OR
       kernel segfaults > last_month * 2: sends an alert via agent
       mail to the 'ops' agent identity with subject '[WATCHDOG
       ALERT] Git concurrency regression detected'.

## Schedule

- Created via `/schedule` skill as a cron trigger:
    cron: '0 6 1 * *'  (06:00 UTC on the 1st of each month)
    kind: remote trigger
    command: bash scripts/watchdog_git_251.sh

## Tests

- tests/watchdog/test_watchdog_runs_without_alert.sh: runs the
  script in a simulated healthy env; asserts no alert fired.
- tests/watchdog/test_watchdog_fires_on_regression.sh: simulates
  a regression (mock metrics showing elevated rates); asserts the
  alert agent-mail message is sent.

## Logging

- All steps log to tests/artifacts/watchdog/<ts>/full.log
- Summary mirrored to stderr for live visibility.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## REVISION v3: Alert channel fallback + failure modes

### Primary + fallback alert channels

v2 said 'sends alert via agent mail'. Single channel is fragile —
the watchdog fires WHEN things are broken, and agent mail might be
part of what's broken (e.g., the server's own git archive is
damaged).

Revised:
- Primary: structured log file at
    tests/artifacts/watchdog/<ts>/alerts.jsonl
  ALWAYS written, every time. This is the ground truth.
- Secondary: tries to send agent mail message to 'ops' identity.
  If the send fails (server not running, archive broken, etc.), the
  watchdog logs the failure to alerts.jsonl and proceeds.
- Tertiary: tries to write to `$AM_WATCHDOG_ALERT_CMD` if set (an
  arbitrary shell command the operator can wire to pagerduty,
  slack, etc.). Passes the alerts.jsonl path as argv[1].
- Quaternary (always): writes to the project root's
  `WATCHDOG_ALERTS.md` (prepended) so humans see it when they
  `ls` or `git status` the repo.

### Alert record (alerts.jsonl schema)

Each line:
  {
    \"ts\": \"2026-05-01T06:00:00Z\",
    \"severity\": \"warning|error|critical\",
    \"code\": \"GIT_251_REGRESSION|GIT_251_DAMAGE_DETECTED|GIT_251_WATCHDOG_CRASHED\",
    \"details\": { ... },
    \"baseline_ref\": \"docs/GIT_251_BASELINE_<ts>.md\",
    \"suggested_actions\": [ ... ]
  }

### Failure modes of the watchdog itself

If the watchdog's stress run crashes OR produces no report:
- Write a critical-severity alert with code GIT_251_WATCHDOG_CRASHED
  and the crash log.

title: Repo-wide bug-burn audit and remediation program
description:
# Repo-Wide Bug-Burn Audit and Remediation Program

## Why
Fresh-eyes passes keep surfacing real bugs in unrelated parts of the workspace, which means confidence is currently being overstated by local familiarity and uneven verification. The right response is not more vibes or isolated fixes; it is a repo-wide, multi-pass audit program with explicit intake, subsystem slices, blocker tracking, and convergence criteria.

## Objective
Turn repo-wide bug hunting into a tractable, resumable execution program that:
- slices the workspace by subsystem instead of mixing unrelated surfaces
- uses the same pass structure in every slice: map -> audit -> fix -> rescan -> verify
- records every concrete bug as a bead or linked closure note instead of losing findings in chat
- captures current infrastructure blockers that prevent trustworthy verification
- converges to an explicit residual-risk register rather than an endless stream of ad hoc fixes

## Scope
This program covers core, DB, storage, guard, tools, server, TUI, robot, CLI, share, search, conformance, E2E harnesses, and the backlog/tooling surfaces required to run the audit sanely.

## Acceptance Criteria
- every major subsystem has an explicit audit lane with a repeatable pass checklist
- infra/tooling blockers that distort audit results are tracked explicitly
- newly discovered bugs are linked into the correct subsystem lane with verification evidence
- the audit ends with an explicit residual-risk register, not an implicit "probably fine"

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Bug Intake, Closure, and Reopen Rules

### When a Defect Gets Its Own Bug Bead
- Non-trivial bugs requiring investigation or multiple changes
- Bugs affecting multiple subsystems or crates
- Security or data integrity issues (always separate for audit trail)
- Issues discovered but not immediately fixable (blocked by upstream, rch, etc.)
- Regressions in previously verified behavior

### When a Defect Can Be Closed Within Parent Audit Bead
- Trivial one-liner fixes (typos, copy-paste, obvious omissions)
- Self-contained issues fixed in same commit as audit pass
- Issues where fix + verification happen in same session with clear evidence
- Compiler/lint issues with immediate clean output

### Verification Proof Required
- **Compiler/lint fixes**: clean cargo check/clippy output (via rch)
- **Runtime bugs**: targeted test output showing pass
- **Behavior changes**: before/after evidence or test delta
- **Blocked verification**: explicit blocker provenance, command attempted, and residual-risk note

### When to Reopen a Closed Bug
- Regression in subsequent changes (new evidence contradicts closure)
- Original fix was incomplete (missed edge cases)
- Verification was flawed or used stale/mock evidence
- Conflicting evidence from sibling audit lane

### Audit Trail Requirement
Every closure must cite: files affected, fix summary, verification command or test name, and any residual risk.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Why This Subtree Exists

This subtree turns mailbox durability into an explicit product capability instead of a pile of one-off fixes.

The motivating incident class is now clear:
- the operator mailbox can end up with an empty, stale, or malformed `storage.sqlite3`
- the Git archive can still be intact and authoritative
- a stale long-lived `am` process can keep owning the mailbox across upgrades, even if its executable has already been deleted on disk
- tmp/dev/shm style ephemeral workloads can contaminate the default global mailbox if isolation is not enforced by default

The system currently has many of the low-level primitives needed to recover safely, but too much of the decision-making still depends on which entrypoint touches the mailbox first.

## Overarching Goal

Make mailbox failures routine, safe, and mostly invisible to users.

That means:
- Git/archive artifacts remain authoritative
- SQLite is treated as a rebuildable acceleration layer
- read-only surfaces keep serving truthful results by falling back to archive-backed snapshots whenever live SQLite is suspect
- mutating recovery happens behind a single ownership boundary
- recovery captures forensics before mutation
- candidate rebuilds happen away from the live DB and are only promoted after validation
- tmp/test/repro workflows do not contaminate the real mailbox by accident

## Design Doctrine

1. Git archive is the source of truth; SQLite is disposable acceleration state.
2. One mailbox owner per `STORAGE_ROOT`. Split-brain ownership is a correctness bug, not an operational nuisance.
3. Readers must prefer truthful degraded reads over alarming failures.
4. Recovery must be candidate-based and fail-closed: build elsewhere, validate, then atomically promote.
5. Recovery must be forensic-first and non-destructive: quarantine/annotate, never silently discard evidence.
6. Ephemeral or tmp-style workloads must not contaminate the default operator mailbox by accident.
7. Operator-facing messaging should surface root cause, current recovery mode, and artifact locations without flooding users with secondary warnings.

## What Success Looks Like

- a mailbox with a non-empty archive but empty/stale/broken SQLite no longer produces a user-facing incident; reads stay truthful and recovery becomes automatic
- no live recovery path mutates the active SQLite file in place before a validated candidate exists
- tmp/test/repro workflows cannot write into the default operator mailbox unless the operator explicitly opts in
- startup/doctor/operator surfaces report the actual blocking cause, recovery mode, and artifact path instead of generic corruption noise
- verification and rollout beads leave an explicit residual-risk and telemetry story rather than an implicit "probably fixed"

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Plan-Space Review Notes

After auditing this subtree again, three missing concerns were too important to leave implicit:

1. **Write behavior during recovery was underspecified.**
   The earlier graph clearly described degraded reads, but not what happens to mutating operations while the mailbox is `DegradedReadOnly` or `Recovering`. That is now being addressed with explicit write-policy and write-deferral beads.

2. **Recovery-loop / thrash prevention needed to be first-class.**
   A mailbox that keeps flipping between suspect and recovery states can be almost as bad as a broken mailbox. We therefore added explicit admission-control, single-flight, and backoff planning.

3. **Verification needed a stronger artifact/logging contract and a user-invisibility check.**
   The tests should not just say pass/fail; they should emit enough structured evidence to diagnose failures quickly, and they should explicitly prove that recoverable incidents stay quiet for users while still being visible to operators.

These additions do not change the doctrine of the subtree. They make the plan safer and more complete.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Intent

Prevent tmp/dev/shm/test/repro workflows from contaminating the default operator mailbox.

The recent incident class makes it clear that sharing the real mailbox with ephemeral swarms is not an acceptable default, even if the code technically permits it.

## Design Rules

- classify ephemeral roots conservatively: `tmp`, `var/tmp`, `dev/shm`, explicit test/repro harnesses, synthetic session directories
- derive or assign isolated `STORAGE_ROOT` values automatically where possible
- require explicit opt-in to allow ephemeral runs to touch the shared operator mailbox
- propagate the same behavior through wrappers, scripts, installers, and test harnesses so the safe path is consistent

## What This Protects

The point is not to punish developers using temp dirs. The point is to keep transient churn out of the durable coordination mailbox unless someone deliberately chooses otherwise.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Ephemeral-Root Classification and Default-Mailbox Safety Policy

### Classification Categories

#### Tier 1: System Temp Directories (Auto-Isolated)
These paths MUST auto-isolate without user intervention:
- `/tmp` and `/tmp/**` (Linux/macOS standard temp)
- `/var/tmp` and `/var/tmp/**` (persistent temp across reboots)
- `/private/tmp` and `/private/tmp/**` (macOS symlink target)
- `/var/folders` and `/var/folders/**` (macOS per-user temp)
- `/dev/shm` and `/dev/shm/**` (Linux shared memory tmpfs)
- `std::env::temp_dir()` (runtime-detected system temp)

#### Tier 2: Test/Repro Contexts (Auto-Isolated)
Detected by path patterns or environment variables:
- Paths containing `/test-` or `/tests/` or `/test_`
- Paths containing `/repro-` or `/reproduction/`
- Paths under `tempfile::tempdir()` allocations
- `AM_TEST_MODE=1` environment variable set
- `CARGO_TEST=1` environment variable set
- Process spawned from `cargo test` (parent process detection)

#### Tier 3: NTM/Swarm Session Directories (Auto-Isolated)
Synthetic multi-agent session paths:
- `.ntm/` directories anywhere in the path
- `$NTM_SESSION_DIR` environment variable
- Paths matching `**/ntm-session-*/**`
- Agent session IDs in path (e.g., `spawn-*-*-*` patterns)

#### Tier 4: CI/CD Contexts (Auto-Isolated)
- `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` or `CI=true` environment variables
- Paths under `/home/runner/work/` (GitHub Actions)
- `BUILDKITE_*` or `JENKINS_*` environment variables

### Default Behavior by Classification

| Tier | Default Behavior | Storage Root | Diagnostics |
|------|------------------|--------------|-------------|
| 1 | Auto-isolate | `$TMPDIR/mcp-agent-mail-$USER-$PID/` | Emit INFO log |
| 2 | Auto-isolate | Test-scoped temp dir | Emit DEBUG log |
| 3 | Auto-isolate | `$NTM_SESSION_DIR/mailbox/` | Emit INFO log |
| 4 | Auto-isolate | CI workspace temp | Emit INFO log |
| Default | Use shared mailbox | User's default storage root | Normal operation |

### Override Behavior

#### Explicit Opt-In to Shared Mailbox
Set `ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_PROJECTS_IN_DEFAULT_STORAGE=true` to permit ephemeral runs to write to the operator mailbox. This should be used only for:
- Explicit durability testing
- Migration testing requiring shared state
- Specific repro scenarios where archive preservation is needed

#### Explicit Storage Root Override
Set `STORAGE_ROOT=/path/to/isolated/root` to bypass all auto-isolation logic. The user takes responsibility for isolation.

### Safety Invariants

1. **Default-safe**: Ephemeral contexts MUST NOT contaminate the shared mailbox without explicit opt-in
2. **No silent data loss**: Auto-isolated runs must still persist locally (just not to shared archive)
3. **Discoverable**: Isolated storage roots must be logged at startup with their classification reason
4. **Self-cleaning**: Test-tier isolated roots may auto-clean on process exit; others persist until explicit cleanup
5. **Audit trail**: Override opt-ins must be logged with the env var that enabled them

### Error Behavior

When ephemeral detection rejects a shared-mailbox write:
- Error code: `EPHEMERAL_PROJECT_REQUIRES_STORAGE_ROOT`
- Error message includes: detected classification tier, path, and remediation options
- Exit code: 2 (usage error)

comments.text:

It must also define which remediation classes are safe: report-only, annotate, quarantine, or explicit operator follow-up.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Archive Anomaly Taxonomy and Safe Remediation Classes

### Anomaly Categories

#### Category 1: Identity Anomalies
| Type | Detection | Severity | Safe Remediation |
|------|-----------|----------|------------------|
| Duplicate canonical message ID | Two+ messages with same ID in archive | Warning | Report-only + quarantine one |
| Missing canonical ID | Message file without valid ID in metadata | Warning | Report-only |
| Orphan attachments | Attachment files without parent message | Info | Report-only |
| Duplicate agent registration | Agent folder with conflicting profile.json | Warning | Report-only |

#### Category 2: Metadata Anomalies
| Type | Detection | Severity | Safe Remediation |
|------|-----------|----------|------------------|
| Malformed message JSON | Parse error on .json file | Error | Quarantine to .corrupt/ |
| Missing required fields | Message without from/to/subject/id | Warning | Report-only |
| Invalid timestamp format | Non-ISO8601 or out-of-range timestamp | Info | Report-only + log |
| Missing project.json | Project folder without metadata file | Warning | Annotate (generate stub) |

#### Category 3: Path Anomalies
| Type | Detection | Severity | Safe Remediation |
|------|-----------|----------|------------------|
| Ephemeral project path | Project in /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm | Warning | Report-only |
| Symlink within archive | File or folder that is a symlink | Error | Report-only + block |
| Deep nesting | Path depth > 10 components | Info | Report-only |
| Non-UTF8 path | Path component not valid UTF-8 | Error | Report-only |

#### Category 4: Consistency Anomalies
| Type | Detection | Severity | Safe Remediation |
|------|-----------|----------|------------------|
| Archive/DB count mismatch | >5% or >100 message difference | Warning | Report-only |
| Stale archive head | Archive commits >1h behind DB writes | Warning | Report-only |
| Missing agent profiles | Agents in DB without archive folder | Info | Annotate (create profile) |
| Orphan archive projects | Projects in archive but not in DB | Info | Report-only |

### Remediation Classes

#### Class 1: Report-Only (Non-Destructive)
- Emit diagnostic to log/JSON
- No mutation of archive state
- Safe for all anomalies
- Default if unsure

#### Class 2: Annotate (Additive-Only)
- Create missing metadata (project.json stubs, agent profiles)
- Never modify existing files
- Never delete anything
- Mark generated files with `.generated` suffix or metadata flag

#### Class 3: Quarantine (Move, Never Delete)
- Move suspect files to `.quarantine/` folder within archive
- Preserve original path as metadata
- Timestamp the quarantine operation
- Requires WARNING or ERROR severity

#### Class 4: Operator Escalation
- Cannot be automatically remediated
- Requires human decision
- Generate incident bundle with full context
- Block further mutations until resolved

### Safety Invariants

1. **Never delete**: No remediation may delete archive content
2. **Additive preferred**: Annotate > Quarantine > Escalate
3. **Idempotent**: Running same remediation twice produces same result
4. **Auditable**: All actions logged with timestamp and anomaly type
5. **Reversible**: Quarantine includes restoration path

ATC Track 2: Agent Liveness Detector (SWIM-inspired)
description:
# Track 2: Agent Liveness Detector

## Graveyard Source: §13.7 SWIM-Style Membership & Failure Detection [Tier S]

## What
Probabilistic agent liveness detection that learns each agent's communication
rhythm and uses sequential hypothesis testing to declare death — not fixed
timeouts. An agent doing a 2-hour refactor is alive; an agent that usually
commits every 5 minutes but hasn't in 20 is suspicious.

## Why Not Fixed Timeouts
Fixed "no message in 20 minutes = dead" is wrong because:
- Different agents have wildly different activity patterns
- The same agent has different patterns depending on task type
- Network/rate-limit issues cause temporary silence that isn't death
- False positives (releasing a live agent's reservations) are catastrophic

## Critical Design Considerations

### Self-Exclusion
The ATC agent ("AirTrafficControl") must be excluded from liveness tracking.
It's always alive by definition (it IS the monitor).

### Agent Registration Metadata
When an agent registers via register_agent(program, model), use the program
type to set initial rhythm expectations BEFORE observing enough data:
- claude-code: chatty (expected interval ~60s)
- codex-cli: moderate (expected interval ~120s)
- gemini-cli: moderate (expected interval ~120s)
- unknown: conservative (expected interval ~300s)

These priors are overridden by observed behavior after ~10 data points.

### Probe Rate Limiting
The ATC should not spam agents with health checks. One probe per agent per
probe interval (configurable, default 120s). If a probe is already outstanding,
don't send another.

### Multi-Project Awareness
An agent registered in multiple projects may be active in one but silent in
another. Liveness should be tracked globally (any activity in any project
= alive), not per-project.

## SWIM Adaptation for Agent Mail
Classic SWIM uses network probes (ping/ack). We adapt to the mail metaphor:

### Per-Agent State Machine
```rust
enum AgentLivenessState {
    Alive,
    Suspect { since: i64, probe_sent_at: Option<i64> },
    Dead { declared_at: i64 },
}
```

### Evidence Signals (per-agent, GLOBAL across projects)
- `last_message_ts`: timestamp of most recent sent/received message
- `last_commit_ts`: timestamp of most recent git commit (from events)
- `last_reservation_action_ts`: last reserve/release/renew
- `avg_inter_activity_interval`: EWMA of time between any activity
- `session_start_ts`: when the agent registered

### Rhythm Learning (per-agent)
```rust
struct AgentRhythm {
    /// EWMA of inter-activity intervals (microseconds)
    avg_interval: f64,
    /// EWMA of squared deviations (for variance estimation)
    var_interval: f64,
    /// Number of observations
    observation_count: u64,
    /// Decay factor for EWMA (0.1 = ~10 samples half-life)
    alpha: f64,
    /// Program-type prior (from registration metadata)
    prior_interval: f64,
}
```

When a new activity is observed, update:
```
delta = now - last_activity
avg = (1-α)*avg + α*delta
var = (1-α)*var + α*(delta - avg)²
```

For the first ~10 observations, blend with the program-type prior:
```
effective_avg = (observation_count * avg + 3 * prior_interval)
              / (observation_count + 3)
```

### Suspicion Threshold
Instead of a fixed timeout, suspicion triggers when:
```
elapsed_since_last_activity > avg_interval + k * sqrt(var_interval)
```
where k is calibrated so P(false_positive) ≤ budget (default k≈3 for ~0.3%).

### Indirect Probing
Before declaring Suspect, the ATC sends a lightweight probe:
```
send_message(to: agent, subject: "[ATC] Health Check",
  body: "Are you still active? Reply to confirm.",
  thread_id: "atc-health-{agent_name}")
```
If no reply within 2× the agent's p95 response time → transition to Suspect.

### Sequential Declaration Test (SPRT)
Before transitioning Suspect → Dead, accumulate evidence using a Sequential
Probability Ratio Test:
- H0: agent is alive (will resume activity)
- H1: agent is dead (will not resume)
- Log-likelihood ratio updated each tick: LR += log(P(silence|dead)/P(silence|alive))
- Declare Dead when LR > log((1-β)/α) where α = false positive budget
- Configured for false-positive budget ≤ 1 per 100 agent-hours

### Dead → Release
When an agent is declared Dead:
1. Log the declaration with full evidence (posterior, SPRT score, probe history)
2. Send an advisory message to all agents sharing threads with the dead agent
3. Auto-release the dead agent's file reservations (after configurable grace)
4. The agent can "resurrect" by sending any message (resets to Alive)

## Dependency
- Requires Track 1 (Decision Core) for the liveness loss matrix
- The DecisionCore<LivenessState, LivenessAction> drives state transitions

## Files
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/atc.rs` (liveness module within ATC)

## Tests
- Unit: agent with regular rhythm → Alive classification
- Unit: agent with 5× avg silence → Suspect transition
- Unit: probe response resets to Alive
- Unit: resurrection after Dead via new message
- Unit: SPRT false-positive rate ≤ budget over 10000 simulated agents
- Unit: ATC agent excluded from liveness tracking
- Unit: program-type prior sets reasonable initial rhythm
- Unit: multi-project: activity in project A keeps agent alive for project B
- Unit: probe rate limiting (max 1 outstanding probe per agent)
- Integration: liveness detector interacts with decision core correctly

title: takeover identity probe cannot recognize an auth-gated Agent Mail peer (401) — service --takeover refuses and crash-loops until Restart backoff
description: Observed on trj upgrading to v0.3.26: agent-mail.service (ExecStart: am serve-http --takeover --port 8765) could not replace a live INTERACTIVE am (v0.3.24) serving 8765 with HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN auth. The identity probe got 401, classified the listener as 'Unknown process listening on 127.0.0.1:8765', refused to terminate a non-Agent-Mail process (correct fail-safe), exited 1, and systemd restart-looped (stopped manually at counter 2 — same shape as the 75,347-restart incident). Fixes to consider: (1) identity probe should recognize an Agent Mail peer without auth — e.g. an unauthenticated /health or server banner endpoint, or auth-exempt identity handshake; (2) probe should send the configured bearer token when present in the unit env; (3) service unit should use StartLimitBurst/RestartPreventExitStatus so a refused takeover does not loop. Until fixed: manual sequence is stop the interactive am, then systemctl --user start agent-mail.

title: CLI: share verify/decrypt parity (signature + age)
description:
## Objective
Implement `share verify` and `share decrypt` with legacy semantics.

## Scope
- `share verify`:
  - Validate SRI hashes and optional Ed25519 signature.
  - `--public-key` uses provided base64 key; else use manifest signature.
- `share decrypt`:
  - `--output` defaults to filename sans `.age` (or `_decrypted`).
  - `--identity` (age key file) is mutually exclusive with `--passphrase`.

## Tests
- Unit tests for signature verification and decrypt flag validation.
- Integration tests decrypting a bundle produced by share export.

## Logging/Artifacts
- Store verification results under `tests/artifacts/cli/share_verify/<timestamp>/`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. share verify/decrypt match legacy flags, defaults, and exit codes.
2. Signature validation and age decrypt succeed on valid inputs and fail loudly on invalid.
3. Mutual‑exclusion flag handling matches legacy.
close_reason: Added CLI integration tests for share verify/decrypt parity; validated exit codes + defaults

title: Batch read/ack state transitions for swarm notification bursts
description:
Goal: add explicit batch primitives or internal batching for read and acknowledgement updates during large notification bursts.

Rationale: many agents acknowledging the same coordination wave should not force one transaction and archive event per recipient when the intent can be grouped safely. This is a classic batching/flat-combining opportunity.

Scope: preserve existing acknowledge_message and mark_message_read APIs; add internal batch helpers first, then optionally expose CLI/operator batch surfaces if useful.

Fallback/safe mode: if any row-level update fails validation, return per-item status and keep successful committed rows explicit. Do not coalesce across different projects without a proof.

Acceptance: SQL transaction helper, per-item result contract, unit tests for partial failures/idempotency, archive/event emission policy, and an integration test with 100+ acks proving fewer transactions while preserving read_ts/ack_ts semantics.
notes: Idea-wizard refinement pass: closure evidence should follow docs/VERIFICATION_COVERAGE_LEDGER.md. Prefer R0/R1 real-path evidence for transport, persistence, search, robot/operator, and load-lab claims. Performance acceptance should report p50/p95/p99 plus CPU/RSS/DB-query or queue-depth evidence where applicable. Test/repro workloads must use isolated STORAGE_ROOT and must not touch the operator mailbox. Stub-only tests can support design confidence but do not close user-facing or persistence/performance claims.
