title: ATC feature-vector schema versioning + forward-migration pattern when features evolve
description:
# ATC feature-vector schema versioning

## Why this bead exists

The ATC feature vector is NOT the DB schema — it is the set of fields extracted from each tool-dispatch event and stored in `atc_experiences.features` (likely a JSON blob or structured column). This schema evolves independently of the DB schema:
- Seam 1 seals an initial feature set
- Later work (new atc_regime signals, new atc_fairness metrics, additional atc_participation features) may add, remove, or rename feature fields
- Existing rows have the *old* feature set embedded in them

Without versioning, one of two things happens:
- **Silent breakage**: policy engine reads old rows, expects new features, gets `null`, produces wrong decisions
- **Silent correctness loss**: new features used only for recent rows, old rows silently down-weighted or ignored, but rollups and trend analysis become inconsistent over time

## Scope

### Add `feature_schema_version` to experiences

- New column (schema v17 addition; coordinates with br-bn0vb.28): `feature_schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`
- Every insert records the version active at that time
- Baseline v1 = sealed feature set from Seam 1

### Forward-migration pattern

When the feature schema evolves to v2:
1. Document the delta (added / removed / renamed fields) in `docs/ATC_FEATURE_SCHEMA_VERSIONS.md`
2. Policy engine's feature-reader code uses `feature_schema_version` to know which fields to expect
3. Migration policy for old rows — two strategies depending on change type:
   - **Additive change** (new field, old rows missing it): reader treats absent field as "not observed"; trend aggregations exclude rows without the field
   - **Breaking change** (renamed or type-narrowed field): run offline backfill `am atc reprocess-features --from-version=N --to-version=N+1` that reads each old row and writes a v+1-compatible variant, OR explicitly mark old rows as `retired_schema=true` so the policy engine excludes them

### Version-aware rollups

- Rollups are scoped to a feature-schema-version (`atc_experience_rollups.feature_schema_version`)
- Mixed-version rollups are rejected; the refresh logic groups by version
- Operator surface (robot/TUI) shows distribution of rows by feature version (helps identify "we have a lot of v1 legacy data")

### Tooling

- `am atc feature-schema list-versions` — show all versions present in the ledger + when each was active
- `am atc feature-schema diff <from> <to>` — show the semantic diff between two versions
- `am atc reprocess-features` — forward-migrate rows (dry-run + apply modes)

## Test plan

### Unit

1. Insert v1 row → version=1 recorded
2. Bump schema to v2, insert new row → version=2 recorded; v1 rows unchanged
3. Read v1 row with v2 expectations → reader handles gracefully per strategy
4. Rollup refresh groups correctly by version
5. Reprocess tool (dry-run) reports what would change; no mutation
6. Reprocess tool (apply) migrates old rows; new version recorded
7. Reprocess idempotent (running twice same result)
8. Operator surface shows version distribution

### Integration

- Seed ledger with 1000 v1 rows; bump to v2; run workload; verify v1 and v2 rows coexist and rollups are correct per-version
- Run reprocess; verify all rows at v2 afterward

### Chaos

- Reprocess interrupted → partial state preserved; re-run resumes
- Storage exhausted during reprocess → clean error; no corrupted rows

## Logging requirements

```
atc.feature_schema.version_detected { version }
atc.feature_schema.row_inserted { experience_id, version }
atc.feature_schema.read_version_mismatch { row_version, reader_version, strategy }
atc.feature_schema.reprocess_start { from_version, to_version, row_count_estimate, dry_run }
atc.feature_schema.reprocess_complete { rows_migrated, skipped, errors, duration }
```

### Metrics

- `atc_experiences_by_version_gauge{version}`
- `atc_rollups_by_version_gauge{version}`
- `atc_feature_reprocessing_operations_total{result}`

## Non-goals

- Not supporting arbitrary version rollbacks (forward-only)
- Not auto-migrating rows (always operator-initiated via `am atc reprocess-features`)
- Not storing full schema JSON per row (version integer + central schema registry; cheaper)

## Dependencies

- Depends on br-bn0vb.1 (sealed v1 contract)
- Depends on br-bn0vb.28 (schema v17 — adds the version column)
- Related to br-bn0vb.26 (policy engine read) — engine must respect version
- Feeds br-bn0vb.4 (rollups) — rollups must be per-version

## Definition of done

- Version column present and populated
- Reader handles mixed-version reads
- Reprocess tool works (dry-run + apply)
- Tests pass
- docs/ATC_FEATURE_SCHEMA_VERSIONS.md committed with v1 description (the baseline) and migration patterns for future versions

title: ATC Seam 2.2: DB resolve_experience() with outcome labels + censor reasons
description:
# ATC Seam 2.2: DB resolve API

## Preconditions

- br-bn0vb.2 (insert API) closed

## Scope

Add `resolve_experience(experience_id, outcome, censor_reason?, attribution_window?)` to `atc_queries.rs`. Transitions a row from OPEN → RESOLVED (or CENSORED or EXPIRED) exactly once.

## API signature (draft)

```rust
pub async fn resolve_experience(
    cx: &Cx,
    pool: &DbPool,
    experience_id: ExperienceId,
    resolution: Resolution,
) -> Result<ResolveOutcome, DbError> { ... }

pub enum Resolution {
    Resolved { label: OutcomeLabel, attribution_window_micros: i64 },
    Censored { reason: CensorReason },
    Expired,
}

pub enum ResolveOutcome {
    Applied,          // row transitioned
    AlreadyResolved,  // idempotent no-op
    NotFound,         // experience_id doesn't exist
}
```

## Requirements

- Idempotent: calling resolve twice with same outcome is a no-op, returns AlreadyResolved
- Calling resolve with different outcomes after the first must be rejected (not silently overwritten) — this is a critical invariant for learning integrity
- Uses atc_labeling.rs for OutcomeLabel values; atc_labeling defines 7 action-family rules and 8 censor reasons per memory log 2026-03-18
- Atomic within a single transaction
- Emits structured tracing span with transition details
- Updates rollup counters (but rollup logic can live in Seam 2.3 and be called from this function)

## Tests

- Unit: happy path OPEN → RESOLVED
- Unit: idempotent double-resolve with same outcome
- Unit: double-resolve with DIFFERENT outcome → error (preserves learning integrity)
- Unit: resolve non-existent id → NotFound
- Property: any sequence of resolve calls respects the monotonicity invariant (no going backward)

## Definition of done

- API implemented + tested
- Integration with atc_labeling's OutcomeLabel enum
- Rollup invocation stubbed or integrated (depends on Seam 2.3)
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria — test + logging rigor

### Unit tests (required)

1. **Happy path** — OPEN → RESOLVED with valid outcome label, row state changes exactly once
2. **Idempotent same-outcome** — resolve(id, Resolved{Acknowledged}), then resolve(id, Resolved{Acknowledged}) → second returns AlreadyResolved, row unchanged
3. **Conflicting re-resolve rejected** — resolve(id, Resolved{Acknowledged}), then resolve(id, Resolved{Read}) → returns DbError::ConflictingResolution, row remains Acknowledged. **Critical invariant: learning integrity.**
4. **Resolve to CENSORED** — valid censor reason transitions row correctly
5. **Resolve to EXPIRED** — attribution window passed, transitions row, timestamp recorded
6. **Resolve non-existent id** — returns NotFound, no side effects
7. **Concurrent resolve of same row** — two tasks call resolve(id, ...) at the same time → exactly one succeeds (Applied), other returns AlreadyResolved
8. **All OutcomeLabel variants** — parameterized test hitting every variant from atc_labeling.rs (7 action families × N outcomes)
9. **All CensorReason variants** — parameterized test for each of 8 censor reasons from atc_labeling.rs
10. **Rollup notification** — resolve triggers rollup update (via Seam 2.3 integration); rollup counter increments correctly

### Property tests

- Sequence of resolve calls on the same id is order-independent up to idempotency (the first wins; subsequent calls are AlreadyResolved)
- Resolving N random rows in parallel produces exactly N rows in RESOLVED state

### Structured logging

DEBUG-level span on each resolve:
```
atc.db.resolve_experience {
  experience_id, outcome_label, prior_state, new_state,
  attribution_window_micros, resolve_latency_micros,
  rollup_notified: bool
}
```

WARN-level span on conflicting re-resolve (integrity violation):
```
atc.db.resolve_conflict {
  experience_id, existing_outcome, attempted_outcome, actor
}
```

### E2E validation

- Integration: send + ack message roundtrip → exactly one row transitions from OPEN to RESOLVED with label=Acknowledged
- Integration: try to ack same message twice → exactly one transition, second is idempotent
- Integration: integrity-violation test — manually call resolve with two different outcomes → clear error, no silent corruption

### Documentation

- Rustdoc warns about the ConflictingResolution case; explicitly documents that it is intentional (not a bug to silence)
- Runbook entry: "if you see ConflictingResolution in logs, here's how to interpret it"

title: am atc explain <decision_id>: inverse-engineer a decision to debug policy behavior
description:
# am atc explain <decision_id>: decision forensics

## Why this bead exists

When ATC produces an unexpected decision in production, operators need to answer: "why did the engine choose X?" Today:
- The engine emits an `atc.decision` tracing span (from br-bn0vb.20 observability) but it's buried in logs
- The feature vector that fed the decision is in `atc_experiences`
- The applied rules are encoded in `atc.rs` + `atc_labeling.rs` + `atc_policy_certificates.rs`
- There's no single command that assembles all three into a human-readable story

Without this, diagnosis is: "grep logs + query DB + read source code simultaneously". A single-command forensics tool shrinks that to 30 seconds.

## Scope

`am atc explain <decision_id> [--format json|md|toon]` reports:

### Section 1: Decision metadata
- decision_id, timestamp, policy_version, decision_kind
- action_taken, confidence, safe_mode_state_at_decision_time

### Section 2: Input features
- The experience_ids that fed the decision (might be N rows for aggregate decisions)
- For each: the full feature vector at decision time (from the stored row; if feature_schema_version evolved since, note "reader sees legacy features")

### Section 3: Applied rules
- Which atc_labeling rule matched
- Which risk budget applied
- Which precondition families were evaluated (atc_effect_semantics)
- Which assumptions were loaded (atc_assumptions)
- All EV gates passed / failed with numeric values

### Section 4: Alternate choices
- What decisions were considered but rejected
- For each rejected alternative: why (budget violation? assumption failed? confidence below threshold?)

### Section 5: Trace links
- Trace span IDs (if available) for span-forwarding tools
- Git archive paths for any promoted artifacts related to this decision

## Test plan

### Unit

1. Explain for a simple known decision (fixture) → human-readable output matches expected
2. Explain for a safe-mode fallback → output clearly shows safe-mode engaged + reason
3. Explain for an aggregate decision using N rows → all N experience_ids listed
4. Unknown decision_id → error with helpful suggestion ("did you mean X?")
5. Decision from prior policy version → output clearly shows the policy version in use AT decision time, not the current version

### Integration

- E2E: force a known decision via test harness, explain it, verify expected output
- E2E with verbosity: `--verbose` expands every rule with source-code cross-reference

### Output formats

- `json`: machine-parseable; stable schema versioned
- `md`: human-readable narrative suitable for posting in a bug report
- `toon`: compact for agent consumption

## Logging requirements

The explain tool itself emits:
```
atc.explain.query { decision_id, format }
atc.explain.result { found, experience_ids_referenced, rules_matched, output_format }
atc.explain.not_found { decision_id, similar_ids_suggested }
```

## Non-goals

- Not a policy editor (can't change decisions through this tool)
- Not a full re-simulation (uses stored features + recorded rule applications; doesn't re-run math)
- Not a replay of the decision under current policy (that's a separate tool if ever needed)

## Dependencies

- Depends on br-bn0vb.20 (observability) — explain consumes the tracing+metrics schemas
- Depends on br-bn0vb.26 (policy engine read) — explain reads experiences
- Depends on br-bn0vb.29 (feature versioning) — explain respects the version at decision time
- Feeds br-bn0vb.21 (rollback runbook) — incident runbook uses `am atc explain` as a step

## Definition of done

- Subcommand implemented with 3 output formats
- Tests cover happy path + edge cases
- Documentation: `am atc explain --help` + example in OPERATOR_RUNBOOK.md
- Cross-referenced from the rollback runbook

title: ATC.31: am atc simulate — prospective policy dry-run on historical scenarios for safe exploration
description:
# am atc simulate: prospective policy dry-run

## Why this bead exists

br-bn0vb.30 gives retrospective forensics (why DID the engine decide X). Operators also need **prospective** simulation: "if we changed policy parameter P from 0.1 to 0.05, how would the last 1000 decisions have differed?"

Without simulation, policy tuning = live experimentation with real decisions. Risky and slow. Simulation enables safe parameter sweeps on historical data.

## Scope

```bash
am atc simulate --policy <file.json> --since <ts> [--until <ts>]
                [--dry-run-confidence 0.9]
                [--output tests/artifacts/atc/simulation_<date>.json]
                [--format json|md|toon]
```

### What it does

1. Loads a proposed policy bundle from a JSON file (or from stdin)
2. Loads experiences from the historical range
3. Runs the engine over those experiences with the new policy (WITHOUT touching prod policy)
4. Compares: old policy decisions vs proposed policy decisions
5. Reports: which decisions differ, by how much, which stratums are most affected, counterfactual outcomes if computable

### Example

```
am atc simulate --policy new_policy.json --since 2026-04-01 --format md

# Policy simulation report
Period: 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-17 (17 days)
Experiences considered: 12,430
Decisions evaluated: 891

## Summary
- Same decision: 782 (87.8%)
- Different action: 67 (7.5%)
- Different confidence: 42 (4.7%)
- Different safe-mode entry: 0 (0%)

## By stratum
| Stratum | Same | Different | Net impact |
| ack_required-urgent | 234 | 12 | +8 Acknowledged |
| reservation-exclusive | 198 | 23 | +4 Conflicted-flagged |
...

## Notable divergences
[decision_id_1]: old=AllowWithWarning, new=Block, confidence change +0.15 → investigate
...

Run: am atc explain decision_id_1 --policy new_policy.json
```

### Non-invasive

- Reads only; never writes to atc_experiences or atc_rollups
- Uses read-only DB connection to avoid any accidental mutation
- Emits structured simulation result (not a new experience row)

## Test plan

### Unit

1. Simulate with an identical policy → 0 differences (sanity)
2. Simulate with a clearly-stricter policy → expected direction of divergence
3. Invalid policy file → error with clear schema-violation detail
4. Empty time range → empty report (not an error)
5. Very large range (100K+ experiences) → bounded memory + time; progress indicator

### Integration

- Load a real policy bundle + simulate on historical data; report matches expected deltas
- Simulation does NOT modify any DB state (verify by pre/post checksums)
- Parallel simulations (two simultaneous invocations) don't interfere

### Logging

```
atc.simulate.start { policy_file, since, until, experiences_count_estimate }
atc.simulate.progress { experiences_processed, decisions_evaluated, elapsed_ms }
atc.simulate.complete { policy_file, total_decisions, divergences, output_path }
```

## Non-goals

- Not a policy-training system (just evaluation)
- Not multi-policy comparison in one run (use script to orchestrate multiple)
- Not counterfactual outcome simulation beyond what the engine can compute from stored features

## Dependencies

- Depends on br-bn0vb.5 (replay API — simulation iterates experiences)
- Depends on br-bn0vb.26 (engine read path — simulation uses same reader)
- Depends on br-bn0vb.29 (feature versioning — simulation respects version at historical time)
- Complements br-bn0vb.30 (explain is retrospective, simulate is prospective)

## Definition of done

- Subcommand with all options
- Non-invasive guarantee tested (pre/post DB checksums equal)
- Example policy + simulation report committed to docs/
- `docs/ATC_POLICY_SIMULATION.md` with usage patterns

title: ATC Seam 2.3: rollup maintenance + stratum aggregation
description:
# ATC Seam 2.3: Rollup aggregation

## Preconditions

- br-bn0vb.2 (insert) closed
- br-bn0vb.3 (resolve) closed

## Scope

Maintain the `atc_experience_rollups` v16 table. Rollups are pre-aggregated summaries per (stratum, time_bucket) so ATC policy engine and operator surfaces can read fast.

## Strategy

Two possible designs:

### Option 1: Inline-update rollups on every insert/resolve
Simple, keeps rollups real-time, but adds cost to hot path.

### Option 2: Batch-recompute rollups on a periodic tick (e.g., every 5 min)
Adds latency to rollups but keeps insert/resolve fast. Still real-time enough for learning.

Recommended: **Option 2** per the README Implementation Map "append-friendly hot path, free of write amplification".

## API signature

```rust
pub async fn refresh_rollups(
    cx: &Cx,
    pool: &DbPool,
    now_micros: i64,
    lookback_micros: i64,
) -> Result<RollupSummary, DbError> { ... }
```

## Requirements

- Scan `atc_experiences` for rows updated in the last `lookback` window
- Compute per-stratum counts (OPEN/RESOLVED/CENSORED/EXPIRED by outcome label and action family)
- UPSERT into `atc_experience_rollups`
- Emit structured span
- Bounded runtime: < 100ms for 100K experience rows

## Tick integration

The ATC tick loop in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/atc.rs` already runs at a cadence (memory log mentions DecisionCore.alpha matching replay tick cadence). Piggyback rollup refresh on that tick.

## Tests

- Unit: single experience → rollup row with count=1
- Unit: N experiences, varied stratums → correct per-stratum counts
- Unit: re-running refresh on same data is idempotent (no double-count)
- Perf: 100K rows rolled up in < 100ms

## Definition of done

- refresh_rollups() implemented + tested
- Integrated into ATC tick
- Rollup table correctly populated after test workload
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria — test + logging rigor

### Unit tests (required)

1. **Single-row roll-up** — one experience row in, rollup has count=1 for that stratum
2. **Multi-row aggregation** — N experiences across M stratums, rollup row-counts exactly match
3. **Idempotent refresh** — calling refresh_rollups twice on unchanged data produces identical rollups (no double-count)
4. **Window-bounded refresh** — refresh with lookback=30s only aggregates rows touched in last 30s; older rows unchanged
5. **Rollup preservation under retention** — when retention compacts raw experiences, their rollup counts are preserved
6. **Concurrent refresh + insert** — insert happens during refresh; the new row either lands in this rollup or the next, never lost or double-counted
7. **Transitions counted correctly** — an experience transitioning from OPEN to RESOLVED decrements OPEN count by 1 and increments RESOLVED count by 1 in the rollup (atomic)
8. **Empty window** — refresh with zero rows in window is a no-op with clean logs
9. **Stratum explosion guard** — if stratum cardinality exceeds configured max, emit WARN and cap (don't grow unbounded)
10. **Schema evolution** — adding a new stratum type doesn't break old rollup rows

### Property tests

- Any valid sequence of insert + resolve + refresh produces rollup counts that match direct-SQL aggregation over raw rows (conservation property)

### Perf tests (criterion)

- 100K experience rows refreshed in < 100ms
- Incremental refresh (30-sec window of 1000 rows) in < 10ms
- Memory footprint bounded (no leak under hour-long soak)

### Structured logging

```
atc.rollup.refresh_start { lookback_micros, strata_count_before }
atc.rollup.refresh_complete { duration_micros, strata_updated, rows_scanned, rows_applied }
atc.rollup.stratum_updated { stratum_key, from_counts: {...}, to_counts: {...} }  # DEBUG only
atc.rollup.cardinality_warning { stratum_type, current_count, limit }             # WARN if near cap
```

Per-tick aggregate counter:
- `atc_rollup_refresh_duration_micros_histogram`
- `atc_rollup_rows_updated_total{stratum}`

### Integration

- Tick integration: refresh runs on ATC tick cadence
- `am robot atc --rollups` returns human-readable rollup summary
- TUI Atc screen shows rollup sparklines

### Documentation

- `docs/ATC_DB_API.md` section on rollup semantics and refresh cadence
- Rustdoc with example usage

title: ATC Seam 2.4: retention_compact() + replay() + query_open_experiences()
description:
# ATC Seam 2.4: Retention, replay, and query APIs

## Preconditions

- br-bn0vb.2-4 closed

## Scope

Three remaining read/maintenance APIs:

### query_open_experiences(since?, stratum?, limit?)
Returns open (unresolved) experience rows, filtered by time range and/or stratum. Used by:
- Outcome resolution sweep (Seam 4) to find rows whose attribution window expired
- Operator surfaces (Seam 5) to show "currently learning about N events"

### retention_compact(max_age_micros, retain_recent_rollups)
Deletes experience rows older than `max_age_micros` but preserves the corresponding rollup entries (aggregated history is cheaper to keep than raw rows). Per atc_retention.rs policy.

### replay(from_seq?, to_seq?)
Returns full ledger state for audit/soak/debug. Used by:
- Transparency bundles (cold path per Implementation Map)
- Debug tooling when investigating ATC decisions

## API signatures

```rust
pub async fn query_open_experiences(
    cx: &Cx,
    pool: &DbPool,
    filter: OpenExperienceFilter,
) -> Result<Vec<ExperienceRow>, DbError>;

pub async fn retention_compact(
    cx: &Cx,
    pool: &DbPool,
    max_age_micros: i64,
    preserve_rollups: bool,
) -> Result<CompactSummary, DbError>;

pub async fn replay(
    cx: &Cx,
    pool: &DbPool,
    range: SequenceRange,
) -> Result<ExperienceStream, DbError>;
```

## Tests

- Unit: query respects since + stratum filters
- Unit: retention_compact deletes expected rows, preserves rollups
- Unit: replay returns rows in stable seq order
- Soak: retention runs nightly, keeps DB size bounded over 7-day workload

## Definition of done

- All three APIs implemented
- Tests pass including soak
- Integrated with atc_retention.rs config
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria — test + logging rigor

### Unit tests (required)

#### query_open_experiences
1. Returns empty when none open
2. Returns N when N are OPEN
3. Respects `since` filter (only rows newer than timestamp)
4. Respects `stratum` filter (only matching stratum)
5. Respects `limit` (pagination); results stable across queries (same order)
6. Does NOT return RESOLVED / CENSORED / EXPIRED rows
7. Returns rows in deterministic order (suitable for pagination)

#### retention_compact
8. Deletes rows older than max_age_micros
9. Preserves rollups (rollups remain after raw rows deleted)
10. Does NOT delete still-OPEN rows regardless of age (warns instead — stale OPEN rows are a bug to investigate)
11. Dry-run mode reports what would be deleted without mutating
12. Atomic: interrupted mid-compaction leaves DB consistent
13. Emits an audit record per compaction run (to Git archive per README cold-path boundary)

#### replay
14. Returns rows in stable sequence order
15. Respects `from_seq` / `to_seq` bounds
16. Streams without loading all into memory (usable on 1M-row DB)
17. Deterministic: same range = same bytes

### Property tests

- retention_compact preserves the count invariant: sum(rollups) == total_experiences_ever_written - compacted_count
- replay(from, to) followed by replay(to, end) equals replay(from, end) (seam property)

### Perf tests

- query_open_experiences: 1000 rows returned in < 10ms p95
- retention_compact: 100K rows aged-out in < 5 seconds (slow-path acceptable; runs nightly)
- replay: 1M rows streamed in < 30 seconds

### Soak test

- 7-day virtual-time soak (via LabRuntime): workload 1000 events/hour; retention nightly; DB file size bounded (no monotonic growth)

### Structured logging

```
atc.query.open_experiences { filter_kind, returned_count, duration_micros }
atc.retention.compact_start { max_age_micros, preserve_rollups, dry_run }
atc.retention.compact_complete { rows_deleted, rollups_preserved, duration_micros }
atc.retention.open_row_too_old_warning { experience_id, age_days }   # WARN — shouldn't happen
atc.replay.stream_start { from_seq, to_seq }
atc.replay.stream_complete { rows_streamed, duration_micros }
```

Metrics:
- `atc_open_experiences_gauge{stratum}` — exposed continuously
- `atc_retention_rows_deleted_total` — cumulative
- `atc_replay_invocations_total`

### Integration

- Nightly retention run wired to ATC tick loop (on its own schedule, not every tick)
- `am atc retention --dry-run` / `am atc retention --apply` CLI commands
- `am atc replay --from <seq> --to <seq> --format json` for forensic investigation

### Documentation

- `docs/SPEC-atc-retention-policy.md` with the full policy
- Rustdoc examples

title: ATC Seam 3.1: wire send_message + fetch_inbox to atc_note_message_sent/received
description:
# ATC Seam 3.1: Wire message hot path to ATC note functions

## Preconditions

- br-bn0vb.1 (Seam 1 core contract) closed
- br-bn0vb.2 (insert_experience DB API) closed

## Scope

In `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/lib.rs` at the tool-dispatch boundary:

- On successful `send_message`: call `atc_note_message_sent(...)`, which in turn calls `insert_experience(...)` with the correct event-derived `ExperienceRow`
- On `fetch_inbox` return (when new messages are observed for an agent): call `atc_note_message_received(...)` equivalently

## Implementation outline

1. Identify the dispatch callback where `send_message` result becomes visible post-tool-return.
2. Derive an `ExperienceRow` from the tool arguments + result:
   - event_kind: MessageSent
   - from_agent, to_agents, subject_hash (not subject itself — privacy)
   - importance, thread_id, ack_required
   - features: participation features (atc_participation.rs), regime features (atc_regime.rs)
3. Call `atc_note_message_sent(row)` already defined in `mcp-agent-mail-server/src/atc.rs`.
4. `atc_note_message_sent` must call `insert_experience` via Seam 2.1 API.
5. For `fetch_inbox`: if the response includes new messages (crosscheck: recipient's last_read_seq), emit MessageReceived experiences for each new message.

## Perf budget

- Adds ≤ 1ms to send_message p95. Most of the added cost is the insert, so batching into coalescer if possible (or async-fire-and-forget with bounded buffer) is acceptable.
- If insert latency is > 500µs, use a bounded `asupersync` channel to defer the insert off the hot path — BUT preserve ordering per (agent, thread) so learning sequences are coherent.

## Tests

- Integration: send a message, observe a new row in atc_experiences
- Integration: fetch inbox with 3 new messages, observe 3 new rows
- Perf: send_message p95 increase < 5% vs pre-wiring baseline
- Property: every successful send_message produces exactly one experience row (no duplicates, no misses)

## Non-goals

- Not wiring reservation events (sibling bead)
- Not resolving outcomes (seam 4)

## Definition of done

- Hot-path wiring complete for send + receive
- Perf budget met
- Integration tests demonstrate row creation
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria — test + logging rigor

### Unit tests (required)

1. **send_message in live mode** — inserts exactly one MessageSent row with correct feature vector
2. **send_message in shadow mode** — zero rows inserted; one tracing span emitted at TRACE level
3. **ATC_LEARNING_DISABLED=1** — no compute, no log, no insert
4. **fetch_inbox with N new** — emits N MessageReceived experience rows
5. **fetch_inbox with zero new** — zero experience rows
6. **Product-bus routed message** — same wiring (no duplicates, correct project attribution)
7. **Attachments** — feature vector includes metadata (count, total size); no extra rows
8. **Edge inputs** — empty subject/body, unicode, large messages — derivation never panics, vectors well-formed, sizes bounded
9. **Hot-path budget** — insert latency < 500µs p95; deferred-channel fallback engages if insert > threshold
10. **Error isolation** — panic in derivation does NOT fail the tool call (ATC is side-channel)

### Integration tests

- `tests/e2e/test_atc_message_wiring.sh` — full E2E with real DB: 20 msgs across 3 agents; verify correct experience row counts
- Mode-switch test: shadow → live flip picks up new inserts; historical messages not retroactively inserted (gap is recorded)
- Stress suite: 30-agent workload with ATC wired; no new errors introduced

### Chaos tests

- Panic in derivation → tool call still returns success; WARN-level span logged
- DB unavailable mid-insert → tool call succeeds; derivation error logged

### Structured logging

```
atc.hot_path.note_message_sent { tool, from, to_count, importance, thread_id, experience_id, write_mode, wiring_latency_micros }
atc.hot_path.note_message_received { recipient, message_id, thread_id, experience_id, write_mode }
atc.hot_path.batch_summary { window_secs: 5, inserts_attempted, inserts_succeeded, inserts_deferred, derivation_errors }
```

### Perf budget

- send_message p95 regression < 5% vs pre-wiring baseline (verified by br-bn0vb.15)
- fetch_inbox p95 regression < 5%
- Zero regression on the 10-test stress gauntlet

### Documentation

- `docs/ATC_HOT_PATH_WIRING.md` documents the wiring points
- Rustdoc on atc_note_message_sent / atc_note_message_received explains invocation contract

# ATC Seam 3.2: Wire file reservation events to ATC

## Preconditions

- br-bn0vb.1 (Seam 1) + br-bn0vb.2 (insert) closed

## Scope

Wire the reservation tool cluster to the existing ATC note functions:
- `file_reservation_paths` success → `atc_note_reservation_granted`
- `file_reservation_paths` conflict → `atc_note_reservation_conflicts`
- `release_file_reservations` success → `atc_note_reservation_released`
- `renew_file_reservations` → `atc_note_reservation_renewed` (if needed — create the function if not)
- `force_release_file_reservation` → `atc_note_reservation_force_released`

## Implementation outline

Similar to Seam 3.1 pattern:
1. Post-tool-dispatch hook observes result
2. Derives ExperienceRow with event_kind: ReservationGranted/Conflict/Released/etc.
3. Features: path-pattern fingerprint (hashed globs), ttl, exclusive flag, agent, conflict-vs-clean
4. Calls the corresponding atc_note_* function → insert_experience

## Perf budget

- ≤ 500µs added to reservation tool p95
- Use same deferral pattern as Seam 3.1 if insert is slow

## Tests

- Integration: grant a reservation, observe row
- Integration: cause a conflict, observe Conflict row
- Integration: release a reservation, observe Release row linked (via experience_id chain) to the Grant row
- Property: every reservation tool call produces exactly one experience row

## Definition of done

- Wiring complete for all reservation tools
- Linked experiences (grant → release) traceable via experience_id chain
- Tests demonstrate row creation for all variants
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria — test + logging rigor

### Unit tests

1. **Grant success → ReservationGranted row** (shadow + live modes tested)
2. **Grant conflict → ReservationConflict row** with attributed contending agent
3. **Release success → ReservationReleased row with experience_id link to the original grant**
4. **Force release → distinct event kind ReservationForceReleased** (distinguishable from normal release)
5. **Renew success → ReservationRenewed row** (if we make it a distinct event kind)
6. **Exclusive vs non-exclusive reservations** — feature vector distinguishes; both produce rows

# ATC Seam 3.3: Wire build slots to ATC

## Preconditions

- br-bn0vb.1 + br-bn0vb.2 closed

## Scope

Build slots are feature-flagged off by default (WORKTREES_ENABLED=false). When enabled, wire them:
- acquire_build_slot → atc_note_build_slot_acquired (create this function in atc.rs)
- renew_build_slot → atc_note_build_slot_renewed
- release_build_slot → atc_note_build_slot_released

## Rationale

Build slot lifetimes are short-bounded advisory leases, very similar to file reservations — they're a natural learning signal about coordination effectiveness.

## Priority note

Lower priority (P3) than Seams 3.1 and 3.2 because:
- The feature is off by default
- Learning signal from build slots is less dense than messaging/reservation events
- Can land after the main loop closes

## Tests

- Integration: with WORKTREES_ENABLED=true, acquire a slot, observe row
- Integration: with WORKTREES_ENABLED=false, no experience rows are created for slot events (guard check)

## Definition of done

- Wiring present behind feature flag
- Tests demonstrate rows only created when enabled
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria — test + logging rigor

### Unit tests

1. **WORKTREES_ENABLED=true, acquire succeeds** → one BuildSlotAcquired experience row, feature vector captures slot id + branch + ttl
2. **WORKTREES_ENABLED=false, acquire rejected by existing guard** → tool returns guard error; NO experience row created (feature is off)
3. **acquire + renew + release sequence** → three linked experience rows (Acquired → Renewed → Released)
4. **acquire + TTL expire without release** → sweep can resolve as Expired (overlap with reservation sweep tests)
5. **Conflict: two agents acquire same slot** → first wins BuildSlotAcquired, second gets BuildSlotConflict with attribution
6. **Force-release** → distinct event kind BuildSlotForceReleased
7. **Shadow / live / disabled modes** — all three tested
8. **Feature-flag off bypass** — when WORKTREES_ENABLED=false, atc_note_build_slot_* functions return early, zero compute overhead

### Integration

- E2E: with WORKTREES_ENABLED=true, acquire + work + release flow; 3 experience rows visible
- E2E: with WORKTREES_ENABLED=false, no experience rows created during equivalent flow (feature disabled)
- Stress: 10 slots × 20 contentions in a row, verify no deadlocks

### Structured logging

```
atc.hot_path.note_build_slot_acquired { agent, slot_id, branch, ttl_s, experience_id, write_mode }
atc.hot_path.note_build_slot_renewed { experience_id, original_experience_id, new_ttl_s }
atc.hot_path.note_build_slot_released { experience_id, original_experience_id, duration_held_micros }
atc.hot_path.note_build_slot_conflict { attempting_agent, blocking_agent, slot_id }
```

### Perf

- Adds < 500µs per build_slot tool p95
- Zero compute when WORKTREES_ENABLED=false (fast-return early)

### Documentation

- Build slot event schema added to `docs/ATC_HOT_PATH_WIRING.md`
- Note that build slot ATC wiring respects the WORKTREES_ENABLED gate (not just a runtime rejection but also no atc_experiences rows)

title: ATC Seam 4.1: outcome resolution on acknowledge_message + mark_message_read
description:
# ATC Seam 4.1: Resolve message-outcome experiences on ack/read

## Preconditions

- br-bn0vb.3 (resolve_experience DB API) closed
- br-bn0vb.6 (Seam 3.1 send/receive wiring) closed so resolution has something to resolve

## Scope

Wire `acknowledge_message` and `mark_message_read` tool dispatches to resolve the corresponding MessageSent experience:

- `acknowledge_message(message_id)` → find the experience row for the SEND (not the receive) of that message; resolve it with outcome = Acknowledged
- `mark_message_read(message_id)` → resolve with outcome = Read (if not already Acknowledged)
- Implicit: if message sits in inbox for > ack_stale window with ack_required=true, the outcome resolves to AckOverdue (handled by sweep, Seam 4.3)

## Implementation outline

1. In the post-dispatch hook for acknowledge_message/mark_message_read, look up the experience row by message_id.
2. Call `resolve_experience(experience_id, Resolution::Resolved { label, attribution_window })`.
3. Label comes from atc_labeling.rs mapping — per memory log 2026-03-18b, atc_labeling has 7 action-family rules.

## Edge cases

- Ack before sent has been observed by ATC: race condition; handle gracefully (retry once, then censor)
- Ack for a message not in ATC ledger (e.g., pre-dates ATC enablement): censor with reason `PreLearningEra`
- Double ack: idempotent (resolve_experience handles this)

## Tests

- Integration: send → fetch inbox → ack. Observe resolved experience row.
- Integration: send → read (not ack). Observe Read resolution.
- Integration: send → read → ack. Ack wins (overrides Read), final label is Acknowledged.
- Race: fast ack before ATC propagation — behavior is well-defined.

## Definition of done

- Ack and read dispatches resolve experiences correctly
- Race conditions handled
- Tests pass
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria — test + logging rigor

### Unit tests

1. **Ack resolves matching MessageSent** — the SEND row (not the receive) transitions to RESOLVED with label=Acknowledged
2. **MessageReceived row stays OPEN** after ack — receive side is a separate experience; it tracks inbox-visit behavior, not ack
3. **Mark-read resolves as label=Read** if not already Acknowledged
4. **Ack wins over Read** — if row is Read, ack upgrades it to Acknowledged; the audit log records the upgrade
5. **Ack for unknown message_id** — tool still succeeds; ATC logs a WARN; no row created
6. **Ack for pre-learning message** — experience row didn't exist in ledger; tool succeeds; ATC logs at DEBUG
7. **Idempotent double-ack** — second ack is no-op
8. **Race: ack before ATC propagation** — documented behavior; retry logic with bounded attempts; final outcome is correct
9. **Ack in shadow mode** — does NOT resolve actual rows (since there are none); logs would-resolve at TRACE
10. **Partial failure: resolve API error** — tool call still succeeds (side-channel); error logged at WARN; sweep (Seam 4.3) cleans up later

### Integration

- Send → ack roundtrip via MCP, assert row transitioned to Acknowledged
- Multi-recipient ack: message sent to 3 agents; when one acks, the SINGLE underlying MessageSent row transitions; the other 2 recipients' MessageReceived rows are independent
- Ack across thread: reply that acks → still resolves the original; reply-that-doesn't-ack → original stays OPEN

### Chaos

- Ack arrives during DB WAL checkpoint — resolve retries, succeeds
- Concurrent acks from same agent (shouldn't happen but might) — one wins, other is idempotent

### Structured logging

```
atc.hot_path.note_ack { agent, message_id, tool, experience_id_resolved?, outcome, write_mode, latency_micros }
atc.hot_path.ack_for_unknown_message { message_id, agent }       # WARN
atc.hot_path.ack_race_retry { message_id, attempt_n }             # DEBUG
atc.hot_path.ack_upgrade_read_to_acked { message_id, experience_id }  # INFO — historical audit
```

### Metrics

- `atc_acks_total{outcome: acknowledged | read | already_resolved | unknown}`
- `atc_ack_latency_micros_histogram`

### Documentation

- Ack resolution semantics in `docs/ATC_HOT_PATH_WIRING.md` (including the ack-wins-over-read rule)
close_reason: Completed: resolved message_sent ATC rows on acknowledge_message/mark_message_read with ack-over-read upgrade path, doc note, and server tests

title: ATC Track 4: Evidence Ledger — Decision Audit Trail
description:
# Track 4: Evidence Ledger

## Graveyard Source: §0.8 Evidence Ledger pattern, alien-artifact-coding §2

## What
Every ATC decision is logged with full context: the posterior belief distribution,
the loss matrix consulted, the action chosen, the expected loss, and the evidence
that led to the decision. This makes the ATC fully auditable and debuggable.

## Why
An ATC that makes invisible decisions is worse than no ATC. When the ATC
releases an agent's reservations, the operator needs to understand WHY.
The evidence ledger answers: "What did the ATC see, what did it believe,
and what would have happened if it chose differently?"

## Data Model
```rust
struct AtcDecisionRecord {
    /// Unique decision ID
    id: u64,
    /// Timestamp of the decision
    timestamp_micros: i64,
    /// Which subsystem made the decision
    subsystem: AtcSubsystem, // Liveness | Conflict | LoadRouting | Synthesis
    /// The entity the decision concerns
    subject: String, // agent name or thread ID
    /// Posterior belief at decision time
    posterior: Vec<(String, f64)>, // [(state_name, probability)]
    /// Action chosen
    action: String,
    /// Expected loss of chosen action
    expected_loss: f64,
    /// Expected loss of the next-best alternative (for "how close was it?")
    runner_up_loss: f64,
    /// Key evidence that drove this decision
    evidence_summary: String,
    /// Whether the calibration guard was healthy at decision time
    calibration_healthy: bool,
    /// Whether safe mode was active
    safe_mode_active: bool,
}
```

## Storage
The ledger is stored in-memory as a bounded ring buffer (last 1000 decisions).
It's also surfaced through the existing event system (MailEvent) so the TUI
can display it and the git archive captures it.

No new DB tables — the ledger piggybacks on the existing event ring.

## Evidence-to-Message Bridge
When the ATC takes a non-trivial action (not "ignore"), it sends a message
to the affected agent AND logs to a #atc-decisions thread:
```
[ATC Decision #42] Declared agent BlueFox as Suspect.
Evidence: no activity for 847s (avg interval: 120s, 5.8σ).
Posterior: P(alive)=0.12, P(flaky)=0.41, P(dead)=0.47.
Action: suspect (expected loss: 3.2, vs. declare_alive: 18.1).
Probe sent at {timestamp}. Will escalate to Dead if no response in 240s.
```

## Dependency
- Requires Track 1 (Decision Core) — logs decisions from the core
- Independent of Tracks 2/3 — can be built in parallel once Track 1 exists

## Files
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/atc.rs` (ledger module within ATC)

## Tests
- Unit: decision records are correctly formatted
- Unit: ring buffer evicts oldest when full
- Unit: evidence summary is human-readable
- Unit: runner_up_loss is correctly computed from loss matrix
- Integration: decisions flow through to MailEvent ring

title: AM Reliability Hardening Program (session-history root-causes)
description:
# AM Reliability Hardening Program

**Origin.** This epic operationalizes `COMPREHENSIVE_ISSUES_AND_PROBLEMS_WITH_AM_BASED_ON_COMPLETE_SESSION_HISTORY_ANALYSIS.md`: six successive session-history mining passes across the local host and the reachable fleet (`ts1`, `ts2`, `css`, `csd`, `mac-mini-max`; `mac-mini-old` unreachable). Each pass superseded the prior one and they CONVERGED on the same root-cause clusters. This epic is the elaborated, self-contained execution graph for that convergence; the source markdown need not be re-read once these beads exist.

**Core thesis.** The session history does NOT support a single-cause story ("SQLite randomly corrupts"). It shows MULTIPLE independent failure classes that all surface to agents as the same opaque outcome ("Agent Mail is broken" / "database disk image is malformed"). Real B-tree corruption with measurable data loss coexists with: frankensqlite pragma false-positives, 0-byte-WAL false-positives, schema/migration drift, stale Python co-resident writers, TUI/runtime liveness gaps, lock contention with no owner intelligence, CLI/MCP name mismatch, reservation DB↔JSON drift, macOS TMPDIR symlink rejection, and host pressure. The product defect is that `am` collapses all of these into one scary message and does not (a) CLASSIFY the state, (b) record durable INTENT before failing, (c) offer a scope-bounded next SAFE command, or (d) tell agents when it is safe to continue read-only.

**The repeating bad workflow to eliminate.** Agent tries register/fetch_inbox/reserve/send/release → `am` fails opaquely → agent gives up, stops before editing, or cannot cleanly close out → doctor may help but its next action is not always exact, trustworthy, or safe to auto-apply. Downstream repos have started FORBIDDING agents from running `am doctor repair/reconstruct`/`am service restart` — a second-order signal that the default UX is not yet agent-proof.

**Desired end-state.** Every `am` failure: (1) names the state class (host pressure / DB corruption / schema drift / diagnostic false positive / service dead / TUI stuck / path-canonicalization), (2) durably records any required intent, (3) provides a one-command scope-bounded repair when one exists, (4) otherwise provides a read-only fallback + precise escalation summary. Doctor never prints a global integrity OK it has not earned. Health is multi-verdict. Reservation state is single-sourced and parity-checked.

**Structure.** 13 tracks (child epics A–M). Foundational/enabling tracks: M (frankensqlite pragma conformance) and L (regression fixtures + incident harness) underpin the corruption-authority work; A (typed taxonomy + diagnosis envelope) is the shared primitive consumed by health, degraded-mode, locks, and circuit-breaker work; G (schema gate) is the startup-correctness foundation.

**Hard constraints (from AGENTS.md).** Rust 2024 nightly; `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; asupersync only (NO tokio/reqwest/hyper); sqlmodel_rust/frankensqlite for DB; NEVER enable broadcast messaging; NEVER delete files without written permission; NEVER touch external sibling repos (frankensqlite/asupersync/etc.) — file gaps as beads instead. Verify with cargo check/clippy/test (offload via rch).
notes:
## DEFINITION OF DONE (applies to EVERY task in this program)

This was added after a plan-space review (2026-06-09). No task is "done" until ALL of the following hold — these are non-negotiable and exist BECAUSE the original failures went undetected for months:

1. **Inline unit tests (AGENTS.md testing policy).** Every new/changed code path ships `#[cfg(test)]` tests covering HAPPY path, EDGE cases (empty input, max values, boundary conditions, 0-byte/oversized sidecars, missing columns), and ERROR conditions. Tests run via `cargo test -p <crate>` and must be deterministic (asupersync `LabRuntime`/virtual time for anything concurrent — NO tokio, NO wall-clock sleeps).
2. **Realism floor (docs/VERIFICATION_COVERAGE_LEDGER.md).** A user-facing / transport / persistence / installer / search / crypto path may NOT claim closure on stub-only (R2/R3) evidence — it needs R0/R1 on the decisive dependency path. Corruption/health/reservation/degraded-mode paths are user-facing.
3. **E2E coverage.** Each track has a dedicated `tests/e2e/test_*.sh` script (Track N) with an explicit assertion count, an artifacts dir under `tests/artifacts/...`, and a pass/fail summary. New behavior that crosses the transport/CLI boundary is asserted there, not only in unit tests.
4. **Structured logging & detailed diagnostics (Track N2).** Every new diagnostic/health/degraded-mode/recovery code path emits structured `tracing` events (span + fields + latency) AND contributes to a capturable debug log artifact an agent can attach to an incident. "Great, detailed logging so we can be SURE everything works" is a first-class deliverable, not an afterthought. No `println!` debugging left behind.
5. **Quality gates clean.** `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (pedantic+nursery), `cargo fmt --check`, and `ubs` on changed files — all clean. Offload heavy builds via `rch exec -- ...`.
6. **Backward-incompatible by design is OK** (early dev, no users, no tech debt) BUT do NOT lose existing features/functionality while refactoring (e.g. all 15 doctor verbs, 37 tools, 25 resources, 16 TUI screens, 18 robot subcommands, dual-mode separation, no-broadcast safety must survive).

**Anti-oversimplification guard:** these beads describe the TARGET behavior. When implementing, prefer extending existing surfaces (doctor registry, robot envelopes, health_check) over parallel machinery; preserve the `mutate()` chokepoint, detect-then-fix purity, reversibility, and the no-broadcast rule.
close_reason: Program complete: every track (A-N) and every leaf bead closed with proof. The session-history root-causes now have durable regression coverage: typed corruption taxonomy, doctor purity/undo guarantees, health/selftest surfaces, live-owner locks, CLI/MCP surface corrections, reservation parity, schema/WAL gates, degraded-mode intents, TUI liveness contract, host-pressure evidence emitter, structured logging standards, the L1-L4 incident corpus, and the N13 one-command release gate (am e2e run --tag reliability --release-scorecard) certified 11/11 release_ready=true and documented as a release gate.

title: Track A — Corruption Diagnosis Authority & Typed Taxonomy
description:
**Goal.** Make `am`'s corruption verdicts authoritative and TYPED. Today every storage failure funnels into one string ("database disk image is malformed" / "Database corruption detected. Run 'am doctor repair' or 'am doctor reconstruct'") regardless of whether the underlying state is real B-tree corruption, a frankensqlite pragma limitation, a benign 0-byte WAL, schema drift, a busy lock, FD exhaustion, or host pressure. Agents then make bad decisions (run repair on a healthy DB, abandon coordination, etc.).

**Evidence (anchors).** Local `c488ee28...` proved `am doctor` reported FK-integrity "malformed" while canonical `sqlite3` returned integrity_check ok / quick_check ok / empty foreign_key_check, and a freshly created DB with no FKs still triggered it — a frankensqlite `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` gap, NOT on-disk corruption. mac-mini-max showed real B-tree page-6008 corruption with data loss in the SAME message class. ts1/ts2/css/csd showed `send_message`, `register_agent`, `file_reservation_paths`, `acknowledge_message`, `release_file_reservations`, `fetch_inbox`, `list_agents`, `macro_start_session` all failing with the identical opaque string.

**Code anchors.** `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/error.rs` (`DbError`, `is_corruption_error()` @~220, `is_mvcc_conflict()` @~207, `is_lock_error()` @~190); `crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/lib.rs` "Database corruption detected" recovery-fallback text.

**Output of this track.** A typed taxonomy + classifier, a structured diagnosis envelope embedded everywhere `am` currently says malformed/corrupt, a canonical-SQLite double-probe cross-check, a rule that forbids authoritative "malformed" from an engine that cannot answer the failing op, and corruption-class metrics. Depends on Track M (conformance) and feeds Tracks B, C, D, H, K.
close_reason: Track A — Corruption Diagnosis Authority & Typed Taxonomy COMPLETE. All children closed: A1 (taxonomy/classifier), A2 (structured envelope), A3 (canonical double-probe cross-check 96353bb2), A4 (authority chokepoint 0e4ab0d2), A5 (corruption-class metrics), A6/.1.6 (false-positive fix). The false-positive corruption class is now structurally closed at the reporting boundary.

title: A1: Typed corruption/error taxonomy + classifier
description:
**What.** Replace the single "database disk image is malformed" funnel with a typed taxonomy and a classifier that maps raw engine/IO errors + probe results into ONE of: `MainDbBtreeCorruption`, `WalSidecarCorruption`, `SchemaDriftOrMissingTables`, `EngineProbeLimitation` (frankensqlite cannot answer), `ForeignKeyInconsistency`, `FtsIndexCorruption`, `ConnectionOrConfigError`, `BusyRetryable`, `FdExhaustion`, `PoolExhaustion`, `LiveOwnerNoActivityLock`, `HostPressure`. Each variant carries: severity, `repairable`, `safe_to_retry`, `safe_to_continue_read_only`, `blocks_edits`, and a `recommended_command`.

**Why.** Every downstream track (health verdicts, degraded-mode intents, lock intelligence, circuit breaker, busy/backoff) keys off these classes. Today they all collapse into one scary string, so agents run repair on healthy DBs, abandon coordination, or cannot tell read-degraded from write-blocked.

**Code anchors.** Extend `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/error.rs` (`DbError`, `is_corruption_error`, `is_mvcc_conflict`, `is_lock_error`); thread through the `cli/src/lib.rs` recovery-fallback text and `McpError`.

**Considerations.** Classification must be conservative: never label `MainDbBtreeCorruption` unless an authoritative engine (Track M) confirmed it. Map "Too many open files" → `FdExhaustion`, "Resource temporarily busy" → `BusyRetryable`/`LiveOwnerNoActivityLock`, pool timeout → `PoolExhaustion`, "no such column"/"no such table" → `SchemaDriftOrMissingTables`.

**Acceptance.** Classifier unit tests over the L1/L2 fixtures asserting the correct variant for each historical anchor.

**Depends on M2 (authority), L1+L2 (fixtures).**
close_reason: Implemented conservative typed DB error classifier and MCP classification propagation; focused tests plus RCH remote check/clippy gates passed.

comments.author: ChartreuseCreek
comments.text: A1 implementation complete by ChartreuseCreek. title: A3: Canonical-SQLite double-probe cross-check
description:
**What.** On any corruption-class error, run a READ-ONLY canonical-SQLite cross-check: open the DB read-only/immutable, run quick_check, integrity_check, foreign_key_check, a schema-table probe, and an FTS probe if applicable. **Why.** At least one historical "malformed" incident was NOT proven on-disk; canonical probing returned ok while `am`'s DbConn path failed. Agents must stop being told "database corrupted" when the canonical probe says integrity_check=ok.

**Considerations.** Must be observationally pure (read-only/immutable open; no `-shm`/`-wal` creation) — shares the purity machinery with B2. Bounded/timeout-guarded so a sick host cannot hang the probe.

**Acceptance.** On the L1 FK false-positive fixture, the double-probe flips the verdict to engine-limitation; on a genuinely malformed B-tree fixture it confirms corruption. Tests assert both.

**Depends on M2, A1; shares purity with B2.**

title: am doctor health/WAL probes report false-positive corruption on healthy DBs (live evidence 2026-06-17)
description:
Live evidence from the 2026-06-17 asupersync-clock-bug incident: `am doctor health` repeatedly reported corruption verdicts on a DB that was provably HEALTHY, and the daemon's startup auto-reconstruct acted on them — rewriting storage.sqlite3 every ~10 min, which is itself a corruption-RISK surface on a healthy DB.

## Observed false positives (DB was fine)
1. `fail: live mailbox needs reconstruct: Health probes failed for .../storage.sqlite3 (possible corruption); ... next: am doctor reconstruct --dry-run` — while independent `PRAGMA integrity_check` = ok, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` = 0 rows, `am doctor write-selftest` 10/10 ok, `am doctor mcp-selftest` read_after_write ok, robot health circuit_breakers 'All circuits closed', quick_check OK.
2. `fail: live mailbox needs repair: SQLite WAL sidecar is header-only/truncated at .../storage.sqlite3-wal (32 bytes)` — a 32-byte WAL is a VALID header with zero frames (magic 0x377f0682), the normal state right after a checkpoint. `am doctor fix --dry-run` proposed NO WAL action ([SKIP] wal_mode already enabled), confirming nothing was wrong; after a clean stop the WAL had frames again (294 bytes). The probe raced a transient header-only WAL and called it 'truncated → needs repair'.

## Impact
- Operators/agents conclude the DB is corrupt (the original report that kicked this off was literally 'its SQLite DB is corrupt'). False alarms erode trust in every verdict.
- The daemon's auto-reconstruct/archive-reconcile loop fired on these false positives, rewriting the live DB repeatedly (forensics: storage.sqlite3.corrupt-* created seconds after each restart) — needless DB-rewriting on a healthy DB.

## Real underlying cause (for context; fixed separately)
The write failures that tripped these heuristics were NOT corruption — they were premature request-deadline cancellations of `pool.acquire` caused by an asupersync `wall_now()` dual-epoch clock bug (fixed in /dp/asupersync time/sleep.rs+driver.rs). The doctor mis-attributed an external cancellation/timeout to 'corruption'.

## Ask (fits Track A: A3 double-probe / A4 forbid-unsupported-engine-verdict)
- Require a canonical `integrity_check` (or the A3 canonical-SQLite double-probe) to PASS before any 'needs reconstruct'/'possible corruption' verdict OR any auto-reconstruct/archive-reconcile is triggered.
- Treat a benign header-only/0-frame WAL as healthy, not 'truncated/needs repair' (it's the normal post-checkpoint state); only flag a WAL whose header magic is invalid or whose frames are torn.
- Never let write-path cancellations/timeouts (SQLITE_BUSY, cx-cancelled pool acquire) funnel into the 'corruption' class.

## Code anchors
- crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/doctor/fixers/wal_shm_sidecar_drift.rs (HeaderOnlyWal signal; checkpoint(TRUNCATE) fixer)
- crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/doctor/mod.rs:~2519 test doctor_health_reports_truncated_wal_without_quarantine ('health must not quarantine WAL sidecars')
- crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/error.rs is_corruption_error()/is_lock_error() (per the A-track epic)
- the daemon startup health-gate that triggers auto-reconstruct on these verdicts
close_reason: Fixed: gated the cheap-probe corruption verdict on a canonical full integrity_check in doctor_database_fix_strategy_with_wal_cleanup (drives both am doctor health AND the daemon startup auto-reconstruct). A transient-class verdict ('possible corruption' quick_check result, or a non-lock sanity-probe error e.g. a cancelled pool acquire) is now re-probed with the authoritative canonical engine; a passing integrity_check downgrades Reconstruct/Repair->None and declines to rewrite a healthy DB (fail-safe: only downgrades on PROVEN health). Ask1 (confirm before reconstruct) + Ask3 (cancellations don't funnel into corruption) done; Ask2 (benign header-only/0-frame WAL) already handled by 55fe0e25 magic-aware wal_classify, verified. 5 deterministic tests; check+test(17/17)+fmt+clippy(-D, full workspace) green.

title: Track J — Host-Pressure & Version/Path-Drift Classification

title: Track K — Salvage, Snapshots & Corruption Circuit Breaker
description:
**Goal.** Make recovery prevention-first and loss-honest. `.recover` salvage is an emergency path, not an acceptable normal self-heal, and it loses data silently today.

**Evidence.** mac-mini-max: `.recover` salvage dropped messages 2997→2981 and recipients 6864→6844; original `file_reservations` could not even be counted (recovered 4507). The strongest local Rust session ("SQLite malformed image blocks inbox/ack/send") itself concluded the system needs: scheduled VACUUM+ANALYZE, periodic forced WAL checkpoint after normal op, corruption-specific metrics/alerting/circuit-breaker, a persistent last-known-healthy snapshot, checksummed WAL validation, and prevention knobs (`query_only`, `journal_size_limit`, after-large-transaction integrity probes) — all currently MISSING. css: old Python `fetch_inbox` hit `QueuePool limit of size 3 overflow 4 ... timeout 45` (pool exhaustion). ts1: `send_message` loop "Too many open files. Freed 1 cached repos. Retry" then "Freed 0 cached repos" — eviction freed nothing yet still told agents to retry.

**Code anchors.** recovery/salvage paths + "Full integrity_check" in `cli/src/lib.rs`; `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/pool.rs` (`DbPool`, repo cache); `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/metrics.rs`.

**Output.** Loss-honest salvage reporting, a last-known-healthy verified snapshot/rebuild lane, a DB-health circuit breaker, periodic safe maintenance policy, and pool/FD backpressure metrics + guidance.
close_reason: All children K1-K5 closed (loss-honest salvage, verified snapshot+recovery, DB-health circuit breaker, periodic maintenance policy, pool/FD backpressure metrics). Track K — Salvage, Snapshots & Corruption Circuit Breaker complete.

title: K1: Loss-honest salvage reporting
description:
**What.** When `.recover`/salvage runs, report loss EXPLICITLY: per-table row counts before AND after, which tables could not be counted, which rows were recovered with suspect types (e.g. TEXT id where i64 expected), and what archive replay can/cannot reconstruct. Frame `.recover` as an EMERGENCY path, not normal self-heal.

**Why.** mac-mini-max: `.recover` dropped messages 2997→2981 and recipients 6864→6844 silently; the original `file_reservations` could not even be counted. Doctor must never imply a clean recovery when data was lost.

**Code anchors.** salvage/recover path + integrity reporting in `cli/src/lib.rs`.

**Acceptance.** Salvage emits a before/after loss report incl. uncountable tables + suspect-type rows; the `.recover` TEXT-id recipient fixture (L1 #7) is handled without crashing and reported. Tests.
close_reason: Loss-honest salvage/recover reporting. recover_sqlite_file_with_storage_root now captures best-effort per-table row counts BEFORE recovery (count_salvage_rows, via a WAL-aware read-only temp copy so the malformed original is never opened RW) and AFTER (on the validated replacement before swap), then emits emit_salvage_loss_report to stderr for BOTH the backup-restore and archive-reconstruct branches. Report: per-table before->after, total ROWS LOST (only tables countable in both; growth not counted), tables that could NOT be counted pre-recovery (loss UNKNOWN, never silently zero), and suspect recovered rows (non-integer ids — detect_salvage_suspect_typed_rows catches the L1 #7 sqlite3 .recover TEXT-id recipient). Framed as EMERGENCY, not clean self-heal. 5 unit tests (count present/missing, non-sqlite uncountable, TEXT-id detection, clean db, pure loss diff incl. the 2997->2981 incident numbers). clippy + fmt clean.

title: K2: Last-known-healthy verified snapshot + archive-derived rebuild lane
description:
**What.** Maintain periodic VERIFIED-clean snapshots of the DB (with metadata: timestamp, integrity-verified, row counts) and an archive-derived rebuild path, so recovery restores from a known-good snapshot or rebuilds from the Git archive instead of relying on `.recover` as the first line of defense.

**Why.** The strongest local Rust session listed "no persistent last-known-healthy state snapshot" as a key gap; mac-mini-max proved `.recover` loses data. A verified snapshot lane makes recovery non-lossy in the common case.

**Acceptance.** Verified snapshots are produced + recorded; a recovery flow restores from the latest verified snapshot (or archive rebuild) and reports what it used. Tests with a corrupted-primary + good-snapshot fixture.
notes:
## REVISION (2026-06-09 review): reuse existing reconstruct/archive machinery, don't fork it
The verified-snapshot + archive-derived rebuild lane must INTEGRATE with the existing `am doctor reconstruct` / `am archive restore` surfaces and the canonical-ID-preservation fix (G5/B4), not create parallel recovery machinery. Snapshot restore is the fast path; archive rebuild is the deep path; both must preserve canonical message/reservation IDs and report what they used (per K1 loss-honesty). Snapshots must be integrity-verified (full check, B1) before being recorded as "known-healthy".
close_reason: Implemented last-known-healthy verified snapshot + snapshot-preferred recovery (K2), integrating with existing reconstruct/backup machinery (not forking). New db crate snapshot.rs: VerifiedSnapshotMetadata (created_us, integrity_verified, integrity_kind, schema_version, per-table row_counts, source/snapshot paths, binary_version) persisted as a JSON sidecar next to the .bak; latest_verified_snapshot() (verified+present gate, recomputes bak path so it's relocation-robust); restore_from_verified_snapshot() (re-verifies bak full integrity, staged copy + health-check, removes stale primary WAL/SHM before atomic rename — fast lossless recovery). pool.rs create_verified_snapshot(): runs FULL integrity check on the live DB, and only on Healthy refreshes the proactive .bak (reuses create_proactive_backup) + records the metadata sidecar; returns None (records nothing) when not verifiably clean so a corrupt DB is never recorded as known-good. integrity_guard.rs run_full_cycle now captures a verified snapshot when the periodic full check passes. cli recover_sqlite_file_with_storage_root now PREFERS the verified snapshot (fast path) before the generic backup / archive rebuild (deep path) and reports which source it used (K1 loss-honesty: verified-snapshot-restore mode + before/after counts). Metrics: snapshot_created/verify_failures/restored totals + last_verified_snapshot_us on DbMetrics (surface via am robot metrics resources.pool). Canonical-ID preservation (G5/B4) already handled by the archive-rebuild path; snapshot restore preserves IDs by construction (byte copy of the verified DB). Tests: snapshot lifecycle roundtrip, latest-verified gates, restore-recovers-corrupted-primary fixture, restore-returns-none-without-snapshot, create_verified_snapshot pool integration; 204 db-lib + 17 pool_exhaustion + 24 server green; fmt + clippy(-D) + check clean via rch.

title: K3: DB-health circuit breaker
description:
**What.** Add a circuit breaker: after a hard corruption-class error (A1), STOP normal writes, emit a structured finding (A2 envelope), and route agents to doctor / degraded-mode (Track H) rather than repeatedly hammering a corrupt DB.

**Why.** Listed as a missing piece ("no corruption-specific circuit breaker"). Without it, every subsequent tool call re-hits the corrupt DB and re-emits scary errors, and writes risk worsening damage.

**Code anchors.** wire to A1 classifier + A5 metrics; gate the write paths in `db/src/pool.rs`/`queries.rs`.

**Acceptance.** A simulated hard-corruption error trips the breaker; subsequent writes are refused with the structured finding + degraded-mode guidance; reads/doctor still allowed. Test.

**Depends on A1, A5.**
notes:
## REVISION (2026-06-09 second pass): breaker composes with degraded-mode intents
When the breaker trips, write attempts must ROUTE INTO Track H durable intents (queued-send/release-intent) rather than hard-erroring into a void — i.e. "writes refused" becomes "writes queued + here is the replay command", except where queuing is unsafe. Reads and doctor stay allowed. The breaker auto-RESETS (half-open probe) once a verified-healthy snapshot/repair (K2/B5) restores write capability, and emits A5 metrics on every trip/reset.
close_reason: Added corruption-specific sticky circuit breaker (crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/circuit_breaker.rs). Trips on hard edit-blocking corruption observed in run_with_mvcc_retry; subsequent async-server writes refused immediately with a corruption-class A2 envelope + 'am doctor repair/reconstruct' guidance (reads + CLI/doctor sync path unaffected). Self-heals on a clean integrity check. 14 breaker tests + 136 integrity/mvcc/retry regression green; clippy clean.

title: K4: Periodic safe maintenance policy (checkpoint/VACUUM/ANALYZE/integrity)
description:
**What.** Add bounded, opportunistic maintenance OUTSIDE latency-sensitive request paths: forced WAL checkpoint after normal operation, scheduled VACUUM + ANALYZE, optional full integrity-check scheduling, plus prevention knobs (`query_only` where appropriate, `journal_size_limit`, after-large-transaction integrity probe). Emit metrics for each.

**Why.** The local session listed missing scheduled VACUUM+ANALYZE, missing periodic checkpoint, and limited prevention knobs as gaps that plausibly let corruption-like symptoms recur.

**Acceptance.** Maintenance runs on a bounded schedule off the hot path with metrics; knobs configurable via env (`config.rs`). Tests assert scheduling + that hot-path latency is unaffected.
close_reason: Implemented periodic safe SQLite maintenance policy (K4) by extending the integrity-guard background worker (the existing off-hot-path SQLite maintenance thread). pool.rs: new analyze()/vacuum()/set_journal_size_limit() on the canonical SQLite engine (proven am-doctor-repair path) with bounded busy_timeout + :memory: no-op guards. integrity_guard.rs: run_db_maintenance_cycle() runs due tasks each loop tick — passive WAL checkpoint, ANALYZE, VACUUM on independent cadences + re-applied journal_size_limit; seeded at startup so first run is one interval out (no boot VACUUM storm); pure maintenance_task_due() makes the schedule unit-testable; failures recorded+retried, never fatal; runs only on the guard thread, never the request/dispatch hot path. metrics.rs: per-op run counters, shared failure counter, per-op last-run timestamp gauges, duration histogram (DbMetrics+snapshot) — these flow through DbMetricsSnapshot into am robot metrics (resources.pool) automatically. config.rs knobs: DB_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED, DB_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS(300), DB_ANALYZE_INTERVAL_SECS(6h), DB_VACUUM_INTERVAL_SECS(daily;0=disable), DB_JOURNAL_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES(256MiB). Integrity scheduling already lived in this worker (not duplicated). Tests: maintenance_task_due scheduling (pure), cycle gating+cursor back-off, analyze/vacuum/checkpoint/journal_size_limit on a real file pool + :memory: no-op; 50 core + 16 db + 24 server green; fmt/clippy(-D)/check clean via rch. Note: query_only read-pool pragma and after-large-txn integrity probe (lower-value prevention knobs needing hot-path hooks) deferred to keep this within risk budget.

title: ATC experience-ledger hard row ceiling (bounded eviction) — ts2 unbounded-growth killer
description:
**ts2 incident (the actual killer).** atc_experiences grew UNBOUNDED to 859K rows / 3.36 GB (91% of storage.sqlite3); high-churn writes corrupted SQLite ('page referenced multiple times') -> 5-23 GB memory runaway, never-binding startup, hung tools. Root cause: the only retention is age-based (retention_compact) and validate_retention_compaction enforces a 365-DAY FLOOR, so a high-churn table whose rows are all <365 days old is NEVER pruned. No count/byte ceiling, no automatic sweep.

**Fix (count-based hard ceiling).** Add enforce_experience_row_ceiling(pool, max_rows): when atc_experiences exceeds the configured cap, roll up + evict the OLDEST TERMINAL (resolved/censored/expired) rows down to a hysteresis target, reusing the existing retention_compact_with_conn transaction (preserves rollups + open rows). This is a SAFETY bound that takes precedence over the age-based fidelity window (rollups preserve the aggregate signal). Wire as a new maintenance op in integrity_guard.rs run_db_maintenance_cycle on its own cadence. New config: AM_ATC_EXPERIENCE_MAX_ROWS, AM_ATC_RETENTION_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS. Warn (don't crash) if open-row backlog keeps the table over cap.

**Acceptance.** Pure target/offset math unit-tested; integration test seeds >cap terminal rows and asserts the sweep evicts down to target while preserving rollups + open rows; over-cap-with-no-terminal-rows path warns and is a no-op. Sidecar isolation is the follow-up (br-bvq1x.11.x).
close_reason: Count-based hard ceiling (enforce_experience_row_ceiling) wired into integrity_guard maintenance; rolls up+evicts oldest terminal rows down to 90% hysteresis target, preserves open rows+rollups; config knobs added; clippy+tests green.

title: ATC experience sidecar DB (atc.sqlite3) — blast-radius isolation
description:
**Follow-up to br-bvq1x.11.6.** ATC experience IO already routes through canonical SQLite (queries.rs:1911 open_canonical_atc_conn — avoids the FrankenConnection page-corruption bug), and br-bvq1x.11.6 now bounds row growth. Remaining hardening: ISOLATE atc_experiences/atc_experience_rollups into a dedicated sidecar DB (e.g. <dir>/atc.sqlite3) so ATC churn/bloat/corruption can never affect the mail DB's VACUUM/integrity/backup/size, and so the sidecar is trivially droppable+rebuildable (ATC is pure telemetry).

**Single chokepoint makes this tractable:** all ATC experience IO flows through open_canonical_atc_conn(pool, purpose) (queries.rs) + ensure_file_backed_atc_pool_initialized. Redirect those to the sidecar path and create the ATC schema there.

**Cross-cutting work required (do carefully):**
1. Derive sidecar path from pool.sqlite_path() (sibling atc.sqlite3); create ATC schema (atc_experiences + atc_experience_rollups + indexes) in the sidecar on first open.
2. Schema migration: drop atc_experiences/atc_experience_rollups from the MAIN schema (v18) so existing installs reclaim space on the next VACUUM; sidecar starts fresh (no row migration — telemetry, acceptable to reset).
3. Recovery: reconstruct rebuilds the main DB from the archive; ATC is NOT in the archive, so the sidecar is independent — ensure reconstruct/quarantine don't touch or get confused by it; give the sidecar its own light integrity/drop-on-corrupt handling.
4. Share/export: confirm the scrub/bundle never includes atc.sqlite3 (it's a separate file; verify exclusion).
5. Backups: K2 verified-snapshot + proactive backups target the main DB; decide whether the sidecar is backed up (probably not — droppable).
6. Doctor: a sidecar-aware health line; ensure am doctor doesn't false-flag the new file.

**Acceptance.** ATC writes/reads/rollups/retention/ceiling all operate on atc.sqlite3; main storage.sqlite3 has no atc_* tables; reconstruct + share + backups verified unaffected; tests cover sidecar create/write/read/ceiling + main-DB has no atc tables.
close_reason: ATC telemetry isolated into atc.sqlite3 sidecar. Chokepoint open_canonical_atc_conn → sidecar; ensure_file_backed_atc_pool_initialized creates schema in WAL+0600; run_sqlite_init_once drops legacy atc_* from main. Reconstruct no longer materializes/salvages atc in main. Consumers (robot/tui/cli explain+simulate+reprocess) read the sidecar. Tests: new isolation test + reconstruct asserts no atc in main + storage soak (ceiling). All gates green (db 2687 pass, cli/server clippy, fmt, soak). Follow-ups: br-fv0s1.

title: Track L — Regression Fixtures & Incident-Corpus Harness
description:
**Goal.** Convert the exact historical incidents into a permanent regression suite so every release is tested against real fleet failures — not re-discovered in production. The failure modes are already NAMED; the missing piece is making the live CLI/server/TUI automatically do the sensible thing, which requires deterministic reproductions.

**Evidence / fixture inventory required.** FK false-positive on a fresh DB; 0-byte WAL; corrupt non-empty WAL "too small for header"; malformed B-tree pages (6008, 7811, 30, 27); freelist corruption; short-read page; `.recover` TEXT-id recipient rows (caused `am doctor fix` to crash `expected i64, found TEXT`); missing `messages.recipients_json`; missing required schema tables; legacy Python ISO-TEXT timestamps in integer columns; sqlite sidecar symlink; busy `ANALYZE`/`REINDEX`; rmcp JsonRpcMessage write-decode failure; CLI MCP-name mismatch matrix; too-many-open-files send loop; c8→c16 write-concurrency cliff; deterministic event-loop stall + ATC budget overrun.

**Output.** A corrupted-DB fixture corpus, protocol/CLI fixtures, concurrency + degraded-TUI fixtures, and a repeatable incident-corpus harness (the promotion of the scratch scanners) that emits "host pressure not corruption" evidence. This track is an ENABLER: Tracks A/B/F consume its fixtures.
close_reason: Track L complete: L1 corruption corpus (manifest + 12 fixtures + loader tests), L2 protocol/CLI-surface fixtures (name-mismatch matrix, decode-before-tool, FD-exhaustion classifier), L3 concurrency/degraded-TUI fixtures (mixed-load reproducer, 186ms render-stall heartbeat, ATC budget replay), L4 incident-corpus harness (tests/e2e/test_incident_corpus.sh, per-class scorecard with anchors, release_ready verdict). All four children closed with cargo/e2e proof.

title: L1: Corrupted-DB fixture corpus
description:
**What.** Build a curated, version-controlled corpus of small SQLite databases reproducing the exact on-disk pathologies seen in the fleet. Each fixture ships with a manifest: what it reproduces, the originating incident anchor, the expected typed classification (Track A), and whether canonical SQLite agrees.

**Fixtures (minimum).** (1) FK false-positive: a valid DB where frankensqlite `foreign_key_check` misfires; (2) 0-byte `-wal`; (3) corrupt non-empty WAL "too small for header during rebuild: read 0, need 32"; (4) malformed B-tree page with invalid page-type flag 0x00 (variants around pages 6008/7811/30/27); (5) freelist corruption ("freelist leaf page exceeds db_size"); (6) short read fetching page (got 0 of 4096); (7) `.recover` output with a recipient row whose id is TEXT (historically crashed `am doctor fix` with `expected i64, found TEXT`); (8) DB missing `messages.recipients_json`; (9) DB missing required tables (projects/agents/messages/message_recipients); (10) legacy Python ISO-8601 TEXT in integer timestamp columns; (11) sqlite sidecar symlink; (12) DB that makes `ANALYZE`/`REINDEX` fail busy/corrupt.

**Why.** The failure modes are already named across six passes; deterministic reproductions are the missing piece that lets every other track be tested instead of re-discovered in production.

**Considerations.** Keep fixtures tiny and generated/checked-in deterministically. Document generation steps. Do NOT point tests at any real `~/.mcp_agent_mail_git_mailbox_repo`.

**Acceptance.** Corpus directory + manifest; a loader used by M1, B6, F4, and Track A tests.

title: Track M — frankensqlite Pragma Conformance Lane
description:

title: M1: frankensqlite↔canonical pragma conformance harness
description:
**What.** Build a small, reproducible harness that runs IDENTICAL probes through (a) canonical/system SQLite and (b) the `am` DB layer (`DbConn = sqlmodel_frankensqlite::FrankenConnection`) against the SAME fixture databases AND intentionally corrupted variants, then diffs the verdicts. Cover every pragma/op `am doctor` relies on: `PRAGMA quick_check`, `PRAGMA integrity_check`, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check`, `PRAGMA foreign_key_list`, WAL metadata reads, `user_version`/schema_version reads, and FTS metadata.

**Why.** Local session `c488ee28...` proved frankensqlite reported a healthy DB (including a freshly created FK-free DB) as "database disk image is malformed" because its `foreign_key_check` path was wrong. Doctor cannot be authoritative on an engine whose pragma surface diverges from SQLite.

**Approach.** Fixtures come from Track L (L1). For each (fixture, pragma) pair record: canonical result, frankensqlite result, agree?(bool), and the raw error text. Emit a machine-readable conformance report. Mark each pragma as CONFORMANT / DIVERGENT / UNSUPPORTED for frankensqlite.

**Considerations.** frankensqlite is an external sibling repo — DO NOT edit it (AGENTS.md). This harness lives in the `am` tree (e.g. a dev-only test target / `mcp-agent-mail-db` test) and only OBSERVES frankensqlite. Use canonical SQLite via a read-only path; never let the harness itself mutate fixtures.

**Acceptance.** `cargo test` target that runs the matrix; a generated report enumerating per-pragma conformance; the foreign_key_check divergence reproduced and asserted as a known DIVERGENT entry (so a future frankensqlite fix flips it green).
