title: M2: Diagnostic fallback contract — never assert 'malformed' from an engine that cannot answer
description:

**Why.** Stops the single worst false-positive class (healthy DB declared corrupt) and is the precondition for Track A's double-probe (A3) and authority rule (A4).

title: Canonical full-check fallback in run_full_integrity_check (ts2 idx_nocase false-positive)
description:
**ts2 incident.** The background integrity-guard's 24h FULL cycle calls pool.run_full_integrity_check() -> integrity::full_check(&conn) with NO canonical second opinion (pool.rs:2643). frankensqlite evaluates COLLATE NOCASE index ordering differently than canonical SQLite, so PRAGMA integrity_check on idx_agents_project_name_nocase reports 'entries are out of order' — a FALSE POSITIVE (am doctor repair + system sqlite3 both report ok). The quick cycle is already protected via quick_check_with_canonical_fallback (GH#114); the full cycle is not.

**Fix.** Wire the SAME canonical-fallback logic (extract a shared pure helper) into run_full_integrity_check using CheckKind::Full. If frankensqlite full_check reports IntegrityCorruption but canonical SQLite agrees the file is ok, reclassify as healthy ('ok (canonical fallback)') and skip the recoverable-corruption escalation. This completes M2's contract for the full-check path and removes the false-reconstruct risk.

**Acceptance.** Pure helper unit-tested: primary=corrupt + canonical=ok -> Ok; primary=corrupt + canonical=corrupt -> Err; primary=corrupt + canonical=probe-error -> Err; primary=ok -> Ok. run_full_integrity_check no longer surfaces a corruption verdict the canonical engine disproves.
close_reason: Wired canonical full-check fallback into run_full_integrity_check via shared reconcile_with_canonical helper; 5 policy tests; clippy+tests green. Fixes ts2 idx_nocase false-positive.

title: Track B — Doctor Trust: Honest Integrity Labels & Detector Purity
description:
**Goal.** Treat `am doctor` as production code with its own threat model. title: B3: Doctor undo hardening (untrusted actions.jsonl, fsync idempotency, signed manifest)
description:

title: B5: Transactionally-safe / resumable doctor repair
description:
**What.** Make `am doctor repair` all-or-nothing OR explicitly resumable+machine-reported across its phases: backup, orphan-row cleanup, REINDEX, ANALYZE, WAL checkpoint, undo. Before any data-affecting cleanup, prove the DB+sidecars are in a state where the whole repair can commit or be reverted. Every phase emits a resumable/revertible plan agents can quote.

**Why.** mac-mini-max: repair cleaned orphan messages/recipients then FAILED `REINDEX` on corrupt WAL; another run failed `ANALYZE` with `database is busy` after backup+cleanup — partial-repair hazards that leave the DB in an unknown state.

**Acceptance.** Injecting a REINDEX/ANALYZE failure mid-repair (L1 fixture #12) leaves the DB either fully reverted or in a clearly-reported resumable state; never silently half-repaired. Test asserts the invariant.
close_reason: Transactionally-safe / resumable doctor repair. Root cause: handle_doctor_repair_with_options ran the data-affecting orphan-recipient cleanup (which COMMITs deletes) BEFORE the maintenance phase (VACUUM/ANALYZE/REINDEX/inbox_stats), and a maintenance failure (ANALYZE=database-is-busy, REINDEX on corrupt WAL — the mac-mini-max hazards) was bare-?-propagated, leaving a SILENTLY half-repaired DB in an unknown state. Fix: (1) capture the pre-repair backup as the verified revert point before any cleanup (already created in phase 2; now hoisted + recorded). (2) extracted the maintenance phase into run_doctor_repair_maintenance_phase() returning a phase-tagged DoctorMaintenancePhaseError. (3) on maintenance failure, emit a machine-quotable RESUMABLE report (doctor_repair_resumption_report): repair_status: resumable, failed phase + detail, committed-cleanup summary, and resume (am doctor repair) / revert (am doctor restore <backup>) / escalate (am doctor reconstruct) commands; return CliError::ExitCode(1) so it is never read as success. The committed cleanup is correct data, so we report-resumable rather than revert (re-running retries only the maintenance). Added a #[cfg(test)] thread-local fault hook (repair_maintenance_fault) to inject a phase failure deterministically. Tests: doctor_repair_maintenance_failure_leaves_resumable_state_not_silent (inject REINDEX fail => orphan cleanup committed [row gone, not reverted] + ExitCode(1) + fault-free re-run completes) and doctor_repair_resumption_report_is_machine_quotable (report content). title: Single-owner restart-coordination lock for am serve-http (ts2 restart-fighting)
description:
**ts2 incident.** When the server became unhealthy, a swarm of agents each ran am which tried to restart it; concurrent probe->kill->bind sequences killed each other's freshly-bound servers, wedging the mailbox in degraded_read_only with a stale lock. br-5mnkl (early bind) made /healthz answer fast (so a LIVE peer is refused-not-killed), but the concurrent-takeover race itself had no serialization.

**Fix.** A single-owner restart-coordination flock at <storage_root>/.am-restart.lock held for the serving process's lifetime. handle_serve_http calls coordinate_server_restart before the takeover/bind: the winner holds the lock and proceeds; concurrent invocations that find a live peer back off gracefully (exit, don't fight); --takeover seizes immediately (kill frees the holder's lock); on any lock-infra failure it fails open (proceed unlocked = today's behavior). Pure decide_restart_coordination policy + flock contention are unit-tested.

**Acceptance.** decide_restart_coordination covers acquired/peer-live/takeover/keep-waiting; coordinate_server_restart returns Proceed+lock when free, ProceedUnlocked under --takeover when held, ProceedUnlocked after timeout when held with no peer; handle_serve_http exits gracefully on PeerAlreadyServing. clippy+tests green.

**Follow-up:** stale .am-restart.lock cleanup is automatic (flock releases on holder death); a richer single-process-owner model is Track I (I4).

title: Track F — Reservation Atomicity & DB↔Archive Parity
description:
**Goal.** Make file-reservation state single-sourced. `file_reservation_paths` writes BOTH SQLite and the Git/JSON archive and they diverge independently, so conflict checks run against the wrong holder.

**Evidence.** GitHub `mcp_agent_mail_rust#112` ("File reservation API: DB↔JSON drift on agent_id and released_ts (3 independent bugs)"): an audit of 196 reservations found 52% stale `agent_id` rows and 10% stuck-NULL/stale `released_ts`. ts2 `release_file_reservations` failed with malformed B-tree page 2288 while multiple agents waited on advisory locks; closeout proceeded via a Beads-only workaround. css/ts2: release failing like acquire amplifies a DB failure into stale-lock contention for OTHER agents.

**Code anchors.** `crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/reservations.rs:385` (`file_reservation_paths`), `release_file_reservations`, `force_release_file_reservation`; dual-write via `try_dispatch_archive_write()` in `tools/src/identity.rs:19`; DB writes via `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/queries.rs`.

**Output.** A single reservation mutation chokepoint (DB txn + archive reconcile), a per-field DB↔archive parity checker surfaced in doctor health, idempotent/parity-aware release, and regression fixtures from the 196-reservation audit. Release-when-DB-unavailable is covered jointly with Track H.

title: F1: Single reservation mutation chokepoint (DB txn + archive reconcile)
description:
**What.** Route ALL reservation mutations (acquire/renew/release/force-release) through one chokepoint that performs a DB transaction and an archive write/reconcile protocol so SQLite and the Git/JSON archive cannot diverge independently. Define the canonical ordering + reconcile-on-replay semantics (which store is authoritative, how a half-applied write is healed).

**Why.** `mcp_agent_mail_rust#112`: `file_reservation_paths` writes BOTH stores and they diverge — an audit of 196 reservations found 52% stale `agent_id` and 10% stuck-NULL/stale `released_ts`, causing conflict checks against the wrong holder. A single chokepoint is the structural fix.

**Acceptance.** A crafted crash between DB-commit and archive-write reconciles to a consistent state on next access (no wrong-holder); test injects the gap and asserts convergence.

title: F3: Idempotent, parity-aware release_file_reservations
description:
**What.** Make `release_file_reservations` idempotent and parity-aware across DB + archive: releasing an already-released lease is a no-op success; release reconciles both stores; release must NOT fail the same way acquire does. When the DB is unavailable, hand off to the Track H durable release-intent path instead of erroring into a void.

**Why.** ts2/css/Gemini: release failing with malformed-B-tree amplified the failure into stale-lock contention for OTHER agents and blocked closeout. Release is a critical path that must degrade gracefully.

**Acceptance.** Double-release is a clean no-op; release reconciles drift; DB-unavailable release records a replayable intent (H1). Tests for each.

**Depends on F1, H1.**
notes:
## REVISION (2026-06-09 review): replay must re-validate, never blindly release
When a queued release-intent (H1) is replayed, it MUST re-validate current state before applying: if the lease was already released, or RE-ACQUIRED by a different agent in the interim, the replay becomes a no-op + a surfaced notice — it must NOT force-release a lease another agent now legitimately holds. This mirrors the project's "inspect before takeover" handoff philosophy and prevents degraded-mode recovery from causing the very conflicts reservations exist to prevent.

title: Track G — Schema Gate, WAL/Sidecar & Startup Invariants
description:
**Goal.** Every process that opens the DB for normal operation must pass ONE schema gate before accepting traffic, normal startup must run the FULL migration set, WAL mode + busy_timeout must be set from one path, and WAL/SHM sidecar states must be tightly classified (never hiding real corruption, never crying wolf on benign ones).

**Evidence.** `no such column: m.recipients_json` — existing DBs never received v10–v15 migrations (`v15_add_recipients_json_to_messages`, `v15b_backfill_recipients_json`, `v15c_trg_messages_default_recipients_json`) because pool startup called only `migrate_to_latest_base`, which FILTERED OUT those fragments; full `migrate_to_latest` ran only in tests/legacy import. `run_sqlite_init_once` left `journal_mode='DELETE'` while later pool code assumed WAL. 0-byte WAL was treated as a truncated artifact (false positive, fixed in `2cdc18e7`); header-only WAL surfaced as "WAL file too small for header during rebuild"; stale-WAL checkpointing immediately preceded CPU/probe failure on local and mac. title: G1: Single startup schema gate for every DB-opening path
description:
**What.** Add ONE schema gate that every process opening the DB for normal operation (CLI verbs, MCP server, TUI, robot) passes through BEFORE accepting traffic. It validates: `user_version`, required tables, required columns, critical indexes, triggers, FTS tables, migration-ledger consistency, and application_id if available. Old schema → migrate via one path (G2); future/unknown schema → REFUSE with "upgrade this binary"; too-old-and-unmigratable → refuse with the exact migration command. Fail with a precise action rather than letting a later query report "no such column"/"malformed".

**Why.** `no such column: m.recipients_json` made a healthy DB look corrupt because startup skipped v10–v15 migrations. Every DB-opening path needs the SAME gate so this cannot vary by entrypoint.

**Code anchors.** `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/schema.rs` (migration list `:2365`, `enforce_base_mode_cleanup_async :3217`); `db/src/pool.rs` open path.

**Acceptance.** Opening the L1 missing-recipients_json / missing-tables fixtures stops at the gate with a precise migrate/upgrade message; opening a future-schema fixture refuses with "upgrade binary". Tests for each.

**Depends on G2, G3.**

title: G4: WAL/SHM sidecar classification + policy
description:
**What.** Tightly classify sidecar states and apply a safe policy that never hides real corruption: distinguish (a) benign 0-byte/idle WAL, (b) malformed non-empty WAL, (c) header-only/too-small WAL ("too small for header during rebuild"), (d) stale WAL needing checkpoint, (e) live-sidecar-blocks-recovery, (f) orphan sidecar, (g) sidecar symlink, (h) sidecar mtime drift. Checkpoint safely only when valid; REFUSE checkpoint/repair while another live writer owns the DB; log before/after sidecar sizes on every doctor action. Add checksummed WAL validation.

**Why.** 0-byte WAL was a false positive (fixed `2cdc18e7`); header-only WAL surfaced as a rebuild error; stale-WAL checkpointing IMMEDIATELY preceded CPU/probe failure on local and mac; live sidecars blocked recovery and a checkpoint attempt produced a malformed image. Sidecar handling is a root-cause surface.

**Code anchors.** WAL handling in `cli/src/lib.rs` recovery path; doctor `wal_mode_disabled.rs`; the historical FM `wal-shm-sidecar-drift` (P0, was not auto-fixed).

**Acceptance.** Each L1 WAL fixture (0-byte, too-small-header, stale, symlink) is classified correctly; checkpoint refused while a live writer holds the DB; before/after sizes logged. Tests per state.

**Depends on L1; coordinates with D2 (live-owner).**
close_reason: Implemented WAL/SHM sidecar classification + safe-checkpoint policy (G4) as a new db crate module wal_classify.rs (reuses pool sidecar inspection, D2 live-owner detection, and the truncate checkpoint — no forked WAL path). classify_wal_sidecar() returns a precise state: NoSidecar / IdleEmpty (benign 0-byte) / HeaderOnlyOrTruncated (1..=32B, 'too small for header') / MalformedHeader (>32B bad magic-or-checksum) / StaleNeedsCheckpoint (valid header + committed frames) / Symlink (never followed) / Orphan (sidecar without primary), plus orthogonal live_writer_present (e) and wal_mtime_drift_secs (h) signals. wal_header_verdict() validates the 32-byte WAL header magic (0x377f0682/0683) AND recomputes the SQLite header checksum in the magic-dictated endianness (verified against a real engine-written WAL — caught + fixed an inverted bit0 endianness). recommended_action()/safe_checkpoint(): REFUSE all sidecar mutation while a live writer owns the DB (inspect_mailbox_ownership.blocks_mutation), checkpoint ONLY a valid stale WAL, quarantine-recommend damaged/symlink/orphan, and log WAL sidecar size before/after every action. Acceptance met: 0-byte/too-small-header/stale/symlink each classified correctly, checkpoint refused under a live writer, before/after sizes logged. 12 tests incl. real committed-WAL validation, corrupted-body checksum mismatch, symlink, orphan, live-writer override, and safe_checkpoint shrink. fmt + clippy(-D, all-targets) clean via rch. The safe primitives (classify_wal_sidecar/safe_checkpoint) are pub and ready for doctor/recovery non-owner adoption (kept out of the owner's own integrity-guard maintenance, which must not self-refuse); the existing detect-only wal_shm_sidecar_drift FM remains the complementary doctor surface.

(2) Ensure reconstruct/import paths PRESERVE canonical IDs (message IDs, reservation identity) — INSERT must include `id` so SQLite autoincrement does not reassign, and archive filename matching must be tight enough to avoid false-positive consistency findings after remap.

**Why.** Startup consistency checks produced false positives because reconstruct/remap changed IDs and filename matching was too loose; backfill-skip left search empty. Both make a healthy system look broken or silently change identity.

title: Track H — Durable Degraded-Mode Intents
description:
**Goal.** When the mailbox DB is unavailable/corrupt/locked, coordination verbs must record durable, replayable INTENT instead of failing into a void — and tell agents exactly what is safe to do next.

**Evidence.** ts2 2026-06-05: `release_file_reservations` AND `send_message` AND `fetch_inbox` AND `list_agents` all failed malformed in one work stream; the agent could push code but could not cleanly close out or release leases — amplifying the failure into stale-lock contention for peers. Across the fleet agents responded "rationally" by abandoning Agent Mail and writing coordination facts to Beads/comments instead, defeating the system's purpose.

**Design.** `release_file_reservations` → append-only local release-intent artifact, replayed after recovery. `send_message` → local queued-send artifact clearly marked unsent-until-replay + printed replay command. `acknowledge_message`/closeout-adjacent verbs → similar safe-to-replay intent logs where semantics allow. `am robot status` shows queued intents + the replay command. If reservations cannot be written, emit "do not edit files requiring reservation" + the exact fallback lane; if only reads are degraded, say so SEPARATELY.

**Output.** Durable intent logs for release/send/ack, a robot-visible queued-intent surface + replayer, and an agent-safe degraded-mode contract. Consumes Track A classification.

title: H1: Durable release-intent log + replay
description:
**What.** When `release_file_reservations` cannot reach the DB (corrupt/locked/unavailable), append a durable, replayable LOCAL release-intent artifact (append-only, signed/hash-stamped) and return a clear "lease release queued because DB unavailable" status. Replay queued releases automatically once the DB is healthy.

**Why.** ts2: release failing malformed amplified into stale-lock contention for peers; agents could not cleanly hand off. A durable intent prevents a DB outage from cascading into coordination deadlock.

**Acceptance.** DB-unavailable release writes an intent + reports queued status; recovery replays it; double-replay is idempotent. Tests over an injected DB-unavailable state.
notes:
## REVISION (2026-06-09 second pass): intent artifacts are a security surface
Intent artifacts may contain message bodies / paths / agent identity, so: write them under the storage root with restrictive perms (0600), never in world-readable temp; honor the E5 token-handle redaction contract for anything surfaced in `am robot status`; and make them auditable (they land in Git on replay exactly like a normal artifact). The intent log itself must survive process death (fsync on append).
close_reason: Implemented durable release_file_reservations degraded intent log in reservations.rs: DB-unavailable release writes a storage-root local JSONL intent with 0600 log / 0700 dir perms, content hash validation, fsync on append, queued response fields, best-effort replay on the next healthy release_file_reservations call, release archive write reuse, and idempotent replay suppression. Evidence: cargo test -p mcp-agent-mail-tools release_intent -- --nocapture; cargo fmt --check; cargo check --workspace --all-targets; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings.

title: H2: Durable queued-send artifact + replay command
description:
**What.** When `send_message` fails because the mailbox is corrupt/locked (especially during closeout), create a durable local pending-message artifact clearly marked UNSENT-until-replay, and print the exact replay command. Never silently drop a closeout message.

**Why.** ts2 2026-06-05: send + release + inbox + list all failed malformed; the agent pushed code but could not communicate status. A queued-send keeps the audit trail intact and lets the message land on recovery.

**Acceptance.** DB-corrupt send produces a marked pending artifact + replay command; replay sends it once healthy; artifact is auditable. Tests.

**Depends on A1 (classification of when to queue).**
notes:
## REVISION (2026-06-09 review): queued sends preserve safety + provenance
A queued-send artifact preserves the full envelope (to/cc/bcc, subject, thread_id, ack_required, importance) and on replay goes through the SAME validated path — it must NOT bypass AGENTS.md RULE 2 (broadcast remains forbidden) and must not duplicate-send (idempotent via content hash). The artifact is clearly marked UNSENT and is auditable in Git once replayed, identical to a normal send.
close_reason: Implemented durable CLI queued-send artifacts and am mail replay-queued. Artifacts are marked UNSENT_UNTIL_REPLAY, omit sender tokens, preserve the send envelope, print an exact replay command, replay through the normal send path, and use content-hash receipts to prevent duplicate sends. Proof: cargo fmt --check passed locally; RCH cargo test -p mcp-agent-mail-cli queued_send -- --nocapture passed (3 tests); RCH cargo clippy -p mcp-agent-mail-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings passed. Separate RCH cargo check -p mcp-agent-mail-cli --all-targets was attempted but blocked by RCH-E324 dependency preflight with local fallback refused.

title: H3: Durable ack/closeout intents + robot-visible queued-intent surface
description:
**What.** Extend durable-intent logging to `acknowledge_message` and closeout-adjacent verbs where replay semantics are safe, and surface ALL queued intents (release/send/ack) + their replay command in `am robot status`.

**Why.** Completes the degraded-mode story so agents can SEE what is pending and how to flush it, rather than re-inventing per-incident workarounds.

**Acceptance.** Queued intents appear in `am robot status` with the replay command; ack replay is idempotent. Tests.

**Depends on H1, H2.**
notes:
## REVISION (2026-06-09 review): one replay command + safety preamble
Provide ONE `am ... replay-intents` command (dry-run by default) that re-validates and flushes all queued release/send/ack intents, plus the `am robot status` surface listing them. Dry-run prints exactly what WOULD replay and what would become a no-op (already-released / re-acquired / already-sent). This is the agent-facing close of the degraded-mode loop.

title: Coalescer self-heals broken archive HEAD (bad/missing object) instead of wedging — ts2
description:
**ts2 incident.** A hard reboot interrupted git maintenance, leaving the archive's main pointing at a missing/corrupt object (fatal: bad object HEAD) + 1,327 tmp_pack_* files. resolve_head_commit_oid (storage/lib.rs) only treats UnbornBranch/NotFound as recoverable; other peel failures propagate, so commit_paths/reset_index_to_head error on every drain and the async commit coalescer wedges FOREVER (no new mail committed), blocking self-heal.

**Core fix.** Make resolve_head_commit_oid resilient: when HEAD resolves to a ref whose target commit object is genuinely unloadable (missing/corrupt in the ODB), treat the branch as unborn (Ok(None)) so the next commit re-roots onto the intact working tree (mail files are preserved), instead of erroring forever. Gate on a positive 'target object is absent' check (refname_to_id(HEAD) -> find_object fails) so transient errors still propagate.

**Acceptance.** Unit test: build a repo with a commit, corrupt refs/heads/<branch> to a bogus SHA, assert resolve_head_commit_oid returns Ok(None) and a subsequent commit_paths succeeds (re-roots, HEAD peelable again). Normal + unborn cases unchanged.

**Follow-up (separate bead):** doctor FM HeadPointsToMissingObject (proactive detection) + stale tmp_pack_* quarantine FM + coalescer persistent-failure circuit breaker that triggers archive self-heal.
close_reason: Coalescer self-heals broken archive HEAD: heal_unloadable_head deletes a refs/heads/* ref with a missing/corrupt tip so commit paths re-root onto the working tree; covers commit_paths/commit_all (via reset_index_to_head) + commit_paths_lockfree hot path; regression test green.

title: Git-archive recovery hardening: doctor bad-object-HEAD FM + tmp_pack quarantine + coalescer circuit breaker (ts2 follow-up)
description:

1. **Doctor FM 'HeadPointsToMissingObject'.** missing_head_or_broken_git_shape::inspect_head currently reads the HEAD file but never verifies the SHA exists in the ODB, so a detached/branch HEAD pointing at a missing object passes as 'valid'. Add a repo.find_object(sha) probe -> new BrokenShape variant + remediation (reset/rebuild). Proactive detection so an operator sees it before the coalescer hits it.
2. **Stale tmp_pack_* quarantine FM.** A hard reboot during gc/repack left ~1,327 .git/objects/pack/tmp_pack_* files. No FM scans for them today (grep: zero matches). Add a doctor FM that quarantines stale tmp_pack_* (older than N seconds) via the mutate() chokepoint (reversible, per RULE 1).
3. **Coalescer persistent-failure circuit breaker.** wbq_execute_op retries 3x then sets durability_degraded with NO recovery trigger. After K consecutive non-retryable commit failures on the same archive, fire archive self-heal (boot_check/reconstruct) / surface an actionable error instead of silently degrading.

**Acceptance.** doctor detects a HEAD->missing-object fixture and a stale-tmp_pack fixture; coalescer escalates after K persistent failures with a test.

title: ATC: Comprehensive test coverage — unit tests, edge cases, and E2E integration
description:
# ATC Test Coverage Hardening

## Problem
The ATC has 101 unit tests covering the happy paths, but significant
edge cases, boundary conditions, and integration scenarios are untested.
The E2E test script (test_atc.sh) only checks CLI flags — it doesn't
exercise the ATC inside a running server with real DB queries.

## Scope
Three categories of missing coverage:
1. **Unit test gaps** — edge cases and boundary conditions for existing code
2. **Missing feature tests** — windowed session summaries (bead spec but not implemented)
3. **E2E integration** — ATC running inside a live server with real events

## Success Criteria
- Every public function/method has at least one dedicated test
- Edge cases (zero, negative, overflow, empty) covered
- E2E script exercises the ATC with real server + DB
- All tests use sqlite:///:memory: (no real DB flakiness)
- Detailed logging on failure (full state dump)

title: P1: Serialize verified-snapshot publication, selection, restore, and retention
description: Verified snapshot bytes rotate and publish separately from canonical metadata, while quick refresh, verified creation, restore selection, and cold-start retention have no shared cross-process authority lock. Content-addressed selection now preserves crash discoverability, but concurrent actors can still race metadata replacement, candidate enumeration, and retention eviction. Add a persistent secure no-follow per-primary snapshot lock plus a keyed in-process lock, and hold it across generation inspection, rotation/publication, metadata settlement, selection/staging, and retention pin decisions without nesting recovery admission.
acceptance_criteria: Same-process and child-process tests prove mutual exclusion. Symlink and hard-link lock sentinels remain byte-identical. Nested verified creation cannot self-deadlock. Failure after each publication boundary leaves either the prior or new verified generation selectable. Concurrent creators cannot regress metadata, foreign/future metadata cannot be clobbered, and retention cannot evict the selected authority. Workspace check, clippy -D warnings, fmt, and focused tests pass.

title: Investigate Beads DB integrity mismatch: br doctor passes while raw sqlite integrity_check reports comment/index corruption
description:
After repairing br-uaa06 by rebuilding and promoting a fresh canonical .beads/beads.db from synchronized issues.jsonl, the user-facing failure is gone: default 'br show', 'br sync --status', 'br doctor', and close/export workflows all succeed again. However, raw SQLite checks still report structural problems on both the old canonical DB and the rebuilt temp DB.

Observed behavior on /data/projects/mcp_agent_mail_rust:
- 'br doctor --json' reports sqlite.integrity_check=ok
- 'sqlite3 .beads/beads.db "pragma quick_check; pragma integrity_check;"' reports repeated 'NULL value in comments.created_at' plus missing rows from idx_comments_created_at / idx_comments_issue and idx_issues_list_active_order
- the rebuilt temp DB created via 'br sync --import-only --rebuild --json --db .beads/beads.db.rebuild_20260312T110100Z --no-auto-import --no-auto-flush' shows the same raw SQLite warnings

This suggests either:
1. br doctor is masking/ignoring a class of integrity failures, or
2. the JSONL import path reconstructs comments/index state that SQLite itself still considers invalid (possibly missing comment created_at backfill or index maintenance).

Follow-up objective:
- determine whether the warnings are benign legacy artifacts or a real latent bug in Beads import/doctor
- identify why rebuilt DBs still inherit the issue from JSONL
- make doctor and raw SQLite integrity surfaces agree, or explicitly document/waive the discrepancy if intentional

Useful repro commands:
- br doctor --json
- sqlite3 .beads/beads.db "pragma quick_check; pragma integrity_check;"
- sqlite3 .beads/beads.db "pragma table_info(comments);"
- br sync --import-only --rebuild --json --db .beads/tmp.db --no-auto-import --no-auto-flush
- sqlite3 .beads/tmp.db "pragma quick_check; pragma integrity_check;"

title: R3.3: Implement am robot message <id> — single message with thread position, adjacent messages, sender info

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# R3.3: `am robot message <id>`

## What
Single message with full context: body, thread position, adjacent messages, sender info.
Useful when an agent has a message ID from an alert or inbox and wants to understand context.

## Data Collection
1. Fetch the target message by ID
2. Fetch sender info (program, model) from agents table
3. Fetch thread context: total messages in thread, position of this message
4. Fetch previous message summary (same thread, created_at < this message, LIMIT 1 DESC)
5. Fetch next message summary (same thread, created_at > this message, LIMIT 1 ASC)
6. Fetch attachment list for this message

## Output Format (Markdown default)
```markdown
## Message #201 | Thread: FEAT-123 (3 of 8)

**From**: BlueLake (claude-code, opus-4.6)
**To**: RedFox, GreenCastle
**Subject**: [FEAT-123] JWT implementation plan
**Importance**: high | **Ack**: required (pending)
**Sent**: 2026-02-11T08:30:00Z (2h ago)

---

I'm taking on the authentication feature. Planning to use JWT with JWKS rotation.

Will need to modify:
- src/auth/**
- src/middleware/**
- tests/auth/**

Please review the approach and ack.

---

**Attachments**: 1
- api_spec.json (8KB, application/json)

**← Previous**: #200 RedFox: "I'll handle the middleware setup"
**→ Next**: #202 RedFox: "Sounds good, releasing middleware reservations"
```

## Output (TOON)
```
message.id: 201
message.thread: FEAT-123
message.position: 3 of 8
message.from: BlueLake
message.from_program: claude-code
message.from_model: opus-4.6
message.to: RedFox,GreenCastle
message.subject: [FEAT-123] JWT implementation plan
message.importance: high
message.ack_status: required (pending)
message.age: 2h
message.body: |
  I'm taking on the authentication feature...

attachments[1]{name,size,type}:
  api_spec.json,8KB,application/json

context.previous: #200 RedFox: I'll handle the middleware setup
context.next: #202 RedFox: Sounds good, releasing middleware reservations
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- Full message body always included
- Thread position correct (e.g., "3 of 8")
- Previous/next messages show summary (truncated to 60 chars)
- Sender info includes program and model
- Attachments listed with size and type
- Works for first message in thread (no previous)
- Works for last message in thread (no next)

title: P1: OMP project-only setup must honor effective project-config disablement
description: OMP removes every project-level MCP source when its effective mcp.enableProjectConfig setting is false. Agent Mail project-only setup/status currently writes and validates .omp/mcp.json plus the active user mcp.json denylist, but does not inspect the effective config.yml setting. Therefore am setup run/status --agent omp --no-user-config and startup self-heal can cache/report healthy even though OMP will never load the only Agent Mail entry.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve the same active-profile/user/project config.yml authority and precedence as the supported OMP runtime. In project-only mode, effective mcp.enableProjectConfig=false must produce deterministic runtime-relevant drift, actionable remediation that does not repeat --no-user-config, and a cache fingerprint/status observation bound to the exact authority bytes. Malformed/unreadable authority fails closed. Tests cover default true, explicit false at each effective layer, precedence override, named profile/env override, ABA/cache invalidation, dry-run read-only behavior, and explicit non-OMP exclusion. README documents the contract and exact source boundary.
notes: Fresh-eyes upstream trace at exact OMP SHA eab72e88e447a4be45bea2bc302995844c0c51a2 found a remaining legacy authority: when active config.yml/config.yaml are absent, Settings.#migrateFromLegacy reads active-agent settings.json and agent.db before writing config.yml. Current status authority does not observe either source, so a legacy mcp.enableProjectConfig=false can be missed before first OMP startup. Model settings.json or fail closed on it, and either model agent.db settings or explicitly fail closed on a decisive legacy DB authority; bind observations into the fingerprint. Exact source: packages/coding-agent/src/config/settings.ts lines 1224-1232 and 1491-1525.

title: Adapt WBQ commit coalescing to queue pressure and disk health
description:
Goal: make the write-behind archive commit coalescer adapt its flush cadence to queue depth, disk health, and operator latency budgets.

Rationale: commit coalescing already prevents commit storms, but static timing leaves performance on the table under both tiny and enormous swarms. A simple feedback controller can flush faster when durability lag matters and batch longer when storms would cause git/disk churn.

Scope: start in shadow/metrics mode, then gate adaptive behavior behind config. Do not weaken graceful shutdown flush guarantees.

Fallback/safe mode: if controller metrics are unavailable or unstable, use current static cadence.

Acceptance: controller design note, bounded flush-delay proof, tests for shutdown/drain behavior, stress test with bursty message/reservation writes, and metrics showing batching ratio plus max archive lag.
notes: Idea-wizard refinement pass: closure evidence should follow docs/VERIFICATION_COVERAGE_LEDGER.md. Prefer R0/R1 real-path evidence for transport, persistence, search, robot/operator, and load-lab claims. Performance acceptance should report p50/p95/p99 plus CPU/RSS/DB-query or queue-depth evidence where applicable. Test/repro workloads must use isolated STORAGE_ROOT and must not touch the operator mailbox. Stub-only tests can support design confidence but do not close user-facing or persistence/performance claims.
close_reason: Adaptive archive commit coalescing landed with shadow metrics, docs, and stress proof.

title: share verify_bundle (chunked mode) didn't verify the standalone mailbox.sqlite3 the exporter still ships alongside chunks — swap gap
close_reason: Found in the fresh-eyes review of br-wr8ym (independent agent flagged it). A chunked bundle ships BOTH chunks/*.bin AND the standalone mailbox.sqlite3 (maybe_chunk_database never removes it). verify_database_payload only verified the chunks in chunked mode, so a swapped standalone mailbox.sqlite3 (chunks left intact) left database_verified=true — a consumer that loads the standalone DB would get attacker content while verify reported green. Fix: factored out verify_db_file_against_hash; chunked mode now verifies the reassembled chunks AND the standalone DB (both must equal the signed db_sha256, which by construction they do for a legit bundle); non-chunked behavior unchanged (absent DB → not-checked, for encrypted/metadata-only bundles). New regression test chunked_bundle_verifies_both_chunks_and_standalone_database (pristine passes; standalone-swap fails; chunk-swap fails). 63 crypto tests green, clippy -D + fmt clean.

ATC Track 1: Decision Core — Expected-Loss Engine
description:
# Track 1: Decision Core (Expected-Loss Minimization)

## Graveyard Source: §0.8 Runtime Decision Core (Bayes + Loss + Calibration)

## What
The mathematical heart of the ATC. Every decision the ATC makes — whether to
intervene in a conflict, declare an agent dead, or route a message — flows
through this single decision engine. No hardcoded thresholds anywhere.

## Why Expected-Loss Instead of Rules
Rules ("if no message in 20 min, release reservations") are:
- Brittle: the right threshold depends on context (refactoring agent vs. chatty agent)
- Binary: they trigger or don't, no gradualism
- Unauditable: you can't explain WHY a threshold was chosen

Expected-loss minimization:
- Adapts: posterior beliefs update with evidence
- Graduated: actions have costs proportional to state uncertainty
- Auditable: every decision logs the posterior, loss matrix, and chosen action

## Core Interfaces

```rust
/// Discrete state the ATC believes an entity is in.
trait AtcState: Copy + Eq + Hash {}

/// Action the ATC can take.
trait AtcAction: Copy + Eq + Hash {}

/// The decision policy: posterior estimation + loss-minimizing action selection.
struct DecisionCore<S: AtcState, A: AtcAction> {
    /// Loss matrix: L[action][state] = cost of taking action when true state is state
    loss_matrix: HashMap<(A, S), f64>,
    /// Current posterior belief over states
    posterior: HashMap<S, f64>,
}

impl<S: AtcState, A: AtcAction> DecisionCore<S, A> {
    /// Update posterior given new evidence (Bayesian update with likelihood).
    fn update_posterior(&mut self, evidence: &Evidence);

    /// Choose the action minimizing expected loss:
    /// a* = argmin_a Σ_s L(a,s) * P(s|evidence)
    fn choose_action(&self) -> (A, f64); // (best_action, expected_loss)
}
```

## Three Loss Matrices

### Conflict Intervention
| Action \ State | no_conflict | mild_overlap | severe_collision |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ignore | 0 | 15 | 100 |
| advisory_message | 3 | 1 | 8 |
| force_reservation | 12 | 4 | 2 |

Rationale: ignoring a severe collision is catastrophic (100 = wasted agent hours).
Advisory messages are cheap (3) but insufficient for severe conflicts.
Force-reserving when there's no conflict is wasteful (12) but harmless.

### Agent Liveness
| Action \ State | alive | flaky | dead |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| declare_alive | 0 | 3 | 50 |
| suspect | 8 | 2 | 6 |
| release_reservations | 100 | 20 | 1 |

Rationale: releasing a living agent's reservations is disastrous (100).
Failing to release a dead agent's reservations blocks other agents (50).

### Load Routing
| Action \ State | underloaded | balanced | overloaded |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| route_here | 1 | 3 | 25 |
| suggest_alternative | 8 | 2 | 3 |
| defer | 15 | 8 | 1 |

## Evidence Types
- message_sent(agent, timestamp) → updates liveness + load
- message_received(agent, timestamp) → updates liveness
- reservation_created(agent, paths) → updates conflict graph + load
- reservation_released(agent, paths) → updates conflict graph
- commit_detected(agent, files) → updates liveness + conflict
- health_pulse(agent, status) → updates liveness
- no_activity(agent, duration) → updates liveness toward suspect/dead

## Posterior Initialization
When a new agent is first seen, the posterior must be initialized:
- Liveness: P(alive)=0.95, P(flaky)=0.04, P(dead)=0.01 (strong alive prior)
- Conflict: P(no_conflict)=0.90, P(mild)=0.08, P(severe)=0.02 (optimistic)
- Load: P(balanced)=0.60, P(underloaded)=0.30, P(overloaded)=0.10 (neutral)

These priors are immediately overridden by evidence. After ~5 observations,
the prior is effectively washed out by data. The key requirement is that
the initial prior does NOT trigger aggressive actions (no false deaths,
no unnecessary interventions on a brand new agent).

## Posterior Update Rule
The posterior update uses likelihood-weighted EWMA, not full Bayesian updating
(which would require storing the full history of observations):

```
P(state | new_evidence) = normalize(
    P(state) * likelihood(new_evidence | state)^alpha
)
```

where alpha controls how fast the posterior moves (default 0.3 = moderately
responsive). This is cheaper than full Bayes (O(1) per state per update) and
converges to similar beliefs under stationary evidence distributions.

## Implementation Notes
- The DecisionCore is generic — instantiated 3 times with different S/A types
- Posterior is a simple categorical distribution (3-5 states max)
- Evidence updates use exponentially-weighted moving averages, not full Bayes
  (keeps computation O(1) per update, no matrix inversions)
- Loss matrix values are configurable via env vars for tuning
- Every decision is logged to the evidence ledger with full posterior snapshot

## Files
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/atc.rs` (primary, new file)

## Tests
- Unit test: given known posterior + loss matrix, verify argmin action
- Unit test: posterior update converges to true state under repeated evidence
- Unit test: loss matrix asymmetry produces correct action ordering
- Property test: for any valid posterior, chosen action has minimal expected loss

title: P0: Freeze SQLite and archive path authority across cwd and symlink drift
description: The process-wide SQLite identity cache is keyed only by raw PathBuf although resolution depends on current cwd and symlink targets. A fresh cache hit can make two physical databases share a pool/init gate/message-id allocator and can retire the wrong allocator after recovery; DbPool also stores the raw path, so later connections may open a different file. Freeze file-backed SQLite and storage-root authorities once, uncached, at construction and use the same resolved path for cache keys, init gates, allocator lookup, opens, cache namespaces, and recovery retirement.

title: R2.4: Implement am robot overview — cross-project unified summary (per-project unread/urgent/ack counts)

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# R2.4: `am robot overview`

## What
Cross-project aggregation. When an agent works in a multi-project environment, this shows a unified view of all projects with per-project counts.

## Data Collection
For each project in the database:
1. Query unread message count (for current agent, or all if agent unknown)
2. Query urgent message count
3. Query ack-overdue count (ack_required AND ack_ts IS NULL AND created_at < 30min ago)
4. Query active reservations count

## SQL (per project)
```sql
-- Unread count
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE project_id = ? AND to_agent = ? AND read_at IS NULL;

-- Urgent count
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE project_id = ? AND to_agent = ? AND read_at IS NULL AND importance = 'urgent';

-- Ack-overdue count
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE project_id = ? AND to_agent = ? AND ack_required = 1 AND ack_ts IS NULL AND created_at < ?;

-- Active reservations
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM file_reservations WHERE project_id = ? AND expires_at > ?;
```

Can be optimized into a single query with CASE/SUM per project.

## Output Format
```
projects[3]{slug,unread,urgent,ack_overdue,reservations}:
  backend-api,5,1,0,3
  frontend-app,2,0,1,2
  shared-lib,0,0,0,0

total_unread: 7
total_urgent: 1
total_ack_overdue: 1

_alerts[1]{severity,summary}:
  warn,1 ack-overdue message in frontend-app

_actions[1]:
  am robot inbox --project frontend-app --ack-overdue
```

## Agent Identity
- If agent is known: filter messages to that agent's inbox
- If agent unknown: show total counts across all agents
- Add _alert if agent not detected

## Acceptance Criteria
- Lists all projects in database
- Per-project counts are accurate
- Totals match sum of per-project counts
- _alerts generated for projects with ack-overdue items
- Works with 0 projects (empty table, clean output)

title: test orphan leak: mcp_agent_mail_tools not killed on SIGTERM
description:
## Symptom

`mcp_agent_mail_tools` test binary leaks as PPID=1 orphan after `cargo test` runs are interrupted. Survives for days, holding RAM (lower CPU than frankenscipy orphans but still wasting resources).

## Evidence (2026-05-08 fleet sweep)

| Host | Binary | Age |
|---|---|---|
| vmi1152480 | `mcp_agent_mail_tools` (PID 1783365) | 8d 7h |
| vmi1153651 | `mcp_agent_mail_tools` (PID 1888107) | 8d 7h |

8-day-old test orphans across 2 fleet machines.

## Suspected root cause

Same class as the frankenscipy orphan bug: `cargo test` does not propagate SIGTERM to spawned test binaries when the parent is killed. Without process-group propagation, child binaries become orphans (PPID=1) and continue running.

## Proposed fix directions

- Use `setsid` or process-group propagation in test invocation
- Add cooperative shutdown signal handler in the test binary itself
- Audit the test for any blocking IO (mailbox polls, agent registration) that doesn't honor a cancellation token

## Cross-reference

Parallel ticket filed in `frankenscipy` repo for `fsci_sparse-*` / `fsci_integrate-*` orphans (same root cause class, ~15 occurrences). Fix in either repo likely informs the other; if a shared test-runner helper exists, fix there.
close_reason: Durable in-repo guardrail (.config/nextest.toml slow-timeout terminate-after) bounds hung-test orphans to minutes under the recommended cargo nextest run; test code provably free of unbounded hangs (bounded retries + per-test isolated DBs); verified 1759 core tests pass under config. Residual bare-cargo-test orphan path is fleet-orchestration territory (documented).

comments.author: RubyHollow
comments.text:
RESOLVED (RubyHollow/Opus 4.8, 2026-06-27) — durable in-repo guardrail landed; took over from WhiteDuck (dead 40d).

ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS: The leaked binary `mcp_agent_mail_tools` is the LIB unit-test binary. For it to survive "for days" a unit test must block forever. Audit shows the test code is provably free of UNBOUNDED hangs: (1) both tool-layer retry loops in identity.rs (persist_agent_registration_token_with_retry:82, register_agent:1521) are bounded at <=4 attempts; (2) the inner DB MVCC retry budget is bounded (~29s); (3) pool busy_timeout is bounded (60s); (4) tools unit tests use PER-TEST isolated DBs (`sqlite:///:memory:` or a fresh tempfile::tempdir()), so there is no cross-test shared-DB deadlock. mcp-agent-mail-core's own lock_order::stress_no_deadlock_under_contention and git_binary::spawn_timeout_after_5s_on_hung_shim tests pass. Conclusion: the multi-day orphan is ENVIRONMENTAL (a degraded fleet host putting a pool/fsync/flock syscall into uninterruptible D-state at the instant cargo is killed), not a code deadlock. The title "not killed on SIGTERM" is consistent with D-state. Also: the test binary installs NO signal handler (signal_hook lives only in the cli/server runtime), and an orphan never receives a deliverable signal anyway, so an in-binary cooperative SIGTERM handler cannot help.

FIX: Added .config/nextest.toml. cargo-nextest (0.9.133, already installed; project is already NEXTEST-env-aware via core/config.rs; rch references it) runs each test in its OWN process group and, via slow-timeout{period=60s, terminate-after=4, grace-period=10s}, SIGTERM->SIGKILLs the whole group after ~4min. That converts "orphan survives for days" into "killed after minutes", and the SIGKILL-to-process-group reaches even a wedged child. leak-timeout=1s fails a test that leaks a subprocess holding the stdout pipe. A [profile.ci] adds retries=1. Documented the orphan-safe runner in AGENTS.md (Testing section).

VERIFICATION: nextest accepts the config (schema-valid; ran a throwaway crate -> profile:default). Real-workspace proof: `cargo nextest run -p mcp-agent-mail-core` => 1759 passed / 0 skipped, slowest 5.05s << 240s threshold (no false-trip), config honored. Pure-config change (no Rust touched) -> no clippy/fmt impact.

RESIDUAL (honest scope): plain `cargo test` ignores .config/nextest.toml and cargo has no equivalent per-test kill knob, so a hung test under bare `cargo test` killed mid-run can still orphan. That is inherent to cargo and belongs to fleet orchestration — run the orphan-prone path under `cargo nextest run` (now documented) or have the fleet pt/process-reaper SIGKILL D-state am/test orphans. CROSS-REF: the frankenscipy fsci_sparse-*/fsci_integrate-* orphan ticket (same class) needs its own .config/nextest.toml in that repo.

title: [completion-debt of br-8ujfs.5.4] E4 TUI segfault toast — formatter, rate limiter, escalation, badge counter, env gate, six unit tests
description:
# E4: TUI System Health toast for git_segfault_retry events

## Why this debt exists

Original `br-8ujfs.5.4` was closed in pass 2 with closer (1494) admitting the TUI wiring was deferred ('structural'). Verification: upstream tracing events exist in `git_cmd.rs` and `guard/lib.rs`, but `tui_screens/system_health.rs` (4049 lines) has zero references to segfault / 2.51 / git_segfault. Six unit tests + one integration test named in revision v2 are absent. Toast formatter, rate limiter, escalation, badge counter, env gate all missing.

## Spec — preserves all original requirements verbatim

When the TUI is running, the operator should see this the FIRST time it happens, not read about it in logs tomorrow.

### Original deliverables (preserved)

- Hook E3's tracing event (`git_segfault_retry` per E6 catalog) into the existing toast pipeline in `tui_screens/system_health.rs`.
- **First occurrence per session**: WARNING toast (yellow) with text:
  > `git 2.51.0 segfault retried on <repo>. Set AM_GIT_BINARY or upgrade git to stop seeing this.`
- **Subsequent occurrences**: suppressed individually, but System Health screen grows a `git segfault retries: N` badge that increments live via the metrics counter.
- Dismissible via `Ctrl+Y` (existing toast focus binding).
- Respects `AM_TUI_TOAST_ENABLED=false` (existing env knob).

### Additional design (V2 revision — explicit, not adding scope)

- **Rate limiter**: even within a session, if 30+ retries occur in < 5min, emit ONE follow-up WARNING toast at the 30-retry mark with text:
  > `git 2.51.0 segfault retries reached 30 in 5min — production impact likely. Investigate.`
- **Escalation**: if exhausted-retry count > 0 (i.e. `git_segfault_retry_exhausted_total` increments), emit ERROR toast (red) with text:
  > `git 2.51.0 retry EXHAUSTED on <repo>. Operations failing. Set AM_GIT_BINARY immediately.`
- **Badge format**: `git segfault retries: N` plain when N=0..29; `git segfault retries: N (HIGH)` highlighted yellow when 30+; `git segfault retries: N (EXHAUSTED M)` red when exhausted ≥ 1.
- **Env gate**: `AM_TUI_GIT_SEGFAULT_TOAST_ENABLED` (default `true`) — operator can disable just this category of toast independently of the global toast switch.

## Current state

- Toast pipeline: existing infrastructure in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_app.rs::NotificationQueue` and `tui_app.rs::toast_for_event` (verified during pass 1 deepening for br-1m6a.4).
- Tracing event source: `git_cmd.rs` already emits `git_segfault_retry` (E3 — already shipped).
- Metrics counters: `git_segfault_retry_attempted_total`, `git_segfault_retry_succeeded_total`, `git_segfault_retry_exhausted_total` exist per E6 catalog (verify; if missing, depends on E6 / `br-j1qwr`).
- System Health screen: `tui_screens/system_health.rs` has badge infrastructure for similar metrics — extend, don't reinvent.

## Target state

A new toast handler `git_segfault_retry_toast_handler()` in `tui_screens/system_health.rs`:

1. Subscribes to `git_segfault_retry` tracing events via the existing `tracing-subscriber` Layer.
2. Per session state: `first_emitted: bool`, `retry_count: u32`, `exhausted_count: u32`, `window_start: Instant`, `window_count: u32`.
3. On event:
   - If `!first_emitted` AND toast subsystem enabled: emit WARNING toast, set `first_emitted=true`.
   - Always: increment `retry_count`. Update badge via `system_health.set_badge("git_segfault_retries", retry_count)`.
   - Rate-limiter: if `(now - window_start) < 5min` AND `window_count >= 30`: emit follow-up WARNING toast (once per window). Else if `(now - window_start) >= 5min`: reset window.
   - Escalation: if event is exhausted variant: increment `exhausted_count`, emit ERROR toast (always — escalation overrides rate limiter).
4. All toast formatters live in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/toast_format.rs` (or local fn) — pure (no I/O), unit-testable.

## Non-goals (verbatim)

- No changes to robot CLI surface — robot reads metrics, E3 event already feeds it.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

### Implementation

- [ ] `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/system_health.rs` defines `git_segfault_retry_toast_handler` that consumes `git_segfault_retry` tracing events.
- [ ] First-occurrence WARNING toast with verbatim text: `git 2.51.0 segfault retried on <repo>. Set AM_GIT_BINARY or upgrade git to stop seeing this.` — `<repo>` substituted from `repo_slug` field.
- [ ] Rate-limited follow-up WARNING toast at 30-retry mark per 5min window with verbatim text: `git 2.51.0 segfault retries reached 30 in 5min — production impact likely. Investigate.`
- [ ] Escalation ERROR toast on exhausted retry with verbatim text: `git 2.51.0 retry EXHAUSTED on <repo>. Operations failing. Set AM_GIT_BINARY immediately.`
- [ ] System Health badge `git segfault retries: N` updates live; format changes per thresholds (plain → HIGH → EXHAUSTED M).
- [ ] Toast dismissible via existing `Ctrl+Y` toast-focus binding (no new binding).
- [ ] `AM_TUI_TOAST_ENABLED=false` suppresses ALL toasts (existing global knob respected).
- [ ] `AM_TUI_GIT_SEGFAULT_TOAST_ENABLED=false` suppresses only this toast category — global toast still works for unrelated events.
- [ ] All formatters factored into pure functions (no I/O, no env reads inside) for unit-testability.

### Tests

- [ ] All 6 unit tests below present in `system_health.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- [ ] 1 integration test in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/tests/segfault_toast.rs` covering the badge wire-up.
- [ ] E2E test `tests/e2e/test_segfault_toast.sh` produces structured logs and exits 0 on healthy run.

### Cross-references

- [ ] Toast text matches the metrics catalog in E6 (`br-j1qwr`) — e.g. uses `repo_slug` field name not `repo` or `project_slug`.
- [ ] Tracing event consumed via the existing `mcp_agent_mail::*` target prefix per E6 conventions.
notes:
## Testing strategy

### Unit tests (`tui_screens/system_health.rs::tests`, naming: `segfault_toast_*`)

Six tests required by the original spec, plus four covering the V2 additions:

1. `segfault_toast_first_event_emits_warning` — fixture event { repo_slug: "data-projects-foo" }, assert toast severity=WARNING, text matches verbatim including substituted slug.
2. `segfault_toast_subsequent_event_increments_badge_only` — emit 5 events, assert exactly 1 toast was queued, badge count is 5.
3. `segfault_toast_respects_global_toast_disabled_env` — `AM_TUI_TOAST_ENABLED=false`, emit event, no toast queued; badge still increments.
4. `segfault_toast_respects_specific_category_disabled_env` — `AM_TUI_GIT_SEGFAULT_TOAST_ENABLED=false` only, emit event, no segfault toast queued; OTHER toast categories still emit (assert via control event).
5. `segfault_toast_dismissible_via_ctrl_y` — emit toast, simulate Ctrl+Y key event, toast removed from queue.
6. `segfault_toast_badge_format_plain_below_threshold` — count=29, badge text == `git segfault retries: 29`.
7. `segfault_toast_badge_format_high_above_30` — count=30, badge text contains `(HIGH)` and yellow style.
8. `segfault_toast_badge_format_exhausted_when_exhaust_count_positive` — exhausted_count=1, badge text contains `(EXHAUSTED 1)` and red style.
9. `segfault_toast_rate_limit_emits_followup_at_30` — rapid-fire 30 events within 5min, assert exactly 2 toasts queued (first + 30-mark).
10. `segfault_toast_window_resets_after_5min` — fixture clock advance 5min after 30, additional event past window, no follow-up emitted in next window until 30 again.
11. `segfault_toast_escalation_emits_error_on_exhausted` — fixture event variant=exhausted, assert toast severity=ERROR, text matches verbatim.
12. `segfault_toast_formatter_pure_no_env_reads` — assert formatter calls do not touch std::env (use a deny mock or static analysis on the function body).

### Integration test (`crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/tests/segfault_toast.rs`, new)

Builds a minimal MailApp, wires the handler, emits 3 fake `git_segfault_retry` events spaced 1s apart:

- assert exactly 1 WARNING toast in queue
- assert badge value reflects 3
- assert events.jsonl-like internal log captured 3 events
- swap to fake exhausted event, assert ERROR toast queued

### E2E test (`tests/e2e/test_segfault_toast.sh`, new)

Universal JSON-line logging schema; per scenario captures `$LOG_DIR/$scenario/{stdout,stderr,exit,state.json}`.

Scenarios:

- `s1_first_event_warning_visible_in_tui_state` — start server in TUI mode (or headless TUI), inject fake retry via test harness or by triggering the racer shim (cross-references br-kgck8), poll `/mail/api/health/notifications` (or robot equivalent), assert exactly 1 toast with WARNING severity.
- `s2_subsequent_events_only_update_badge` — inject 4 more, assert toast queue length unchanged, badge value 5.
- `s3_global_toast_disabled_suppresses` — restart with `AM_TUI_TOAST_ENABLED=false`, inject event, assert no notification.
- `s4_specific_disabled_suppresses_only_segfault` — restart with `AM_TUI_GIT_SEGFAULT_TOAST_ENABLED=false`, inject segfault event AND a control event (e.g. `agent_registered`), assert only control toast in queue.
- `s5_thirty_in_window_emits_followup` — inject 30 events within 5min (test-clock controlled), assert 2 toasts.
- `s6_exhausted_emits_error_toast` — inject one exhausted event, assert ERROR toast.
- `s7_dismissal_clears_active_toast` — emit toast, send Ctrl+Y via PTY, assert removed.

End-of-run summary line with replay command.

### Repro / verification

```bash
cargo test -p mcp-agent-mail-server segfault_toast -- --nocapture
cargo test -p mcp-agent-mail-server --test segfault_toast -- --nocapture
bash tests/e2e/test_segfault_toast.sh
```

### Logging schema (universal e2e)

Every event in `events.jsonl`: `{ ts, test, scenario, level, message, data, latency_ms?, artifact_path? }`. Per-scenario subdir captures stdout/stderr/exit/state.json/diff.log.

## References

- Original spec: `br-8ujfs.5.4` (closed). All deliverables preserved.
- E3 tracing event source: `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/src/git_cmd.rs` (already shipped).
- E6 metrics catalog: `br-j1qwr` (open completion-debt).
- Toast pipeline: `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_app.rs::NotificationQueue`.
- System Health screen: `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/system_health.rs`.
- Existing toast precedent: `tui_app.rs::toast_for_event` (br-1m6a.4 patterns).
- Audit verification: `beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T04-08-17Z/beads/br-8ujfs.5.4/verification.json`

title: doctor: auto-reclaim recovery debris after a successful heal so operators never have to clean up by hand
description:
FIELD EVIDENCE (csd machine, 2026-08-12): a 9-day startup-recovery crash loop left 48GB in the mailbox repo: 502 forensic bundles (21.7GiB), 648 sidecar snapshots, 491 top-level reconstruct candidates. After the operator fixed the DB, they still had to run 'am doctor reclaim --max-age-days 0 --keep 2 --yes' manually and then delete the staging dir themselves. The doctor created the junk; the doctor should tidy it once the problem is solved.

ASK: after a SUCCESSFUL heal (startup self-heal repair/reconstruct completing with a healthy post-verify, and the am doctor repair/reconstruct verbs succeeding), automatically run the existing reclaim consolidation (equivalent of am doctor reclaim --keep <small N> --yes) scoped to recovery debris older than the successful heal, so stale forensic bundles/quarantines/reconstruct candidates from the failure episode are consolidated into <storage_root>/doctor/reclaimable/<ts>/ without operator action. RULE 1 constraint: never delete — reclaim only MOVES into the reversible staging dir; the final rm remains a human decision (print the staging path + size). Keep the newest K artifacts per category (default keep=2) as forensics for the episode just resolved. Must be a no-op when there is no stale debris, must never run when the heal FAILED, and must be skippable via env (AM_DOCTOR_AUTO_RECLAIM=0 or similar config).

ACCEPTANCE: (a) integration test: seed fake stale forensic bundles + reconstruct candidates, run a successful self-heal, assert debris beyond keep-N is consolidated under doctor/reclaimable/ and DB untouched; (b) failed-heal test: debris untouched; (c) disable-env test; (d) output clearly reports staged bytes + path and that nothing was deleted.
close_reason: Implemented + verified: post-heal auto-reclaim consolidates recovery debris (move-only per RULE 1) + refused reconstruct candidates quarantined into retention category; tests green (evidence in comments)

title: P1: Persist installer-selected bearer before any client config write
description: Fresh install can generate and export a bearer token, then write it into external MCP client configs before the native am setup run durably saves the same credential to config.env. update_mcp_configs only warns and continues on native setup failure. The running service may temporarily inherit or capture the shell token, but a later restart or alternate launch can resolve a different or empty credential while durable client configs keep the generated bearer, leaving every client unauthorized. title: Track G: BOCPD + Conformal Prediction for Tool Metrics
description:
**Background**

The tool metrics system currently uses static thresholds for alerting. BOCPD (Bayesian Online Change-Point Detection) can detect regime shifts in tool latency/throughput, and Conformal Prediction provides distribution-free prediction intervals for SLO monitoring.

**Graveyard references:** Section 12.13 (BOCPD), Section 12.1 (Conformal Prediction).

**EV calculation (BOCPD):** (severity=4 * breadth=4 * feasibility=3) / (risk=3 * effort=2) = 8.0
**EV calculation (Conformal):** (severity=4 * breadth=4 * feasibility=4) / (risk=3 * effort=2) = 10.7

- Wired into tool metrics screen and TUI display with clear operator semantics

- Integration tests validate detector + conformal interoperability over streaming tool metrics

title: P1: Prove every strict mailbox-schema predicate independently

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
DESIGN RATIONALE (2026-02-13, RubyPrairie):

WHY A TREE WIDGET FOR THREADS:

Current thread display is a flat list of messages. When agent conversations are deep
(10+ messages with nested replies), it's extremely difficult to understand the reply
structure and find specific sub-conversations.

The frankentui Tree widget with 5 guide styles (Plain, Rounded, Bold, Double, ASCII) provides
exactly the hierarchical navigation needed. Key advantages:
1. Visual reply depth at a glance (indentation + guides)
2. Collapse old branches to focus on recent activity
3. Expand specific sub-conversations without losing context
4. Natural keyboard navigation (Left=collapse, Right=expand)

TREE CONSTRUCTION FROM FLAT MESSAGES:

Messages in Agent Mail have:
- message_id: unique ID
- reply_to_id: optional, references parent message
- thread_id: groups messages into threads

Algorithm:
1. Collect all messages in thread
2. Build parent->children map using reply_to_id
3. Messages with no reply_to_id are root nodes
4. Sort children by created_at ascending
5. Build recursive TreeItem structure

Edge cases:
- reply_to_id references non-existent message: treat as root
- Circular references (shouldn't happen but): detect and break cycle

comments.text:
# Track 2: am flake-triage — Native Flake Analysis

## What it replaces
scripts/flake_triage.sh (194 lines of bash)

## Current behavior
Three modes of operation:
1. **reproduce**: Re-run a specific test from a failure artifact JSON file
2. **scan**: Walk directory trees to find failure artifact files, summarize them
3. **detect**: Multi-seed flake detection — run a test N times with different seeds,
   report if it passes/fails intermittently (true flake vs hard failure)

All JSON parsing uses inline Python one-liners like:
  python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('$file')); print(d.get('test_name',''))"

## External dependencies eliminated
- **python3**: Every JSON operation uses an inline Python script. Rust's serde_json
  replaces this entirely.

## Key improvements
1. **Existing Rust module**: crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/flake_triage.rs already has
   domain logic for flake analysis. The bash script is a less-capable duplicate. This
   track wires the existing module into the CLI.
2. **Structured output**: Instead of printing text, produce JSON with test names,
   failure rates, seed values, and reproduction commands.
3. **Parallel multi-seed**: The detect mode can run N seeds in parallel using
   std::process::Command with thread pooling, much faster than bash's sequential loop.
4. **Cross-platform**: No bash-specific path handling or process management.

## CLI interface
```
am flake-triage scan [--dir <path>] [--json]
am flake-triage reproduce <artifact.json> [--json]
am flake-triage detect <test_name> [--seeds N] [--parallel] [--json]
```

## Implementation location
crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/flake_triage.rs (new module, wraps core::flake_triage)
Wire into Cli enum in crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/lib.rs

- scripts/flake_triage.sh (the script being replaced)
- crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/flake_triage.rs (existing Rust module to wrap)
- crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/lib.rs (CLI structure to extend)

title: Export dashboard aggregates from a read-only consistent SQLite snapshot
description: Fresh-eyes audit finding: the dashboard demo-pack exporter opens the source database without an explicit read-only policy and calculates the six public aggregate counts with independent queries outside a single snapshot transaction. A concurrent mailbox write can therefore produce a mutually inconsistent pack, while an exporter should never obtain write capability to the private source. Open the source in enforced read-only mode, acquire one stable SQLite read snapshot for all aggregate queries and provenance, fail closed if that contract cannot be established, and add concurrency tests proving the exported totals all come from one database state without creating or mutating source files.
close_reason: Fixed and verified. The exporter opened the source with default create-read-write flags (only canonicalize() prevented creating an empty db at the source path) and ran six unbracketed COUNT queries. Now: feature-gated exporter module used by bin + tests. (1) Read-only proven fail-closed at open: PRAGMA user_version=<current> no-op header write must be rejected with SQLITE_READONLY — chosen after measuring that BEGIN IMMEDIATE succeeds on read-only connections on SQLite 3.46.1 (the first probe design failed its own tests, which is exactly why the tests exist). (2) Mode-split open after measuring that plain read-only WAL opens CREATE -shm/-wal when absent: live mailbox (sidecars exist) joins the existing WAL creating nothing; quiescent source opens immutable=1 and quiescence is re-verified post-read, failing closed if a writer appeared. (3) All six aggregates in one deferred read transaction, expiry cutoff computed once. Proof: 29/29 crate tests incl. 5 new (missing-source not created; write rejection; 200 snapshot reads mutually consistent against a live committing writer; byte-level before/after directory comparison shows zero files created/mutated; immutable path fails closed on mid-read writer). fmt + clippy clean. Committed on main, pushed.

title: Release train + rollout playbook: staged sequencing for the 90 bead outcomes across N releases
description:
# Release train + rollout playbook

## Why this bead exists

The 90 beads across 6 epics deliver dozens of user-visible outcomes — many safe, some risky (ATC live mode, archive perf fix, WASM decision). Landing them all in one release is unsafe. Landing them in random order creates coordination problems (e.g., UX.1 `am check` references gates that don't exist yet).

We need a **release train plan** that:
- Groups outcomes into releases (e.g., v0.3.0 = docs + conformance; v0.3.1 = archive perf + CI gates; v0.4.0 = ATC live)
- Identifies canary windows for risky changes
- Defines "definition of shippable" per release
- Documents rollback path per release
- Coordinates with external dependencies (Python reference fixture regen, etc.)

This is a **top-level coordination bead** (sibling to br-ldpdv meta) — it doesn't block any specific epic but blocks the actual rollout.

## Scope

### Deliverable: `docs/RELEASE_TRAIN_PLAN.md`

Structured as:

```markdown
# Release Train Plan (reality-check + idea-wizard outcomes)

## Release sequencing

### v0.3.0 — "Docs + Conformance foundation"
**Goal**: accurate documentation + strict conformance baseline
**Closes**: br-o217s (all children) + br-a2k3h (all children)
**Risk**: low — mostly prose + test additions
**Canary**: 1 week on internal install before tagging release

### v0.3.1 — "Archive perf + CI gates"
**Goal**: batch write under budget + drift prevention
**Closes**: br-8qdh0 (all children), br-bb0gt.1 (am check)
**Risk**: medium — perf fix has rollback plan (br-8qdh0.9)
**Canary**: 2 weeks with ARCHIVE_WRITE_MODE=auto (fast with fallback)

### v0.3.2 — "WASM decision executed"
**Goal**: /web-dashboard reality matches docs
**Closes**: br-il53l (chosen branch + observability/a11y if SHIP)
**Risk**: depends on branch — RETIRE is low, SHIP is high

### v0.4.0 — "ATC foundation (shadow mode default)"
**Goal**: ATC DB layer + hot-path wiring, SHADOW MODE as default
**Closes**: br-bn0vb.1-13, .18, .19, .20, .21, .22, .24, .25, .28, .29
**Risk**: medium — shadow mode is safe; live mode NOT enabled
**Canary**: 4 weeks shadow observation

### v0.4.1 — "ATC live mode"
**Goal**: enable live writes after shadow observation
**Closes**: br-bn0vb.14-17 (Seam 6 + disclaimer removal), .23, .26, .27, .30, .31
**Risk**: high — ATC actually records production data
**Pre-requisites**: Seam 6 validation artifacts (E2E, perf, soak) all committed
**Canary**: 2 weeks live with aggressive monitoring

### v0.5.0 — "UX polish"
**Goal**: ergonomic enhancements built on stable core
**Closes**: br-bb0gt (remaining .2-.5), br-ldpdv (meta)
**Risk**: low

## Cross-cutting considerations per release

### Blocker matrix
- Each release has a "must-close-before-tag" list + "nice-to-have" list
- Blocker beads must close 100%; nice-to-have at operator discretion

### Canary criteria
- No user-visible regressions (defined per epic: latency budgets, no crashes, no data loss)
- All new CI gates green
- No open P0/P1 bugs against release
- Operator sign-off (human judgment)

### Rollback per release
- v0.3.0: revert commits (docs-only; low rollback risk)
- v0.3.1: flip ARCHIVE_WRITE_MODE=legacy (runbook in br-8qdh0.9)
- v0.3.2: revert the retire changes OR revert the ship changes per branch
- v0.4.0: ATC_LEARNING_DISABLED=1 (kill switch per br-bn0vb.19)
- v0.4.1: flip ATC_WRITE_MODE=shadow (reverts to prior release's default)
- v0.5.0: revert (UX-only)

### Coordination with external
- Python reference fixtures regenerated + synced (br-a2k3h.7) before v0.3.0 tag
- CHANGELOG.md updated per release (template committed)
- Installer checksums refreshed per AGENTS.md L108 coordination with ACFS
```

### Release readiness checklist (per release)

Template at `docs/RELEASE_READINESS_TEMPLATE.md`:
- [ ] All blocker beads closed
- [ ] CI green (all gates, including new ones)
- [ ] Canary observation period elapsed
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md drafted + reviewed
- [ ] Rollback procedure tested on staging
- [ ] Operator sign-off

### Dependencies between releases

Explicit constraints:
- v0.3.1 requires v0.3.0 (CI gates reference doc counts fixed in v0.3.0)
- v0.4.0 requires v0.3.1 (archive perf must be fixed before ATC adds write volume)
- v0.4.1 requires v0.4.0 (shadow mode data collected before live)
- v0.5.0 depends on v0.4.1 (agent health scoring needs resolved experiences)

## Test plan

N/A (documentation + process). Verification:
- Plan reviewed by repo owner
- Sequencing walk-through confirms no broken dependencies
- Each release has a canary plan
- Rollback per release tested once (dry-run on staging)

## Non-goals

- Not committing to specific calendar dates (sequence is relative)
- Not a contract with users (the project doesn't have an SLA)
- Not a substitute for per-bead acceptance criteria

## Dependencies

- Depends on the 5 reality-check epic plans existing (they all do)
- Depends on br-ldpdv (meta) for final reality-check pass after v0.5.0
- Feeds the actual release process for all 90 bead outcomes

## Definition of done

- `docs/RELEASE_TRAIN_PLAN.md` committed
- Release readiness template at `docs/RELEASE_READINESS_TEMPLATE.md`
- Each release has documented canary + rollback
- Plan referenced from CHANGELOG.md header + OPERATOR_RUNBOOK.md
