title: [completion-debt of br-1m6a.17] JSON stats showcase in startup banner — same-day refactor removed it; current banner has no JSON blob
description:
# Restore JSON stats showcase in startup banner

## Why this debt exists

Original bead `br-1m6a.17` was closed but a same-day refactor (commit `33ab58a0`) deleted the entire Stats Showcase block from `render_startup_banner()`. Current banner has no JSON blob; `emit_startup_showcase()` (`crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/lib.rs:7278-7314`) emits banner + ConsoleCaps + summary only. The original spec is preserved verbatim below — none of the original requirements are dropped.

## Current state

- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/console.rs::render_startup_banner()` prints banner header + ConsoleCaps + summary lines, no JSON.
- `emit_startup_showcase()` in `lib.rs` is the single call site; it does not pass any structured stats.
- Sensitive-value masking utility (`mask_json` / `mask_sensitive_value`) exists at `console.rs:20-149` (from br-1m6a.18) — ready to use.
- Active-theme accessor lives in the centralized theme system (`crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/theme.rs` from br-1m6a.12).
- `ftui-extras` is already a dependency for the showcase TUI; no new crate needed if `features = ["syntax"]` is enabled on the existing dep.

## Target state

A real, machine-parseable, masked, syntax-highlighted startup-state JSON block printed by the banner.

### Required keys (verbatim from br-1m6a.17 spec)

- `endpoint` (string, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/`)
- `web_ui` (string or null, the `/mail/` URL when web UI is exposed)
- `uptime` (string, RFC3339 of process start)
- `environment` (string, "dev" | "test" | "prod")
- `auth_enabled` (bool, `HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` set OR JWT enabled)
- `tools_log_enabled` (bool)
- `log_tool_calls_enabled` (bool)
- `stats`: object with sub-keys
  - `projects` (number)
  - `agents` (number)
  - `messages` (number)
  - `file_reservations` (number, active only)
  - `contact_links` (number)
- `storage_root` (string, abbreviated to `~/...` or `<XDG_DATA_HOME>/...` for display)

## Design

1. New module `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/banner_json.rs` (or inline in `console.rs` — caller's choice; small enough either way).
2. Function `build_startup_state_json(cx: &Cx, ctx: &StartupContext) -> serde_json::Value`:
   - Pulls counts from db pool (lightweight queries — `SELECT COUNT(*)` × 5).
   - Sanitizes `storage_root` and `endpoint` via `console::sanitize_known_value`.
   - Returns a `serde_json::Value::Object` with keys in a fixed order (use `serde_json::Map` with `preserve_order` feature OR explicit insertion order; assert ordering in unit test).
3. Render via `ftui_extras::SyntaxHighlighter::with_theme(theme::syntax_theme())`:
   - `let pretty = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&masked)?;`
   - `let highlighted = highlighter.highlight(&pretty, "json")`;
   - When stdout is NOT a TTY: emit plain `pretty` (no ANSI), so log scrapers parse cleanly.
4. Apply `mask_json` from `br-1m6a.18` BEFORE pretty-printing — sensitive keys (`auth_*`, `*_token`, `*_url` userinfo) replaced with `<redacted>`.
5. Wire into `emit_startup_showcase()` in `lib.rs` — emit AFTER ConsoleCaps, BEFORE summary.
6. Operator escape: env `AM_BANNER_JSON_DISABLED=1` skips the section entirely (operators with strict log size budgets).
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `render_startup_banner()` emits a delimited JSON section between markers `--- BEGIN STARTUP STATE (JSON) ---` and `--- END STARTUP STATE (JSON) ---`.
- [ ] All 10 required keys present in the JSON object: `endpoint`, `web_ui`, `uptime`, `environment`, `auth_enabled`, `tools_log_enabled`, `log_tool_calls_enabled`, `stats.{projects,agents,messages,file_reservations,contact_links}`, `storage_root`.
- [ ] The embedded JSON parses cleanly via `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>` after ANSI stripping. Test asserts.
- [ ] Sensitive values masked: `HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` → `<redacted>`, `DATABASE_URL` userinfo (`postgres://user:pass@host/db` → `postgres://user:<redacted>@host/db`), absolute paths in `AM_GIT_BINARY` → basename only.
- [ ] Syntax highlighting active when `stdout.is_terminal()`; plain JSON when piped.
- [ ] Key ordering deterministic across two consecutive runs (asserted by integration test).
- [ ] `AM_BANNER_JSON_DISABLED=1` skips the section (no markers, no JSON in output).
- [ ] Stats counts non-negative; gracefully degrade to `null` if a query fails (not zero — null preserves the "unknown" signal).
- [ ] Active theme honored: highlight colors come from `theme::active_theme()` (br-1m6a.12), so cycling theme changes JSON colors.
- [ ] Unit tests, integration test, AND e2e test all present and passing on local run.
notes:
## Testing strategy

### Unit tests (in `console.rs` or `banner_json.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`)

Naming convention: `banner_json_<scenario>_<expectation>`. All required:

1. `banner_json_emits_all_required_keys` — build value, assert each of the 10 keys present.
2. `banner_json_parses_as_valid_json` — pretty-print + ANSI strip + `serde_json::from_str` round-trip.
3. `banner_json_masks_bearer_token` — fixture with `HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN=secret123`, assert `<redacted>` in output.
4. `banner_json_masks_database_url_userinfo` — fixture `postgres://u:p@h/d`, assert `postgres://u:<redacted>@h/d`.
5. `banner_json_masks_am_git_binary_absolute_path` — `/usr/local/bin/git-2.50.x` → `git-2.50.x`.
6. `banner_json_keys_deterministic_ordering` — two builds, byte-identical key order.
7. `banner_json_disabled_env_var_skips_section` — set `AM_BANNER_JSON_DISABLED=1`, assert markers absent.
8. `banner_json_uses_active_theme_for_highlighting` — swap theme, assert color codes change.
9. `banner_json_plain_when_no_tty` — fixture with `is_terminal=false`, assert no ANSI escapes.
10. `banner_json_failed_count_query_emits_null` — inject a fake DB error, assert `stats.projects` is `null` not `0`.

### Integration test

`crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/tests/banner_json_smoke.rs` (new):

- Spawn `emit_startup_showcase()` in-process with a seeded DB (5 fixture projects, 12 agents, 50 messages, 3 reservations, 7 contact links).
- Capture stdout via `tracing-subscriber::fmt::TestWriter` or a pipe.
- Strip ANSI.
- Extract JSON between markers, `serde_json::from_str`.
- Assert exact stats counts match seeded fixture.
- Run twice, byte-compare key order (deterministic ordering check).

### E2E test (`tests/e2e/test_banner_json.sh`)

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
LOG_DIR="${PROJECT_ROOT}/tests/artifacts/banner_json/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

# Universal JSON-line logging helper
log_event() {
  local level="$1"; shift; local scenario="$1"; shift; local message="$1"; shift
  local data="${1:-{}}"
  printf '{"ts":"%s","test":"banner_json","scenario":"%s","level":"%s","message":%s,"data":%s}
'     "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$scenario" "$level"     "$(printf '%s' "$message" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(sys.stdin.read()))')"     "$data" | tee -a "$LOG_DIR/events.jsonl"
}

# Scenario 1: banner contains JSON block with required keys (TTY simulated)
# Scenario 2: piped output is plain JSON (no ANSI)
# Scenario 3: AM_BANNER_JSON_DISABLED=1 skips the section
# Scenario 4: masked secrets visible in output
# Scenario 5: stats counts match fixture DB

# Each scenario:
#   - Captures stdout, stderr, exit code under $LOG_DIR/<scenario>/{stdout,stderr,exit}
#   - Logs structured JSON event for entry, observation, pass/fail
#   - On failure: log full diff between expected vs actual JSON
# At end: emit summary { total, passed, failed, log_dir, replay_cmd }
```

Required structured-log fields per event: `ts` (RFC3339 UTC), `test`, `scenario`, `level` (info/warn/error/pass/fail), `message` (string), `data` (object — scenario-specific fixtures, observed counts, diffs, latency_ms).

### Repro/verification commands

```bash
# Unit + integration
cargo test -p mcp-agent-mail-server banner_json -- --nocapture

# E2E
bash tests/e2e/test_banner_json.sh
ls -la tests/artifacts/banner_json/$(ls -t tests/artifacts/banner_json/ | head -1)/events.jsonl
jq -s 'group_by(.scenario) | map({scenario: .[0].scenario, events: length})' \
  tests/artifacts/banner_json/$(ls -t tests/artifacts/banner_json/ | head -1)/events.jsonl

# Smoke against running server
mcp-agent-mail config show 2>&1 | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | \
  awk '/--- BEGIN STARTUP STATE/,/--- END STARTUP STATE/' | \
  python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin),indent=2))'
```

## References

- Original spec: `br-1m6a.17` (closed, status=tombstone-equivalent)
- Sensitive masking utility: `br-1m6a.18` (closed, lives in `console.rs:20-149`)
- Theme system: `br-1m6a.12` (closed, `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/theme.rs`)
- Console banner: `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/console.rs::render_startup_banner()`
- Showcase wiring: `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/lib.rs::emit_startup_showcase()` (~line 7278)
close_reason: Implemented startup-state JSON banner with masking, deterministic tests, and E2E coverage

Keep a verified fd/inode identity through the move or use an atomic no-replace/rename-exchange protocol plus a concurrent replacement regression; do not treat flock as protection for Git existence locks.

title: ATC Track 3: Conflict Detector — Wait-For Graph + Tarjan SCC
description:
# Track 3: Conflict Detector (Wait-For Graph + Tarjan SCC)

## Graveyard Source: Tarjan's SCC (graph algorithms), Wait-For Graphs (DB theory)

## What
Maintains a real-time resource dependency graph across all agents and file
reservations. Detects two distinct classes of problems:

1. **Hard conflicts (deadlocks)**: actual overlapping exclusive reservations
   creating circular wait chains. Only hard conflicts can deadlock.
2. **Soft conflicts (advisories)**: interest signals suggesting two agents are
   converging on the same files without proper coordination.

This distinction is critical: deadlock detection (Tarjan SCC) only runs on
the hard conflict graph. Soft conflicts trigger lightweight advisories.

## Why a Graph, Not Pairwise Checks
Pairwise conflict detection is O(n²) agents and misses transitive deadlocks
(A→B→C→A). A directed graph with SCC detection is:
- O(V+E) per check via Tarjan's algorithm
- Catches cycles of any length
- Only runs on reservation change events (not every tick)
- Provides the exact cycle for targeted resolution

## Critical Design Considerations

### Multi-Project Scoping
Reservations are scoped per-project. An agent holding src/lib.rs in project A
does NOT conflict with an agent holding src/lib.rs in project B. The conflict
graph must partition by project_key:
```rust
struct ConflictGraph {
    per_project: HashMap<String, ProjectConflictGraph>,
}
```

### Self-Exclusion
The ATC agent ("AirTrafficControl") must be excluded from conflict tracking.

### Advisory Rate Limiting
Per-agent cooldown (default: 1 advisory per agent per 5 minutes).
```rust
struct AdvisoryThrottle {
    last_advisory: HashMap<AgentId, i64>,
    cooldown_micros: i64, // default: 300_000_000 (5 min)
}
```

### Existing Pattern Matching Infrastructure
Reuse fnmatch overlap logic from crates/mcp-agent-mail-guard/src/lib.rs.

## Data Model

### Hard Conflict Graph (Per-Project)
Only includes edges where BOTH agents hold active, overlapping, exclusive
reservations. These are the only edges that can form deadlock cycles.

```rust
struct HardEdge {
    holder: AgentId,
    blocked: AgentId,
    contested_patterns: Vec<String>,
    since: i64,
}

struct ProjectConflictGraph {
    project_key: String,
    /// Hard edges: overlapping exclusive reservations
    hard_edges: HashMap<AgentId, Vec<HardEdge>>,
    /// Soft edges: interest signals (for advisories only, NOT deadlock detection)
    soft_interests: HashMap<AgentId, HashMap<String, InterestSignal>>,
    /// All active reservations indexed by pattern
    reservations_by_pattern: HashMap<String, Vec<(AgentId, ReservationInfo)>>,
    generation: u64,
}
```

### Hard Conflict Detection (Event-Driven, Only on Reservation Changes)
On every reservation_created/released/renewed event:
1. Identify the project scope
2. Update reservations_by_pattern for that project
3. For each pattern in the new reservation, check for overlapping EXCLUSIVE
   reservations held by other agents (using fnmatch overlap from guard crate)
4. If exclusive overlap found, add HardEdge(s) to the graph
5. Run Tarjan's SCC on the hard_edges graph only
6. Any SCC with |V| > 1 is a deadlock cycle

### Soft Conflict Detection (Event-Driven, On Messages)
On message events, extract file patterns from the subject line (lightweight
pattern matching, NOT full body parsing):
1. Look for patterns like "src/*.rs", "lib.rs", "Cargo.toml" in subject
2. Record as InterestSignal for the sending agent
3. If two agents have recent interest in overlapping patterns and neither has
   a reservation → send advisory (respecting rate limit)

Soft conflicts NEVER trigger Tarjan SCC or deadlock resolution. They're
purely informational advisories.

### Tarjan's SCC Implementation (Hard Edges Only)
```rust
fn find_deadlock_cycles(graph: &ProjectConflictGraph) -> Vec<Vec<AgentId>> {
    // Standard Tarjan's algorithm on hard_edges only:
    // - DFS with index/lowlink tracking
    // - Stack-based SCC collection
    // - Return only SCCs with |V| > 1 (true cycles)
    // O(V+E) time, O(V) space
}
```

### Deadlock Resolution Protocol
When a cycle is detected:
1. Score each agent in the cycle:
   ```
   score = reservation_age_micros * 0.4
         + time_since_last_message * 0.3
         + inverse_task_priority * 0.3
   ```
2. Feed into the conflict DecisionCore (Track 1) with loss matrix
3. If action = advisory_message: send to the lowest-scoring agent
   (respecting rate limit):
   ```
   [ATC] Deadlock detected in {project}. You hold {patterns} needed by
   {other_agent}. Consider releasing to unblock the cycle.
   ```
4. If action = force_reservation: auto-release the lowest-scorer's oldest
   reservation in the cycle (only in non-safe-mode)
5. Log the full cycle, scores, and resolution to the evidence ledger

## Dependency
- Requires Track 1 (Decision Core) for the conflict intervention loss matrix
- Operates on reservation data already in TuiSharedState (DbStatSnapshot)
- Reuses fnmatch logic from mcp-agent-mail-guard crate

## Files
- crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/atc.rs (conflict module within ATC)

## Tests
- Unit: no reservations → empty graph, no conflicts
- Unit: two non-overlapping exclusive reservations → no hard edge
- Unit: two overlapping exclusive reservations → hard edge
- Unit: overlapping NON-exclusive reservations → no hard edge (compatible)
- Unit: same pattern in different projects → no conflict (project scoping)
- Unit: A→B→A hard cycle detected as deadlock
- Unit: A→B→C→A three-agent hard cycle detected
- Unit: soft conflict (interest overlap) → advisory, NOT deadlock
- Unit: soft conflict does NOT appear in Tarjan SCC input
- Unit: deadlock resolution scores agents correctly
- Unit: pattern overlap detection (exact, prefix-glob, wildcard)
- Unit: ATC agent excluded from conflict graph
- Unit: advisory rate limiting enforced (no spam)
- Property: Tarjan SCC on hard edges finds all and only true cycles
- Integration: reservation change events trigger graph updates

title: P0: Pin dist sibling dependencies to immutable commits
description: The tag triggered dist workflow clones frankensearch, fast cmaes, and beads rust from mutable default branch tips in lint, test, and build. Rerunning the same tag can therefore compile different dependency bytes or fail after an incompatible upstream change. Release outputs are not reproducible from the tagged source alone.
acceptance_criteria: Every dist lint, test, and build dependency checkout resolves frankensearch, fast cmaes, and beads rust to the same exact reviewed forty character commit IDs. One reviewable authority or a mutation sensitive parity check prevents lane drift. YAML validation and pin completeness checks pass. The same tag rerun cannot select newer sibling commits. A real workflow run confirms all gates and artifacts before closure.

# E6: Observability spec — single source of truth for all events/metrics

## Why this debt exists

Original `br-8ujfs.5.6` was closed in pass 2 with NONE of the deliverables present. Verification: the named doc `docs/OBSERVABILITY_git_251.md` does not exist; the four named JSON Schemas do not exist; the three named test scripts do not exist. No closing comment justifies the absence. Several sibling beads (E4 toast, F5 health sweep, etc.) reference E6 conventions — without this doc, they will drift.

## Spec — preserves all original requirements verbatim plus adds versioning + drift detection

The single source of truth for naming, fields, metric labels, and JSON Schemas across the git-2.51.0 mitigation epic (and beyond — the conventions generalize).

## Deliverable: `docs/OBSERVABILITY_git_251.md` (new)

### Section 1 — Naming conventions (verbatim from original)

- tracing target prefix: `mcp_agent_mail::<component>::<subcomponent>`
- event names: snake_case, verb_or_state (e.g. `flock_acquired`, `git_segfault_retry`, `reservation_activity_result`)
- field names: snake_case; units in the name (`duration_ms`, `wait_seconds`, `size_bytes`). No bare `duration`.

### Section 2 — Required fields for every `run_git_locked`-adjacent event

- `repo_slug` (tokenized project identifier)
- `caller` (static site string; populated by macro)
- `args_hash` (sha256 of joined argv; raw args gated on `AM_LOG_GIT_ARGS=1`)
- `duration_ms` (number)
- `outcome` (enum: `success` | `retrying` | `succeeded_after_retry` | `exhausted` | `error`)
- `git_version` (from cached resolution)

### Section 3 — Metrics catalog (verbatim from original, complete table)

| metric | type | labels | added in | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `git_repo_lock_acquisitions_total` | counter | `repo_slug` | B2 | per-process mutex acquisitions |
| `git_repo_lock_wait_seconds` | hist | `repo_slug` | B2 | buckets [1ms, 10ms, 100ms, 1s] |
| `git_flock_wait_seconds` | hist | `repo_slug` | B3 | OS flock acquisition wait |
| `git_flock_timeout_total` | counter | `repo_slug` | B3 | flock timeouts |
| `git_flock_readonly_total` | counter | `repo_slug` | B3 | downgrade-to-read events |
| `run_git_locked_total` | counter | `caller`,`outcome` | B4 | every shell-out git call |
| `run_git_locked_duration_seconds` | hist | `caller` | B4 | end-to-end |
| `run_git_locked_in_flight` | gauge | `caller` | B4 | concurrency |
| `run_git_locked_contention_seconds` | hist | `caller` | B4 | wait on inner mutex+flock |
| `git_segfault_total` | counter | `repo_slug`,`caller` | E1/E3 | observed segfault exits |
| `git_segfault_retry_attempted_total` | counter | `caller` | E2 | first retry initiated |
| `git_segfault_retry_succeeded_total` | counter | `caller`,`attempt_n` | E2 | retry recovered |
| `git_segfault_retry_exhausted_total` | counter | `caller` | E2 | retries gave up |
| `git_segfault_retry_latency_seconds` | hist | `caller`,`outcome` | E2 | retry round-trip |
| `reservation_activity_duration_seconds` | hist | `repo_slug` | C2 | libgit2 reservation walk |
| `pathspec_walk_duration_seconds` | hist | `repo_slug` | C3 | pathspec compile + walk |
| `doctor_fix_orphan_refs_actions_total` | counter | `op`,`outcome` | F1/F3 | manual operator action |

### Section 4 — Evidence ledger event schemas

For every event in §3, ship a JSON Schema describing the structured tracing payload. Schemas live in `docs/schemas/git_251/`:

- `docs/schemas/git_251/run_git_locked.schema.json` — covers all `run_git_locked_*` events
- `docs/schemas/git_251/git_segfault_retry.schema.json` — covers E1/E2/E3 events
- `docs/schemas/git_251/git_repo_lock.schema.json` — covers B2 events
- `docs/schemas/git_251/git_flock.schema.json` — covers B3 events
- `docs/schemas/git_251/reservation_activity.schema.json` — covers C2 events
- `docs/schemas/git_251/pathspec_walk.schema.json` — covers C3 events
- `docs/schemas/git_251/doctor_fix_orphan_refs.schema.json` — covers F1/F3 events
- `docs/schemas/git_251/health_sweep.schema.json` — covers F5 events (cross-references br-66evl)
- `docs/schemas/git_251/boot_check.schema.json` — covers F8 events (cross-references br-8lp54)

Each schema has:
- `$schema`: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
- `$id`: stable URI under `https://schemas.mcp-agent-mail/git_251/<name>.schema.json`
- `title`, `description`
- `type: object`, `additionalProperties: false`
- `required: ["ts","level","target","name","fields"]` plus event-specific required field set
- `properties.fields.properties` enumerated per Section 2 baseline + extras

### Section 5 — Versioning + drift detection (NEW for V2 revision)

The doc declares a `spec_version` (semver). When a new event/field is added:
1. Bump `spec_version` patch (e.g. 1.0.0 → 1.0.1).
2. Add a `## Changelog` entry at the bottom of the doc.
3. Add the corresponding JSON Schema to `docs/schemas/git_251/`.

Drift-detection automation (NEW):
- `scripts/check_observability_drift.py` (new) — scans the codebase for `tracing::*!(target = "mcp_agent_mail::*", ...)` invocations, extracts the event name + field set, cross-references against the metrics-catalog table in §3 and the JSON Schemas. Emits a list of:
  - Code emits NOT in spec doc (drift: code ahead)
  - Spec entries NOT in code (drift: doc ahead)
  - Field-set mismatches between code emit and schema
- CI gate: this script runs as a workflow step; non-zero exit fails the PR with a clear diff.

### Section 6 — Cross-references

Sibling beads that consume E6:
- `br-fqs7t` — E4 TUI toast: uses `git_segfault_retry` event; toast text includes `repo_slug`.
- `br-66evl` — F5 health sweep: emits `git_ref_integrity_*` events (also schema'd here).
- `br-8lp54` — F8 boot integrity: emits `boot_check_*` events (also schema'd here).
- `br-kgck8` — G2 stress harness: asserts metrics catalog entries are emitted by all 4 scenarios.

## Non-goals

- Not creating a new metrics infrastructure — uses existing `tracing` subscriber + Prometheus exporter.
- Not auto-generating schemas from code — explicit hand-authored schemas; CI enforces consistency via the drift check.
- Not changing existing event names mid-flight (would break dashboards). Document current names; future renames go through a deprecation cycle.

### JSON Schemas

- [ ] Each schema validates against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12.
- [ ] Each schema's `required` field includes `["ts","level","target","name","fields"]` plus event-specific required fields per §2.
- [ ] Per-schema `additionalProperties: false` (strict — drift caught early).

### Drift-detection script

- [ ] `scripts/check_observability_drift.py` exists, executable, has `--help`.
- [ ] Script enumerates `tracing::*!(target = "mcp_agent_mail::*", ...)` calls via `ast-grep` (preferred) or `rg` (fallback).
- [ ] Script cross-references against §3 catalog AND §4 schemas.
- [ ] Script emits structured findings (JSON to stdout) with categories: `code_ahead`, `doc_ahead`, `field_mismatch`.
- [ ] Exit 0 when consistent; exit 1 with non-empty findings list when drift detected.

### CI integration

- [ ] `.github/workflows/observability_drift.yml` (or addition to existing CI workflow) runs the drift check on PRs touching `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/`, `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/`, or `docs/OBSERVABILITY_git_251.md`.
- [ ] Workflow surfaces drift findings as a PR comment (or the GitHub Actions summary).

### Tests

- [ ] All 9 schemas have at least one positive sample (valid event JSON) AND one negative sample (rejected) under `tests/fixtures/observability/<event_name>/{valid_*.json,invalid_*.json}`.
- [ ] Schema-validation test: `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/tests/observability_schemas.rs` (new) loads each schema, validates positive/negative samples.
- [ ] Drift-check unit tests in `scripts/tests/test_check_observability_drift.py` (new) — covers all three drift categories.

notes:
## Testing strategy

### Unit tests on the drift-check script (`scripts/tests/test_check_observability_drift.py`, new)

Naming: `test_drift_<scenario>_<expectation>`.

1. `test_drift_no_drift_returns_zero` — fixture: code emits exactly what spec lists, exit 0, empty findings.
2. `test_drift_code_ahead_emits_finding` — fixture: code emits `git_new_event` not in spec, finding category `code_ahead`.
3. `test_drift_doc_ahead_emits_finding` — fixture: spec lists `git_old_event` not in code, finding category `doc_ahead`.
4. `test_drift_field_mismatch_emits_finding` — fixture: code emits `repo_slug` only; spec requires `repo_slug` + `caller`; finding category `field_mismatch`.
5. `test_drift_ignores_test_only_targets` — fixture: `tracing::*!(target = "tests::*"`)`; not flagged.
6. `test_drift_handles_macro_expansion` — fixture: event emit hidden inside macro; ast-grep recurses (or fallback rg with documented limitation).
7. `test_drift_emit_json_lines_envelope` — assert stdout is JSON-parseable structured findings, schema { findings: [{category, name, location, detail}] }.

### Schema validation tests (`crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/tests/observability_schemas.rs`, new)

For each of the 9 schemas:

- `<schema_name>_validates_positive_sample` — load `tests/fixtures/observability/<event>/valid_<n>.json`, assert validates.
- `<schema_name>_rejects_negative_sample` — load `tests/fixtures/observability/<event>/invalid_<n>.json`, assert rejected with expected error path.
- `<schema_name>_required_fields_match_spec_section_2` — parse schema, assert every Section 2 required field is in the schema's `required` array.

### E2E test (`tests/e2e/test_observability_drift.sh`, new)

Universal JSON-line logging schema. Per scenario captures stdout/stderr/exit.

Scenarios:

- `s1_clean_repo_no_drift` — fresh checkout, drift script exits 0.
- `s2_simulate_code_drift` — copy a fixture file under `/tmp` that emits a fake event not in spec, run drift script with that as input dir, assert exit 1 + finding category `code_ahead`.
- `s3_simulate_doc_drift` — fixture spec doc with extra entry not in code, assert exit 1 + `doc_ahead`.
- `s4_simulate_field_mismatch` — fixture event emit missing required field, assert exit 1 + `field_mismatch`.
- `s5_real_repo_consistency` — run against the actual repo (sanity check the spec doc IS consistent with code at landing time).

### Repro / verification

```bash
# Schema validation
cargo test -p mcp-agent-mail-server --test observability_schemas -- --nocapture

# Drift unit tests
python3 -m pytest scripts/tests/test_check_observability_drift.py -v

# E2E
bash tests/e2e/test_observability_drift.sh

# Manual drift check against current code
python3 scripts/check_observability_drift.py | jq '.'
```

### Universal e2e logging

Per-scenario subdir under `$LOG_DIR/<scenario>/`: `stdout.log`, `stderr.log`, `exit`, `findings.json` (the script's output captured for postmortem).

End-of-run summary line: `{ "ts":..., "test":"observability_drift", "summary":{ "scenarios":5, "passed":N, "failed":M, "log_dir":"...", "replay_command":"bash tests/e2e/test_observability_drift.sh --replay $LOG_DIR" } }`.

## References

- Original spec: `br-8ujfs.5.6` (closed) — preserved verbatim.
- Sibling consumers: br-fqs7t, br-66evl, br-8lp54, br-kgck8 (all reference E6 conventions).
- Audit verification: `beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T04-08-17Z/beads/br-8ujfs.5.6/verification.json`

title: Doctor FM: detect active python-server co-resident DB writer (P0 corruption root cause)
description: From B6 audit (br-bvq1x.2.6). The historical FM python-server-coresident-write has NO live doctor FM. An active legacy Python server writing storage.sqlite3 concurrently with the Rust server is a P0 corruption root cause (cited in integrity_page_malformed.rs and wal_shm_sidecar_drift.rs as a reason for drift). Today the corruption SYMPTOM is detected (integrity FMs) and a STALE python shadow is detected (fm-runtime-processes-stale-python-server-shadow), but a LIVE concurrent writer is not flagged before it corrupts. Add a detect-only FM under runtime_processes that flags a live non-Rust process holding/writing the same DB (e.g. via lock owner inspection or open-fd scan), with remediation guidance. Detect-only by design (doctor must not kill foreign processes). Anchors: doctor/fixers/integrity_page_malformed.rs, runtime process owner model (process_owner.rs), pool owner inspection.
close_reason: Implemented fm-runtime-processes-coresident-db-writer (P0, detect-only): pure over the I4 ProcessOwnerModel, flags a live Python mcp_agent_mail co-resident writer holding storage.sqlite3 open (conf 1.0) or its advisory lock (0.9) before it corrupts. Wired into registry + both dispatch arms; auto-surfaces via fixers/capabilities/explain and 'am doctor fix --list'. B6 disposition doc updated (gap resolved). Follow-up br-epoqj filed for truly-foreign non-python writers (filtered upstream). Verified: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean (all-targets), 8 FM tests + 696 doctor::fixers tests pass.

title: disk_monitor: remove unsafe malloc_trim that violates #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
description:
Commit 09077180 added `unsafe { nix::libc::malloc_trim(0); }` to `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/disk_monitor.rs` (line ~158). However, the server crate has `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at line 1 of lib.rs. This is a hard compilation error on any cfg(target_os="linux") build.

Fix: Remove the malloc_trim call entirely (the uncommitted working tree already has this fix from another agent). The alternative is to move malloc_trim into a separate helper crate that doesn't forbid unsafe, but the simpler fix is removal since the memory reclaim benefit is marginal.

Repro: `cargo check -p mcp-agent-mail-server --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
close_reason: Removed unsafe malloc_trim call. Committed as 947f3824.

title: P1: Make doctor read-only strategy honor committed hot-WAL state
description: Doctor dry-run and startup planning can inspect an immutable live main file while ignoring valid committed WAL frames. That can report tables or rows missing and choose Repair or Reconstruct from stale main-file state. Route every read-only planning decision through a private full-family snapshot whose guard lives for the connection lifetime.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with decisive rows committed only in WAL produces the same doctor strategy as a quiesced checkpointed equivalent. Dry-run and list modes preserve exact source main, WAL, SHM, journal, FrankenSQLite sidecars, names, and bytes. Nonregular and racing sidecars fail closed. Workspace check, clippy -D warnings, fmt, and focused tests pass.

title: P1: Walk canonical archive directories by stable no-follow descriptors
description: The message-id archive scanner now opens the final Markdown leaf with O_NOFOLLOW, but every projects/year/month directory is classified by pathname and then reopened by pathname. A concurrent rename/symlink replacement between metadata/file_type and read_dir can redirect the supposedly authoritative scan to a different tree, publish a false floor, or omit canonical IDs.
acceptance_criteria: The canonical archive walk binds every ancestor directory and leaf to stable no-follow descriptors (or an equivalent generation witness) and fails closed on replacement/drift. A deterministic race hook swaps a year/month ancestor after classification but before descent and proves no floor is published; stable valid, malformed, leaf-symlink, and bounded-read controls remain correct. Required checks/tests pass.

title: P1: Publish share SQLite snapshots atomically without clobber
description: The share snapshot destination path is checked with exists() and then published with overwrite-capable std::fs::rename. A raced regular file, dangling symlink, or another publisher can be replaced, destroying evidence. Successful publication also does not durably sync the destination parent before reporting success.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot publication uses an atomic no-replace primitive with bounded collision handling or a clear fail-closed error. Deterministic mutation-sensitive tests plant regular-file and dangling-symlink destinations after name selection and prove their bytes/type plus the private source remain intact. Successful publication syncs the destination parent before success; injected sync failure is reported honestly. Required workspace check, clippy -D warnings, fmt, and focused tests pass.

title: P1: Make recovery writer-drain proof deterministic and isolate test state
description: The positive write-barrier regression sleeps speculatively and accepts either Drained or Idle, so it can pass without ever observing an active writer. Test reset also mutates process-global barrier state behind a module-private mutex while pool tests may use the same barrier in parallel. Add an explicit writer-start handshake, require the Drained outcome, and provide one shared test-serialization boundary for every process-global barrier mutation.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation-sensitive test cannot pass unless one writer is registered before drain begins, drain reports Drained, a late writer is excluded, and release unblocks it. All tests that reset or depend on global barrier state share one serialization guard. Repeated bare-test and nextest runs pass without cross-test interference; workspace check, clippy -D warnings, and fmt pass.

title: [completion-debt of br-8ujfs.7.2] G2 stress demonstration — stress_pipeline_with_known_bad_git harness extension + retry-rate gate + 4-scenario coverage
description:
# G2: Stress demonstration with known-bad git binary

## Why this debt exists

Original `br-8ujfs.7.2` was closed pointing at `libgit2_index_race_immunity.rs` (a structural test) but the spec-required extension to `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/stress_pipeline.rs` was never added. Verification (audit pass 2026-05-09T00-49-33Z): enumerated every `#[test]` in the 3506-line `stress_pipeline.rs` — zero references to `AM_GIT_BINARY` / `2.51.0` / `known_bad_git`.

## Spec — preserves all original requirements verbatim

Empirical evidence that B+C+E layers defend the server when operator leaves broken git in place. Method: extend `stress_pipeline.rs` with a new test gated on `AM_TEST_GIT_251 != 0`. Run 30-agent message pipeline + 10-project concurrent ops with `AM_GIT_BINARY=/path/to/git-2.51.0`. Assert zero escalated errors; retries fine; segfault events fine.

Original success thresholds (preserved):
- ≤ 5% of shell-out git calls experience retry. Above that = deeper problem than 2.51.0; escalate.
- 0 retries for libgit2-backed paths (migration is working).
- 0 corrupted artifacts in the archive after the stress window.

## Current state

- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/stress_pipeline.rs` exists; tests cover normal stress patterns (30-agent message pipeline, 10-project concurrent ops, WBQ saturation, pool exhaustion, sustained 30s mixed workload, thundering herd, etc.) — see README L262-280.
- `libgit2_index_race_immunity.rs` (sibling test file) is structural — covers C8 (libgit2 immunity) but not the operator-deployed-broken-git scenario.
- `run_git_locked` (B4) exists in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/src/lib.rs` (or git_cmd.rs); has retry-on-segfault path.
- Operator runbook coverage exists; what's missing is the test-side artifact.

## Target state — 4-scenario harness

New test module: `crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/stress_pipeline_known_bad_git.rs` (separate file is cleaner than appending 500+ lines to the existing 3506-line file; matches existing pattern of one scenario per file).

### Scenario coverage

1. **Scenario A — Clean baseline** (no broken git): runs the existing 30-agent pipeline + 10-project concurrent ops with the system git unmodified. Establishes baseline retry-rate (should be 0).
2. **Scenario B — Synthetic racer** (no real 2.51.0 needed): wraps git via a shim shell script that injects an artificial SIGSEGV with probability 5% on `git update-ref` and `git commit` calls. Tests retry-on-segfault path WITHOUT requiring the actual buggy binary on the test box (CI-friendly).
3. **Scenario C — Real 2.51.0** (gated): if `AM_GIT_BINARY=<path-to-real-2.51.0>` is set AND `AM_TEST_GIT_251=1`, runs the same workload against the actual buggy binary. CI does NOT set these by default; runs locally on dev workstations only.
4. **Scenario D — Real 2.51.0 + flock layer disabled** (negative control, gated): same as C but with `AM_GIT_FLOCK_DISABLED=1` to verify the flock layer (B3) is what's actually preventing corruption. Expected: corruption rate spikes; test ASSERTS the spike to confirm flock is load-bearing.

### Retry-rate metric assertions

- Scenarios A, B, C, D all emit `git_segfault_retry_*` metrics (see E6 catalog in br-j1qwr).
- Scenario A: `retry_rate < 0.5%`.
- Scenario B: `retry_rate ∈ [3%, 8%]` (synthetic 5% with confidence interval).
- Scenario C: `retry_rate ≤ 5%` (per original threshold).
- Scenario D: `retry_rate ≤ 5%` BUT `archive_corruption_count > 0` asserted (negative control).

### Artifact pipeline

Per scenario, write to `tests/artifacts/stress/git_251/<UTC>/<scenario>/`:
- `metrics.json` — captured Prometheus-format metrics at end of run
- `events.jsonl` — every retry, segfault, lock event recorded chronologically
- `summary.json` — { scenario, total_calls, retries, segfaults, retry_rate, duration_ms, archive_corruption_count, libgit2_retries (must be 0) }
- `stdout.log`, `stderr.log` — full subprocess capture
- `replay.sh` — re-run command for postmortem

### Threshold TOML

`crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/fixtures/stress_pipeline_thresholds.toml`:

```toml
[scenario_a]
retry_rate_max = 0.005          # 0.5%
archive_corruption_max = 0
libgit2_retries_max = 0

[scenario_b]
retry_rate_min = 0.03
retry_rate_max = 0.08
archive_corruption_max = 0
libgit2_retries_max = 0

[scenario_c]
retry_rate_max = 0.05
archive_corruption_max = 0
libgit2_retries_max = 0

[scenario_d]
retry_rate_max = 0.05            # retry layer still works
archive_corruption_min = 1       # asserts flock IS load-bearing
libgit2_retries_max = 0
```

Test reads TOML, asserts measured values fall within thresholds. Editable without recompile = operator can tune for slower CI hosts.

### Synthetic racer (Scenario B)

`crates/mcp-agent-mail-storage/tests/fixtures/git_segfault_shim.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Wraps system git; injects synthetic SIGSEGV on update-ref / commit
# with configurable probability.
set -euo pipefail
PROB="${AM_TEST_RACER_PROB:-0.05}"
TRIGGERS="${AM_TEST_RACER_TRIGGERS:-update-ref,commit}"
for trig in ${TRIGGERS//,/ }; do
  if [[ "$*" == *" $trig "* ]] || [[ "$*" == *" $trig" ]]; then
    if awk -v p="$PROB" 'BEGIN{srand(); exit !(rand() < p)}'; then
      kill -SEGV $$ 2>/dev/null || exit 139
    fi
  fi
done
exec /usr/bin/git "$@"
```

(Equivalent Rust harness OK — shell shim is simplest.)

### Operator documentation

Update `docs/GIT_251_FINDINGS.md` (A1) with a new section:

> ### Reproducing under stress
>
> ```bash
> # Synthetic (no buggy git binary needed)
> AM_TEST_GIT_251=1 cargo test --test stress_pipeline_known_bad_git scenario_b
>
> # Real 2.51.0 (requires installed buggy binary)
> AM_TEST_GIT_251=1 \
> AM_GIT_BINARY=/path/to/git-2.51.0 \
> cargo test --test stress_pipeline_known_bad_git scenario_c
>
> # Negative control (verifies flock is load-bearing)
> AM_TEST_GIT_251=1 \
> AM_GIT_BINARY=/path/to/git-2.51.0 \
> AM_GIT_FLOCK_DISABLED=1 \
> cargo test --test stress_pipeline_known_bad_git scenario_d
> ```
>
> Artifacts under `tests/artifacts/stress/git_251/<UTC>/`. Replay any scenario via `./replay.sh`.

## Non-goals (verbatim from original)

- Not eliminating segfaults in kernel log (every retry = one segfault). We measure server survival, not git's bug.

notes:
## Testing strategy — unit + integration + scenario tests + bench

### Unit tests (in `stress_pipeline_known_bad_git.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`)

Test the test infrastructure (these run unconditionally):

1. `racer_shim_prob_0_never_injects` — set AM_TEST_RACER_PROB=0, run shim 100 times against `git status`, all succeed.
2. `racer_shim_prob_1_always_injects_on_target_subcommand` — PROB=1 + TRIGGERS=update-ref, `git update-ref` exits with SIGSEGV.
3. `racer_shim_passes_through_unrelated_commands` — PROB=1 + TRIGGERS=commit, `git status` always passes through.
4. `threshold_toml_parses_valid_fixture` — load file, all 4 scenario tables populated.
5. `threshold_toml_rejects_negative_retry_rate` — fixture with -0.05 → parse error.
6. `threshold_toml_rejects_min_above_max` — retry_rate_min=0.5, retry_rate_max=0.1 → parse error.
7. `artifact_writer_emits_all_six_files` — run a fake scenario, assert metrics.json/events.jsonl/summary.json/stdout.log/stderr.log/replay.sh all exist and parse.
8. `artifact_writer_replay_sh_is_executable` — exec bit set; reading the file shows the literal cargo test invocation.

### Scenario tests (`#[test]` in same file)

9. `scenario_a_clean_baseline` — unconditional. Runs 30-agent + 10-project workload with system git. Asserts retry_rate < 0.5%, no corruption, no libgit2 retries. Writes artifacts. Duration budget: 60s on dev workstation.
10. `scenario_b_synthetic_racer` — gated on `AM_TEST_GIT_251=1`. Sets `GIT_EXEC_PATH` or `AM_GIT_BINARY` to the shim. Runs same workload. Asserts retry_rate in [3%, 8%], no corruption, no libgit2 retries. Writes artifacts. Duration budget: 90s.
11. `scenario_c_real_2510_gated` — gated on `AM_TEST_GIT_251=1` AND `AM_GIT_BINARY` pointing at a real 2.51.0. Runs same workload. Asserts retry_rate ≤ 5%, no corruption, no libgit2 retries.
12. `scenario_d_real_2510_no_flock_gated` — gated like C plus `AM_GIT_FLOCK_DISABLED=1`. Asserts retry_rate ≤ 5% but archive_corruption ≥ 1 (negative control proves flock is load-bearing).

### Integration with E6 metrics catalog

Each scenario asserts that the following metrics are emitted at least once with sane values (cross-references E6 / br-j1qwr):

- `git_segfault_total{repo_slug,caller}` — count > 0 in scenarios B/C/D, 0 in A
- `git_segfault_retry_attempted_total{caller}` — count > 0 in B/C/D, 0 in A
- `git_segfault_retry_succeeded_total{caller,attempt_n}` — count > 0 in B/C, 0 in A; in D, count may be > 0 but corruption still occurs (flock disabled)
- `git_segfault_retry_exhausted_total{caller}` — should be 0 in all healthy runs

### E2E test (`tests/e2e/test_stress_known_bad_git.sh`, new)

Wraps the cargo test invocations and provides a uniform operator-facing entrypoint with structured logging:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# E2E: G2 stress with known-bad git
# Usage: bash tests/e2e/test_stress_known_bad_git.sh [a|b|c|d|all]
# Optional env: AM_GIT_BINARY (real 2.51.0 path for scenarios c/d)

set -euo pipefail
LOG_DIR="tests/artifacts/stress/git_251/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

# Universal JSON-line event logger (same schema as other E2Es)
log_event() { ... ts/test/scenario/level/message/data/latency_ms ... }

run_scenario() {
  local name="$1" gate_envs="$2"
  if ! eval "$gate_envs" cargo test --test stress_pipeline_known_bad_git "scenario_$name" -- --nocapture; then
    log_event error "$name" "scenario_failed" "{}"
    return 1
  fi
  log_event pass "$name" "scenario_passed" "{}"
}

# Default: scenario A only. With AM_TEST_GIT_251=1: A+B. With AM_GIT_BINARY set: A+B+C+D.
```

E2E logging requirements:
- Per-scenario `$LOG_DIR/$scenario/` subdir with stdout/stderr/exit/replay.sh.
- Top-level `$LOG_DIR/events.jsonl` with universal schema events.
- End-of-run summary line with { scenarios_run, passed, failed, log_dir, replay_command }.

### Repro / verification commands

title: ATC Track 5: Calibration Guard — Conformal Self-Monitoring
description:
# Track 5: Calibration Guard (Conformal Self-Monitoring)

## Graveyard Source: §12.1 Conformal Prediction, §0.8 Calibration Layer

## What
The ATC monitors its own prediction accuracy and automatically switches to
conservative (safe) mode when its predictions degrade. This prevents a
miscalibrated ATC from causing more harm than good.

## Why
Without self-monitoring, the ATC could:
- Systematically declare live agents as dead (false positives)
- Miss real conflicts (false negatives)
- Route messages to overloaded agents consistently

The calibration guard catches these failure modes BEFORE they cause damage.

## Ground Truth Definitions (Critical)
Each subsystem needs a concrete definition of "was the prediction correct?"

### Liveness Ground Truth
- Predicted Alive + agent sends message within 2× avg_interval → CORRECT
- Predicted Alive + agent declared Dead by SPRT within next interval → INCORRECT
- Predicted Dead + agent sends message (resurrection) → INCORRECT (false death)
- Predicted Dead + no activity for 10× avg_interval → CORRECT

### Conflict Ground Truth
- Predicted "no conflict" + no reservation conflict occurs → CORRECT
- Predicted "no conflict" + reservation conflict occurs → INCORRECT (miss)
- Predicted "conflict" + reservation conflict occurs → CORRECT (true positive)
- Predicted "conflict" + no conflict in next 5 min → AMBIGUOUS (don't count;
  the advisory may have PREVENTED the conflict — can't penalize success)

### Load Routing Ground Truth
- Routed to agent + agent responds within 2× avg_response_time → CORRECT
- Routed to agent + agent doesn't respond within 5× avg_response_time → INCORRECT
- For the "defer" action: if deferred message is eventually handled within
  10 min → CORRECT; if it sits unhandled for 30+ min → INCORRECT

### Handling Ambiguity
The conflict case is tricky: successful interventions look like false positives.
Solution: only count CLEAR outcomes. Ambiguous cases are excluded from the
coverage calculation but logged to the evidence ledger for manual review.

## Mechanism
### Coverage Tracking
```rust
struct CalibrationWindow {
    /// Sliding window of recent predictions with outcomes
    outcomes: VecDeque<PredictionOutcome>,
    /// Window size (default 50 recent unambiguous decisions)
    window_size: usize,
    /// Required coverage rate (default 0.85)
    required_coverage: f64,
    /// Current coverage (computed incrementally)
    current_coverage: f64,
    /// Count of ambiguous outcomes (tracked but excluded)
    ambiguous_count: u64,
}

struct PredictionOutcome {
    subsystem: AtcSubsystem,
    predicted_state: String,
    actual_outcome: OutcomeKind, // Correct | Incorrect | Ambiguous
    timestamp: i64,
    decision_id: u64, // links to evidence ledger
}
```

### Safe Mode Activation
When coverage drops below threshold (default 85% over last 50 clear outcomes):
1. Log the degradation with full window history to evidence ledger
2. Switch ALL decision cores to conservative mode:
   - Liveness: only declare dead after 3× normal evidence threshold
   - Conflict: send advisories but never force-release reservations
   - Load routing: fall back to "fewest active reservations" heuristic
3. Emit a toast notification in the TUI: "ATC safe mode active"
4. Send a message to the #atc-status thread explaining the degradation
5. Continue monitoring — exit safe mode after AM_ATC_SAFE_MODE_RECOVERY_COUNT (default 20)
   consecutive correct predictions above threshold

### Signal Consumption from Track 11
Track 5 does NOT maintain its own e-value monitor — it consumes signals from
Track 11's three components:
- **E-process miscalibrated?** → primary safe mode trigger
- **CUSUM regime change (degradation)?** → immediate safe mode
- **CUSUM regime change (improvement)?** → safe mode exit candidate
- **Regret tracker suggestions** → surfaced in evidence ledger for operator

The CalibrationGuard struct holds a reference to the martingale engine
and queries it on each tick, delegating all the statistical machinery
to Track 11. Track 5 owns the POLICY (when to enter/exit safe mode);
Track 11 owns the EVIDENCE (how confident are we that something is wrong).

## Dependency
- Requires Track 1 (Decision Core) — wraps the core with monitoring
- Requires Track 4 (Evidence Ledger) — logs calibration state changes

## Files
- `crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/atc.rs` (calibration module within ATC)

## Tests
- Unit: perfect predictions → coverage = 1.0, healthy = true
- Unit: 50% wrong predictions → coverage = 0.5, healthy = false
- Unit: safe mode activation when coverage drops below threshold
- Unit: safe mode deactivation after recovery
- Unit: ambiguous outcomes excluded from coverage calculation
- Unit: e-value monitor accumulates evidence correctly
- Unit: conservative mode produces different (safer) actions
- Unit: each subsystem's ground truth definition produces correct outcomes
- Integration: safe mode propagates to all decision cores

title: B.2: Wire ledger into backpressure, SLO, retention, and TUI diff decisions
description:
**Background**

The evidence ledger from B.1 is only useful if actual decisions are recorded into it. This task wires the ledger into the 5 highest-value decision points in the codebase:

1. **Cache eviction** (cache.rs) -- each eviction decision records: cache size, evicted key age, frequency, queue (small/main for S3-FIFO).
2. **Backpressure level** (if implemented in server) -- records: queue depth, recent latency p99, action (accept/defer/reject).
3. **Deferred touch flush** (cache.rs:502) -- records: shard count, pending count, elapsed since last flush, action (flush/defer).
4. **Coalesce join/timeout** (coalesce.rs:258) -- records: key, role (leader/joiner), timeout_ms, action outcome.
5. **TUI render strategy** (when D is implemented) -- records: frame state, budget remaining, action (incremental/full/deferred).

**Scope / Adoption wedge**

At each decision point, add a single `evidence_ledger().record(...)` call. This is a one-liner addition at each site. The evidence JSON is constructed from local variables already in scope.

For cache eviction (highest value): in the `lru_evict_if_full` function (or S3-FIFO equivalent), after each eviction:

```rust
evidence_ledger().record(
    "cache.eviction",
    serde_json::json!({
        "cache_size": map.len(),
        "evicted_age_secs": entry.inserted.elapsed().as_secs(),
        "evicted_freq": entry.access_count,
    }),
    "evict",
    Some("hit_rate >= 0.85"),
    0.9,
    "s3fifo_v1",
);
```

For coalesce outcomes: in `execute_or_join` after determining role:

```rust
evidence_ledger().record(
    "coalesce.outcome",
    serde_json::json!({
        "key_hash": hash(&key),
        "inflight_count": self.inflight_count(),
    }),
    if was_joined { "joined" } else { "executed" },
    Some("join_rate >= 0.3"),
    0.8,
    "coalesce_v1",
);
```

**Risks / Safe Mode**

- Risk: Adding overhead to hot paths. Mitigation: `record()` is < 1 microsecond (mutex + VecDeque push_back). Benchmark to confirm.
- Risk: serde_json::json! macro allocations. Mitigation: Only allocate in trace-level paths; use compile-time feature flag `evidence-ledger` to strip all recording calls in production if needed.
- Fallback trigger: If any benchmark shows > 2% regression from recording calls, add `#[cfg(feature = "evidence-ledger")]` around all call sites.

**Validation**

After wiring, run the existing stress tests and verify:
1. Evidence ledger has entries for all 5 decision points.
2. No test regression (all 1000+ tests pass).
3. Overhead measurement: insert 10K items into cache, measure total time with and without ledger recording; difference must be < 5%.

**Tests (5 required)**

1. `evidence_cache_eviction_recorded` -- trigger eviction, verify ledger has "cache.eviction" entry
2. `evidence_coalesce_outcome_recorded` -- run coalesce with joiners, verify entries
3. `evidence_deferred_flush_recorded` -- trigger flush, verify entry
4. `evidence_no_regression_cache_stress` -- 10K inserts, wall time < 1.05x baseline
5. `evidence_multiple_decision_points` -- exercise all 5 points, verify query returns distinct types
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Evidence recording hooks are added at all planned decision points (backpressure, SLO, retention, TUI diff, and one additional guard point)
- Each hook emits structured payloads with decision inputs, selected action, confidence/expected loss, and correlation ID
- Unit tests verify payload schema, redaction compliance, and behavior when ledger is disabled/unavailable
- Integration tests validate outcome-backfill linking and cross-component decision trace continuity
- E2E scenario exercises decision spikes and confirms ledger and runtime behavior remain stable
- Performance overhead remains within agreed budget and is evidenced by benchmark artifacts
- Diagnostic logs expose dropped-record reasons, write failures, and per-point emission counters
notes:
## Plan-Space Review Findings (2026-02-13)

**CRITICAL: 3 of 5 decision points don't exist yet.** Backpressure (#2) is not implemented. TUI render strategy (#5) requires Track D. Scope down to the 3 implementable points NOW:
1. Cache eviction (cache.rs) — EXISTS
2. Deferred touch flush (cache.rs:502) — EXISTS
3. Coalesce join/timeout (coalesce.rs:258) — EXISTS

Points 4-5 should be marked as "wire when available" with a TODO comment, not hard-required.

**CRITICAL: No global `evidence_ledger()` accessor defined.** B.1 defines the struct but not the singleton. Add to this bead's scope: `pub fn evidence_ledger() -> &'static EvidenceLedger { static LEDGER: OnceLock<EvidenceLedger> = OnceLock::new(); LEDGER.get_or_init(|| EvidenceLedger::new(1000)) }` in a new `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/evidence.rs` module.

**FIX: Snippet error.** The coalesce snippet uses `hash(&key)` which isn't a free function in Rust. Use `{ use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher, BuildHasher}; let mut h = std::hash::RandomState::new().build_hasher(); key.hash(&mut h); h.finish() }`.

**FIX: Test 5 is unimplementable.** `evidence_multiple_decision_points` says "exercise all 5 points" but only 3 exist. Change to "exercise all 3 implementable points."

**Additional test:** `evidence_record_overhead` — time 10K `record()` calls, verify p99 < 1 microsecond.

description:
## Summary
In TUI V2 E2E runs, send_message returns successful deliveries with payload IDs, but immediate and retried fetch_inbox calls for the recipient return [] for at least 5 attempts.

## Reproduction
1. register agents and set contact policy open.
2. send_message from RedHawk -> BlueFalcon succeeds with deliveries payload id.

title: P0: Unify release signing provenance across build paths
description: The current DSR style release manifest marks every archive unsigned and publishes no Sigstore bundles. title: Track 3: Context & Discovery — robot thread, search, message, navigate

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# Track 3: Context & Discovery Commands

## T3.1: `am robot thread <id>`

Render a complete conversation thread in agent-consumable format.
This is where Markdown format shines — conversations are natural in Markdown.

Default format: Markdown (override with --format toon|json)

Output:
```markdown
## Thread: FEAT-123 — Add authentication layer
**Messages**: 8 | **Participants**: BlueLake, RedFox, GreenCastle | **Last activity**: 5m ago

---

### [1] BlueLake → RedFox, GreenCastle | 2h ago | importance: high | ack: required
**Subject**: [FEAT-123] Starting auth implementation

I'm taking on the authentication feature. Planning to use JWT with JWKS.
Will need to modify: src/auth/**, src/middleware/**, tests/auth/**

---

### [2] RedFox → BlueLake | 1h45m ago | importance: normal | ack: done ✓
**Subject**: Re: [FEAT-123] Starting auth implementation

Sounds good. I have reservations on src/middleware/** — let me release those first.

---
(... remaining messages ...)
```

Flags:
  --limit N          Max messages (default: all)
  --include-bodies   Always include bodies (default: true for robot)
  --since <ts>       Only messages after timestamp
  --format md        Markdown (default for this command)

## T3.2: `am robot search <query>`

Full-text search with faceted results. More powerful than `am mail search`
because it includes relevance scores and aggregated facets.

```
am robot search "authentication JWT"
am robot search "deploy" --kind messages --importance urgent
am robot search "reservation conflict" --since 24h
```

Output:
```
_meta.query: authentication JWT
_meta.total_results: 12
_meta.elapsed_ms: 45

facets:
  by_thread: FEAT-123(5), AUTH-001(3), MISC(4)
  by_agent: BlueLake(4), RedFox(3), GreenCastle(5)
  by_importance: high(3), normal(8), urgent(1)

results[10]{id,relevance,from,subject,thread,snippet,age}:
  201,0.95,BlueLake,JWT implementation plan,FEAT-123,"...JWT with JWKS rotation...",2h
  198,0.87,RedFox,Auth middleware review,FEAT-123,"...middleware chain for auth...",3h
  ...
```

## T3.3: `am robot message <id>`

Single message with full context: body, thread position, adjacent messages.
Useful when an agent gets a message ID and wants to understand context.

Output includes:
- Full message body
- Thread ID and position (message 3 of 8)
- Previous message summary (for reply context)
- Next message summary (if exists)
- Sender info (program, model)
- Attachments list

## T3.4: `am robot navigate <uri>`

Resolve any MCP resource URI and return its data in robot format.
This is the "universal accessor" — any resource:// URI that the TUI
can deep-link to, the agent can access via this command.

```
am robot navigate resource://inbox/BlueLake
am robot navigate resource://thread/FEAT-123
am robot navigate resource://tooling/metrics
am robot navigate resource://views/ack-overdue/BlueLake
```

This is essentially a CLI wrapper around the MCP resource system,
but with robot-friendly formatting.

title: META: re-run reality check after all 5 epics close; verify no new gaps emerged during implementation
description:
# META: Reality check epilogue

## Why this bead exists

Epics br-o217s, br-il53l, br-bn0vb, br-8qdh0, br-a2k3h were born from a single reality-check session (2026-04-17). Implementing them over weeks or months inevitably causes **new** drift:
- New tools might be added during the work
- New README claims might be written
- A test might start depending on something that was supposed to be retired
- Performance characteristics might have shifted

The discipline that created this epic set is worth re-applying once the set closes. This bead captures that discipline as a scheduled task.

## Scope

Run `/reality-check-for-project` (the Claude skill) against this repo after **all** of the following close:

- br-o217s (docs alignment)
- br-il53l (WASM decision executed, either branch)
- br-bn0vb (ATC loop closed + disclaimer removed)
- br-8qdh0 (archive perf under budget)
- br-a2k3h (conformance coverage complete)

Expected findings: zero new-category gaps. Acceptable findings: minor drift (if any) is closed as part of this bead, not opened as a new epic.

## Process

1. Start fresh reality-check session (don't consult this bead set; run the skill clean)
2. Produce a fresh Vision Checklist against current README + AGENTS.md + docs/
3. Compare to `reality-check_2026-04-17_findings.md` (commit this bead's original findings somewhere traceable)
4. Categorize findings:
   - DONE: gap from original is now closed (expected state)
   - REGRESSED: gap was closed but reopened during implementation (must fix)
   - NEW: gap not in original reality check (investigate: did we introduce a new feature without docs? did something change externally?)
   - PERSISTENT: original gap still open (indicates an epic didn't fully deliver; file follow-up bead)
5. File new beads for any REGRESSED / NEW / PERSISTENT items

## Deliverables

- `reality-check_<new-date>_findings.md` committed to docs/
- A diff artifact comparing 2026-04-17 to the new run
- A one-line CHANGELOG entry: "Reality check epilogue: <n> regressions found, <m> new gaps, all tracked"

## Test plan

- Epilogue verifies the implementation work actually delivered on intent (the whole point)
- Any findings produce follow-up beads, each with their own DoD

## Logging requirements

- The new reality-check report is itself the log
- If the report finds zero issues, that is explicitly recorded

## Non-goals

- Not running this continuously; it's a one-shot closure gate
- Not re-doing the Phase 4 ambition rounds automatically (those happen when/if the team decides to do another pass)

## Dependencies

- Depends on all 5 epics closing. Use `br dep add br-REALITY_META br-o217s --type blocks` etc. for each epic (add after all children land so the graph is clean).

## Definition of done

- Reality check run completed
- New findings doc committed
- Any NEW/REGRESSED/PERSISTENT gaps converted to beads
- This bead closes when the re-run produces a "no outstanding gaps" outcome OR the outstanding gaps are tracked
close_reason: Completed: re-ran the post-epic reality check, fixed /mail/ws-state deferred-browser doc drift inline, and found no new untracked gap category

title: [epic] P0 TUI Incident: eliminate tab-lag + flashing across all screens without reducing robustness
description:
## Objective
Completely remove the extreme lag and flashing behavior when tabbing through TUI screens, while preserving visual parity and robustness. This incident is treated as a hotpath correctness/performance bug, not a cosmetic optimization.

## Non-Negotiable Constraints
- Do not weaken robustness to save CPU (for example, no collapsing MCP/HTTP worker parallelism to fragile single-thread behavior).
- Do not change the visual language or UX semantics of the TUI; performance work must be behaviorally isomorphic.
- Fix root causes in the true hotpath, including cross-project causes in `/dp/asupersync`, `/dp/frankentui`, `/dp/frankensqlite`, and `/dp/frankensearch`.
- Keep transport/tool correctness and cancellation safety intact.

## Evidence Driving This Epic
- Live process profiling showed main-thread saturation and worker wake-timeout churn.
- `strace` showed repeated short-timeout futex waits across worker threads.
- Event-loop patterns indicated repeated zero-timeout drains (`poll(..., 0)`) and redraw bursts.
- App static analysis showed `Tick` currently drives all screens, including inactive ones.

## Deliverable
A dependency-structured, end-to-end remediation program that:
1. Identifies and fixes root causes across runtime/event-loop/app/screen/data layers.
2. Verifies no regression in robustness or UI behavior.
3. Installs durable perf/flash guardrails in tests and CI.
acceptance_criteria:
1. P95 tab-to-screen activation latency is <= 75ms on dev reference machine and <= 120ms on CI baseline.
2. CPU while idle on TUI dashboard is materially below pre-fix incident baseline.
3. No visible flashing occurs during screen traversal under deterministic PTY replay.
4. No reduction in transport/runtime robustness (threading, cancellation, backpressure safety preserved).
5. Cross-project fixes in `/dp/asupersync` and `/dp/frankentui` are validated by targeted regressions.
6. CI includes repeatable traversal and flash-regression gates.
Plan-space hardening requirements:
1. Comprehensive unit tests must cover happy path, edge cases, boundary conditions, invariants, and failure paths introduced by this bead.
2. Comprehensive integration/E2E (PTY/stress where relevant) scripts must validate end-user behavior, degraded-mode behavior, and recovery paths for this bead.
3. Detailed diagnostics logging/artifacts are mandatory: scenario IDs, timestamps, timing breakdowns (p50/p95/p99 where applicable), failure reason codes, key counters, and artifact file paths.
4. Verification commands and reproduction steps must be documented so failures are locally reproducible by another engineer.
close_reason: All dependent tracks closed (A-G); incident remediation epic complete

title: identity test: hot_health_check_does_not_advance_writer_epoch fails in isolation (epoch +2 = one WriteGuard cycle; cached-pool miss on hot path?) — pre-existing at 845f1438
close_reason: Fixed: get_authoritative_live_db_pool treated any pool-cache miss as cold bootstrap and bracketed get_or_create_pool with an archive-read WriteGuard — but POOL_CACHE holds Weak refs, so any health check after the last DbPool handle dropped re-entered the durable-writer epoch (+2) and invalidated archive-read snapshot generations. At HEAD this failed the full tools suite, not just isolation. Now an initialized on-disk mailbox (file present, non-empty) opens via the zero-footprint strict query-only path (get_live_read_db_pool); only genuinely cold bootstrap (missing/empty file or memory db with no live pool) keeps the WriteGuard bracket. Both callers (health_check, check_file_reservation_conflicts) are read paths. Second finding via strace: byte-exact family neutrality is impossible at HEAD because frankensqlite's process-global namespace retains the bootstrap RW fd and re-opens drive WAL-checkpoint housekeeping through it, bumping only header change-counter bytes 24..28/92..96 (113->121, data pages identical) — engine gap filed br-mmnyj; test now masks exactly those two fields and asserts everything else byte-for-byte. Verified: target test green isolated + full tools suite 904/904, clippy --all-targets -D warnings green, fmt green, ubs on touched files: only pre-existing whole-file findings.

title: P0: Fail closed when installer cannot generate a cryptographic bearer token
description: install.sh generate_bearer_token falls through from openssl and /dev/urandom to a date/PID sha256 pipeline and ultimately the fixed literal placeholder-token-replace-me. On hosts missing those tools or when the pipeline fails, every installation can publish a predictable bearer into the service and MCP client configs.
acceptance_criteria: Bearer generation succeeds only from an operating-system or cryptographic RNG and produces the required entropy/encoding, otherwise installation stops before service or client credential mutation. A causal shell test shadows/makes unavailable every RNG dependency and proves nonzero failure plus byte-identical credential-bearing configs; positive openssl and urandom controls produce nonempty distinct tokens without printing them. No fixed or time/PID-derived fallback remains.

title: P0: Read canonical config.env without following authority swaps
description: Runtime user-env discovery selects config.env with Path::is_file and then reloads it with fs::read_to_string. Both follow symlinks and the separate select/read calls race. An attacker or stale link can redirect HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN after secure setup, while an obstructed canonical XDG path may silently fall through to a legacy HOME credential.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical user credential discovery and read use one bounded regular-file no-follow authority and fail closed on symlink, non-regular, unreadable, invalid UTF-8, oversized, or swapped inputs without consulting a lower-precedence stale credential. Parent-directory authority is bound or revalidated at the read seam. Mutation-sensitive tests cover canonical leaf and parent symlink/swap, custom-XDG obstruction versus conflicting HOME token, oversized/invalid input, ordinary canonical and legacy migration controls, and a fresh-process restart. Targeted tests, check, clippy -D warnings, and fmt pass remotely.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Root-cause trace: the current is_file selection and later read_to_string both follow links and race. Returning an empty user-env map alone is unsafe because no bearer or JWT makes the loopback HTTP control plane intentionally unauthenticated. Repair will use one bounded no-follow candidate read, stop on any higher-priority obstruction, retain an explicit authority error in Config, and reject server startup before mailbox or listener mutations. Unix will bind the parent directory handle and open the leaf with openat; other targets will revalidate parent identity.

title: Quarantine experimental SQLite paths from startup health
description:
## What
Add a regression guard that keeps startup, health, doctor fast probes, and normal operator paths off FrankenSQLite or other experimental SQLite adapter paths unless a test or explicit opt-in intentionally selects them.

## Why
A real user startup crash reached a FrankenSQLite RefCell panic after mailbox repair. Even when the immediate code path is fixed, this class should not regress silently through path dependencies, feature flags, or future health/startup changes.

## How
Audit dependency and feature boundaries for mcp-agent-mail-cli, mcp-agent-mail-server, mcp-agent-mail-db, and beads integration. Add a focused dependency-tree or compile-time assertion where feasible, plus a runtime smoke fixture that launches the startup/health path against a repaired mailbox and asserts no FrankenSQLite frames or RefCell panic signatures appear in stderr/log artifacts. Keep any optional FrankenSQLite usage explicit and named.

## Acceptance criteria
- Startup, health_check, doctor fast verdict, and bare `am` startup smoke cover the repaired-mailbox scenario that previously crashed.
- Tests fail if the normal path reintroduces sqlmodel_frankensqlite/frankensqlite DB connections without an explicit opt-in.
- Panic-signature artifact checks include thread name, stderr, and backtrace snippets when present.
- Verification runs through rch for cargo gates and uses an isolated STORAGE_ROOT, never the operator mailbox.
- Documentation or inline comments explain the allowed experimental boundary without creating compatibility shims.
close_reason: Added canonical SQLite startup/health guards and repaired-mailbox panic-signature regression coverage; verified with rch targeted tests plus workspace fmt/check/clippy.

title: Search backfill visibility and stale-index guard
description:
## What
Expose Search V3 cold-start/backfill state clearly and prevent stale lexical indexes from silently looking healthy after startup recovery, migration, or reconstruct.

## Why
Search is a major user-facing surface. Startup backfill is intentionally delayed/backgrounded for responsiveness, but operators and agents need to know when results are partial, stale, or rebuilding.

## How
Add a shared search-index health model with last backfill time, indexed message count, skipped count, index generation, source DB identity, rebuild in-progress flag, and stale reason. Surface it in robot health/status, tooling diagnostics, and release health if appropriate.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests cover fresh, delayed, failed, stale-after-reconstruct, and in-memory DB cases.
- Robot JSON/toon reports partial/stale search state with safe remediation.
- Search queries can include diagnostics or warnings when index state is known partial.
- E2E scenario reconstructs or migrates a mailbox and proves search state transitions from stale/rebuilding to fresh.
- No user-facing path blocks indefinitely waiting for backfill.

title: Reservation expiry herd forecast
description:
## What
Add a reservation topology forecast that identifies expiry herds, contention bursts, and soon-to-conflict file paths before they turn into commit-blocking surprises.

## Why
Reservations expire by TTL, which is good for crash recovery but can create herds under swarm work: many agents lose leases at once, renew too late, or concentrate on the same hot paths. Operators and agents need advance warning and suggested renew/release actions.

## How
Use existing active reservation data, symmetric glob overlap logic, and robot/TUI reservation views to compute expiry buckets, overlapping path hotspots, stale holder risk, and suggested actions. Keep this advisory; do not auto-renew or force-release.

## Acceptance criteria
- Robot reservations/status reports expiry-herd buckets and top conflict hotspots.
- Tests cover overlapping globs, shared vs exclusive leases, expired leases, soon-expiring leases, and stale holder metadata.
- TUI or web reservation surface can show the same summary if in scope.
- Recommendation output includes exact safe commands and evidence.
- No behavior weakens advisory reservation semantics or bypasses pre-commit guard rules.

title: Agent identity lifecycle diagnostics
description:
## What
Add diagnostics for stale, duplicate, confusing, or half-registered agent identities across projects and product buses.

## Why
Large swarms accumulate many agent identities. Operators need to distinguish active agents, stale but harmless profiles, malformed names, duplicate client sessions, and identity/config mismatches without deleting anything.

## How
Extend doctor/robot agents views with lifecycle categories: active, idle, stale, missing profile artifact, DB-only, archive-only, duplicate pane mapping, policy mismatch, and likely wrong project. Provide explainers and safe remediation commands such as re-register, mark read, refresh pane identity, or quarantine via doctor where already supported.

## Acceptance criteria
- Diagnostics cover DB/archive/profile/pane identity disagreements with machine-readable reason codes.
- Tests build isolated projects with stale profile, missing archive, duplicate pane identity, malformed explicit name, and cross-project mismatch cases.
- Human output remains concise and points to robot/json for full details.
- No diagnostic deletes identities or profiles.
- Agent-name validation rules remain adjective+noun compatible.

title: Share export privacy regression corpus
description:
## What
Build a focused privacy regression corpus for share/export/static-bundle/live-verify paths.

## Why
Share/export is high-trust: it packages mailbox data for external viewing. The scrubber, bundle builder, crypto/decrypt path, and live verifier need fixtures that prove private fields stay private while useful metadata remains verifiable.

## How
Create deterministic fixture mailboxes with messages, attachments, secrets, bearer-looking strings, private paths, contact metadata, reservations, products, and encrypted share data. Run export, verify, decrypt where applicable, and static/live verification against the corpus.

## Acceptance criteria
- Corpus covers message bodies, subjects, attachments, env-like secrets, path redaction, recipient metadata, contact links, reservations, and product links.
- Tests assert both absence of private raw strings and presence of required public proof metadata.
- Live-verify/static-export fixtures produce replayable artifacts with schema versions.
- Crypto/share tests use real encrypt/decrypt paths where applicable, not stubs.
- Docs explain how to add new privacy fixtures when export fields change.

title: Forensic timeline since last healthy run
description:
## What
Add a doctor/robot timeline that answers: what changed since the last known healthy mailbox run?

## Why
When an incident happens, the first useful operator question is not just what is broken now, but what changed: version, config, schema, archive commits, repair actions, search index generation, WAL state, or client setup. Today that archaeology is scattered across logs and artifacts.

## How
Record or derive lightweight health checkpoints from doctor health/check/fix, startup success, release health, and repair/reconstruct runs. Build a report that compares the current state to the last healthy checkpoint and links to relevant artifacts/commands.

## Acceptance criteria
- Report includes last healthy timestamp, binary/version, schema version, storage root, database path, search index generation, recent repair/reconstruct run ids, and archive commit summary.
- Tests cover no checkpoint, healthy-to-unhealthy, repair-to-healthy, binary upgrade, and config drift cases.
- Robot and doctor output include concise next actions plus artifact links.
- Privacy-sensitive fields are redacted.
- The timeline is read-only by default and does not run repair automatically.
