title: Post-repair startup self-heal barrier
description:
## What
Add an explicit barrier after automatic startup repair: rerun decisive consistency probes, record the post-repair verdict, and only continue startup when the mailbox is actually healthy enough for the selected mode.

## Why
Startup self-healing is valuable only if it does not continue into a crash or degraded runtime after printing a reassuring message. The operator should see whether repair really cleared orphan rows, sidecar drift, or corruption before the server accepts work.

## How
Extend the startup repair control flow around database consistency findings. After repair, rerun the same integrity checks used to choose repair vs reconstruct, capture before/after counts, and emit a concise human line plus structured JSON/event evidence. If findings remain, fail closed or enter the existing degraded/reconstruct guidance path rather than launching the TUI.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests cover repaired-to-clean, repaired-but-still-dirty, repair-error, and dry-run paths.
- E2E scenario seeds orphan recipient rows, runs bare `am` or the native startup harness, and asserts the second-pass consistency verdict before startup continues.
- Output distinguishes silent successful self-heal from explicit escalation, with artifact paths for full details.
- The barrier is idempotent and does not mutate in dry-run/check-only modes.
- R0/R1 evidence uses real SQLite files and isolated STORAGE_ROOT.
notes: Implemented startup self-heal post-repair verification barrier with repair-error propagation, forensic bundle surfacing, dry-run non-mutation coverage, and an orphan-recipient startup e2e scenario. Verified with cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, startup_database_self_heal tests, and doctor_repair_dry_run_preserves_orphaned_message_recipients.

title: Sanitized incident support bundle
description:
## What
Create an operator command that packages a sanitized incident bundle for startup crashes, repair/reconstruct failures, and mailbox consistency incidents.

## Why
When a mailbox fails, maintainers need enough state to reproduce the control-flow decision without receiving private message bodies, secrets, bearer tokens, or whole archives. Current forensic bundles are useful locally but not tailored for safe sharing.

## How
Add an `am doctor support-bundle` or adjacent doctor subcommand that gathers versions, config shape, schema versions, integrity findings, redacted stderr/stdout, repair/reconstruct reports, selected sidecar metadata, and replay commands. Redact message bodies, auth tokens, paths as configured, and attachment contents by default. Include a manifest describing exactly what was included and omitted.

## Acceptance criteria
- Bundle manifest lists every file, redaction mode, command, version, and source path class.
- Redaction tests cover message bodies, subjects when requested, env secrets, bearer tokens, home paths, and attachment names.
- E2E recovery-chaos scenario emits a support bundle and validates that it is sufficient to identify repair vs reconstruct decisions.
- The command never deletes source evidence and refuses to follow symlinks outside the chosen output root.
- Docs explain safe-sharing limits and exact reproduction commands.
close_reason: Implemented am doctor support-bundle with sanitized manifests, redaction coverage, recovery-chaos assertions, and docs. Verified with support_bundle tests, fmt/check/clippy gates, bash -n, and git diff --check.

title: Build-slot admission for verification lanes
description:
## What
Use build slots and robot/operator signals to coordinate heavy verification lanes: cargo workspace gates, clippy, ignored load tests, e2e suites, and benchmarks.

## Why
Large shared checkouts can waste time and destabilize machines when many agents launch expensive cargo/e2e/bench jobs at once. The project already has build slots, but agents need an obvious wrapper or recommendation path for verification admission.

## How
Add an `am verify`/`am-run` enhancement or robot recommendation that acquires an appropriate build slot before heavy work, emits wait/deny guidance when another holder is active, and records artifact links after completion. Integrate rch command shapes from repo policy without hiding the actual command.

## Acceptance criteria
- Build-slot leases protect at least workspace cargo check/clippy/test and selected e2e/perf lanes.
- Robot status/health can explain who holds the lane, expiry, and safe next action.
- Tests cover successful acquire, contention, TTL expiry, renew, release, and command failure cleanup.
- Documentation gives exact examples for `rch exec -- cargo ...` lanes.
- No command is auto-run without showing the command and preserving stdout/stderr artifacts.
close_reason: Added am verify build-slot admission lanes backed by am-run/rch, artifact capture for stdout/stderr/command metadata, robot status verification-lane recommendation, docs, and focused tests. Verified with rch cargo tests, fmt/check/clippy gates.

title: MCP client config drift diff
description:
## What
Add a non-mutating client-configuration drift report for Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, GitHub Copilot CLI, and generic MCP clients.

## Why
Agent Mail works best when all agents point at the same transport, auth, timeout, and endpoint contract. Today setup can repair some cases, but operators need an exact diff before allowing changes across several client config files.

## How
Extend `am setup status`, `am doctor check`, or `am tooling diagnostics` with a machine-readable config inventory: detected clients, config paths, current server entry, expected entry, drift reason, risk, and exact remediation command or patch plan. Keep mutation behind existing explicit setup/fix flows.

## Acceptance criteria
- JSON and human output cover missing, stale stdio, stale HTTP path, wrong bearer header, wrong timeout, duplicate entries, and unsupported client cases.
- Tests use temp config homes for all supported client families and do not touch real user config.
- Drift report redacts tokens and home-specific sensitive paths where appropriate.
- Operator docs show dry-run first and explicit fix second.
- No broad broadcast or unrelated setup mutation is introduced.

Verified with rch cargo fmt --check, core setup drift tests, workspace check/clippy, and CLI JSON smoke.

title: Mailbox schema invariant fuzz harness
description:
## What
Add a schema-invariant fuzz and regression harness for mailbox relational integrity across messages, recipients, threads, acks, contacts, file reservations, products, and build slots.

## Why
Most repair incidents show up as relational drift: orphan recipient rows, stale references, duplicate deliveries, missing thread rows, or inconsistent ack/read state. A compact invariant harness gives future migrations and repair work a sharper safety net.

## How
Define canonical invariants in the DB crate and generate randomized operation sequences against isolated SQLite files. - Focused unit/property tests and an ignored heavier rch lane are documented.

title: Archive bloat pack planner
description:
## What
Add a doctor/operator planner that measures archive Git repository bloat, explains pack/loose-object state, and recommends safe pack-archive maintenance without deleting user data.

## Why
Agent Mail archives are intentionally Git-backed. Large swarms can create many artifacts and commits, so operators need to understand repository growth and maintenance impact before performance degrades.

## How
Extend existing archive diagnostics or pack-archive surfaces with repo size, loose object counts, packfile age, commit cadence, largest artifact categories, and expected maintenance commands. Keep remediation explicit and reversible where possible; no file deletion.

## Acceptance criteria
- Report includes per-project and global archive size, loose object count, packfile count, oldest/newest pack age, and top artifact categories.
- JSON output includes threshold verdicts and exact safe maintenance commands.
- Tests create synthetic archives with loose objects and packed objects and assert planner verdicts.
- Operator docs explain pack/repack risks, no-delete policy, and how to preserve evidence before maintenance.
- The planner does not run destructive cleanup automatically.
close_reason: Implemented archive pack maintenance planner with JSON thresholds, safe commands, focused tests, and operator docs.

title: Overseer intervention safety audit
description:
## What
Audit and harden the Web UI overseer compose/intervention path so human high-priority messages remain powerful, explicit, and fully auditable without creating a hidden broadcast or policy bypass footgun.

## Why
The overseer can bypass contact policies and interrupt agents. That is useful for human control, but it is also a privileged surface that needs crisp recipients, reason text, audit records, and redaction-safe logs.

## How
Review `/mail/{project}/overseer/compose` and related routes/actions. Add explicit recipient summaries, confirmation for multi-recipient sends, structured audit events, CSRF/auth regression coverage where applicable, and tests proving broadcast remains unsupported.

## Acceptance criteria
- Overseer sends always enumerate explicit recipients and never map to `broadcast=true`.
- Audit artifacts include human overseer marker, reason, recipient list, thread id, and timestamp without leaking tokens.
- Tests cover unauthorized access, missing recipient, multiple explicit recipients, contact-policy bypass semantics, and broadcast rejection.
- Web/HTML and JSON routes agree on success/error semantics.
- Documentation states when overseer intervention is appropriate and how agents should observe it.

doctor: try in-place REINDEX before repair/reconstruct when integrity damage is index-only ('wrong # of entries in index')
description:
FIELD EVIDENCE (csd machine, 2026-08-12): startup self-heal saw 'Health probes failed ... possible corruption', chose Reconstruct, and the archive rebuild correctly REFUSED promotion (would lose 41 projects/2102 agents/21128 messages vs archive candidate with 0 projects). The systemd unit then crash-looped every ~5.4 min for 9 days, writing a ~45MB reconstruct candidate + forensic bundle per attempt (~22GB debris). The actual damage was TWO corrupt indexes on file_reservations (idx_file_reservations_project_agent_released, idx_file_reservations_project_released_expires) — integrity_check reported only 'wrong # of entries in index ...' rows, foreign_key_check clean, no page/row damage. A plain REINDEX fixed it in seconds with zero row loss (verified on copy: all 17 tables byte-identical, schema unchanged, WAL preserved).

ASK: when the canonical double-probe confirms corruption AND every corruption row matches the index-entry-count class (wrong # of entries in index <name>, and/or 'row X missing from index <name>') with clean foreign_key_check and no other damage rows, attempt an in-place targeted REINDEX (per damaged index; fall back to global REINDEX) BEFORE escalating to Repair/Reconstruct. Backup the DB file first (existing backup machinery), then re-run the full canonical battery; only if still corrupt escalate to the existing Repair/Reconstruct strategy. Wire into both startup self-heal strategy selection and am doctor repair. Detection must be conservative: any non-index-class corruption row disqualifies the fast path.

ACCEPTANCE: (a) unit tests for the classifier (index-only rows -> reindex candidate; mixed rows -> not); (b) integration test that corrupts only an index b-tree on a real DB, runs the self-heal path, asserts REINDEX healed it with zero row loss and no reconstruct candidate/forensic bundle was produced; (c) failed-REINDEX path still escalates to today's behavior.

comments.text:
# T6.1: Implement Deterministic Output Capture with Regex Normalization

## What to build
Run CLI commands, capture their output, and normalize non-deterministic content
(timestamps, PIDs, temp paths) so golden files are stable across runs. Replaces
the sed pipelines in bench_golden.sh.

## Current bash behavior
```bash
output=$(am --help 2>&1)
# Normalize timestamps like "2026-02-11T14:23:45Z"
output=$(echo "$output" | sed -E 's/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]+Z/TIMESTAMP/g')
# Normalize PIDs
output=$(echo "$output" | sed -E 's/pid [0-9]+/pid PID/g')
# Normalize temp paths
output=$(echo "$output" | sed -E 's|/tmp/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+|/tmp/TMPDIR|g')
```

## Rust implementation
```rust
struct NormalizationRule {
    pattern: Regex,
    replacement: &'static str,
}

const DEFAULT_RULES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    // ISO-8601 timestamps
    (r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T[\d:]+(\.\d+)?Z?", "TIMESTAMP"),
    // Unix timestamps (microseconds)
    (r"\b1[67]\d{14}\b", "UNIX_MICROS"),
    // PIDs
    (r"pid \d+", "pid PID"),
    // Temp paths
    (r"/tmp/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+", "/tmp/TMPDIR"),
    // Cargo target dir
    (r"/data/tmp/cargo-target/[^\s]+", "CARGO_TARGET"),
    // Home directory
    (r"/home/\w+", "/home/USER"),
];

fn normalize_output(raw: &str, rules: &[NormalizationRule]) -> String

fn capture_command(cmd: &[String]) -> Result<CapturedOutput, Error> {
    let output = Command::new(&cmd[0]).args(&cmd[1..]).output()?;
    Ok(CapturedOutput {
        stdout: String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string(),
        stderr: String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string(),
        exit_code: output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),
    })
}
```

## Implementation notes
- Compile regexes once (lazy_static or OnceLock)
- Apply rules in order (some rules may interact)
- The normalization must be deterministic: same input → same output regardless of platform
- Consider normalizing ANSI color codes too (strip or preserve based on flag)

## Location
crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/golden.rs (new module)

title: db/engine: WAL re-open of a namespace-retained mailbox re-checkpoints via process-global RW fd — header change-counter bumps defeat byte-exact read-neutrality (needs frankensqlite no-checkpoint read open or ns quiescence)

comments.author: GentleSparrow
comments.text: Evidence (br-lg5dd investigation, GentleSparrow 2026-07-26): strace of hot_health_check_does_not_advance_writer_epoch_or_touch_sqlite_family shows the bootstrap pool's O_RDWR fd for hot-health.sqlite3 (fd 8, opened during get_db_pool bootstrap) remains open after the pool drops — held by frankensqlite's process-global namespace (the -fsqlite-ns-gate/-ns-use machinery). When health_check later opens the same path via the strict query-only pool (DbConn::open_file_read_only, SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY), WAL-checkpoint housekeeping runs THROUGH that retained RW fd: bursts of header pwrite + same-bytes page copy at offset 303104 + ftruncate-to-same-size, bumping the header file-change-counter (offset 24-27) and version-valid-for (92-95) from 113 to 121 (+8 over two bursts). Data pages, -wal, -shm all byte-identical; only the two counter fields move. So SQL-level query_only and even engine READ_ONLY open flags do not give byte-exact family neutrality while the namespace retains a writer fd. sqlmodel-frankensqlite 0.3.0 exposes open_schema_only ('avoid introducing writer semantics such as close-time checkpoints') but that cannot serve general health/reservation queries. Fix needs upstream frankensqlite: a no-checkpoint general read open, or namespace writer-fd quiescence/release on last pool close. Until then the identity hot-health test masks exactly bytes [24,28) and [92,96) of the main db (see br-lg5dd).

comments.author: GentleSparrow
comments.text: Scope disposition (GentleSparrow, full-fix sweep): this is engine-level work in the sibling frankensqlite/sqlmodel-frankensqlite crates, NOT fixable in mcp_agent_mail_rust. In-repo mitigations are already complete: br-lg5dd masks exactly the two header change-counter fields in the hot-health family assertion (everything else byte-strict), and br-29u5s documents the second manifestation (stale ns sidecars across quarantine/promotion make post-promotion opens fail — same ns-lifecycle root). What upstream needs to provide, in preference order: (1) a general-purpose no-checkpoint read open (open_schema_only's contract extended to full-query reads), (2) namespace writer-fd quiescence/release when the last in-process pool for a path closes, (3) an explicit ns retire/transition API for quarantine+replace flows. Whoever owns the frankensqlite checkout should pick this up alongside br-29u5s; both close together when the engine API lands. Leaving open (visibility), unassigned, priority P3 stands.

title: am doctor repair/reconstruct under a live owner emits a process-group signal (SIGSTKFLT/16) that kills sibling processes in a shared group
description: DISCOVERED while writing N6 (br-bvq1x.14.6) e2e. When `am doctor repair` (and `am doctor reconstruct`) run under a LIVE owner (a running `am serve-http` holding the same mailbox) inside a NON-INTERACTIVE shell (job control off, e.g. `bash test.sh` / CI), the command emits signal 16 (SIGSTKFLT on Linux/x86-64) that propagates to the whole process group — killing the calling shell (exit 144 = 128+16) and any siblings, NOT just am. setsid on either the server or the repair, and `trap '' 16` in the shell, did NOT prevent it (suggesting a kill(0,sig)/process-group broadcast or an asupersync-runtime signal sent too broadly). The supervised-owner REFUSAL itself is correct (exit 3, classification 'supervised-owner-required') and observed cleanly in an INTERACTIVE shell where job control isolates the server's job group. Impact: an operator/CI wrapper that runs `am doctor repair` while a server shares its process group could have the wrapper script killed. Likely low-severity (real operators use interactive shells or systemd-isolated servers) but worth root-causing. Repro: background `am serve-http --no-tui --no-auth --port N`, wait for /healthz, then `am doctor repair` in the same non-interactive bash => exit 144, shell dead. Investigate the coordination/supervised-drain path + asupersync signal usage for a process-group-scoped send. N6 e2e scopes AROUND this (covers D2 locks owner_state + D4 drain verdict; skips the repair/reconstruct-refusal black-box assertion with a note).
close_reason: Resolved: refusal under a live owner is now signal-safe; added an e2e regression guard. Re-verified on the released v0.3.17 binary with strace (fully isolated mailbox, both verbs): am doctor repair AND reconstruct under a live mailbox owner in a non-interactive setsid shell REFUSE cleanly (exit 3, classification supervised-owner-required) with ZERO SIGSTKFLT emitted and the calling shell survives. The bug does not reproduce — SIGSTKFLT(16) appears NOWHERE in our source (the only signal send is nix::kill to a SPECIFIC pid, never the process group/kill(0)); likely resolved by the supervised-owner + restart-coordination hardening since the 2026-06-16 report (0c1e9457 single-owner restart lock, 2f3d62ae unified process-owner model). Converted the test_locks_live_owner.sh (N6) e2e_skip into a real regression guard (am commit 02cc915f, pushed main+master): new amrun_isolated runs each verb in its OWN session (setsid) + signal-traces it (strace), so any future regression is contained to a child session — never kills the harness — and surfaces as a clean failure (exit != 3 and/or SIGSTKFLT in trace). Suite passes 14/0/0 (was 8 pass + 1 skip); shellcheck clean. FOLLOW-UP (optional): the sibling skips citing br-mms51 in test_doctor_integrity_purity_undo.sh / test_degraded_intents_replay.sh / test_cli_mcp_surface.sh can now be revisited (they skip partly to avoid mutation too, so each needs its own live-owner setup). REOPEN if a fresh prod exit-144 artifact appears.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Investigation (CalmAspen 2026-06-22, source-only): (1) Our signal code is correctly scoped — send_unix_signal (cli/lib.rs:5282) uses nix kill(specific_pid, SIGTERM/SIGKILL); the only killpg (terminate_child_process_group, cli/lib.rs:61697) targets am-run/verify CHILD commands placed in their OWN process group via setpgid (:61706), so it cannot reach the caller's shell. The repair/reconstruct supervised-owner guard REFUSES (exit 3), no signal. (2) SIGSTKFLT (sig 16) is referenced NOWHERE in our crates or /dp/asupersync; it is a legacy signal the kernel does not normally generate, so it must be explicitly sent — sender not locatable from source. (3) Not source-fixable without repro. NEXT: build am; bg 'am serve-http --no-tui --no-auth --port N'; wait /healthz; in NON-INTERACTIVE bash run 'strace -f -e trace=%signal -o /tmp/sig.trace am doctor repair'; grep trace for kill/tgkill sig 16 to find the sender thread. title: Add NUMA-conscious large-memory cache sizing and hotset controls
description:
Goal: let operators on 256GB+ machines intentionally allocate larger bounded caches for hot mailbox/search/product-bus data without risking runaway memory or poor locality.

Rationale: the project should take advantage of large RAM machines, but only through explicit budgets, observability, and eviction behavior. This complements adaptive cache admission and read snapshots.

Scope: config and metrics first: per-cache memory caps, current footprint estimates, hotset hit/miss accounting, and optional high-memory profile presets. Avoid unsafe memory tricks.

Fallback/safe mode: default budgets stay conservative; invalid or excessive config clamps to safe bounds with diagnostics.

Acceptance: config docs, tests for budget parsing/clamping, cache metric snapshots, memory pressure behavior, and a benchmark showing high-memory profiles improve repeated hot-view workloads without changing outputs.

Performance acceptance should report p50/p95/p99 plus CPU/RSS/DB-query or queue-depth evidence where applicable. Test/repro workloads must use isolated STORAGE_ROOT and must not touch the operator mailbox. Stub-only tests can support design confidence but do not close user-facing or persistence/performance claims.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DESIGN (pane %4): generation-stable keying via (db_generation_id, rowid) composite.

Root cause confirmed: reservation `id` is a GLOBAL autoincrement; archive artifacts stored per-project-slug. Across DB generations (fresh DB restarts AUTOINCREMENT at 1) the same global id is reused for reservations in *different* projects, leaving stale `id-<id>.json` under old project dirs. Parity (tools/reservation_parity.rs) keys by (project_slug, id) and its archive_id_collisions counter fires for every (None-db, Some-archive) whose id exists in DB under a *different* project -> the 607 collisions. Reconstruct (db/reconstruct.rs) globs ALL *.json, reads id from CONTENT, INSERT OR REPLACE by id -> cross-generation loss.

FIX:
1. db_identity(generation_id) table seeded once per physical DB via lower(hex(randomblob(16))) (fresh DB => new generation). Accessor queries::db_generation_id.
2. Stamp db_generation into reservation archive JSON at all build sites (tools/reservations.rs). Storage names the stable artifact id-<id>-g<gen>.json (flat, guard-safe read_dir) when db_generation present; legacy id-<id>.json still recognized. Central format/parse helper in core::reservation_artifact.
3. Parity becomes generation-aware: artifacts whose generation != current DB generation are counted as foreign_generation_artifacts (informational, EXCLUDED from total()); legacy (un-generationed) keep existing (project,id) collision logic. => two generations produce zero id-collisions + clean parity.
4. Reconstruct dedups by (project, generation, archived_id); no longer collapses cross-generation ids => non-lossy.
5. New archive-normalize reservation fixer: migrate legacy id-<id>.json -> id-<id>-g<gen>.json when current DB has the matching row; quarantine foreign-generation debris via Op::Rename (no deletion).

Keeping legacy sha1(pattern).json write (parity ignores it; not a source of id-collisions) to stay surgical. Implementing in staged per-crate commits with inline tests.

title: Track E: Coalesce Sharding
description:
**Background**

The `CoalesceMap` in `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/coalesce.rs` uses a single `Mutex<HashMap<K, Arc<Slot<V>>>>` (line 186) for all in-flight requests. Under high concurrency (10+ agents calling tools simultaneously), this becomes a contention point because every `execute_or_join` call must acquire the mutex to check or insert.

**Graveyard reference:** DashMap-style sharding. Split the single HashMap into N shards (N=16), each with its own Mutex. Route keys to shards via FNV hash. Contention drops by a factor of N because threads accessing different shards never contend.

**EV calculation:** (severity=5 * breadth=5 * feasibility=3) / (risk=3 * effort=2) = 12.5
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- 16-shard coalescer implemented with stable key-to-shard distribution
- Unit tests cover shard routing, leader/joiner correctness, timeout/error propagation, and cleanup invariants
- Integration tests prove behavioral isomorphism with single-mutex baseline across randomized schedules
- Stress/E2E concurrency tests show reduced contention and no stale inflight entries
- Bench artifacts include lock wait, throughput, latency tail, and fairness metrics
- Isomorphism proof includes deterministic replay harness and mismatch diagnostics
- tracing diagnostics capture shard id, wait duration, outcome class, and contention snapshots

title: P0: Block binary publication when release lint or tests fail
description: The tag triggered dist workflow marks lint as continue on error and builds even when the test job fails. A tag can therefore create downloadable binaries after known red gates. This contradicts the required release gate and makes publication status non causal.
acceptance_criteria: The release job requires successful workspace formatting clippy tests and required release gates before publication. A deliberately failing lint and a deliberately failing test each prevent artifact publication. Any rerun occurs only after green evidence is recorded.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Static source repair is committed at 69717edc. The dist build requires lint and test, and release directly requires lint, test, and build with no always condition or continue on error override. Canonical mandatory commands are cargo fmt all check, cargo check workspace all targets, cargo clippy workspace all targets deny warnings, and cargo test workspace. YAML parsing and five in memory negative controls passed. Static only: no deliberate failing tag run and no publication attempt occurred, so acceptance remains in progress.

title: P1: Never trust a fresh proactive backup by mtime alone
description: create_proactive_backup skips a fresh standalone regular .bak solely by mtime, assuming published bytes remain immutable, but the file is owner-writable and can be corrupted or replaced. A fresh non-SQLite file is currently blessed by a regression test, causing the integrity guard to forfeit a healthy backup refresh for up to the max-age window.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh-skip requires a retained-handle identity/health authority bound to the published generation; byte or inode replacement forces a staged online refresh while an unchanged verified generation still takes the cheap path. A mutation-sensitive test corrupts a fresh backup with unchanged mtime/length and proves immediate refresh from the healthy live DB. Raced replacements fail closed without clobber. Workspace check, clippy -D warnings, fmt, and focused tests pass.

title: J.2: Regression safety gate for alien enhancements
description:
**Background**

The alien enhancement tracks modify critical code paths (cache, coalesce, queries, TUI rendering). The existing 1000+ tests must continue to pass after each track is merged. This bead establishes the regression safety protocol.

**Scope**

1. Before each track merge, run the full test suite: cargo test --workspace
2. Before each track merge, run cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings (0 warnings)
3. Before each track merge, run cargo fmt --check
4. Run the 15 existing E2E test scripts in tests/e2e/
5. Run the stress tests in crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/tests/stress.rs
6. Document any test changes required by each track (tests that need updating because the optimization changes behavior — e.g., eviction order changing from LRU to S3-FIFO)

**Per-track regression checklist (copy for each track merge):**
- [ ] cargo fmt --check passes
- [ ] cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passes (0 warnings)
- [ ] cargo test --workspace passes (all existing tests)
- [ ] E2E tests pass (tests/e2e/*.sh)
- [ ] Stress tests pass
- [ ] Any behavior-changing tests updated with comments explaining the change
- [ ] git diff shows no unintended changes to other modules

**Tests (3 required)**

1. regression_all_workspace_tests — run cargo test --workspace, capture pass/fail count
2. regression_clippy_clean — verify 0 clippy warnings
3. regression_e2e_scripts — run all E2E bash scripts, verify exit codes

**Success criteria:**
- Zero test regressions across all track merges
- Any intentional test changes are documented in the bead's notes field
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Regression gate enforces fmt, clippy -D warnings, workspace tests, target stress suites, and alien E2E matrix
- Gate publishes per-track pass/fail breakdown and links to generated artifacts/log bundles
- Unit checks verify gate script behavior for missing artifacts, partial failures, and timeout handling
- Integration checks ensure gate can run against both feature-on and feature-off fallback paths
- E2E validation confirms gate correctly blocks regressions and surfaces actionable diagnostics
- Logs include command lines, durations, exit codes, and normalized error classification

description:
# Epic: Documentation Alignment Sweep

## Background

A 2026-04-17 reality check (skill: /reality-check-for-project) found multiple drift points between the README.md / AGENTS.md marketing surface and the actual code. None of these are product defects — the code is production-grade — but they materially undersell or overclaim several dimensions in a way that would mislead a reader doing their own reality check.

## Summary of drift points found (evidence: reality-check session 2026-04-17)

| Claim | Reality | Evidence file:line |
|---|---|---|
| "36 MCP tools" (README L15, L89) | **37** tools | crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/lib.rs:1670-1720 |
| "34 MCP tools" (AGENTS.md L264) | **37** tools | same |
| "33 MCP resources" (README L89) | **25** resources | crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/resources.rs |
| "15-screen TUI" (README L91, AGENTS.md L346) | **16** screens (added Atc) | crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/tui_screens/mod.rs:85-122 |
| "Search V3 Tantivy Lexical Baselines" (BUDGETS.md) | Lexical path of **frankensearch**; "Tantivy" is a stale name | benches/BUDGETS.md L154-182 |
| "no ad-hoc SQL fallback path" (README L441) | An intentional SQL plan exists for empty/non-searchable queries | crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/search_service.rs:3467-3472 |
| "Search V3 via frankensearch with lexical/semantic/hybrid routing" (README L95) | Lexical path unconditional; semantic/hybrid behind `#[cfg(feature = "hybrid")]` | crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/search_service.rs:29-65 |
| "conformance against Python reference, 23 tools all passing" | **34** fixture tool definitions (3 Rust-native tools have no parity); previously referenced "23" is legacy from pre-parity state | crates/mcp-agent-mail-conformance/tests/conformance/fixtures/python_reference.json |
| "ATC learning writes experience rows and resolves outcomes" (top of ATC section) | Rich library, but no hot-path INSERT into atc_experiences yet; README's own Implementation Map acknowledges wiring is future work | crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/lib.rs (no atc_note_* calls from tool dispatch) |
| Identity cluster documents 3 tools in README (register_agent, create_agent_identity, whois) | 6 tools actually registered (+ resolve_pane_identity, cleanup_pane_identities, list_agents) | TOOL_CLUSTER_MAP in crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/lib.rs |

## Why this matters

The reality-check skill's Rule 3 ("Check bead coverage against every vision goal"): the marketing-level claims at the top of README are the first thing anyone measures us against. Over-claim on WASM/ATC is addressed under separate epics (WASM decision, ATC loop closure). This epic covers the strictly-documentation fixes — no code changes required.

## Scope

Strictly edits to README.md, AGENTS.md, benches/BUDGETS.md, and (if touched) docs/RUNBOOK-search-v3-migration.md. No code behavior changes. No new features. No test updates required (these are prose corrections).

## Non-goals (explicit)

- Any WASM frontend work — see sibling epic (WASM decision).
- Any ATC learning loop code wiring — see sibling epic (ATC closure).
- Any archive batch-write perf work — see sibling epic (perf).
- Any conformance fixture generation — see sibling epic (conformance backfill).
- Do NOT adjust tool/resource/screen counts by *removing* tools to make docs match — the discrepancy is "we have more than we advertise", not "we advertise more than we have".

## Sequencing

Documentation tasks can be landed concurrently; a single doc-consolidation commit per task (or one rollup commit) is fine. The ATC-disclaimer task (child task 6) has a soft dependency on the ATC epic existing so the cross-reference link lands in both directions. The search-naming task (child 4) should land alongside the WASM disclosure task so readers see a consistent "what's feature-flagged, what's aspirational" story.

## Acceptance criteria (for closing this epic)

All child tasks closed AND:
- `rg -nF 'We have 36 MCP tools' README.md` returns 0 hits (and equivalent for stale "34 tools" / "33 resources" / "15-screen" / "23 tools all passing" / "Tantivy Lexical" phrasings).
- `rg -nF '37 MCP tools' README.md` AND `rg -nF '25 MCP resources' README.md` AND `rg -nF '16-screen' README.md` all return matches.
- Visual diff review of README + AGENTS.md + BUDGETS.md confirms consistent counts.

title: Docs: threat model document consolidating security posture (web-dashboard, JWT, bearer, archive, ATC)
description:
# Threat model documentation

## Why this bead exists

Security concerns are scattered across docs today:
- JWT + JWKS auth referenced in multiple places
- /web-dashboard security review in br-il53l.8 (WASM-scoped)
- ATC privacy audit in br-bn0vb.22 (ATC-scoped)
- Share/export crypto in mcp-agent-mail-share
- Bearer-token handling in HTTP transport
- Pre-commit guard as defense-in-depth

No single document describes the **threat model** — assets, adversaries, attack surfaces, mitigations. Security reviews become piecemeal; regressions go unnoticed.

## Scope

Write `docs/SPEC-threat-model.md` covering:

### 1. Assets (what we protect)

- Agent identities (pseudonymous but link to humans via commits)
- Message content (may contain code, secrets, PII)
- Reservation state (who's editing what)
- ATC learning data (aggregates of agent behavior over time)
- Bearer tokens + JWT signing keys
- Archive Git history (immutable record)

### 2. Adversaries

- **Curious user on same machine** — wants to read other users' mailboxes
- **Malicious agent** — wants to read/modify other agents' data, spam others
- **Network eavesdropper** — monitors HTTP transport
- **Compromised process** — reads/writes archive, poisons ATC ledger
- **Exfiltration via error channels** — verbose logs leaking secrets
- **Supply chain** — malicious dependency
- **Physical access** — unencrypted disk

### 3. Attack surfaces

- MCP transport (stdio + HTTP)
- `/mail/*` web UI routes (auth via bearer)
- `/web-dashboard/*` routes (if SHIP)
- CLI commands reading config/archive
- Git archive file permissions
- SQLite file permissions + WAL + backup/restore
- Installer script (curl|bash supply chain)
- Release artifact (cosign signature)

### 4. Mitigations (existing + gaps)

| Surface | Mitigation | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP transport | Bearer token | ✓ required; localhost-unauth opt-in |
| JWT auth | JWKS + kid verification | ✓ |
| Archive integrity | Git commit signing | ✗ not implemented |
| SQLite at-rest encryption | OS-level (user responsibility) | ✓ documented |
| Broadcast messaging | Hard-coded reject | ✓ critical invariant |
| Pre-commit guard | Reservation enforcement | ✓ |
| ATC data minimization | Secret-detection + redaction | Bead br-bn0vb.22 |
| /web-dashboard security | Bearer + CSRF + XSS | Bead br-il53l.8 (SHIP branch) |
| Installer integrity | cosign signature | ✓ verify flag |
| Supply chain | Cargo.lock review + cargo-audit | Partial — recommend audit cadence |

### 5. Out of scope (documented)

- Multi-tenant isolation (single-user tool)
- Network-level encryption (assume HTTPS terminator in front or localhost-only)
- Persistent PII protection (single-user; no GDPR obligations)

### 6. Review cadence

- Threat model reviewed annually OR when a new attack surface lands
- Every new public-facing endpoint requires threat-model update
- Security incidents update the "lessons" section

### 7. Related specs

Cross-reference:
- br-il53l.8: /web-dashboard security review
- br-bn0vb.22: ATC privacy
- docs/SPEC-doctor-forensic-bundle-schema.md
- docs/SPEC-ephemeral-root-policy.md (already exists)

## Test plan

- Document exists, is linked from README and AGENTS.md
- Each section covered (no TODO markers in shipped version)
- Cross-references resolve to real specs/beads
- A review checklist included so future incremental changes can audit against it

## Definition of done

- `docs/SPEC-threat-model.md` committed
- Linked from README Documentation table
- Review checklist at end usable in PR reviews
- `am check doc-drift` (UX.1 gate) includes: `rg -nF 'TODO' docs/SPEC-threat-model.md` returns 0
close_reason: Completed: aligned threat model spec and linked it from README

title: Supply chain audit cadence: cargo-audit + cargo-deny weekly CI + monthly Cargo.lock review
description:
# Supply chain audit cadence

## Why this bead exists

The threat model bead (br-o217s.10) lists supply chain as an adversary with the mitigation "Partial — recommend audit cadence". No mitigation actually exists today beyond ad-hoc review. Rust's ecosystem has rich tooling (cargo-audit against rustsec/advisory-db, cargo-deny for license + duplicate + unmaintained + banned) that, if not CI-enforced, drift over time.

## Scope

### Weekly CI job

`.github/workflows/supply-chain-audit.yml`:
- Runs `cargo audit` → fails on any CVE with severity >= Medium
- Runs `cargo deny check` with policy file (licenses + bans + advisories + sources)
- Opens a bead (auto-created via br CLI from within CI) on findings
- Artifacts: full audit JSON committed to `tests/artifacts/audit/<date>.json`

### cargo-deny policy

`deny.toml`:
```toml
[advisories]
vulnerability = "deny"
unmaintained = "warn"
yanked = "deny"

[bans]
# No duplicate versions of critical deps
multiple-versions = "warn"
deny = [
  # List of banned crates (e.g., old tokio if we ever accidentally pull it)
]

[licenses]
allow = ["MIT", "Apache-2.0", "BSD-2-Clause", "BSD-3-Clause", "ISC", "Unicode-DFS-2016", "Zlib"]
copyleft = "deny"  # No GPL/AGPL contamination

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "warn"
```

### Monthly manual review

An OPERATOR_RUNBOOK.md section "Monthly supply chain review" with:
- `cargo tree` walk to look for newly-introduced or bloated deps
- `cargo outdated` to see what's lagging
- Manual cargo-crev trust review for any new high-weight deps

### Tokio-ecosystem guard

Extra check beyond cargo-audit: `am check supply-chain` runs:
- `cargo tree | grep -E "^[├└│]" | grep -iE "\\b(tokio|reqwest|hyper|axum|tower|async-std|smol)\\b"`
- Asserts output is EMPTY (per AGENTS.md: "Forbidden crates: tokio, hyper, reqwest, axum, tower, async-std, smol")
- Catches accidental transitive introduction of tokio ecosystem

## Test plan

- CI job green on clean repo
- Deliberate-injection test: add a deliberately-vulnerable dep to a feature branch; verify CI catches it + opens bead
- Monthly review: first review committed as template; dated
- Tokio-guard catches deliberate introduction of `tokio = "1"` in a test Cargo.toml

## Structured logging

```
supply_chain.audit.start { workspace_hash }
supply_chain.audit.cargo_audit { advisories_found, highest_severity, crates_affected }
supply_chain.audit.cargo_deny { violations, license_issues, banned_hits }
supply_chain.audit.tokio_guard { tokio_refs_found }
supply_chain.audit.summary { verdict, bead_opened_id? }
```

## Non-goals

- Not integrating commercial SCA tools (overkill for a single-user project)
- Not full SBOM generation (cargo-audit output is enough)
- Not pinning every indirect dep (Cargo.lock handles this already)

## Dependencies

- Builds on br-o217s.10 (threat model) — this operationalizes one of its mitigations
- Feeds br-bb0gt.1 (`am check`) — `am check supply-chain` gate

## Definition of done

- Weekly CI job green
- Monthly review template committed + first review dated
- Tokio-guard wired in `am check`
- Injection test verifies the gate actually fires
- Runbook section complete
close_reason: Completed: added weekly cargo-audit/cargo-deny workflow and deny.toml tokio-ecosystem guard

title: Docs: operator playbook / cookbook — 10+ canonical copy-paste recipes for common workflows
description:
# Operator playbook / cookbook

## Why this bead exists

The README teaches concepts. AGENTS.md teaches agents. OPERATOR_RUNBOOK.md handles diagnostics. What's missing: **a cookbook of canonical workflows** — copy-paste recipes for the 10 most common operator tasks.

Examples of tasks without current recipe coverage:
- "I want to start 3 agents on the same project for a refactor — what's the fastest start?"
- "An agent crashed mid-session, how do I clean up their reservations?"
- "I want to run the server on port 9000 with bearer auth disabled for local testing"
- "I want to see what Alpha did over the last 24 hours"
- "I want to see which files are currently contested between agents"
- "I want to enable ATC shadow mode for 1 week"
- "I want to test the archive perf fix locally before upgrading"
- "I want to migrate from Python mcp_agent_mail to Rust"
- "I want to export my mailbox and send to a collaborator"
- "An agent went rogue and is spamming — how do I suspend them?"

Each of these has existing commands, but operators have to assemble them. A cookbook compresses that to copy-paste.

## Scope

### Deliverable: `docs/OPERATOR_COOKBOOK.md`

Structured as a numbered list of recipes, each with:
- **Goal** (1-sentence intent)
- **Commands** (exact copy-paste, working)
- **Expected output** (what success looks like)
- **Troubleshooting** (top 1-2 failure modes + fixes)

### Minimum recipe set (v1)

Start with these 10 recipes; add more as patterns emerge:

1. **Fast 3-agent session start**
```bash
cd /path/to/repo
am                                      # auto-detect, configure, start
am robot status --format json | jq '.health'
```

2. **Clean up crashed-agent reservations**
```bash
am robot reservations --all | jq '.reservations[] | select(.agent_status == "stale")'
am file_reservations release --force --agent=<Name> --reason="Crashed"
```

3. **Local testing with custom port + no auth**
```bash
am serve-http --port 9000 --no-auth
curl http://127.0.0.1:9000/health
```

4. **Audit an agent's last 24h**
```bash
am robot timeline --agent=<Name> --since=24h --format md
am robot analytics --agent=<Name>
am atc explain --agent=<Name> --since=24h  # if ATC live (br-bn0vb.30)
```

5. **Current file contention**
```bash
am robot reservations --conflicts
am doctor check --verbose
```

6. **Enable ATC shadow mode for 1 week**
```bash
ATC_WRITE_MODE=shadow am serve-http
# ... wait 1 week ...
am atc what-is-stored | jq '.totals'
am atc explain --random --limit=5  # sanity check
```

7. **Test archive perf fix locally**
```bash
ARCHIVE_WRITE_MODE=fast am bench --quick
ARCHIVE_WRITE_MODE=legacy am bench --quick
# compare results
```

8. **Migrate from Python mcp_agent_mail**
```bash
am legacy detect
am legacy import --dry-run
am legacy import
am doctor check
```

9. **Export mailbox for collaborator**
```bash
am share wizard  # interactive
# or
am share export -o ~/mailbox-share.zip --encrypt
```

10. **Suspend a rogue agent**
```bash
am robot agents --health <Name>       # confirm identity
am atc kill-switch on --agent=<Name> --reason="Rogue: spamming"   # if feature wired
# or
am file_reservations release --force --agent=<Name>
am contacts policy --agent=<Name> --policy=none  # block incoming contacts
```

### Structure

Each recipe is a stand-alone section; operator doesn't need context from other recipes. Cross-links only where one recipe naturally leads into another.

### Verification process

- Every command in a recipe is actually runnable on current `am`
- Expected output matches actual observed output (spot-checked per release)
- Troubleshooting sections are written from observed failures, not imagined

## Test plan

### Automated

`tests/docs/cookbook_commands_test.sh`:
- Parses the cookbook for code blocks
- Each command: dry-run or safe-run against a test mailbox
- Asserts: no command fails the CLI parser; every `am` subcommand exists
- Does NOT run destructive commands (skip `release --force`, `share export`, migration)

### Manual

- Periodic walkthrough: operator (or reviewer) walks a fresh user through 3 random recipes; notes any confusion; feeds back to cookbook

### Structured logging

Recipes are docs, not code. No logging requirements. But the automated test emits:
```
cookbook.verify.recipe_start { recipe_number, title }
cookbook.verify.command_checked { command, parseable, subcommand_exists }
cookbook.verify.recipe_complete { recipe_number, commands_verified }
```

## Non-goals

- Not a full user manual (focused on top-10 workflows)
- Not replacing README or OPERATOR_RUNBOOK (additive)
- Not translated to other languages

## Dependencies

- Depends on br-o217s.1-3 (counts correct in cross-referenced docs)
- Depends on ALL epics for recipe completeness — but can land with v1 recipes that reference only shipped features
- Recipes referencing unshipped features (e.g., `am atc kill-switch` from br-bn0vb.19) get `[experimental]` tag + cross-ref

## Definition of done

- `docs/OPERATOR_COOKBOOK.md` committed with 10+ recipes
- All commands in recipes parse successfully
- Linked from README + AGENTS.md + OPERATOR_RUNBOOK.md
- Cookbook-command verification test in CI
- At least one fresh-user walkthrough logged

title: BUDGETS.md + README: rename 'Tantivy Lexical' to 'frankensearch lexical', disclose feature flag
description:
# Task: Fix Search V3 naming drift and document feature flag

## Scope

Three related inaccuracies in the search documentation:

1. **`benches/BUDGETS.md`** labels the 2026-02-18 baselines "Search V3 Tantivy Lexical Baselines". The actual engine is **frankensearch** (see workspace deps in `Cargo.toml` + ADR-003). Tantivy is a transitive dep inside frankensearch's lexical tier, not the engine name we advertise.

2. **README L441** states: "Search V3 via frankensearch with lexical/semantic/hybrid routing (**no ad-hoc SQL fallback path**)". In reality, `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/search_service.rs:3467-3472` routes empty/non-searchable queries through a SQL plan — an intentional fallback, not ad-hoc, but the phrase "no ad-hoc SQL fallback" is still misleading.

3. **README L95** describes "lexical/semantic/hybrid routing" as if all three modes ship by default. The semantic and hybrid code paths at `crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/search_service.rs:29-65` are gated behind `#[cfg(feature = "hybrid")]`. Default builds are lexical-only.

## Edits required

**benches/BUDGETS.md** (L154-182):
- Rename section: "Search V3 Tantivy Lexical Baselines" → "Search V3 frankensearch lexical-tier baselines"
- Add a one-line note: "Tantivy is the lexical backend inside frankensearch; see ADR-003 for the full stack."

**README.md** L441 (Key Design Decisions):
- Current: "Search V3 via frankensearch with lexical/semantic/hybrid routing (no ad-hoc SQL fallback path)"
- Propose: "Search V3 via frankensearch — lexical tier ships by default; semantic + hybrid fusion behind the `hybrid` Cargo feature. Empty and non-searchable queries route through a deterministic SQL plan (not ad-hoc fallback)."

**README.md** L95 (Feature table row):
- Current: "Hybrid Search — Search V3 via frankensearch with lexical, semantic, and hybrid routing"
- Propose: "Hybrid Search — Search V3 via frankensearch. Lexical tier default; semantic + hybrid fusion behind `hybrid` feature flag."

**README.md** L1112-1121 (Search Architecture section):
- Update "Legacy SQLite FTS artifacts still exist for migration hygiene and cleanup, but the current search architecture is the Search V3 path, not ad-hoc direct SQL fallback." — this is correct for FTS but doesn't address the intentional SQL plan for non-searchable queries. Add one sentence acknowledging the SQL plan routing for degenerate queries, citing the search_service.rs location.

**docs/ADR-003-search-v3-architecture.md** (if needed):
- Verify this ADR already describes feature-flag gating; if not, add a section "Feature flags and deployment modes" explaining which builds have which tiers.

**docs/RUNBOOK-search-v3-migration.md** (if needed):
- Verify this runbook is current w.r.t. feature-flag reality; fix any passages that imply hybrid is always on.

## Verification

```bash
rg -nF 'Tantivy Lexical' benches/BUDGETS.md README.md docs/   # 0
rg -nF 'frankensearch lexical' benches/BUDGETS.md             # >= 1
rg -nF 'hybrid feature' README.md                              # >= 1
rg -nF 'feature = \"hybrid\"' README.md docs/                  # >= 1
```

## Considerations

- Do NOT change code behavior. This is purely prose correction.
- Don't overstate the SQL plan — it handles edge cases, not mainline queries; the frankensearch path dominates.
- Keep the ADR-003 reference pointer intact.
- The term "Tantivy" appears correctly in ADR-003 for historical implementation context; don't purge that term from ADR-003, only from the current user-facing BUDGETS/README.

## Definition of done

- All rg checks above pass
- Anyone reading README can tell which search tiers ship in their build and how to enable more
- Benchmarks are labeled with the engine they actually exercise
close_reason: Renamed Tantivy Lexical to frankensearch lexical in BUDGETS.md and README.md

# Task: Add interim disclaimer to ATC section clarifying architecture-phase status

## Scope

The README's ATC presentation sells ATC Learning as an active feature (feature bullet "ATC Learning Implementation Map", TUI screen, robot command). The Implementation Map section (L1022-1067) is internally honest that wiring is future work — but that honesty lives in a section most marketing-level readers won't reach.

Until the sibling epic **br-bn0vb (ATC Learning Loop Closure)** lands its Seam 6 validation (acceptance: live send_message produces an observable experience row), the README should carry a clear disclaimer at the **top of the ATC section** — not buried in the Implementation Map.

## Edits required

Insert a callout at the top of the ATC Learning Implementation Map section (README.md, just before L1022):

```markdown
> **Status (as of $DATE): architecture-phase, not learning-phase.** The ATC module
> scaffolding, schema, policy engine, evidence ledger, and operator surfaces all
> exist and are tested. What the system does *not* yet do in production builds is
> write real experience rows on tool dispatch or resolve outcomes from real
> execution signals. Epic br-bn0vb tracks closing that loop. Until it closes,
> `am robot atc` and the TUI Atc screen report availability + summaries but no
> live learning.
```

(Substitute the actual date when landing the edit.)

Also add a shorter pointer at the feature-bullet level. The README doesn't have a top-level ATC feature bullet today, but if one is added during the docs sweep, mark it "(architecture-phase)".

## Soft dependency

This bead depends on **br-bn0vb.1** (Seam 1 audit) closing first, so the exact wording accurately reflects which seams are done and which remain. Alternatively, we can land the disclaimer pre-audit with language "scaffolding exists, hot-path wiring is future work" which is currently accurate.

## Removal trigger

This disclaimer MUST be removed when Epic br-bn0vb Seam 6.1 (E2E full-learning-event test) passes. The removal is its own follow-up bead (`br-bn0vb.7`) under the ATC epic.

```bash
rg -nF 'architecture-phase' README.md   # >= 1 until br-bn0vb closes, then 0
```

## Considerations

- Be precise: do NOT say "ATC doesn't work" — the engine works, it's just not receiving live production events yet.
- Do NOT say "disabled" — the surfaces are reachable, they just have nothing live to show.
- Cross-link to epic br-bn0vb by ID so a reader can trace to the closure work.

title: Docs: CI check that auto-verifies tool/resource/screen counts match code (prevent future drift)
description:
# Task: CI drift-prevention check for doc counts

## Why this bead exists

The reality-check (2026-04-17) found the README had drifted by:
- +1 to -3 tools across different claims (36 vs 34 vs actual 37)
- 8 over-claim on resources (33 vs actual 25)
- 1 under-claim on screens (15 vs actual 16)
- "Tantivy Lexical" naming for what is actually frankensearch
- Misleading "no ad-hoc SQL fallback" claim

These drifted over months of active development because nobody re-counted. After sibling beads br-o217s.1-7 correct the counts, we need an **automated check** that prevents the SAME drift from returning next time someone adds a tool/resource/screen without updating README.

## Implementation

Add `tests/docs_drift_check.rs` (or `crates/mcp-agent-mail-conformance/tests/doc_consistency.rs` — wherever fits the existing test layout):

```rust
#[test]
fn readme_tool_count_matches_code() {
    let actual = load_tool_cluster_map().len(); // from TOOL_CLUSTER_MAP in tools/src/lib.rs
    let readme = std::fs::read_to_string("README.md").unwrap();
    let claimed = extract_claim(&readme, r"(\d+) MCP [Tt]ools").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        actual, claimed,
        "README claims {} tools but code has {}. \
         Update README.md L15/L89/L547 or sibling count claims, or regenerate via `am tooling directory`.",
        claimed, actual
    );
}

#[test]
fn readme_resource_count_matches_code() { ... }

#[test]
fn readme_screen_count_matches_code() { ... }

#[test]
fn agents_md_tool_count_matches_readme() { ... }

#[test]
fn budgets_search_naming_is_current() {
    // forbidden stale phrases
    let budgets = std::fs::read_to_string("benches/BUDGETS.md").unwrap();
    for stale in &["Tantivy Lexical"] {
        assert!(!budgets.contains(stale),
                "BUDGETS.md contains stale phrase {:?}. Use 'frankensearch lexical' instead.",
                stale);
    }
}
```

## Logging requirements

Each failing assertion must produce an actionable message including:
- What was expected (number from code)
- What was found (number from docs)
- Which file(s) + line(s) to update
- Which source of truth was consulted (e.g., "TOOL_CLUSTER_MAP at crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/lib.rs:1670")
- A hint about the sibling beads that did the original correction (so future developers find the precedent)

## Test coverage

Tests that must pass:
1. readme_tool_count_matches_code — 37 expected
2. readme_resource_count_matches_code — 25 expected
3. readme_screen_count_matches_code — 16 expected
4. agents_md_tool_count_matches_readme — same number in both
5. agents_md_resource_count_matches_readme — same
6. agents_md_screen_count_matches_readme — same
7. budgets_search_naming_is_current — no "Tantivy Lexical" stale phrasing
8. readme_atc_disclaimer_toggles_correctly — disclaimer present iff ATC loop not yet closed (soft; harder to automate perfectly but can gate on existence of br-bn0vb.14 closed marker or similar)

## Tests that SHOULD fail when they're supposed to

Include a negative test case (runnable separately, e.g., `#[ignore]`) that deliberately modifies a temp README and verifies the check catches the drift. Prevents the test itself from silently no-oping.

## CI integration

- Tests run as part of `cargo test -p mcp-agent-mail-conformance` or similar
- No additional CI job needed; piggyback on existing test workflow

## Non-goals

- Not auto-fixing README (that's too aggressive; failing CI is enough signal)
- Not validating every README claim (would become a never-ending maintenance burden); just the numeric/naming drift vectors that already hit us
- Not enforcing prose style

## Definition of done

- Test file compiled and passing locally
- Test integrated into CI workflow
- Deliberate drift (e.g., claiming 99 tools in a test README fixture) causes test failure with a clear error message
- Tests documented in the conformance crate README or a comment block at the top of the test file
close_reason: Completed: added docs drift consistency guard with README/AGENTS count assertions and stale-search naming checks

# docs/ comprehensive sweep

## Why this bead exists

Sibling beads br-o217s.1-3 correct tool/resource/screen counts in README.md and AGENTS.md. But the repo's `docs/` directory contains 30+ markdown files — ADRs, spec docs, runbooks, migration guides, rollout playbooks. Many of them were written at various times and may carry stale numbers.

A targeted grep while fixing README is insufficient: some docs embed numbers in narrative prose ("the system currently supports 34 tools across 9 clusters..."), in table headers, or in JSON fixture snippets. Need a deliberate pass.

## Scope

### Files in scope

Walk every file under `docs/` and any `*.md` in the repo root (except CHANGELOG.md and the 5 reality-check epic plans themselves). Key files likely affected:

- docs/ADR-001 / ADR-002 / ADR-003
- docs/RUNBOOK-search-v3-migration.md

- docs/DUAL_MODE_ROLLOUT_PLAYBOOK.md
- docs/SPEC-search-v3-query-contract.md

- docs/TUI_V2_CONTRACT.md + TUI_V2_PARITY_DIFF.md

- docs/SPEC-search-v3-quality-gates.md
- docs/SPEC-tui-v2-product-contract.md
- docs/SPEC-unified-search-corpus.md
- docs/VERIFICATION_COVERAGE_LEDGER.md
- docs/CYCLE_SEMANTICS.md
- docs/REGRESSION_BOUNDARIES.md
- docs/INCIDENT_* files
- All TEMPLATE_* files

### What to verify in each

Using a comprehensive grep pass for each doc file:

1. Tool count (any "34" / "36" / "37 tools" or equivalent phrasing)
2. Resource count (any "20+" / "25" / "33 resources" phrasing)
3. TUI screen count (any "15" / "16 screens" phrasing)
4. Search-engine naming ("Tantivy" where "frankensearch" is meant)
5. "Ad-hoc SQL fallback" phrasing
6. "23 tools all passing" or equivalent conformance phrasing
7. Tool cluster names (some docs group into different clusters than the current 9)
8. Transport path references (should match current /mcp/ and /mail/ etc.)
9. Port references (8765 is canonical)
10. Binary names (mcp-agent-mail + am)

### Edit discipline

- For each file found to contain stale content: fix in-place
- If a file is genuinely historical (ADR describing a past decision that was correct at the time), ADD a dated note at the top, don't alter the historical content
- ADRs should be treated differently from RUNBOOKs: ADRs are immutable decision records; RUNBOOKs are living operational docs

### Artifact

- `docs/DOC_SWEEP_AUDIT_<date>.md` — one row per file in scope, with:
  - file path
  - issues found (counts of stale-count / stale-naming / etc.)
  - action taken (fixed inline / added historical note / no action needed)
  - before/after grep verification

## Test plan

- Verification grep pass after edits: every "old count" phrase returns 0 matches OR is within an explicit ADR historical context
- Cross-check with br-o217s.8 (CI drift check): expand its scope to include docs/ directory, not just README+AGENTS.md
- Random-sample read: 5 files re-read end-to-end, verify no remaining inconsistencies

## Logging requirements

Per-file audit log:
```
docs.sweep.file_scanned { path, stale_patterns_matched, category: "adr"|"runbook"|"spec"|"template" }
docs.sweep.edit_applied { path, pattern, action: "fix_inline"|"historical_note"|"skip" }
docs.sweep.summary { files_scanned, files_edited, patterns_total, patterns_remaining }
```

## Dependencies

- Depends on br-o217s.1, .2, .3 (primary count corrections) — this bead is the broader sweep after the canonical source-of-truth files are set
- Feeds br-o217s.7 (consistency sweep) — the final sweep should include docs/ verification commands
- Related to br-o217s.8 (CI drift check) — extend the CI check to cover docs/

## Definition of done

- All in-scope files scanned
- Audit doc committed with per-file results
- CI drift check extended to cover docs/ (at least the grep for forbidden phrases)
- Re-running reality-check finds no doc-level stale counts

title: ATC durable learning store for file-backed mailboxes
description:
## What
Design and implement a safe durable ATC experience-store path for normal file-backed operator mailboxes. Today the runtime contains validated ATC append/resolve/rollup code, but server-side writability still refuses file-backed pools, leaving live learning unavailable for the normal deployment shape.

## Why
ATC is most valuable under large real swarms, which use persistent file-backed mailboxes. Keeping learning effectively memory-only means the operator loses longitudinal calibration, policy replay, and postmortem value exactly where it matters.

## How
Start with the existing canonical ATC query/write helpers in `mcp-agent-mail-db::queries`. Choose the least risky boundary: either a dedicated ATC sidecar SQLite file under STORAGE_ROOT or a proven canonical-connection path with strict feature gates. Preserve `AM_ATC_WRITE_MODE=off` as default until canary gates pass. Never increase Git write amplification.

## Risks
This area previously destabilized file-backed FrankenConnection writes. The implementation must fail closed to shadow/off, never corrupt the main mailbox, and include recovery/backup behavior before enabling live mode.

## Success criteria
- File-backed live ATC append/resolve/query works under an isolated STORAGE_ROOT.
- Main mailbox `PRAGMA quick_check` remains clean after high-volume ATC rows.
- Recovery/reconstruct preserves or explicitly rebuilds ATC data.
- Unit + integration + no-mock e2e coverage prove append, resolve, restart, and fallback behavior.
- rch-run check/clippy/test gates pass for touched crates.
close_reason: Implemented file-backed durable ATC learning-store enablement with real canonical SQLite transition and integrity proof coverage

title: ATC privacy and retention operator report

## What
Add an operator report showing what ATC learning data is stored, how much exists per project/stratum, what has suspected-secret flags, and what retention/redaction options are available.

title: Artifact retention and budget governor
description:
## What
Create a retention and budget governor for test, perf, forensic, and e2e artifacts so long swarm sessions can keep useful evidence without unbounded disk growth.

## Why
This repo intentionally produces proof artifacts. On high-volume agent systems, artifacts can become their own reliability problem if not summarized, indexed, and pruned/quarantined safely.

## How
Inventory artifact roots, define retention classes, add `am doctor artifacts` or tooling diagnostics, and emit warnings before disk pressure. Never delete by default; recommend archive/compress/quarantine commands.

## Risks
No automatic deletion without explicit operator command. Avoid hiding evidence needed for postmortems.

## Success criteria
- Artifact roots and sizes are reported with retention class.
- Disk-pressure warnings include exact largest roots and safe remediation.
- Tests use temp artifact trees and prove no default deletion.
- Docs describe retention policy and manual cleanup workflow.

title: Archive tamper-evidence verifier

## What

Git is the audit ledger. Operators need a clear answer when archive artifacts and SQLite disagree, especially after manual edits, crashes, or migrations.

- Verifier reports drift classes with severity and safe next action.

title: ATC live-canary SLO gate with automatic fallback
description:
## What
Add an operator-facing live-canary gate for ATC write mode promotion. The gate should compare no-ATC, shadow, and live/canary behavior on real operator paths and automatically recommend or enforce fallback when SLOs regress.

## Why
ATC learning should become useful without requiring operators to guess whether live mode is safe. A clear canary verdict makes rollout understandable: what changed, what budget was consumed, and what fallback was applied.

## How
Build on `docs/ATC_PERF_BUDGETS.md`, `scripts/bench_atc_perf_gate.sh`, robot ATC snapshots, and existing `AM_ATC_WRITE_MODE`/executor modes. Add a persisted canary report with p50/p95/p99, error count, write-amplification, DB health, and recommendation. Expose it in robot/TUI before changing defaults.

## Risks
The gate must not silently enable live mode on the shared mailbox. It must distinguish host noise from real regressions and keep operator override paths explicit.

## Success criteria
- Canary report captures latency, quick_check, ATC rows, and fallback decision.
- Live mode can be disabled automatically or recommended for disable when SLOs fail.
- Robot and TUI show last canary verdict with artifact path.
- E2E uses isolated STORAGE_ROOT and produces replayable logs.
- rch-run check/clippy/tests pass for touched crates.

title: Replayable swarm capacity simulator from mailbox traces
description:
## What
Build a capacity simulator that converts real mailbox/topology traces into replayable load plans for 100, 1k, and 10k agent scenarios. It should exercise messages, reservations, build slots, search, robot snapshots, and ATC observations without touching the operator mailbox.

## Why
The project already has strong stress tests, but operators running huge swarms need forecast-style answers: how many agents can this machine handle, which surface saturates first, and what cache/profile settings should they choose?

## How
Use anonymized archive/SQLite snapshots, the existing load lab, robot analytics topology, and `AM_CACHE_PROFILE` controls. Generate deterministic scenarios with configurable agent/message/reservation distributions and produce JSON summaries with p50/p95/p99, RSS, DB query counts, queue depth, and cache hit ratios.

## Risks
Synthetic traces can lie. The simulator must preserve enough real structure to predict contention and must label all generated evidence as replay/simulation rather than production measurement.

## Success criteria
- CLI or test harness can replay a captured trace into an isolated STORAGE_ROOT.
- Reports include latency, throughput, CPU/RSS, DB, WBQ, and cache metrics.
- Fixtures prove stable results for at least 100 and 1k agent scenarios.
- Artifacts land under `tests/artifacts/perf/swarm_capacity/`.
- rch-run ignored/load tests are documented with exact commands.

title: No-mock mailbox recovery chaos harness
description:
## What
Create a no-mock recovery chaos harness that repeatedly boots real server/CLI flows against intentionally damaged isolated mailboxes: malformed SQLite, header-only WAL, live sidecars, archive drift, orphan recipients, stale locks, and interrupted repair/reconstruct runs.

## Why
The user-visible failure class is startup/repair reliability. Unit tests catch many details, but confidence comes from replaying real `am` and `doctor` surfaces against real files with forensic artifacts.

## How
Extend existing e2e/doctor/reconstruct patterns. Every scenario must create its own STORAGE_ROOT, capture stdout/stderr/exit/server logs/forensic bundles, and assert both operator text and machine-readable JSON. Avoid deleting evidence; quarantine or leave artifacts.

## Risks
Chaos tests can be slow or flaky. Keep a fast smoke lane for CI and ignored heavier lanes for rch workers. Never run against the default operator mailbox.

## Success criteria
- `tests/e2e/test_recovery_chaos.sh` or native `am e2e` suite covers at least 8 real damage scenarios.
- Each scenario emits structured logs and replay command.
- Repair vs reconstruct decisions are asserted, not inferred from exit code alone.
- Forensic bundle manifests are inspected for expected sidecars/backups.
- rch-run smoke gate passes; ignored heavy lane is documented.
close_reason: Completed recovery chaos harness and doctor repair hardening

- Robot JSON/toon and at least two TUI screens render recommendations.
- Tests cover ranking, dedupe, redaction, and stale-evidence suppression.

title: ATC tests: AgentRhythm + Liveness boundary conditions
description:
# AgentRhythm & Liveness Boundary Condition Tests

## Tests to Add

1. **observe with out-of-order timestamps**: call observe(100), then
   observe(50). The delta should be clamped to 0 via .max(0). Verify
   avg_interval doesn't go negative.

2. **observe with same timestamp twice**: delta=0. Verify no division
   by zero or NaN in variance calculation.

3. **is_suspicious before any observation**: last_activity_ts=0 should
   return false regardless of now_micros.

4. **suspicion_threshold with zero variance**: after many identical-interval
   observations, var_interval → 0. Threshold = avg + k*0 = avg. Verify
   silence just above avg triggers suspicion.

5. **AgentLivenessEntry resurrection from Dead**: set state=Dead, call
   observe_activity. Verify state resets to Alive and SPRT/suspect fields
   clear.

6. **evaluate_liveness skips Dead agents**: register agent, manually set
   to Dead, verify evaluate_liveness returns empty actions for that agent.

7. **observe_activity for unregistered agent**: call observe_activity
   with an agent name that was never registered. Verify it's silently
   ignored (no panic, no new entry created).

## Files
- crates/mcp-agent-mail-server/src/atc.rs (add to mod liveness_tests and engine_tests)

title: P1: Resolve idempotent message replays before consuming a new ID
description: create_message_with_recipients_impl reads the DB floor and allocates a fresh explicit message id before its transaction checks the idempotency claim. Every replay/conflict burns an id, scans archive state unnecessarily on a cold allocator, and at i64::MAX returns allocator exhaustion instead of the already-committed replay/conflict result.
acceptance_criteria: An existing idempotency claim returns its exact replay or conflict outcome without allocating or advancing the message-id high-water. Concurrent first claims still elect exactly one fresh message and preserve payload conflict semantics. A mutation-sensitive test seeds the allocator at i64::MAX plus a valid prior claim and proves replay succeeds while a truly fresh request fails closed; high-water remains unchanged for replay/conflict. Required checks/tests pass.

title: ATC Track 14: Queueing-Theoretic Load Router — Provable Response Time Guarantees
F7 (upstream sqlmodel-pool): PooledConnection::drop max-lifetime path builds a throwaway current-thread runtime per close — close synchronously or use a reaper thread
[cli] clippy no-deps fails on CLI lints

title: ATC Track 7: Session Synthesizer (Monotone Accumulation + Incremental Rendering)
GH#161: serve-http RSS grows to multiple GB under load (glibc arena fragmentation, no #[global_allocator]) → memory_pressure=Critical → health_check RED
close_reason: GH#161 fixed: mimalloc global_allocator on both binaries; compiled+linked, clippy green. Commit 4c81509b.

title: Stale cache test agent_invalidate_clears_all_matching_stale_id_entries asserts pre-GH#169 last-write-wins id (expects 56, canonical is 55)
close_reason: Fixed stale assertion: agent_invalidate_clears_all_matching_stale_id_entries asserted get_agent==Some(56) (pre-GH#169 last-write-wins) but GH#169 pins the canonical lowest-id (55). Updated to Some(55); the test's real purpose (invalidate id=None clears all matching by-id entries 55 AND 56) is preserved + documented.

title: busy_timeout 60s exceeds dispatch deadline 30s: queries outlive their zombified dispatch
description: SQLite busy_timeout=60s (db/src/schema.rs ~279) but blocking-dispatch client deadline is 30s (ECOSYSTEM_CLIENT_DEADLINE_MS, core/src/config.rs:18). A lock-contended query blocks its OS thread up to 60s while dispatch gave up at 30s and zombified the permit. Align busy_timeout below the dispatch deadline (e.g. 20s) or make it adaptive.
close_reason: Runtime busy_timeout 60s -> DB_RUNTIME_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=20s (< 30s dispatch deadline, compile-time-guarded); startup pragma gate follows; off-deadline recovery/maintenance paths keep 60s with comments

title: P1: Fingerprint the complete stable SQLite recovery family
description: The durable recovery breaker fingerprint currently covers only the primary file and does not prove a stable read length. Sidecar-only generation changes and concurrent primary mutation can therefore reuse stale authority or publish a ghost fingerprint that matched no complete SQLite family.
acceptance_criteria: Breaker authority fingerprints the complete relevant SQLite family with no-follow stable identity/length/content witnesses and detects concurrent drift. Sidecar-only generation replacement changes the fingerprint; a same-length concurrent primary rewrite cannot publish a mixed/ghost fingerprint; missing and healthy controls are deterministic. Existing breaker compatibility is replaced directly rather than shimmed. Workspace check, clippy -D warnings, fmt, and targeted tests pass.

title: Startup self-heal wedge: TUI/serve-http spin CPU-bound before bind on large mailboxes (bespoke-engine foreign_key_check O(n²))
close_reason: Fixed in 3c7f8c14 (main+master). Root cause: startup doctor_database_fix_strategy (cleanup=true) ran FULL integrity_check + per-row foreign_key_check on the bespoke FrankenSQLite engine (O(child_rows×parent_lookup)); 36k reservations × 2 FKs spun for minutes before the listener bound. Fix: doctor_relational_integrity_diagnostics now prefers the canonical engine (bespoke fallback) and the startup integrity_check uses sqlite_file_check_ok_canonical — matching the already-fast read-only health path. Canonical does the full battery in ~0.3s on 21977 reservations (measured). Verdicts/auto-repair preserved; 22 tests pass + new canonical-engine regression test. Discovered via ts2/css incident reports.

title: Add integration tests for DB + storage pipelines (archive + SQLite consistency)
description: Add integration tests that exercise the full DB+storage pipeline: send_message with archive write verification, reservation creation with artifact check, concurrent operations with consistency assertions. Validates DB-first consistency model end-to-end.

On platforms that admit non-Unicode path bytes, replacement characters can redirect resolution to a different path while diagnostics continue to present the lossy authority.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit path authorities are normalized without lossy conversion where possible, or fail closed with a precise invalid-Unicode error before probing or mutation. Unix mutation-sensitive tests use distinct non-UTF-8 and replacement-character paths and prove the latter is never accessed; ordinary Unicode and Windows-native paths retain behavior; targeted remote tests plus workspace gates pass.
